# How many Delta Sky Club visits does the Amex Platinum give, and what are the rules?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/amex-platinum-delta-sky-club-visits/
Facts checked: 2026-11-21
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

The Platinum Card gives 10 Delta Sky Club visits per year, counted from February 1 to January 31, and only when you fly Delta that day on a ticket that is not basic economy. Guests cost $50 each, and so does each visit after the tenth.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## The numbers

These figures are from Delta's own Sky Club access page. The rules have applied since February 1, 2025.

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Visits included | 10 per Medallion Year (February 1 to January 31) |
| Unused visits | Lost; no rollover, no transfer |
| Extra visits after 10 | $50 per person |
| Guests | Up to two guests, or immediate family, at $50 each per visit |
| Children under 2 | Free |
| Grab and Go (food to take away, no lounge entry) | $25 per person |
| Unlimited visits | After $75,000 of eligible purchases on the card in a calendar year |

The 10 visits are for the cardholder only. They cannot be used to bring a guest in.

## What counts as one visit

A visit is not one door entry. Delta defines it as entries at one or more airports for up to 24 hours, starting from your first entry or Grab and Go use.

| Trip | Visits used |
|---|---|
| One Sky Club before a nonstop flight | 1 |
| Sky Clubs at the departure airport and at a connection, same day | 1 |
| Sky Club before departure and another after landing, within 24 hours | 1 |
| Outbound on Monday, return on Friday, a Sky Club each way | 2 |

So 10 visits cover about five round trips for someone who uses a Sky Club in each direction.

## Which flights qualify

You need a same-day boarding pass for one of these, departing from or arriving at the airport where the lounge is:

- A Delta-operated flight, including Delta Connection.
- A Delta-marketed flight operated by WestJet, with a ticket number starting 006.

Not accepted:

- Delta Main Basic, the airline's basic economy fare. Guests on that fare are refused too.
- Flights on other airlines, including other Delta partners.
- Partner lounges. The benefit is for Delta Sky Clubs only.

## When you can enter

- **Before departure:** only within 3 hours of the scheduled departure time.
- **During a layover:** at any time.
- **After arrival:** Delta's page allows entry on a same-day flight arriving at that airport. Upgraded Points notes this works on domestic arrivals; after an international flight you leave through customs and are outside the secure area.

A phone boarding pass can disappear from the app after landing. Upgraded Points suggests keeping a screenshot.

## Additional cardholders

Each additional Platinum cardholder gets their own 10 visits a year, according to Delta's page. An additional Platinum card costs $195 a year; see [whether an additional card is worth $195](/amex-platinum-authorized-user-worth-195/). The no-fee Companion Platinum Card does not get Sky Club access.

For a couple, this can cost less than paying guest fees. Ten shared visits with one guest at $50 would be $500 in guest fees.

## Unlimited visits

After $75,000 of eligible purchases on the account in a calendar year, visits become unlimited. Purchases by additional cardholders count toward the total. Delta says it usually takes about a week, and up to 12 weeks, to take effect.

Sources differ on how long it lasts. Delta's page, as read, describes the rest of that calendar year and through January 31 of the next calendar year. The Points Guy says it runs through the end of the next program year, which would be a year longer. Confirm with Amex before counting on the longer period.

Even with unlimited visits, guests still cost $50 each.

## What it is worth

A paid visit costs $50, so 10 visits have a list value of $500. The real value depends on how often you fly Delta from an airport with a Sky Club, on a fare above basic economy.

| Delta round trips a year | Visits likely used | Value at $50 each |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0 | $0 |
| 2 | 4 | $200 |
| 5 or more | 10 | $500 |

Frequent Delta flyers may run out. The Delta SkyMiles Reserve card gives 15 visits; see [Platinum vs. Delta SkyMiles Reserve](/amex-platinum-vs-delta-skymiles-reserve/). The Platinum Card's other lounges have separate rules; see [Centurion Lounge guest rules](/amex-platinum-centurion-lounge-guest-rules/).

## Who should skip it

Count Sky Club access as $0 if:

- You rarely fly Delta.
- You usually buy Delta's basic economy fare.
- Your home airport has no Sky Club and you seldom connect through a Delta hub.
- You travel with family and would pay $50 a person each time.

## Quick answers

**How many Sky Club visits come with the Amex Platinum?**
Ten per year, counted from February 1 to January 31. Unused visits do not roll over.

**Can a Platinum cardholder enter a Sky Club on a basic economy ticket?**
No. Delta Main Basic fares are excluded, for the cardholder and for guests.

**How much is a Sky Club guest with the Amex Platinum?**
$50 per guest per visit, for up to two guests or immediate family. Children under 2 are free.

## Sources

- [Delta: Sky Club access rules](https://www.delta.com/us/en/delta-sky-club/access)
- [The Points Guy: Amex Platinum lounge access](https://thepointsguy.com/guide/american-express-platinum-lounge-access/)
- [The Points Guy: guide to Delta Sky Club access](https://thepointsguy.com/loyalty-programs/ultimate-guide-delta-sky-club-access/)
- [Upgraded Points: Sky Clubs on arrival with the Amex Platinum](https://upgradedpoints.com/news/delta-sky-clubs-on-arrival-amex-platinum/)
- [Upgraded Points: Amex Platinum airport lounge access](https://upgradedpoints.com/credit-cards/reviews/american-express-platinum-card/airport-lounge-access/)

# Which subscriptions count for the Amex Platinum digital entertainment credit?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/amex-platinum-digital-entertainment-credit-what-counts/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

The credit covers Disney+ (and Disney+ bundles), Hulu, ESPN streaming, Paramount+, standalone Peacock, YouTube Premium, YouTube TV, The New York Times and The Wall Street Journal, when you pay the provider directly with an enrolled Platinum Card. Netflix, Spotify, Apple TV and Amazon Prime Video are not on the list.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## How the credit works

- Up to $25 back each month, which is up to $300 a year.
- You must enroll once in your Amex account. Charges before enrollment do not count.
- An unused month is lost. If your eligible subscriptions cost $12 a month, you get $12, not $25.
- Statement credits can take up to 8 weeks, though AwardWallet reports they usually post sooner.
- There is one credit per card account. An additional card does not add a second $25.

## What counts, as of November 2026

| Service | Counts | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Disney+ | Yes | Including bundles bought at disneyplus.com, such as Disney+/Hulu/ESPN and Disney+/Hulu/HBO Max |
| Hulu | Yes | Bought at hulu.com |
| ESPN streaming | Yes | Bought directly from ESPN |
| Paramount+ | Yes | Bought at paramountplus.com |
| Peacock | Yes, standalone only | Bundles and add-ons stopped counting on August 1, 2026 |
| YouTube Premium | Yes | Bought directly from YouTube |
| YouTube TV | Yes | Bought directly from YouTube |
| The New York Times | Yes | News, Games, Cooking, Wirecutter, All Access |
| The Wall Street Journal | Yes | Including bundles with Barron's or MarketWatch |
| YouTube Music | Sources disagree | AwardWallet lists it; Amex's own list names only YouTube Premium and YouTube TV |

## What does not count

| Service | Counts |
|---|---|
| Netflix | No |
| HBO Max bought by itself | No |
| Apple TV, Apple Music | No |
| Amazon Prime Video | No |
| Spotify | No |
| Audible | No (removed in October 2025) |

The list is fixed by Amex. A streaming service that is not named earns nothing, however similar it is.

## The billing rule that catches people

The charge must come straight from the provider. These do not count, even for a service on the list:

- A subscription billed through a third party, such as an app store, a cable company or another streaming device's billing.
- A subscription that is part of a cable bundle.
- Gift cards.
- Third-party promotional offers.

If you already pay for Disney+ or Paramount+ through an app store, you would need to cancel there and sign up again on the provider's own website with the Platinum Card for the credit to apply.

## The Peacock change

Until July 31, 2026, some cardholders used a Peacock bundle to get a second service, such as Apple TV, covered by the credit. From August 1, 2026, Peacock bundles, Peacock add-ons and Peacock bought through a third party no longer count. A standalone Peacock plan bought at peacocktv.com still does.

## Annual plans

How an annual subscription is credited is not confirmed. The only limit the sources state is $25 per month, which suggests a single yearly charge would earn $25 once. If you want the full credit, a monthly plan is the safer assumption.

## What it is worth to you

The value is what you already pay for these exact services, capped at $25 a month.

| What you pay today | Yearly value |
|---|---|
| YouTube TV, or two or three listed services totaling $25 or more a month | $300 |
| One mid-priced listed service at about $12 a month | About $144 |
| Only Netflix and Spotify | $0 |

One overlap to know about: the card's separate Walmart+ credit pays for a Walmart+ membership, and AwardWallet notes that Walmart+ includes a choice of Paramount+ or Peacock. If you use that, spend the $25 on something else.

## Who should skip it

Do not count this credit toward the $895 annual fee if:

- Your subscriptions are Netflix, Spotify, Apple or Amazon. None qualify.
- You get streaming through a cable or phone bundle and do not want to change it.
- You would sign up for a service only because the credit pays for it.

To add this to the other credits, see [what the credits are worth](/amex-platinum-credits-real-value/).

## Quick answers

**Does Netflix count for the Amex Platinum digital entertainment credit?**
No. Netflix is not on the list of eligible services.

**Does a subscription billed through an app store count?**
No. The charge must come directly from the provider, such as disneyplus.com or peacocktv.com.

**Do Peacock bundles still count?**
No. Since August 1, 2026, only a standalone Peacock plan bought directly from Peacock counts.

## Sources

- [AwardWallet: Amex Platinum entertainment credit](https://awardwallet.com/credit-cards/amex-membership-rewards/amex-platinum-entertainment-credit/)
- [American Express: the digital entertainment credit](https://www.americanexpress.com/en-us/credit-cards/credit-intel/how-does-the-amex-platinum-digital-entertainment-credit-work/)
- [The Points Guy: Peacock change to the credit](https://thepointsguy.com/news/amex-platinum-peacock-digital-entertainment-credit-update)
- [Upgraded Points: digital entertainment credit](https://upgradedpoints.com/credit-cards/reviews/american-express-platinum-card/digital-entertainment-credit/)

# If the Amex Platinum fee stops being worth it, what are the options and what happens to the points?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/amex-platinum-downgrade-or-cancel-options/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

There are three options: ask Amex for a retention offer and keep the card, downgrade to the Gold Card ($325) or the Green Card ($150), or cancel. Your Membership Rewards points stay if you keep any card that earns them. If the Platinum is your only one and you close it, the points are forfeited.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## The options side by side

| Option | Yearly fee after | Points | Credit report | Main cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Keep, with a retention offer | $895 | Kept | No change | You still pay the fee |
| Downgrade to Gold | $325 | Kept | No new account | Likely no Gold welcome offer later |
| Downgrade to Green | $150 | Kept | No new account | Few benefits |
| Cancel, with another Membership Rewards card open | $0 for this card | Kept | Account closed | Lounge access and credits end |
| Cancel, with no other such card | $0 | Forfeited | Account closed | The points |

There is no downgrade to a card with no annual fee, per Upgraded Points.

## Option 1: ask for a retention offer

Call the number on the card or use chat and ask whether any offer is available. Amex does not publish these offers. Reports vary:

- The Points Guy cites one offer of 50,000 points for keeping the card another year.
- Frequent Miler (2022) reports offers of 30,000 to 55,000 points, some with a spending condition, and statement credits. Some people got nothing.

Do not count on an offer.

## Option 2: downgrade

Upgraded Points (October 2026) reports:

- The account must have been open at least 12 months.
- The choices are the Gold Card, $325, or the Classic Green Card, $150. The Green Card closed to new applicants on July 23, 2026, and is still available as a downgrade.
- It is done by phone or chat, and no change is recorded on your credit report.

**The welcome offer cost.** Amex generally gives a welcome offer once per card. A downgrade counts as having had the new card, and having had a Platinum Card can already block the Gold offer. See [the once-per-lifetime rule](/amex-once-per-lifetime-welcome-offer-rule/).

**Is Gold a fit?** See [Platinum versus Gold](/amex-platinum-vs-gold-which-fits/) and [whether the Gold fee pays back](/amex-gold-card-worth-the-fee/).

## Option 3: cancel

Before closing, the points question comes first.

**If another Membership Rewards card stays open**, the points stay in your account. View From the Wing reports that newer cards may not be pooled into one balance, so confirm both cards show the same balance first.

**If the Platinum is your only such card**, closing it forfeits unused points. Ways to avoid that:

- Transfer the points to an airline or hotel program first. Transfers cannot be reversed. See [what the points are worth](/amex-membership-rewards-points-value/).
- Open a second Membership Rewards card before closing. Frequent Miler names the Blue Business Plus, a business card with no annual fee.

Sources disagree on timing. Doctor of Credit says closing your last such card forfeits the points. AwardWallet (April 2026) says you have 30 days after canceling to use them. Move or use the points before you close.

## What happens to the annual fee

| Situation | Refund reported |
|---|---|
| Close within 30 days after the closing date of the statement that shows the fee | Full refund |
| Close later than that | None |
| Downgrade at any time | Prorated: the unused part is refunded and the new card's fee is charged for the rest |

These rules come from Doctor of Credit (2020) and Frequent Miler (2022). Upgraded Points says only that you "may qualify" for a prorated refund on a downgrade. None was confirmed on an Amex page, so ask the agent to state the refund before you agree.

## Before you act

- Use the [credits](/amex-platinum-credits-real-value/) you have already paid for.
- Closing in the first 12 months is a risk. Search summaries say Amex's terms let it take back welcome points; this is not confirmed.

## Who should skip each option

- **Skip relying on a retention offer** if the card only works for you with one.
- **Skip the Gold downgrade** if you would not use its credits.
- **Skip the Green downgrade** if a no-fee card can hold your points.
- **Skip canceling** until the points are moved, used or held by another card.

## Quick answers

**Do I lose my points if I downgrade the Platinum Card?**
No. The Gold and Green cards both earn Membership Rewards points, so the balance stays.

**Do I lose my points if I cancel?**
Only if no other card that earns Membership Rewards points stays open. In that case unused points are forfeited.

**Will Amex refund the $895 fee?**
A full refund is reported if you close within 30 days after the closing date of the statement showing the fee. After that, no refund on closing is reported.

## Sources

- [Upgraded Points: Amex Platinum upgrade and downgrade process](https://upgradedpoints.com/credit-cards/reviews/american-express-platinum-card/upgrade-downgrade-process/)
- [The Points Guy: downgrading the Amex Platinum to the Gold](https://thepointsguy.com/news/amex-platinum-downgrade-amex-gold)
- [Doctor of Credit: annual fee refund rules by issuer](https://doctorofcredit.com/annual-fee-refund-rules-for-each-card-issuer)
- [Frequent Miler: the strategy before you cancel](https://frequentmiler.com/dont-want-to-pay-that-695-annual-fee-heres-the-strategy-before-you-cancel/)
- [AwardWallet: do Amex points expire](https://awardwallet.com/credit-cards/amex-membership-rewards/do-amex-points-expire/)
- [View From the Wing: check points pooling before you cancel a card](https://viewfromthewing.com/?p=258466)

# American Express Platinum golf benefits: what does the card do for golfers?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/amex-platinum-for-golfers/
Facts checked: 2026-11-23
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

Very little directly. The US Amex Platinum has no free rounds, no green fee credit and no tee time priority; what it offers a golfer is travel help around the trip, mainly a hotel credit, airport lounges and some travel protections.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## What the card does not have

The current benefit lists for the US personal Platinum Card do not mention golf.

| Golf benefit | On the US Amex Platinum? |
|---|---|
| Free or discounted rounds | No |
| Statement credit for green fees | No |
| Priority tee times | No |
| Golf club membership or network access | No |
| Help booking a tee time through the concierge | Not listed on Amex's card page. Upgraded Points says the concierge takes golf reservation requests; you pay for the round |
| Packaged golf trips | None found |

Platinum cards in some other countries, such as Singapore, have golf programs. Those do not apply to the US card.

How this compares with Visa Infinite and Mastercard golf programs is on [premium cards, tee times and golf packages](/premium-credit-card-golf-benefits-tee-times-packages/).

The card costs $895 a year. Nobody should pay that for golf benefits, because there are none to pay for.

## What does help on a golf trip

These benefits are not about golf, but a golf trip can use them.

### The hotel credit

The card gives up to $300 back each half-year, up to $600 per calendar year, on prepaid stays booked through Amex Travel at Fine Hotels + Resorts or The Hotel Collection properties, or on prepaid Airbnb Luxe bookings. The Hotel Collection and Airbnb Luxe need a two-night minimum, and from January 1, 2027, Fine Hotels + Resorts does too.

Fine Hotels + Resorts stays also include a property credit of at least $100 per stay, daily breakfast for two and a guaranteed 4 p.m. late checkout. What the property credit can be spent on varies by hotel, so ask the resort whether golf counts before you book. CNBC Select says the credit "can generally be used on hotel property golf courses to cover green fees."

### Airline fee credit

The card gives up to $200 a year for incidental fees, such as checked bags, on one airline you select in advance. If that airline charges a normal checked bag fee for your clubs, this is the kind of fee the credit is described as covering. Whether a separate oversize or sports equipment fee counts is not confirmed.

### Lounges

On travel days the card gets you into Centurion Lounges, Priority Pass lounges after enrollment, and Delta Sky Clubs up to 10 times a year when you fly Delta that day. Centurion guests cost $50 each, which matters if you travel with a group.

### Travel protections

| Protection | What sources report | Golf caveat |
|---|---|---|
| Trip delay | Up to $500 per trip for delays over 6 hours, round-trip travel, 2 claims per 12 months | Covers delay costs, not a missed tee time |
| Rental car | Secondary cover up to $75,000 when the rental is paid with the card and the rental company's waiver is declined | Secondary means your own insurance comes first |
| Baggage | Reported at up to $2,000 per checked bag, with a conflicting footnote in the same source | Whether golf clubs are covered is not confirmed. Read the benefit terms before relying on it |

### Points

Green fees, pro shop purchases and lessons earn 1 point per dollar. The card's 5 points per dollar apply only to flights and to prepaid hotels booked through Amex Travel.

## Is that enough for a golfer?

Add up only what you would use. One golf trip a year with a two-night prepaid stay at an eligible hotel and checked clubs might return $300 from the hotel credit and up to $200 in airline fees. That is $500 against an $895 fee. The rest has to come from credits that have nothing to do with golf.

## Who should not get it

- Golfers who want rewards on green fees and club spending. This card earns 1 point per dollar there.
- Golfers who drive to their courses and rarely fly or stay in hotels.
- Golfers who stay in ordinary rentals or mid-priced hotels. The hotel credit only works at hotels in Amex's two programs and on Airbnb Luxe bookings.
- Anyone expecting course access or tee time help as a card benefit.

## Quick answers

**Does the Amex Platinum give free rounds of golf?**
No. The US card has no free rounds, green fee credits or tee time priority.

**Can I use the Amex hotel credit at a golf resort?**
Yes, if the resort is in Fine Hotels + Resorts or The Hotel Collection and you prepay through Amex Travel. The credit is for the stay, not for golf.

**Does the card's baggage insurance cover golf clubs?**
Not confirmed. Check the benefit terms before relying on it.

## Sources

- [The Points Guy: Amex Platinum review](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/reviews/amex-platinum-review/)
- [Upgraded Points: Amex Platinum benefits](https://upgradedpoints.com/credit-cards/reviews/american-express-platinum-card/benefits/)
- [American Express: the $600 hotel credit](https://www.americanexpress.com/en-us/travel/get-inspired/Platinum-Card-600-Dollar-Hotel-Credit)
- [American Express: Platinum Card](https://www.americanexpress.com/us/credit-cards/card/platinum/)
- [American Express Singapore: Regional Golf Programme](https://www.americanexpress.com/en-sg/benefits/the-platinum-card/retail-and-lifestyle/regional-golf/)
- [The Points Guy: Amex Platinum lounge access](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/american-express-platinum-lounge-access/)
- [One Mile at a Time: Amex Platinum digital entertainment credit](https://onemileatatime.com/news/amex-platinum-digital-entertainment-credit-improved/)
- [Upgraded Points: Amex Platinum concierge service](https://upgradedpoints.com/credit-cards/reviews/american-express-platinum-card/concierge-service/)

# Does the Amex Platinum charge foreign transaction fees, and how well does it work abroad?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/amex-platinum-foreign-transaction-fees-abroad/
Facts checked: 2026-11-22
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

The Amex Platinum charges no foreign transaction fee on purchases, and its lounge and hotel benefits work around the world. American Express is accepted at fewer merchants abroad than Visa or Mastercard, cash from an ATM is expensive, and several of the card's statement credits apply only in the United States.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## The fee

Amex's cardmember agreement for the Platinum Card lists the foreign transaction fee as "None." Upgraded Points (November 2026) reports the same, and says additional Platinum Cards follow the same terms.

Upgraded Points, citing Amex, puts a typical foreign transaction fee on other cards at 3%.

| Spending in foreign currency | Card with a 3% fee | Amex Platinum |
|---|---|---|
| $1,000 | $30 | $0 |
| $4,000 | $120 | $0 |

Many cards with no annual fee also charge no foreign fee. This saving alone does not cover an $895 annual fee.

**The exchange rate.** Under the agreement, an Amex company converts each foreign charge to US dollars on the day it is processed. The rate is no more than the highest official government rate or the highest interbank rate it identifies for that day or the prior business day.

## Where the card is accepted

Sources describe acceptance abroad this way:

- Upgraded Points, citing Amex, gives more than 170 million accepting locations worldwide. It also says Amex does not have the international footprint of Visa or Mastercard, and that acceptance varies by merchant.
- The Points Guy (2021) says Amex is easier to use in countries such as Australia and Canada, and that in Europe and Asia it varies from merchant to merchant.
- Upgraded Points lists places where Amex is not accepted at all: Belarus, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Russia, Syria, and Crimea and the Donetsk and Luhansk regions of Ukraine.

Both sources suggest carrying a Visa or Mastercard as a second card. No current merchant count that compares the three networks outside the United States was found, so that comparison is not confirmed in numbers.

## What foreign spending earns

| Purchase | Points per dollar |
|---|---|
| Flights booked directly with airlines or through Amex Travel, up to $500,000 a calendar year | 5 |
| Prepaid hotels booked through Amex Travel | 5 |
| Everything else, including restaurants, shops, trains and taxis abroad | 1 |

There is no bonus category for dining or general travel. See [what the points are worth](/amex-membership-rewards-points-value/).

## Paying in dollars at the terminal

Some foreign terminals and ATMs offer to charge you in US dollars. This is dynamic currency conversion. The merchant or ATM operator sets the rate, not Amex. Upgraded Points, citing a European consumer group, says the markup generally runs from 2.6% to 12%. Choosing the local currency leaves the conversion to Amex.

## Cash and ATMs

The agreement treats ATM withdrawals and buying foreign currency as cash advances.

| Term | Detail |
|---|---|
| Fee | 5% of the advance, including any ATM operator fee, with a $10 minimum |
| Interest | From the transaction date, with no grace period |
| Rate | Prime Rate + 21.99%, variable |
| Limit | Cash advance balance may not exceed $8,000; ATMs may set their own limits |

How to set up a PIN for ATM use was not confirmed.

## Benefits that work abroad, and those that do not

| Works outside the US | US only |
|---|---|
| Global Lounge Collection: more than 1,550 lounges in 140 countries, including 15 Centurion Lounges abroad and Priority Pass (enrollment required) | Uber Cash: rides and Uber Eats orders in the US |
| Fine Hotels + Resorts: more than 1,900 hotels worldwide, booked through Amex Travel | Resy credit: US Resy restaurants |
| The $600 hotel credit, on prepaid Amex Travel bookings | lululemon credit: US stores |
| Trip delay and trip cancellation cover | |

Details are on the pages for [lounge guest rules](/amex-platinum-centurion-lounge-guest-rules/), [Priority Pass](/priority-pass-by-card-what-you-get/), [Fine Hotels + Resorts](/fine-hotels-resorts-vs-hotel-collection/), [trip cover](/amex-platinum-trip-delay-cancellation-insurance/) and [the Uber credit](/amex-platinum-uber-credit-worth-it/). Whether the digital entertainment, Walmart+ and Equinox credits work on purchases made abroad is not confirmed.

## Who should skip it

- Anyone who wants one card for a whole trip. Both sources above suggest a backup.
- Anyone who mainly needs cash abroad. A debit card with low ATM fees costs less.
- Anyone who wants bonus points on meals abroad. This card pays 1 point per dollar there.
- Anyone living abroad for most of the year, since the Uber, Resy and lululemon credits need US spending.

## Quick answers

**Does the Amex Platinum charge a foreign transaction fee?**
No. Amex's cardmember agreement lists the foreign transaction fee as none, for the main card and additional cards.

**Is the Amex Platinum accepted everywhere abroad?**
No. Acceptance varies by country and merchant, and sources suggest carrying a Visa or Mastercard as well.

**Can I use the Amex Platinum at an ATM abroad?**
It counts as a cash advance. The fee is 5% with a $10 minimum, and interest starts the same day.

## Sources

- [American Express: Platinum Card cardmember agreement (PDF)](https://www.americanexpress.com/content/dam/amex/en-us/company/legal/cardmember-agreements/public-site-adhoc-2025-09-18/platinum-card-09-18-2025.pdf)
- [Upgraded Points: Amex Platinum international fees](https://upgradedpoints.com/credit-cards/reviews/american-express-platinum-card/international-fees/)
- [The Points Guy: Amex acceptance compared with Visa and Mastercard](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/american-express/amex-now-accepted-in-as-many-places-as-visa-mastercard/)
- [The Points Guy: Amex Platinum review](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/reviews/amex-platinum-review/)
- [The Points Guy: Amex Platinum lounge access](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/american-express-platinum-lounge-access/)

# How do the Amex Platinum Global Entry, TSA PreCheck and CLEAR credits work, and what are they worth?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/amex-platinum-global-entry-clear-credit/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

Charge the application fee to the Platinum Card and Amex credits it back: $120 for Global Entry or up to $85 for TSA PreCheck, once about every four years. A separate credit covers up to $219 a year of a CLEAR+ membership. Together they are worth about $249 a year at face value, and only if you would use the programs.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## The two credits side by side

| | Global Entry or TSA PreCheck | CLEAR+ |
|---|---|---|
| Amount | $120 (Global Entry) or up to $85 (PreCheck) | Up to $219 |
| How often | Once per 4 years for Global Entry; 4.5 years for PreCheck | Every calendar year |
| Enrollment with Amex | Not required | Reported as required |
| Authorized users | Each Platinum additional card gets its own | One per account, shared |
| Value per year | $30 ($120 over 4 years) | $219 |

## Global Entry or TSA PreCheck

**What each program does.** TSA PreCheck is a faster security lane at US airports. Global Entry speeds up US immigration on the way home, includes TSA PreCheck and lasts five years.

**How the credit works.** Pay the application fee with the Platinum Card. The credit posts automatically. Amex's terms, as shown in a search summary of its benefit page, say to allow up to 8 weeks. The credit goes to the first of the two programs you pay for in the period, so you get one, not both.

**Whose application.** One Mile at a Time reports that the fee can be for someone else's application, as long as it is charged to your card. Each authorized user holding a Platinum additional card gets a separate credit.

**What is not covered.** NEXUS, SENTRI and Privium are not eligible, per Amex's terms. That differs from the Chase Sapphire cards, whose credit includes NEXUS.

Sources differ slightly on timing. One Mile at a Time says once every 4 years for either program. Amex's terms give 4 years for Global Entry and 4.5 years for TSA PreCheck.

## CLEAR+

**What it does.** CLEAR+ confirms your identity with an eye or fingerprint scan and takes you to the front of the ID check. The Points Guy counts more than 55 US airports.

**How the credit works.** Pay for the membership with the card and the charge is credited, up to $219 per calendar year. The Points Guy reports that the card must be enrolled first, that Amex quotes two to four weeks for the credit, and that it often posts within days. First-time members finish sign-up in person at a CLEAR airport location. The membership renews automatically.

**The price.** CLEAR+ costs $219 a year since July 1, 2026, so the credit covers one standard membership in full.

| CLEAR+ price paid | Who gets it | Credit left over |
|---|---|---|
| $219 | Standard price | $0 |
| $209 | General Delta or United members, Alaska members | $10 |
| $169 | Holders of an eligible Delta or United credit card | $50 |

The credit can be used in parts and can pay for someone else's membership. An added adult family member costs $125, and at the standard price no credit is left for it.

Sources disagree on the amount. The Points Guy's main text and Amex's card page say $219. The same Points Guy article's FAQ, and a search summary of an Amex travel page, still say $209.

## What they are worth

| Traveler | Realistic yearly value |
|---|---|
| Flies a few times a year from a CLEAR airport, and abroad | $249: $219 plus $30 |
| Flies domestically from an airport without CLEAR | About $19: up to $85 for PreCheck over 4.5 years |
| Already has Global Entry from another card and no CLEAR airport | $0 |

The CLEAR+ credit is worth $219 only if you would pay for CLEAR+ yourself. Many people would not. Amex Platinum's annual fee is $895, so these two credits cover a little over a quarter of it at face value. See [all the credits](/amex-platinum-credits-real-value/).

## Who should skip counting them

- Anyone whose home airport has no CLEAR lanes.
- Anyone who already gets Global Entry or PreCheck paid by another card. A second credit adds nothing unless it pays for someone else.
- Anyone who flies once or twice a year. The time saved is small.
- Anyone who needs NEXUS.

## Quick answers

**Can I get both the Global Entry and the TSA PreCheck credit?**
No. The credit applies to the first program you pay for in the period. Global Entry includes TSA PreCheck.

**Do authorized users get their own credits?**
Each Platinum additional card gets its own Global Entry or PreCheck credit. The CLEAR+ credit is one per account. See [whether an authorized user is worth $195](/amex-platinum-authorized-user-worth-195/).

**Does the CLEAR+ credit cover a family member?**
It can pay for anyone's membership, but it is capped at $219 a year, which is the price of one standard membership.

## Sources

- [One Mile at a Time: Amex Platinum Global Entry and TSA PreCheck credit](https://onemileatatime.com/reviews/credit-cards/american-express/amex-platinum-global-entry-tsa-precheck-credit/)
- [The Points Guy: guide to the Amex Platinum CLEAR credit](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/american-express/guide-to-using-the-amex-platinum-clear-credit/)
- [American Express: application fee credit for Global Entry or TSA PreCheck](https://www.americanexpress.com/en-us/benefits/travel/expedite-your-travel/)
- [American Express: Platinum Card page](https://www.americanexpress.com/us/credit-cards/card/platinum/)

# What does the Amex Platinum actually do for one Hawaii trip a year?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/amex-platinum-hawaii-trip/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

For one Hawaii trip a year, the Amex Platinum mainly gives you up to $300 back on a prepaid stay at certain hotels, plus lounge access at Honolulu and Maui airports. It does little at Kona and Lihue airports, and one trip does not come close to covering the $895 annual fee by itself.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## Lounges at Hawaii airports

There is no Centurion Lounge in Hawaii. What the card opens depends on the island.

| Airport | What a Platinum holder can use | Limits |
|---|---|---|
| Honolulu (HNL) | Delta Sky Club, Terminal 2 near gate F1 | Same-day Delta flight only; uses one of your 10 yearly visits; no basic economy tickets |
| Honolulu (HNL) | IASS Hawaii Lounge, Terminal 2, through Priority Pass | Space permitting; Priority Pass needs enrollment first |
| Honolulu (HNL) | Hawaiian Airlines Premier Club, Terminal 1 near gate A18 | Listed by Amex for the US card, up to 3 hours before departure. One travel site names only the IASS lounge for Priority Pass, so check first |
| Kahului, Maui (OGG) | Two Hawaiian Airlines Premier Club lounges | Up to 2 hours before departure, domestic flights only, space permitting |
| Kona (KOA) | None found | The only lounge is the Hawaiian Airlines Premier Club, which is for Hawaiian and Alaska premium passengers and members |
| Lihue, Kauai (LIH) | None found | Same as Kona; Priority Pass is not accepted there |

Two things to know before you plan around these:

- The Hawaiian Plumeria Lounge in Honolulu no longer takes Priority Pass. Some older guides still list it. It sells a $40 day pass at the desk.
- "None found" for Kona and Lihue comes from the state airport site and lounge guides. Amex's lounge finder did not show results for either.

## The hotel credit in Hawaii

The card gives up to $300 back each half-year, up to $600 per calendar year, on prepaid stays booked through Amex Travel at Fine Hotels + Resorts or The Hotel Collection properties.

On November 20, 2026, Amex Travel listed 40 Hawaii properties in these two programs: 25 Fine Hotels + Resorts and 15 in The Hotel Collection. The list changes.

| Program | Where in Hawaii | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| Fine Hotels + Resorts | Oahu, Maui, Kauai, Big Island, Lanai | Halekulani, Four Seasons Resort Maui at Wailea, Grand Hyatt Kauai, Mauna Lani |
| The Hotel Collection | Oahu, Maui, Kauai, Big Island | Sheraton Waikiki, Hyatt Regency Maui, Ko'a Kea, Hilton Waikoloa Village |

How it works on one trip:

- The booking must be prepaid, made through Amex Travel, and paid with the Platinum Card.
- One trip in one half of the year earns one $300 credit, not both.
- The Hotel Collection needs a two-night minimum. From January 1, 2027, Fine Hotels + Resorts needs two nights too.
- Fine Hotels + Resorts stays also come with daily breakfast for two, a guaranteed 4 p.m. late checkout, a room upgrade when available, and a property credit of at least $100 per stay.

These are higher-priced hotels. If you would normally rent a condo, paying more to use a $300 credit may leave you worse off.

## Other things that help on the trip

| Benefit | What it does |
|---|---|
| Airline fee credit | Up to $200 a year for fees like checked bags on one airline you pick in advance |
| Hotel status | Hilton Honors Gold and Marriott Bonvoy Gold Elite, after enrollment |
| Trip delay cover | Up to $500 per trip for delays over 6 hours, on round-trip travel |
| Rental car cover | Secondary cover up to $75,000 when you pay for the rental with the card and decline the rental company's waiver |

## What it does not cover

- Lounges at Kona and Lihue, or the Sky Club when you are not flying Delta.
- Hotels outside Amex's two programs, condos and most vacation rentals. Only prepaid Airbnb Luxe bookings through Amex Travel count for the hotel credit.
- Whether the hotel credit applies to resort fees is not confirmed.
- Priority Pass restaurants.

## Who should not get it for this

If one Hawaii trip is your only trip of the year, the card returns about $300 on the hotel plus up to $200 in airline fees against an $895 fee. It makes more sense if you would use the second hotel credit and other credits anyway.

## Quick answers

**Is there an Amex Centurion Lounge in Hawaii?**
No. In Honolulu the card opens the Delta Sky Club on Delta flights and Priority Pass lounges.

**Can I use both $300 hotel credits on one Hawaii trip?**
Not in most cases. One credit is for each half of the year, so a single trip earns one.

**Does the card get me into a lounge in Kona or Lihue?**
No lounge access was found at either airport for Platinum holders.

- [Upgraded Points: Amex Platinum benefits](https://upgradedpoints.com/credit-cards/reviews/american-express-platinum-card/benefits/)

# How does the Amex Platinum hotel credit work?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/amex-platinum-hotel-credit-how-it-works/
Facts checked: 2026-11-21
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

The Platinum Card gives up to $300 back in each half of the year, $600 per calendar year, on prepaid bookings made through American Express Travel at Fine Hotels + Resorts or The Hotel Collection, or on Airbnb Luxe stays. Any other hotel booking earns nothing, and an unused half does not carry over.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## The amounts

| Period | Credit | What happens to an unused amount |
|---|---|---|
| January to June | Up to $300 | Lost on July 1 |
| July to December | Up to $300 | Lost on January 1 |
| Calendar year | Up to $600 | Nothing carries over |

If a booking costs less than $300, you get back only what you paid. Several smaller bookings in the same half can add up to the $300, according to One Mile at a Time.

## Which bookings count

Amex's own page lists three kinds of booking. All must be paid with the Platinum Card.

| Booking type | Where to book | Minimum stay |
|---|---|---|
| Fine Hotels + Resorts | Amex Travel site, app or by phone | None in 2026; two nights from January 1, 2027 |
| The Hotel Collection | Amex Travel site, app or by phone | Two nights |
| Airbnb Luxe | Amextravel.com or the Amex Travel app | Two nights |

The booking must be prepaid. Amex Travel shows two ways to pay for these hotels, and only the pay-now choice counts. Bookings paid later at the hotel do not.

Prepaid is not the same as non-refundable. One Mile at a Time notes that many prepaid rates can still be canceled under the hotel's own policy. Check the cancellation terms on the rate before paying.

Airbnb Luxe is on Amex's page, but the guides from The Points Guy and One Mile at a Time do not mention it, so details beyond the two-night minimum are not confirmed.

For how the two hotel programs differ, see [Fine Hotels + Resorts vs. The Hotel Collection](/fine-hotels-resorts-vs-hotel-collection/).

## Which half-year a booking falls in

The date you book and pay decides the half-year, not the date you stay. One Mile at a Time says the timeline is "based on when you make your booking and not when you stay." The Points Guy agrees that a stay does not need to be finished by June 30 to use the first-half credit.

So a booking paid in May for a September stay uses the January to June credit. That leaves the July to December credit free for another booking.

## Small rules that matter

- **Enrollment.** The Points Guy says no registration is needed. One Mile at a Time says in one place that enrollment is required and in another that it is not. Sources disagree, so check the benefits page in your account before booking.
- **Posting time.** Amex says the credit can take up to 90 days. The Points Guy reports about three days on average.
- **Cancellations and changes.** The Points Guy warns that the credit may be reversed if a booking is canceled or changed, and a new credit may not arrive until the next half-year.
- **Additional cardholders.** They can make a booking that earns the credit, but the account gets one $600 a year in total.
- **Taxes and resort fees.** Whether taxes and fees inside the prepaid total count toward the $300 is not confirmed.
- **Points.** Whether a booking paid partly with points earns the credit is not confirmed.

## What it is really worth

The credit is worth $600 only to someone who would have paid for two such stays anyway. Two things reduce it for everyone else.

First, the credit is a part payment. As an example, a $300 credit against a $700 booking still leaves $400 to pay.

Second, AwardWallet notes that Amex Travel prices can differ from the hotel's own price. Compare the two before booking. A $300 credit on a rate that is $120 higher than the direct rate is worth $180.

From 2027 the sums change for short stays. A one-night Fine Hotels + Resorts booking counts today. From January 1, 2027, it will need two nights.

## Who should skip it

Count this credit as $0 if:

- You book hotels with points or stay with one chain to earn status nights.
- You usually pay under $150 a night.
- You do not want to prepay for a hotel.
- You would take a trip only to use the credit.

To see this credit next to the others, see [what the credits are worth](/amex-platinum-credits-real-value/).

## Quick answers

**Is the Amex Platinum hotel credit $600 at once or split?**
Split. It is up to $300 for January to June and up to $300 for July to December.

**Does a one-night stay count for the hotel credit?**
At Fine Hotels + Resorts, yes, until the end of 2026. The Hotel Collection and Airbnb Luxe need two nights, and Fine Hotels + Resorts will too from January 1, 2027.

**Does the stay have to happen in the same half-year as the booking?**
No. Two sources say the half-year is set by when you book and prepay, not when you stay.

## Sources

- [American Express: $600 hotel credit](https://www.americanexpress.com/en-us/travel/get-inspired/Platinum-Card-600-Dollar-Hotel-Credit)
- [The Points Guy: Amex Platinum hotel credit guide](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/american-express/amex-platinum-hotel-credit/)
- [One Mile at a Time: Amex Platinum hotel credit](https://onemileatatime.com/reviews/credit-cards/american-express/amex-platinum-card-hotel-credit/)
- [AwardWallet: Fine Hotels + Resorts guide](https://awardwallet.com/credit-cards/amex-membership-rewards/amex-fine-hotels-and-resorts)

# What do the Marriott Gold and Hilton Gold status from Amex Platinum actually get you?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/amex-platinum-hotel-status-marriott-hilton-gold/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

Hilton Gold is the useful one: a daily food and beverage credit at many US hotels or a continental breakfast abroad, 80% bonus points and possible room upgrades. Marriott Gold is modest: 25% bonus points, 2 p.m. checkout when available and a few hundred welcome points, with no breakfast or lounge access.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## The two side by side

| | Hilton Honors Gold | Marriott Bonvoy Gold Elite |
|---|---|---|
| Bonus points on stays | 80% | 25% |
| Food | Daily food and beverage credit at select US brands; continental breakfast at select brands abroad | None listed |
| Room upgrade | When available, up to Executive Floor rooms | Enhanced room when available; some brands do not take part |
| Late checkout | When available | 2 p.m. on request, when available |
| Welcome gift | Bottled water | 250 or 500 points per stay |
| Award stays | Fifth night free on stays of five nights or more | Not a Gold benefit in the sources read |
| Normally earned with | 25 nights, 15 stays or $6,000 spent in a year | 25 nights in a year |

Sources: The Points Guy, One Mile at a Time and Upgraded Points, all dated 2026.

## How to get the status

It is not automatic. Enroll in the benefits section of your Amex account with your Hilton Honors and Marriott Bonvoy numbers, one enrollment for each program. Status is reported to post in about 72 hours (One Mile at a Time) or 3 to 5 business days (Upgraded Points), so enroll before a trip.

- Status lasts as long as the card is open. No stays are required.
- Authorized users with a Platinum additional card can enroll too. Each card is registered separately.
- The status does not count toward higher tiers. It brings no elite night credits.

## Hilton Gold: the food credit in dollars

At US hotels the breakfast benefit is a daily credit. AwardWallet's June 2026 table:

| Hilton brand (US) | Credit per day | Two guests |
|---|---|---|
| Conrad, LXR, NoMad, Waldorf Astoria | $25 | $50 |
| Canopy, Curio, DoubleTree, Graduate, Hilton Hotels & Resorts, Signia, Tapestry, Tempo | $15, up to $18 in select markets | $30 to $36 |
| Hilton Garden Inn | $10 | $20 |

Embassy Suites, Hampton, Homewood Suites, Home2 Suites, Spark and Tru serve breakfast to every guest, so Gold adds nothing there. Outside the United States, Gold members get a continental breakfast for the member and one registered guest at participating hotels.

**A sum.** Two people, four nights at a US Hilton or DoubleTree: 4 x $30 = $120 in credits. The same four nights at a Hampton: $0 extra, since breakfast is included for everyone.

## Marriott Gold: what is missing

None of the sources read lists breakfast or lounge access for Marriott Gold. Those start at Platinum Elite, which the [Bonvoy Brilliant card](/marriott-bonvoy-brilliant-amex-worth-650/) includes.

## Where sources disagree

- **Hilton lounge access.** One Mile at a Time lists executive lounge access, subject to availability, as a Hilton Gold benefit. The Points Guy describes only possible upgrades to Executive Floor room types. Treat lounge access as not confirmed.
- **Point values.** The Points Guy values Hilton points at 0.4 cents and One Mile at a Time at about 0.5 cents. Either way, the bonus points are a small rebate next to the food credit.

## Things that reduce the value

- Upgrades and late checkout depend on what the hotel has that day. Nothing is guaranteed.
- Other cards give the same Hilton Gold for far less. The [Hilton Surpass](/hilton-surpass-vs-aspire-amex/) includes it at a $150 annual fee.
- Prepaid stays through Amex's own hotel programs bring their own breakfast and credits. See [Fine Hotels + Resorts versus The Hotel Collection](/fine-hotels-resorts-vs-hotel-collection/).

## Who should skip counting it

- Anyone who stays mostly at Hampton, Embassy Suites or other brands where breakfast is already included.
- Anyone who rarely stays at Hilton or Marriott hotels.
- Anyone who already has the same status or higher another way.
- Anyone expecting breakfast or lounge access from Marriott Gold.

For the status alone, the Platinum Card's $895 fee is hard to justify. It is an extra on top of the [credits and lounges](/amex-platinum-credits-real-value/).

## Quick answers

**Does Amex Platinum give free breakfast at Hilton?**
At select US brands Gold gives a daily food and beverage credit of $10 to $25 per person. At select brands abroad it gives a continental breakfast.

**Does Marriott Gold include breakfast or lounge access?**
No source read lists either for Gold Elite. Its main benefits are 25% bonus points and 2 p.m. checkout when available.

**Is the status automatic?**
No. You enroll once for each program in your Amex account, and it stays while the card is open.

## Sources

- [The Points Guy: Amex Platinum hotel elite status](https://thepointsguy.com/guide/amex-platinum-hotel-elite-status/)
- [One Mile at a Time: Amex Platinum hotel elite status](https://onemileatatime.com/reviews/credit-cards/american-express/amex-platinum-hotel-elite-status/)
- [Upgraded Points: Hilton Honors status with the Platinum Card](https://upgradedpoints.com/credit-cards/reviews/american-express-platinum-card/hilton-honors-elite-status-benefits/)
- [Upgraded Points: Marriott Bonvoy status with the Platinum Card](https://upgradedpoints.com/credit-cards/reviews/american-express-platinum-card/marriott-bonvoy-elite-status-benefits/)
- [AwardWallet: Hilton food and beverage credit](https://awardwallet.com/hotels/hilton-honors/hilton-food-beverage-credit)

# How does the Amex Platinum Lululemon credit work, and what counts?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/amex-platinum-lululemon-credit-how-it-works/
Facts checked: 2026-11-21
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

The Platinum Card gives up to $75 back each calendar quarter, $300 a year, on purchases at US lululemon stores and on lululemon.com, once the card is enrolled. Outlet stores, gift cards and orders shipped outside the US are excluded, and an unused quarter is lost.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## The amounts

The credit was added to the card in September 2025. It comes in four pieces.

| Quarter | Credit | Unused amount |
|---|---|---|
| January to March | Up to $75 | Lost on April 1 |
| April to June | Up to $75 | Lost on July 1 |
| July to September | Up to $75 | Lost on October 1 |
| October to December | Up to $75 | Lost on January 1 |

The quarters cannot be pooled. A $300 jacket bought in one visit earns $75, not $300. A $40 purchase earns $40, and the other $35 of that quarter can still be used on a later purchase before the quarter ends.

## How to turn it on

Enrollment is required, and it is done once. The basic cardmember enrolls in the benefits section of the Amex account. After that, a purchase on any card on the account can earn the credit, but the account gets one $300 a year in total. Additional cardholders do not get their own.

Purchases made before enrolling do not count.

## What counts and what does not

| Purchase | Counts? |
|---|---|
| Clothing and gear at a US lululemon retail store | Yes |
| Orders on lululemon.com shipped in the US | Yes |
| Sale items on lululemon.com | No rule against them was found |
| lululemon outlet stores | No |
| Stores outside the US | No |
| Orders shipped outside the US | No |
| Gift cards | No, under the terms |
| lululemon products sold by another retailer | Not listed as eligible |

The terms, as quoted by AwardWallet, say the credit is "Not valid on purchases shipped outside the U.S. or gift card purchases."

### Where sources disagree: gift cards

The terms exclude gift cards. Doctor of Credit reported that physical gift cards bought in a store had still been earning the credit for some people. Its update of October 13, 2026 says gift card purchases no longer work. Electronic gift cards bought online never did. Do not plan on a gift card earning the credit.

### Not confirmed

- Whether purchases in the lululemon app count.
- What happens to the credit when an item is returned.
- Whether the Business Platinum Card has this credit. No source lists it there.

## Timing

Amex's terms allow up to 8 weeks for the credit to appear. AwardWallet says most post within a few days.

Online orders carry one risk near the end of a quarter. Doctor of Credit notes that an online charge may not be completed until the order ships. An order placed on the last day of March could be charged in April and use the next quarter's credit. A purchase in a store is charged the same day.

Apple Pay in a store works, according to the same source.

## What it is really worth

The credit is worth its full amount only on money you would have spent anyway. On an item that costs more than $75, you pay the rest.

| Your habit | Fair value per year |
|---|---|
| You already spend $75 or more a quarter at lululemon | $300 |
| You buy there once or twice a year | $75 to $150 |
| You would buy something small each quarter that you need anyway (socks, a headband) | Less than $300; count what you would have paid elsewhere |
| You never shop there | $0 |

Take the third row as an example. If a $28 item bought with the credit replaces a $10 one you would have bought elsewhere, the credit saved you $10, not $28.

## Who should skip it

Leave this credit out of your sums if:

- No lululemon retail store is near you and you do not want to order clothes online.
- The only store near you is an outlet.
- You live outside the US for most of the year.
- You would not remember to use a credit four times a year.

To see this credit next to the others on the card, see [what the credits are worth](/amex-platinum-credits-real-value/). The Resy credit follows the same quarterly pattern; see [how the Resy credit works](/amex-platinum-resy-credit-how-it-works/).

## Quick answers

**Does the lululemon credit roll over if a quarter is missed?**
No. Each quarter's $75 is lost when the quarter ends.

**Do lululemon outlet stores count?**
No. The credit covers US lululemon retail stores and lululemon.com, and outlets are excluded.

**Do gift cards earn the lululemon credit?**
The terms exclude gift cards. Reports that store-bought gift cards worked have been followed by a report that they no longer do.

## Sources

- [Upgraded Points: Amex Platinum lululemon credit](https://upgradedpoints.com/credit-cards/reviews/american-express-platinum-card/lululemon-credit/)
- [AwardWallet: Amex Platinum lululemon credit](https://awardwallet.com/credit-cards/amex-membership-rewards/amex-platinum-lululemon-credit/)
- [Doctor of Credit: lululemon credit data points](https://www.doctorofcredit.com/maximizing-the-lululmen-300-credit-on-american-express-platinum/)
- [The Points Guy: authorized users on the Amex Platinum](https://thepointsguy.com/guide/why-add-authorized-users-amex-platinum/)

# What are the Amex Platinum Oura and Equinox credits worth if you would not buy them anyway?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/amex-platinum-oura-and-equinox-credits/
Facts checked: 2026-11-21
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

To someone who would not buy an Oura Ring or an Equinox membership anyway, the two credits are worth close to $0. The $200 Oura credit is a discount on a ring that starts at $349, and the $300 Equinox credit pays for a fitness app or a small part of a gym membership.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## The two credits side by side

| | Oura | Equinox |
|---|---|---|
| Amount | Up to $200 a year | Up to $300 per calendar year |
| Pays for | An Oura Ring bought at Ouraring.com | Equinox club memberships or the Equinox+ app |
| Enrollment | Required before buying | Required, through the Amex account and platinum.equinox.com |
| Does not pay for | Oura membership, chargers and accessories, warranties, gift cards, rings from other retailers | Spa services, personal training, day passes, the Equinox shop |
| Unused amount | Lost | Lost on December 31 |

Both are charged in full to the Platinum Card first. The money comes back as a statement credit. Upgraded Points reports the Oura credit usually appears within 48 hours. Amex's terms allow up to 8 weeks.

## The Oura sums

The credit covers hardware only. The ring also has a membership fee that the credit does not touch.

| Item | Cost |
|---|---|
| Oura Ring 4, lowest-priced finishes | $349 plus tax |
| Amex credit | Minus $200 |
| You pay for the ring | $149 plus tax |
| Oura membership | $5.99 a month or $69.99 a year |
| First-year cost with annual membership | About $219 plus tax |

Other finishes cost $399 or $499, and the ceramic model starts at $499, according to Upgraded Points. Upgraded Points also says the ring works with limited features without a membership.

So the credit does not make a ring free. For a person who was about to buy one, it is worth $200. For a person who was not, it is an offer to spend $149 or more.

The credit returns each year, but a ring is not a yearly purchase for most people. Count $200 in the years you would buy one, not $200 every year.

## The Equinox sums

There are two ways to use this credit.

**The app.** Equinox+ is a workout app. It normally costs $39.99 a month. Upgraded Points reports that Platinum cardmembers are offered an annual price of $300, which the credit covers in full. The Points Guy also says the credit can cover a full year of the app. The app does not include entry to Equinox clubs.

**A club membership.** Sources give different prices because rates vary by city:

| Source | Club price per month |
|---|---|
| The Points Guy | $205 to $415 |
| Upgraded Points | $200 to $500, before initiation fees |
| AwardWallet (2025) | $325 for all-access |

At $300 a month, a year costs $3,600. The credit pays for one month of it. Equinox has a little over 100 clubs, in large cities in the US, Canada and the UK, so most people do not live near one.

The membership must be bought through the Amex enrollment page. Subscribing in the Equinox app or directly on the Equinox site does not earn the credit, according to Upgraded Points and AwardWallet. Memberships renew by themselves.

## What each is worth to you

| Your situation | Oura | Equinox |
|---|---|---|
| Already an Equinox club member | - | $300 |
| Would pay for a workout app anyway | - | What that app would have cost you |
| About to buy an Oura Ring | $200 | - |
| Curious, but would not pay full price | Less than $200; you still spend $149 or more | $0 to a small amount |
| No interest | $0 | $0 |

## A related credit

The card also lists up to $300 back on a SoulCycle at-home bike, which costs $2,500 plus tax and needs an Equinox+ membership. It is a discount on a large purchase, not a credit most cardholders will use.

## Not confirmed

- Whether additional cardholders share the one Oura credit. The Equinox credit is one per account.
- Whether the Oura credit resets on January 1 or on another date. AwardWallet describes it as once per calendar year; Upgraded Points calls it an annual credit and gives no reset date.

## Who should skip it

Leave both credits out of your sums if:

- You do not track sleep or fitness and do not plan to start.
- You already own a fitness tracker you are happy with.
- You do not live near an Equinox club and have a workout routine you like.
- You would buy either one mainly because a credit exists.

Together these two credits make up $500 of the card's advertised yearly total. To see how that changes the sums, see [what the credits are worth](/amex-platinum-credits-real-value/).

## Quick answers

**Does the Amex Platinum Oura credit cover the Oura membership?**
No. It covers the ring only, bought at Ouraring.com. The membership is $5.99 a month or $69.99 a year.

**Can the Equinox credit be used without joining a gym?**
Yes. It can pay for the Equinox+ app, which does not include club entry.

**Is an Oura Ring free with the Amex Platinum?**
No. Rings start at $349 plus tax, so at least $149 is left to pay after the $200 credit.

## Sources

- [Upgraded Points: Amex Platinum Oura Ring credit](https://upgradedpoints.com/credit-cards/reviews/american-express-platinum-card/oura-ring-credit/)
- [Upgraded Points: Amex Platinum Equinox credit](https://upgradedpoints.com/credit-cards/reviews/american-express-platinum-card/equinox-credit/)
- [The Points Guy: Amex Platinum fitness benefits](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/amex-platinum-fitness-benefits/)
- [AwardWallet: Amex Platinum Oura Ring credit](https://awardwallet.com/credit-cards/amex-membership-rewards/amex-platinum-oura-ring-credit/)
- [AwardWallet: Amex Platinum Equinox credit](https://awardwallet.com/credit-cards/amex-membership-rewards/amex-platinum-equinox-credit/)

# Is the Amex Platinum a charge card or a credit card, and how does Pay Over Time work?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/amex-platinum-pay-over-time-how-it-works/
Facts checked: 2026-11-21
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

The Platinum Card works like a charge card: it has no preset spending limit, and charges are due in full each month unless a feature called Pay Over Time is active. With Pay Over Time active, eligible charges can be carried as a balance with interest, up to a limit Amex sets, which makes that part of the account behave like a credit card.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## Two balances on one account

The facts on this page come from Amex's Card Member Agreement for the Platinum Card, with a rates table dated September 18, 2025. Your own agreement may show different figures.

The agreement describes two balances:

| Balance | What goes in it | When it is due |
|---|---|---|
| Pay In Full | Charges made while Pay Over Time is inactive, and charges that do not fit under the Pay Over Time Limit | In full, every month |
| Pay Over Time | Eligible charges made while Pay Over Time is active | At least the minimum each month; the rest can be carried with interest |

A traditional charge card has only the first balance. This account can have both.

## How Pay Over Time works

The agreement says: "Pay Over Time has two settings: active and inactive."

- **Active.** Eligible charges are added to the Pay Over Time balance automatically, up to your Pay Over Time Limit. An eligible annual fee can be added too. Each month you may pay the full new balance, the minimum, or any amount between.
- **Inactive.** New purchases and the annual fee go to the Pay In Full balance and are due in full.
- **Changing it.** You can view or change the setting in your online account or by phone. The Points Guy says a change takes effect right away.

Cash advances are not eligible. Amex can suspend the feature based on its view of your credit or the state of the account.

Whether Pay Over Time is active by default on a new Platinum account is not confirmed. Check the setting after the card arrives.

## The Pay Over Time Limit is not a spending limit

The card has no preset spending limit. The agreement says Amex decides whether to approve each charge from your spending and payment record, your credit history and the resources it knows about. A large charge can still be declined.

The Pay Over Time Limit is a separate number. It caps how much you can carry with interest, not how much you can spend. Charges above it are still possible, but they are due in full.

## What it costs

| Item | Amount in the September 2025 agreement |
|---|---|
| APR for Pay Over Time | Prime Rate + 12.74% to Prime Rate + 21.74%, variable |
| Penalty APR | Prime Rate + 26.74%, for at least 6 months after a late or returned payment |
| Minimum due on a Pay Over Time balance | The highest of $40, 2% of the balance, or a tiered formula |
| Late payment fee | Up to $40 |
| Returned payment fee | Up to $40 |
| Annual fee | $895 |

The Prime Rate moves, so the percentage on your statement changes with it.

### How to pay no interest

The agreement says Amex will not charge interest on charges added automatically to Pay Over Time if you pay the Account Total New Balance by the due date each month. The due date is at least 25 days after the billing period closes.

So having Pay Over Time active costs nothing by itself. Interest starts only when you pay less than the full balance.

## Plan It

Plan It is a separate tool on the same account. You split a qualifying purchase into a set number of monthly payments with a fixed monthly fee in place of interest. The agreement caps the fee at 1.33% of the purchase per month, and the fee is shown before you confirm. The minimum purchase size is not stated in the agreement; The Points Guy gives it as over $100.

## Credit reports

The Points Guy says the Pay Over Time Limit is not reported to the credit bureaus. The agreement says Amex does report account information, including a failure to pay as agreed.

## Who should skip it

Pay Over Time is a costly way to borrow. Leave it inactive, or do not rely on it, if:

- You expect to carry a balance often. Compare the rate in your agreement with other ways to borrow first.
- A due-in-full bill in a heavy spending month would be hard to pay.
- You want a fixed, known credit line for planning.

People who pay in full every month are not affected by the rate. For them, the card's cost is the annual fee; see [what the credits are worth](/amex-platinum-credits-real-value/).

## Quick answers

**Is the Amex Platinum a charge card?**
It works like one. Charges are due in full each month unless Pay Over Time is active for eligible charges.

**Does Pay Over Time charge interest if the bill is paid in full?**
No. The agreement says no interest is charged on automatically added charges when the full new balance is paid by the due date each month.

**Can Pay Over Time be turned off?**
Yes. The setting can be changed to inactive online or by phone, and new purchases are then due in full.

## Sources

- [American Express: Platinum Card Member Agreement, September 18, 2025](https://www.americanexpress.com/content/dam/amex/en-us/company/legal/cardmember-agreements/public-site-adhoc-2025-09-18/platinum-card-09-18-2025.pdf)
- [The Points Guy: guide to Amex Pay Over Time](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/american-express/your-ultimate-guide-to-amex-pay-over-time/)
- [Upgraded Points: Amex no preset spending limit](https://upgradedpoints.com/credit-cards/amex-no-preset-limit/)

# How do Amex Platinum purchase protection, return protection and extended warranty work?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/amex-platinum-purchase-protection-return-protection/
Facts checked: 2026-11-21
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

Purchase protection covers a new item that is stolen, damaged or lost within 90 days, up to $10,000 per item and $50,000 per year. Return protection refunds up to $300 per item, $1,000 per year, when a store refuses a return within 90 days. Extended warranty adds up to one year to a manufacturer's warranty of five years or less.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## The limits at a glance

The terms come from Amex's benefit guides, which do not name each card. Upgraded Points (updated November 11, 2026) and AwardWallet tie the $10,000 level to the Platinum Card.

| Benefit | Per item | Per calendar year | Time window |
|---|---|---|---|
| Purchase protection | $10,000 | $50,000 per card | 90 days from purchase |
| Purchase protection, natural disaster | $500 per event | Same cap | Same |
| Return protection | $300 | $1,000 per account | 90 days from purchase |
| Extended warranty | $10,000 | $50,000 per card | Up to 1 extra year |

A payout never exceeds the amount charged to the card. Shipping and handling are not repaid.

## Purchase protection

The $10,000 guide covers damage, loss or theft of an item bought with the card, including a gift. It pays the lesser of the repair cost, the replacement cost or the amount charged. It pays only what other insurance or a retailer does not.

Not covered, in part:

- Items left unguarded, such as in an unlocked car
- Items in the care of an airline or delivery carrier
- Normal wear and product defects
- Damage to sports equipment
- Used and one-of-a-kind items
- Consumables, gift cards and tickets
- Motorized devices and software
- Items bought for resale or for professional use

## Return protection

This applies when a store will not take back an item within 90 days of purchase. The item must be unused and working, bought in the United States or its territories, and charged in full to the card. The yearly cap counts by purchase date.

An item is not eligible if the store's own return policy matches or beats these terms. The guide lists 28 excluded categories, including jewelry, watches, books, software, tickets, formal wear, seasonal items, used items and gift cards.

## Extended warranty

The benefit matches the manufacturer's written warranty for up to one more year. It starts when that warranty, or a paid service contract if longer, ends. The warranty must be valid in the United States or its territories.

It pays to repair or replace the item, or refunds the amount charged, whichever is less. Product recalls are excluded.

## How to claim

| Benefit | First step | Then |
|---|---|---|
| Purchase protection | Notice within 30 days of the loss, at americanexpress.com/onlineclaim or 800-228-6855 | Proof of loss within 60 days |
| Extended warranty | Notice within 30 days of the loss | Proof of loss within 60 days |
| Return protection | Call 800-228-6855 within 90 days of purchase | Papers within 30 days of the call |

Proof for purchase protection can include the itemized receipt, a repair estimate and, for theft, a police report filed before the claim. For return protection, send the store receipt and the card charge record. If Amex asks for the item, it repays that shipping cost.

## Where sources disagree, and what is not confirmed

- The Points Guy's shopping guide lists $1,000 per item for a card it calls the Platinum Credit Card. AwardWallet's fine print also shows $1,000 beside $10,000 in its main text. Upgraded Points and a separate Points Guy article say $10,000.
- The Points Guy lists return protection and extended warranty only for the Schwab, Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley Platinum cards. Upgraded Points says the standard Platinum Card has return protection. AwardWallet lists extended warranty and does not mention return protection.
- Not confirmed: an Amex page that names the Platinum Card for each benefit after the 2025 refresh. The guides are revised 2023 and 2024. Check the guide in your account before relying on a limit.

## The sums

The value is what you would lose without it: items you could not return, or that broke or were stolen in the first 90 days, less what a home or renter's policy would pay.

These benefits alone do not carry an $895 fee. They are one line in the [full count of what the card returns](/amex-platinum-credits-real-value/). Phones have [their own cover](/amex-platinum-cell-phone-protection/).

## Who should skip relying on it

- Anyone whose main purchases are excluded, such as jewelry returns or used goods.
- Anyone who shops mostly at stores with long return windows.
- Anyone who will not keep receipts.

## Quick answers

**How long does Amex Platinum purchase protection last?**
Up to 90 days from the purchase date.

**What is the return protection limit?**
$300 per item and $1,000 per account per calendar year.

**Does the extended warranty cover every item?**
No. The manufacturer's warranty must be five years or less. Motorized devices, software and used items are excluded.

# Is the Amex Platinum referral offer higher or lower than the public offer?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/amex-platinum-referral-vs-public-offer/
Facts checked: 2026-11-22
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

Neither route is reliably higher. In November 2026 the public page and referral links both lead to the same kind of offer, worded as high as 175,000 points, and Amex shows each applicant their own number before they accept. The only way to compare is to look at the number each route gives you.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## What each route shows in November 2026

| Route | Headline wording | Spending requirement | Who sets your number |
|---|---|---|---|
| Amex public page | As high as 175,000 points | $12,000 in the first six months | Amex, per applicant |
| A cardmember's referral link | As high as 175,000 points | $12,000 in the first six months | Amex, per applicant |

The Points Guy reports that the spending requirement and time frame are generally the same across offers. The points figure is the part that varies. Upgraded Points calls the top figure highly targeted and says many applicants are shown less.

## What sources say about referral against public

The sources do not fully agree.

- AwardWallet (June 2026) says that most of the time a referral offer matches the public one, that sometimes it is not as good, and that rare referral-only offers have been higher.
- Upgraded Points (October 2026) says it is "not uncommon" for a referral offer to be higher than the public offer. It does not mention lower ones.
- The Points Guy notes that referral offers can differ a lot from one person's link to another's, even for the same card.

## It has gone both ways before

| When | Referral link | Other route | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| March 2025 | 175,000 points after $8,000 | Public offer of 80,000 points | Frequent Miler |
| December 2021 | Some links gave less than others | A restaurant-booking partner link gave more | Frequent Miler |
| February 2026 on | As high as 175,000 after $12,000 | Same wording on the public page | Frequent Miler, The Points Guy |

Both older offers have expired. They show that the gap can open in either direction and close again. The spending requirement also moved: it rose from $8,000 to $12,000 on February 5, 2026.

## How to compare the two

1. Open the public Platinum page and go through the application until Amex shows your offer. Write down the points and the spending requirement.
2. Do the same through a referral link.
3. Compare the two numbers. If they match, the route makes no difference to you.
4. Accept only the one you want. Declining an offer has no effect on your credit score, according to One Mile at a Time, which reports there is no hard credit check unless you accept.

Read each screen with care. Some reader comments at One Mile at a Time claim an offer was shown only after a hard credit check. That is not verified.

More on the steps: [how to check which offer you are shown](/highest-amex-platinum-welcome-offer-how-to-check/).

## What does not change with the route

- **The lifetime rule.** If you have or had the Platinum Card, you may get no welcome offer by either route. See [the once-per-lifetime rule](/amex-once-per-lifetime-welcome-offer-rule/). Whether referral applications are treated any differently is not confirmed; no source read says they are.
- **The annual fee.** It is $895 either way.
- **The spending requirement.** A higher points figure is worth little if you cannot reach $12,000 in six months with your normal spending. See [what counts toward it](/amex-platinum-welcome-offer-spending-requirement/).

A person who shares a referral link can earn a bonus from Amex if you are approved. That is a reason for them to prefer their link. It is not a reason for you to skip the comparison. [How referral links work](/amex-referral-offer-how-it-works/) covers this.

## Who should skip it

- Anyone who has held the Platinum Card before and is applying mainly for the welcome offer.
- Anyone who would need to spend more than usual to reach $12,000 in six months. Extra purchases or interest can cost more than the points are worth.
- Anyone who would not use enough of the card's credits to cover $895 a year once the first year is over. See [what the credits are worth](/amex-platinum-credits-real-value/).
- Anyone shown a low offer by both routes who is in no hurry. Offers change, and you can decline.

No source can tell you what your offer will be. Offers vary by applicant and change without notice.

## Quick answers

**Is a referral offer always higher than the public offer?**
No. Sources report referral offers that were higher, lower and identical. In November 2026 both routes use the same wording.

**Does checking both routes hurt my credit score?**
Reviewers report that seeing your offer uses a soft check, and a hard inquiry comes only if you accept the card.

**Is the spending requirement different through a referral link?**
Usually not. Both routes currently state $12,000 in the first six months, but read the terms on your own offer screen.

- [Upgraded Points: Amex Platinum welcome offer news](https://upgradedpoints.com/news/amex-platinum-up-to-175k-bonus/)
- [Upgraded Points: Amex Platinum referral bonuses](https://upgradedpoints.com/news/earn-extra-points-with-amex-platinum-referral-bonuses/)
