# What rental car status and insurance come with the Amex Platinum?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/amex-platinum-rental-car-status-and-insurance/
Facts checked: 2026-11-21
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

The Platinum Card gives mid-level status with Hertz, Avis and National once you enroll, and secondary cover for theft or damage to a rental car up to $75,000. Premium Car Rental Protection is a separate paid add-on, about $12 to $25 per rental, that makes the damage cover primary; neither one covers liability.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## The three statuses

None of these is automatic. You enroll for each one through the benefits section of your Amex account. Additional Platinum cardholders can enroll too.

| Program | Status | Normally earned with | Main perks |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hertz Gold Plus Rewards | President's Circle | 15 rentals or $3,000 a year | One-class upgrade at participating locations, choice of car from the President's Circle section, spouse or domestic partner drives free in the US, 50% bonus points |
| Avis Preferred | Preferred Plus | 12 rentals or $5,000 a year | Skip the counter at most locations, upgrade when available, extra points |
| National Emerald Club | Executive | 12 paid rentals or 40 days a year | Book a midsize car and pick any car, full-size or above, from the Executive area (US and Canada); no second-driver fee; a free day after six rentals |

The earning figures and perks are from One Mile at a Time. Upgrades depend on what cars are on the lot.

Upgraded Points says the Amex discount code with Hertz adds a four-hour grace period for returns in the US.

### Hertz deadline: December 31, 2026

Amex told cardholders on July 13, 2026 that they must enroll again for Hertz President's Circle by December 31, 2026, according to Upgraded Points. Those who do not could lose the status and the Amex discount with Hertz. It is done under Car Rental Privileges in the Amex account and can take up to 72 hours.

Whether Avis and National need the same step is not confirmed. The notice named only Hertz.

## The built-in insurance

The card includes Car Rental Loss and Damage Insurance at no extra cost.

| Feature | Built-in cover |
|---|---|
| Type | Secondary: your own auto insurance pays first |
| Theft or damage to the rental car | Up to $75,000 |
| Rental length | Up to 30 consecutive days |
| Liability (damage to other cars, injury to other people) | Not covered |
| Not valid in | Australia, Italy, New Zealand |
| Vehicles excluded | Motorcycles, RVs, certain vans and trucks, peer-to-peer rentals |

To use it, pay for the whole rental with the card and decline the rental company's collision damage waiver.

Secondary means a claim goes to your personal auto policy or other insurance first. The card then covers what that insurance does not, up to its limit.

One source disagrees. One Mile at a Time's article on rental status says the card does not include a collision damage waiver as a standard benefit. Upgraded Points, Your Mileage May Vary and AutoSlash all describe the secondary cover above. Confirm in your card's benefit guide before relying on it.

## What Premium Car Rental Protection adds

This is an optional Amex program, open to most Amex cards. You enroll the card once at no charge. After that, a flat fee is charged each time you pay for a rental with that card, per rental and not per day.

| | Built-in | Premium Basic | Premium Plus |
|---|---|---|---|
| Price per rental (most states) | $0 | $19.95 | $24.95 |
| California residents | $0 | $15.95 | $17.95 |
| Florida residents | $0 | $12.25 | $15.25 |
| Damage and theft | Secondary, up to $75,000 | Primary, up to $75,000 | Primary, up to $100,000 |
| Medical expenses | Up to $5,000 (secondary) | Up to $7,500 per person (secondary) | Up to $15,000 per person (secondary) |
| Personal property | Up to $1,000 per person | Up to $2,500 per person | Up to $5,000 per person |
| Longest rental | 30 days | 42 days (30 for Washington residents) | 42 days (30 for Washington residents) |
| Liability | No | No | No |

Prices and limits are from Your Mileage May Vary (October 2026); Amex's own terms page could not be read. AutoSlash gives the lowest price as $12.95, not $12.25.

Premium does not apply to rentals in Australia, Ireland, Israel, Italy, Jamaica or New Zealand, and it is not offered to New Hampshire residents, according to AwardWallet and Your Mileage May Vary.

Primary means the claim does not go through your own auto policy first. On a week-long rental, $24.95 is about $3.56 a day. Once a card is enrolled, every rental paid with it is charged the fee.

Some other cards include primary cover with no per-rental fee; see [Sapphire Preferred rental car insurance](/chase-sapphire-preferred-rental-car-insurance/).

## Who should skip it

The status is of little use if you rent less than once a year or rent from other companies.

Skip Premium Car Rental Protection if:

- Another card you hold already gives primary cover.
- You rent mainly in the six excluded countries.
- You need liability cover. Neither Amex product provides it.

## Quick answers

**Is Amex Platinum rental car insurance primary or secondary?**
Secondary, up to $75,000 for theft or damage. Your own auto insurance pays first.

**How much does Amex Premium Car Rental Protection cost?**
In most states, $19.95 or $24.95 per rental, not per day. California and Florida residents pay less.

**Is rental car status automatic with the Amex Platinum?**
No. You enroll for Hertz, Avis and National separately, and Hertz needs a new enrollment by December 31, 2026.

## Sources

- [One Mile at a Time: Amex Platinum rental car status](https://onemileatatime.com/reviews/credit-cards/american-express/amex-platinum-car-rental-status-benefits/)
- [Upgraded Points: Amex Platinum hotel and car rental benefits](https://upgradedpoints.com/credit-cards/reviews/american-express-platinum-card/hotel-and-car-rental-benefits/)
- [Upgraded Points: Hertz re-enrollment notice](https://upgradedpoints.com/news/amex-platinum-hertz-benefit-reenrollment/)
- [Your Mileage May Vary: Amex Platinum rental car coverage](https://yourmileagemayvary.com/2026/10/03/amex-platinum-rental-car-coverage-2/)
- [AwardWallet: Premium Car Rental Protection](https://awardwallet.com/credit-cards/amex-membership-rewards/premium-car-rental-protection/)

# How does the Amex Platinum Resy credit work, and can you use it without living in a big city?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/amex-platinum-resy-credit-how-it-works/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

After a one-time enrollment, the Platinum Card gives back up to $100 each calendar quarter ($400 a year) when you pay at an eligible US restaurant listed on Resy. You do not need a reservation, so it works anywhere an eligible restaurant exists, but outside larger cities there may be few or none nearby.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## The basic rules

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Amount | Up to $100 per quarter, $400 per calendar year |
| Quarters | January to March, April to June, July to September, October to December |
| Rollover | None. An unused quarter is lost |
| Enrollment | Required, once, in the benefits section of your Amex account |
| Where | Eligible US restaurants on Resy. Restaurants abroad do not count |
| Reservation | Not needed |
| Card | Personal Platinum. Purchases by additional cardholders count, but there is one $400 per account |
| Timing | Amex says up to 8 weeks. Review sites report it usually takes days |

Several smaller bills in a quarter can add up to the $100. You get back only what you spend.

## You do not need to book through Resy

Resy is a reservation service, but the credit is triggered by paying with the card at the restaurant. Upgraded Points puts it this way: "You don't need to book through Resy for the credit to apply." Walk-ins count. One Mile at a Time adds that takeout counts if you pay the restaurant directly, and that you do not need to tell the staff anything.

## The 2026 change: check for the badge

In summer 2026, Amex updated the terms. A restaurant, winery or cafe must now be marked as eligible for the Resy Credit on the Resy website or app at the time you pay. One Mile at a Time reports that the venue's Resy page shows a badge marking it as eligible for the Resy Credit. A search-result copy of Amex's page gave August 1, 2026 as the start date; that date is not confirmed, because the page itself would not load.

From September 15, 2026, some restaurants that take bookings through Tock also count, with more being added over several months. Tock has been merged into Resy.

So the safe habit is: look up the restaurant on Resy on the day, and check for the badge before you rely on the credit.

## What does not count

- Gift cards and merchandise.
- Restaurants outside the US.
- A restaurant that is on Resy but not marked eligible.

Whether an order through a third-party delivery app, or a payment through a phone wallet, triggers the credit is not confirmed.

## Outside big cities

Amex and the review sites say more than 10,000 US restaurants qualify. That sounds large, but Resy is concentrated in cities. No source gives a count by town size, so the only way to know is to check your own area:

1. Open Resy and search your town, and the nearest larger town.
2. Count the places with the eligibility badge where you would eat anyway.
3. Add the cities you already visit each year.

Then score yourself honestly:

| Your situation | Realistic yearly value |
|---|---|
| Several eligible places you already go to, every quarter | Up to $400 |
| One or two nearby, or you travel to a city most quarters | $200 to $300 |
| None nearby, one or two city trips a year | $100 to $200 |
| None nearby, no city trips | $0 |

Timing matters too. Two city trips in the same quarter still earn only $100. One Mile at a Time notes that people in small towns without Resy restaurants may have to go out of their way to use the credit. A dinner you drive an hour for, only because of the credit, is not a saving.

## Who should skip it

Do not count the Resy credit toward the $895 annual fee if:

- Your area has no eligible restaurant and you seldom travel to a city.
- You eat out mostly at chains or casual places that do not use Resy or Tock.
- You dislike tracking four deadlines a year.

The Platinum Card earns 1 point per dollar at restaurants, so the credit is the card's only real dining benefit. People who eat out every week may want to read [Platinum or Gold](/amex-platinum-vs-gold-which-fits/). For the full list of credits, see [what the credits are worth](/amex-platinum-credits-real-value/).

## Quick answers

**Do you need a Resy reservation to get the credit?**
No. Paying with the enrolled card at an eligible US restaurant is enough. Walk-ins count.

**Does an unused quarter carry over?**
No. Each quarter's $100 ends on the last day of that quarter.

**How do you know if a restaurant qualifies?**
Look it up on the Resy website or app. It must be marked as eligible for the Resy Credit when you pay.

## Sources

- [Upgraded Points: Amex Platinum Resy credit](https://upgradedpoints.com/credit-cards/reviews/american-express-platinum-card/resy-dining-credit/)
- [One Mile at a Time: Amex Platinum Resy credit guide](https://onemileatatime.com/guides/amex-platinum-card-resy-dining-credit/)
- [One Mile at a Time: Resy credits and Tock restaurants](https://onemileatatime.com/news/amex-resy-credits-tock-restaurants/)
- [American Express: the Resy credit](https://www.americanexpress.com/en-us/credit-cards/credit-intel/resy-credit/)

# What travel insurance does the Amex Platinum include, and what does it leave out?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/amex-platinum-trip-delay-cancellation-insurance/
Facts checked: 2026-11-21
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

The Amex Platinum includes trip delay cover up to $500 per trip after more than six hours, trip cancellation and interruption cover up to $10,000 per trip, and baggage cover up to $3,000 per person. It does not pay medical bills abroad or for delayed bags, and each benefit pays only after other insurance and refunds.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## The limits at a glance

These figures come from Amex's Guides to Benefits. The guides do not name each card, so the match to the Platinum Card rests on Upgraded Points (updated November 11, 2026, with the $895 fee) and AwardWallet.

| Benefit | Limit | Main condition |
|---|---|---|
| Trip delay | $500 per trip; 2 claims per card per 12 months | Delay of more than 6 hours for a listed reason |
| Trip cancellation or interruption | $10,000 per trip; $20,000 per card per 12 months | Canceled or cut short for a listed reason |
| Checked baggage | $2,000 per person | Lost, damaged or stolen on a common carrier |
| Carry-on baggage | $3,000 per person | Same |
| All baggage, one trip | $3,000 per person; $1,000 for high-risk items | Entire fare on the card |

New York residents have different baggage limits.

## What counts as a covered trip

For delay, cancellation and interruption, the trip must be round-trip travel by common carrier of no more than 365 days. One-way tickets that bring you back to the city of departure count. The full fare must be charged to the card, or to the card together with its points or frequent flyer awards.

Cover extends to the card member, a spouse or domestic partner, dependent children, and traveling companions whose trip is charged to the card.

## Trip delay

The guide lists four causes: severe weather, terrorist action or hijacking, the carrier's documented equipment failure, and lost or stolen passports or travel documents. It pays "reasonable additional expenses" such as meals, lodging, toiletries and medication. A delay known before you left is excluded.

## Trip cancellation and interruption

Covered reasons:

- Injury, death or sickness of the traveler, a companion, or a family member of either
- Severe weather
- A change in military orders
- Terrorist action or hijacking
- Jury duty or a subpoena that cannot be postponed
- A home made uninhabitable
- Quarantine ordered by a physician

The benefit repays nonrefundable amounts paid to a travel supplier with the card. For an interruption, it also pays extra transport home, up to an economy fare.

## Baggage

The plan pays after the carrier settles its own claim. High-risk items include jewelry, sporting equipment and electronics. Tickets paid with Membership Rewards points qualify. Tickets paid with airline miles do not. There is more on sports gear in [card insurance for a golf trip](/golf-trip-travel-insurance-credit-card/).

## What is not covered

- **Medical bills.** Upgraded Points says treatment costs stay with the card member. The Premium Global Assist Hotline may arrange emergency medical transport at no cost when it approves and coordinates it. That is one source, not confirmed against Amex's own terms.
- **Delayed bags.** The baggage guide has no baggage delay benefit.
- **Pre-existing conditions.** A condition that showed symptoms or needed treatment in the 60 days before purchase.
- **Changing your mind.** Only the listed reasons count.
- **Supplier insolvency.**
- **One-way travel** with no return.

Rental cars are a separate benefit. See [rental car cover on the card](/amex-platinum-rental-car-status-and-insurance/).

## Where sources disagree

- One Mile at a Time says delays for any reason qualify. The guide lists four causes.
- Upgraded Points shows $2,000 for carry-on bags in a table. The guide and AwardWallet say $3,000.
- NerdWallet has said bookings paid with Membership Rewards points are an exception for trip insurance. The guide allows the card combined with its points.

## Filing a claim

| Benefit | Give notice within | Contact |
|---|---|---|
| Trip delay, cancellation, interruption | 60 days; proof of loss within 180 days | 844-933-0648 |
| Baggage | 30 days, per Upgraded Points | 800-228-6855 |

Papers include tickets, the card statement, receipts, and proof of the cause.

## Who should skip relying on it

- Anyone who needs medical cover abroad.
- Anyone booking one-way trips, or paying part of the fare with another card.
- Anyone with prepaid costs above $10,000 per trip.
- Anyone who wants to cancel for reasons not on the list.

This cover alone does not carry an $895 fee. It is one line in the [full count of what the card returns](/amex-platinum-credits-real-value/).

## Quick answers

**Does the Amex Platinum cover medical bills abroad?**
No. Treatment costs are yours. The hotline's transport help is not confirmed against Amex's own terms.

**How long must a delay be before trip delay cover applies?**
More than six hours, for one of four listed causes. The limit is $500 per trip.

**Do award tickets qualify?**
For trip delay and cancellation, the guide allows frequent flyer awards combined with the card. For baggage, tickets paid with airline miles do not qualify.

- [American Express: Baggage Insurance Plan guide (PDF)](https://www.americanexpress.com/content/dam/amex/us/credit-cards/features-benefits/BIP-Benefit-Guide_311-329_EDT_10.20_REV_4.24_a11y.pdf)

# Is the Amex Platinum Uber credit worth anything if you rarely take Uber?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/amex-platinum-uber-credit-worth-it/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

It can be, because the monthly Uber Cash also works on Uber Eats orders in the US, not only on rides. But it comes as $15 a month that expires at the end of each month, so someone who uses neither Uber nor Uber Eats most months should count it as close to $0, not $200.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## What the card gives you

The US personal Platinum Card has two separate Uber benefits.

| Benefit | Amount | How it arrives | What it pays for |
|---|---|---|---|
| Uber Cash | Up to $200 a year | $15 in your Uber account each month, plus $20 extra in December ($35 that month) | Rides and Uber Eats orders in the US |
| Uber One credit | Up to $120 per calendar year | A statement credit on your card bill | Uber One membership fees only |

## How the Uber Cash works

- You add the Platinum Card as a payment method in the Uber app.
- At checkout, Uber Cash must be switched on and an American Express card must be the selected payment method. If the order costs more than your Uber Cash, that card pays the rest.
- It works only in the United States.
- It goes to the primary cardholder, on one Uber account. Additional cardholders do not get their own.
- It cannot be used on a family profile. A card added through Apple Pay or PayPal does not qualify.

## What expires

Everything, monthly. Uber's terms say unused Amex Uber Cash "expires at 11:59 PM Hawaii Standard Time on the last day of each calendar month." Nothing rolls over, so you cannot save three months for one airport ride.

That is the main limit for a light user. The yearly figure is $200, but it is really 12 small pieces:

| If you use it in | You get |
|---|---|
| All 12 months | $200 |
| 6 months (not December) | $90 |
| Only a December trip | $35 |
| Never | $0 |

## Using it on Uber Eats

For people who rarely ride, food is the practical use. A $15 piece may not cover a delivery order once fees and a tip are added, so expect to pay part of the bill yourself. The honest value is $15 off a meal you would have ordered anyway. If you would not have ordered, the credit made you spend money, not save it.

Whether the Amex Uber Cash applies to pickup orders (where you collect the food and skip the delivery fee) is not confirmed. Uber's terms say only that it covers eligible rides and orders where Uber Cash is accepted. Whether it covers the tip is also not confirmed.

## The Uber One credit

Uber One is Uber's paid membership. It is priced at $9.99 a month or $96 a year. Members get a $0 delivery fee on eligible Uber Eats orders, lower service fees, and 6% back on rides as Uber One credits, according to The Points Guy.

The Platinum Card refunds up to $120 per calendar year of Uber One fees. That covers the membership in full either way. The rules:

- The Platinum Card must be the payment method for the membership, charged directly by Uber.
- Uber Cash must be switched off for the membership fee. Any part paid with Uber Cash earns no credit.
- Free trials and discounted portions earn no credit.
- Uber One renews by itself. Removing the card does not cancel it. If you later close the card, cancel the membership in the Uber app or you will keep paying.

Sources differ on whether you must enroll for the Uber One credit. The Points Guy and Upgraded Points say enrollment is required. Uber's page describes only setting the card as the payment method.

A free membership to a service you do not use is worth $0.

## Who should skip it

Leave the Uber benefits out of your sums if:

- You live where Uber and Uber Eats barely operate.
- You do not order delivery and take fewer than a handful of rides a year.
- You spend most of the year outside the US.
- You would only place an order to "use up" the $15.

To see how this fits with the other credits, see [what the credits are worth](/amex-platinum-credits-real-value/).

## Quick answers

**Does unused Amex Uber Cash roll over to the next month?**
No. It expires on the last day of each calendar month, at 11:59 PM Hawaii time.

**Can the Uber Cash be used on Uber Eats?**
Yes. It works on rides and Uber Eats orders in the US, with an Amex card selected as the payment method.

**Do additional cardholders get their own Uber Cash?**
No. The Uber Cash goes only to the primary cardholder, on one Uber account.

## Sources

- [Uber: American Express benefit terms](https://www.uber.com/us/en/u/amex/)
- [Uber: Amex Uber One credit terms](https://www.uber.com/us/en/u/amex-uberone)
- [The Points Guy: Amex Uber Cash guide](https://thepointsguy.com/loyalty-programs/amex-platinum-uber-cash-credit/)
- [The Points Guy: authorized users on the Amex Platinum](https://thepointsguy.com/guide/why-add-authorized-users-amex-platinum/)
- [Upgraded Points: Amex Platinum benefits](https://upgradedpoints.com/credit-cards/reviews/american-express-platinum-card/benefits/)

# Amex Business Platinum vs personal Platinum: how do the fee and credits differ?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/amex-platinum-vs-business-platinum/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

Both cards cost $895 a year and share the same lounge access, hotel status and $600 hotel credit. The difference is in the other credits: the personal Platinum's are for dining, streaming, Uber and retail, and the Business Platinum's are for business costs such as Dell, Indeed, Adobe and a phone bill.

This page is information, not financial advice. Terms change, so check Amex's pages before deciding.

## Side by side

| | Personal Platinum | Business Platinum |
|---|---|---|
| Annual fee | $895 | $895 |
| Additional Platinum card | $195 | $400 (one source) |
| Flights | 5x booked direct or through Amex Travel | 5x through Amex Travel only |
| Prepaid hotels through Amex Travel | 5x | 5x |
| Other bonus earning | None | 2x on purchases of $5,000 or more and on US software, cloud, electronics, shipping and hardware suppliers, up to $2 million a year |
| Everything else | 1x | 1x |
| Points back on award flights | No | 35% back on the selected airline through Amex Travel |
| Centurion Lounges, Priority Pass, Escape, Plaza Premium | Yes | Yes |
| Delta Sky Club | 10 visits a year | 10 visits a year |
| Hilton Gold and Marriott Gold status | Yes | Yes |
| Points program | Membership Rewards | Membership Rewards |

Flights booked directly with an airline earn 5x on the personal card and 1x on the business card. That is the main earning difference for travelers.

## The credits

All amounts are "up to" a year. Most need enrollment.

| Credit | Personal | Business |
|---|---|---|
| Hotel, prepaid through Amex Travel | $600 | $600 |
| Airline fees, one selected airline | $200 | $200 |
| CLEAR+ | $219 | $219 |
| Resy restaurants | $400 | No |
| Digital entertainment | $300 | No |
| lululemon | $300 | No |
| Equinox | $300 | No |
| Uber Cash | $200 | No |
| Oura ring | $200 | No |
| Walmart+ | $155 | No |
| Uber One | $120 | No |
| Indeed | No | $360, $90 a quarter |
| ChatGPT Business | No | $300 |
| Hilton | No | $200, $50 a quarter |
| Dell | No | $150, plus $1,000 after $5,000 of Dell spend |
| Wireless phone service | No | $120, $10 a month |
| Adobe | No | $250 after $600 of Adobe purchases |

The Business Platinum also has two credits for very large spenders: up to $1,200 in Amex Travel flight credits and up to $2,400 toward One AP, after $250,000 of spend in a calendar year. Upgraded Points lists a newer ZO membership credit as well; that one is not confirmed by a second source.

## The plain sum

- **Shared credits:** $600 + $200 + $219 = $1,019 on either card.
- **Personal only:** $400 + $300 + $300 + $300 + $200 + $200 + $155 + $120 = $1,975.
- **Business only, no spending threshold:** $150 + $360 + $300 + $200 + $120 = $1,130. Adobe adds $250 once $600 has been spent there.

Face value is the ceiling, not the result. The test is the same on both cards: count only what you, or the business, would have paid cash for.

A consumer who eats at Resy restaurants, pays for streaming and takes an Uber each month can use $900 of personal-only credits with no change in habits. That person would use little of the business list.

A business that already pays for Indeed job ads, an Adobe plan, a phone line and Dell equipment can use $880 of business-only credits the same way ($360 + $250 + $120 + $150). The same business gets nothing from lululemon or Equinox credits.

The 2x rate matters only for big-ticket buyers. A $20,000 equipment purchase earns 40,000 points on the Business Platinum and 20,000 on the personal card.

## Which pattern favors which card

- **Personal travel, restaurants, streaming, rides:** personal Platinum.
- **Books flights directly with airlines:** personal Platinum, 5x against 1x.
- **Regular purchases of $5,000 or more, or software and hardware spend:** Business Platinum.
- **Pays for flights with points on one airline:** Business Platinum, for the 35% back.
- **Wants lounge access for a spouse or employee:** personal Platinum; its additional card costs less. See [whether an authorized user is worth $195](/amex-platinum-authorized-user-worth-195/).

## Who should skip it

- **Skip the Business Platinum** without real business spending. It is a business card, and its credits pay for business tools.
- **Skip the personal Platinum** if the hotel credit and two or three of the brand credits do not match things already in your budget. The page on [what the credits are worth](/amex-platinum-credits-real-value/) helps with the count.
- **Skip both** if lounge access is the only draw and trips are rare; see [the occasional flyer page](/amex-platinum-worth-it-occasional-flyer/).
- Anyone who carries a balance.

Amex treats the personal and business versions as separate cards for welcome offers. Offers on both vary by applicant and change.

## Quick answers

**Do the personal and Business Platinum cost the same?**
Yes, $895 a year each. Additional Platinum cards differ: $195 on the personal card and a reported $400 on the business card.

**Does the Business Platinum have the Resy and Uber credits?**
No. Neither review read lists Resy, Uber, digital entertainment, lululemon, Equinox, Oura or Walmart+ credits on the business card.

**Is lounge access the same on both?**
Largely yes: Centurion Lounges, Priority Pass, Escape, Plaza Premium and 10 Delta Sky Club visits a year on each.

- [Upgraded Points: Amex Business Platinum review](https://upgradedpoints.com/credit-cards/reviews/amex-business-platinum/)
- [American Express: Platinum Card page](https://www.americanexpress.com/us/credit-cards/card/platinum/)

# Amex Platinum or Capital One Venture X: which fee is easier to earn back?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/amex-platinum-vs-capital-one-venture-x/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

The Venture X fee is easier to earn back. One $300 booking through Capital One Travel plus the 10,000 anniversary miles covers its $395 fee, while the $895 Platinum fee takes several separate credits, most of them tied to named brands.

This page is information, not financial advice. Terms change, so check each issuer's pages before deciding.

## Side by side

| | Amex Platinum | Capital One Venture X |
|---|---|---|
| Annual fee | $895 | $395 |
| Authorized user | $195 each | Free; $125 each for lounge access |
| Main travel credit | Up to $600 a year on prepaid Amex Travel hotels, $300 each half-year | Up to $300 a year on Capital One Travel bookings |
| Other credits | Resy $400, digital entertainment $300, lululemon $300, Uber Cash $200, airline fees $200, CLEAR+ $219 and more | 10,000 miles each account anniversary |
| Flights | 5x booked direct or through Amex Travel | 5x through Capital One Travel, 2x direct |
| Hotels | 5x prepaid through Amex Travel | 10x through Capital One Travel, 2x direct |
| Everything else | 1x | 2x |
| Lounges | Centurion Lounges, 10 Delta Sky Club visits a year, Priority Pass, Escape, Plaza Premium | Capital One Lounges and Landings (seven airports), 1,300+ Priority Pass lounges |
| Lounge guests | Centurion $50 each; two free at Priority Pass | $45 per adult at Capital One Lounges, $35 at Priority Pass |
| Transfer partners | About 16 airlines, Delta included, plus Hilton, Marriott, Choice | 15+ programs; JetBlue is the only US airline |

All credit amounts are "up to" figures. Most Platinum credits need enrollment, and unused amounts do not carry over.

## The Venture X sum

- Fee: $395.
- Travel credit: $300, on flights, hotels or rental cars booked through Capital One Travel.
- Anniversary miles: 10,000, worth $100 when used against a travel purchase at 1 cent each.

$395 minus $300 minus $100 is minus $5. A reader who books at least $300 of travel a year through Capital One's portal is square from the second year on. The miles post at the first anniversary, so year one comes out $95 short on this count.

Two limits matter. The credit works only on bookings made through Capital One Travel, not on travel bought direct. And whether the credit resets on the calendar year or the account anniversary is not confirmed in the sources read.

## The Platinum sum

To cover $895 a reader has to add up credits they would have spent cash on anyway. The larger ones:

| Credit | Yearly amount | What it takes |
|---|---|---|
| Hotel | $600 | Two prepaid stays at Fine Hotels + Resorts or The Hotel Collection, one in each half of the year |
| Resy | $400 | A meal at a US Resy restaurant each quarter |
| Digital entertainment | $300 | A listed subscription every month |
| lululemon | $300 | A purchase each quarter |
| Uber Cash | $200 | A ride or Uber Eats order every month |
| Airline fees | $200 | Bag or seat fees on one airline picked in advance |

Used in full, the hotel credit plus any two of the others passes $895 on paper. Without the hotel credit it takes three or four of them, kept up every month or quarter. The page on [what the credits are worth](/amex-platinum-credits-real-value/) goes through each one.

## Which pattern favors which card

- **A few trips a year, one traveler, mixed spending:** Venture X. The fee is covered with one booking, and 2x applies to every purchase.
- **$30,000 a year of non-travel spending:** Venture X earns 60,000 miles. The Platinum earns 30,000 points.
- **Frequent flyer near a Centurion Lounge or on Delta:** Platinum. Venture X has its own lounges at Dallas Fort Worth, Denver, Dulles, Las Vegas, JFK, LaGuardia and Washington National only.
- **Travels with a partner or children:** Since February 1, 2026 the Venture X charges for every lounge guest. The Platinum charges at Centurion Lounges but admits two guests free at Priority Pass lounges.
- **Stays at luxury hotels twice a year anyway:** Platinum, for the $600 hotel credit.

## Who should skip both

- Anyone who carries a balance. Interest costs more than either card returns.
- Anyone who takes one trip a year and never visits a lounge. A $95 card or a no-fee card costs less.
- For the Platinum: anyone who does not want to track monthly and quarterly credits.
- For the Venture X: anyone who books hotels direct for loyalty benefits and would not use the portal.

Welcome offers on both cards vary by applicant and change, so they are left out of the sums.

## Quick answers

**Does the Venture X pay for itself with no effort?**
Close. It takes $300 of travel booked through Capital One Travel each year, plus the 10,000 anniversary miles from year two.

**Is Venture X lounge access as wide as the Platinum's?**
No. Both include Priority Pass, but the Platinum adds Centurion Lounges and 10 Delta Sky Club visits a year.

**Can Venture X miles go to Delta, United or American?**
No. JetBlue is the only US airline partner. Amex points transfer to Delta.

# Amex Platinum or Chase Sapphire Reserve: which fee is easier to earn back?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/amex-platinum-vs-chase-sapphire-reserve/
Facts checked: 2026-11-21
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

For most travelers the Sapphire Reserve fee is easier to earn back: its $300 travel credit applies to any travel purchase without enrollment, which leaves $495 of the $795 fee to cover. The $895 Platinum fee comes back only through several credits tied to named brands, so it fits people who already spend with those brands or who use Centurion and Delta lounges.

This page is information, not financial advice. Terms change, so check each issuer's pages before deciding.

## Side by side

| | Amex Platinum | Chase Sapphire Reserve |
|---|---|---|
| Annual fee | $895 | $795 |
| Authorized user | $195 each | $195 each |
| Flexible travel credit | None. Up to $200 a year in fees on one chosen airline, not tickets | Up to $300 each account year on any travel |
| Hotel credit | Up to $600 a year, $300 each half-year, prepaid Fine Hotels + Resorts or The Hotel Collection | Up to $500 a year, $250 per prepaid stay of two nights at The Edit hotels |
| Dining credit | Resy, up to $100 a quarter ($400) | Exclusive Tables on OpenTable, up to $150 each half-year ($300) |
| Other credits | Digital entertainment $300, lululemon $300, Uber Cash $200, CLEAR+ $219, Walmart+ $155, Uber One $120, Equinox $300, Oura $200 | StubHub $300, DoorDash promos up to $35 a month, Lyft $120, Peloton $120, Apple TV and Apple Music |
| Flights | 5x booked direct or through Amex Travel | 8x through Chase Travel, 4x direct |
| Hotels | 5x prepaid through Amex Travel, 1x direct | 8x through Chase Travel, 4x direct |
| Dining | 1x | 3x |
| Everything else | 1x | 1x |
| Lounges | Centurion Lounges, 10 Delta Sky Club visits a year, Priority Pass, Escape, Plaza Premium | Sapphire Lounges at eight US airports, 1,300+ Priority Pass lounges |
| Lounge guests | Centurion $50 each; two free at Priority Pass | Two free; $27 each after that |
| Transfer partners | About 16 airlines, Delta included; Hilton 1:2, Marriott, Choice | 16 programs, with United, Southwest and Hyatt at 1:1 |

All credits are "up to" amounts. Most Platinum credits need enrollment, several Reserve credits need activation, and unused amounts do not carry over.

## The Reserve sum

- Fee: $795.
- Travel credit: $300, applied to the first travel charges of the account year.
- Left to cover: $495.

The rest has to come from credits that take a choice. One prepaid two-night stay at an Edit hotel returns $250. Meals at Exclusive Tables restaurants, one in each half of the year, return up to $300. A reader who does both is past the fee: $495 minus $250 minus $300 is minus $55. A reader who does neither pays $495 for lounges, the higher earning rates and the travel cover. The page on [what the Reserve credits are worth](/chase-sapphire-reserve-credits-real-value/) goes through each one.

## The Platinum sum

- Fee: $895.
- No credit works on travel in general.

To reach $895 a reader has to add up credits they would have paid cash for anyway:

| Credit | Yearly amount | What it takes |
|---|---|---|
| Hotel | $600 | Two prepaid stays through Amex Travel, one in each half of the year |
| Resy | $400 | A meal at a US Resy restaurant each quarter |
| Digital entertainment | $300 | A listed subscription every month |
| Uber Cash | $200 | A US ride or Uber Eats order every month |
| Airline fees | $200 | Bag or seat fees on one airline picked in advance |

The hotel credit plus any two of the others passes $895 on paper. Without the hotel credit it takes four of them. The page on [what the Platinum credits are worth](/amex-platinum-credits-real-value/) has the full list.

## Which spending pattern favors which card

- **Books travel direct and eats out often:** Reserve. On $6,000 of flights and hotels booked direct and $4,000 of dining it earns 24,000 + 12,000 = 36,000 points. The Platinum earns 5x only on the flights; hotels booked direct and dining earn 1x.
- **Spends mostly on airfare:** Platinum, at 5x against 4x.
- **Flies Delta or passes through a Centurion Lounge airport:** Platinum. The Reserve has no Delta lounge access.
- **Travels with two guests:** Reserve. Its lounges admit two guests free. Centurion Lounges charge $50 per adult guest.
- **Stays at Hyatt or flies United or Southwest on points:** Reserve. Amex points do not move to those three programs.
- **Would use Resy, Uber and a streaming subscription every month anyway:** Platinum. Those three credits add up to $900 a year.

For a single Hawaii trip, see the [Hawaii version of this comparison](/amex-platinum-vs-sapphire-reserve-hawaii/). For point values, see [Amex points against Chase points](/amex-points-vs-chase-points-which-are-worth-more/).

## Who should skip both

- Anyone who carries a balance. Interest costs more than either card returns.
- Anyone who travels once or twice a year and does not use lounges. A $95 card costs less; see [Preferred against Reserve for a light traveler](/sapphire-preferred-vs-reserve-light-traveler/).
- For the Platinum: anyone who does not want to track monthly and quarterly credits.
- For the Reserve: anyone who would not use the hotel or dining credits and rarely sees a lounge.

Welcome offers on both cards vary by applicant and change, so they are left out of the sums.

## Quick answers

**Which card has the lower fee?**
The Sapphire Reserve, at $795 against $895. After its $300 travel credit, $495 is left to cover.

**Which card has wider lounge access?**
The Platinum. It adds Centurion Lounges and 10 Delta Sky Club visits a year. The Reserve has Sapphire Lounges and admits two guests free.

**Do both cards' points move to Hyatt?**
No. Reserve points move to Hyatt at 1:1. Amex points go to Hilton, Marriott and Choice, not Hyatt.

# Amex Platinum or Delta SkyMiles Reserve for a Delta flyer who wants lounge access?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/amex-platinum-vs-delta-skymiles-reserve/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

For someone who flies only Delta, the Delta SkyMiles Reserve is the closer fit: it costs $650, gives 15 Sky Club visits a year against the Platinum's 10, and adds free checked bags and a companion certificate. The $895 Platinum fits a Delta flyer who also flies other airlines, since its Centurion and Priority Pass access does not depend on a Delta ticket.

This page is information, not financial advice. Terms change, so check the issuer's pages before deciding.

## Side by side

| | Amex Platinum | Delta SkyMiles Reserve |
|---|---|---|
| Annual fee | $895 | $650 |
| Additional card | $195 | $175 |
| Delta Sky Club visits | 10 a year, February 1 to January 31 | 15 per Medallion Year, February 1 to January 31 |
| Sky Club guest passes | None | Four one-time passes a year |
| Centurion Lounges | Yes, on any airline | Only on a same-day Delta flight bought with a US Amex card |
| Other lounges | Priority Pass, Escape, Plaza Premium | None listed |
| Earning on Delta flights | 5 points per dollar | 3 miles per dollar |
| Checked bags on Delta | No bag benefit; $200 airline fee credit can cover bag fees | First bag free, and second bag free on domestic flights, for up to nine people on a reservation |
| Companion certificate | No | One round trip a year after renewal |
| Status help | None | 2,500 MQDs a year, plus 1 per $10 spent |
| Main credits | Hotel $600, Resy $400, digital entertainment $300, Uber Cash $200 and more | Delta Stays $200, Resy $240, rideshare $120 |
| Transfer partners | About 16 airlines, Delta included, plus three hotel programs | None; the card earns SkyMiles |

On both cards a Sky Club visit needs a same-day Delta flight, and Delta's basic fares are not admitted. Entries within 24 hours count as one visit. Extra visits cost $50 each, and both cards become unlimited after $75,000 of spend in a calendar year.

## The lounge sum

Count Sky Club visits by airport days, not flights. Six round trips with no connections outside 24 hours is about 12 visits.

| Delta round trips a year | Visits needed | Platinum (10 included) | Reserve (15 included) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | 8 | Covered | Covered |
| 6 | 12 | 2 extra visits, $100 | Covered |
| 8 | 16 | 6 extra visits, $300 | 1 extra visit, $50 |

At five round trips or fewer both cards cover the visits.

Guests change the count. The Reserve's four guest passes are worth $200 at the $50 guest price. The Platinum has no Sky Club guest passes, and sources disagree on its guest price: The Points Guy says $50 per guest and Upgraded Points says $29.

## The bag and fee sum

The Reserve costs $245 less. It also waives Delta's first checked bag fee, $45 each way on domestic routes.

- One traveler, six round trips, one bag: 12 bags, $540 saved with the Reserve.
- The Platinum's $200 airline fee credit can pay bag fees if Delta is the selected airline. That covers four bags and a bit.

For a Delta flyer who checks a bag, the Reserve is ahead by the fee gap plus the bag fees. From the second year its companion certificate adds a second ticket on one round trip for the taxes and fees.

## Where the Platinum is ahead

- **Trips on other airlines.** Centurion Lounges, Priority Pass and Escape lounges work with any airline. The Reserve's Centurion access needs a Delta ticket bought with an Amex card.
- **Points that move.** Platinum points transfer to Delta at 1 to 1 for a small fee, and to about 15 other airlines. Reserve miles stay with Delta.
- **Earning on airfare.** 5 points per dollar on flights against 3 miles.
- **Credits outside Delta.** See [what the Platinum credits are worth](/amex-platinum-credits-real-value/).

## Which pattern favors which card

- **Flies Delta six or more round trips, checks a bag, chases Medallion status:** Delta Reserve.
- **Flies Delta and one or two other airlines, carry-on only:** Amex Platinum.
- **Flies Delta four times a year or fewer:** neither lounge allowance is used up; compare on credits, or see the [three Delta cards side by side](/delta-gold-vs-platinum-vs-reserve-amex/).
- **Travels with a partner into Sky Clubs:** Delta Reserve, for the guest passes and the lower additional card fee.

## Who should skip both

- Anyone who buys Delta's basic fares. Those tickets do not get Sky Club entry with either card.
- Anyone who wants only the free bag. The Delta Gold card gives that for $150 after a free first year.
- Anyone who carries a balance month to month.

Welcome offers on both cards vary by applicant and change.

## Quick answers

**Which card gives more Delta Sky Club visits?**
The Delta Reserve, 15 a year against 10 on the Platinum. Both become unlimited after $75,000 of spend in a calendar year.

**Can I use a Centurion Lounge with the Delta Reserve?**
Yes, but only when flying Delta the same day on a ticket bought with a US-issued Amex card. Guests cost $50.

**Does the Platinum give a free checked bag on Delta?**
No. Its $200 airline fee credit can cover bag fees on one selected airline, but there is no bag waiver.

## Sources

- [Delta: Sky Club access rules](https://www.delta.com/us/en/delta-sky-club/access)
- [Delta: SkyMiles American Express personal cards](https://www.delta.com/us/en/skymiles/airline-credit-cards/american-express-personal-cards)
- [One Mile at a Time: Delta Reserve card review](https://onemileatatime.com/delta-reserve-credit-card-review/)

# Amex Platinum or Amex Gold: which fits someone who travels a few times a year but eats out every week?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/amex-platinum-vs-gold-which-fits/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

For someone who eats out every week and flies a few times a year, the Gold Card is the closer fit: it earns 4 points per dollar at restaurants and costs $325 a year. The Platinum Card earns 1 point per dollar at restaurants and costs $895; it suits that person only if they would use its lounges and its travel credits.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## Fees and earning rates

| | Gold | Platinum |
|---|---|---|
| Annual fee | $325 | $895 |
| Restaurants | 4 points per dollar, on up to $50,000 a year | 1 point |
| US supermarkets | 4 points, on up to $25,000 a year | 1 point |
| Flights booked with the airline or Amex Travel | 3 points | 5 points, on up to $500,000 a year |
| Prepaid hotels through Amex Travel | 5 points | 5 points |
| Everything else | 1 point | 1 point |
| Airport lounges | None | Centurion, Priority Pass, 10 Delta Sky Club visits and others |
| Hotel status | None listed | Hilton Gold, Marriott Gold |
| Foreign transaction fees | None | None |

Both cards earn the same kind of points, Membership Rewards.

## Credits

All amounts are "up to", and unused pieces are lost.

| Credit | Gold | Platinum |
|---|---|---|
| Resy restaurants | $100 a year ($50 each half-year) | $400 a year ($100 each quarter) |
| Uber Cash | $120 a year ($10 a month) | $200 a year ($15 a month, $35 in December) |
| Dining at named partners | $120 a year ($10 a month): Grubhub, Buffalo Wild Wings, Five Guys, The Cheesecake Factory, Wonder | None |
| Dunkin' | $84 a year ($7 a month) | None |
| Hotel (prepaid, Amex Travel programs) | None | $600 a year ($300 each half-year) |
| Airline incidental fees | None | $200 a year |
| Digital entertainment | None | $300 a year ($25 a month) |
| Paper total | $424 | $2,994 for the 11 main credits |

Most Gold credits need enrollment.

## The points for this reader

Take an example: $100 a week at restaurants ($5,200 a year) and $2,000 a year on flights.

| Spending | Gold | Platinum |
|---|---|---|
| Restaurants, $5,200 | 20,800 points | 5,200 points |
| Flights, $2,000 | 6,000 points | 10,000 points |
| Total | 26,800 points | 15,200 points |

The Gold earns 11,600 more points in this example. The Platinum only catches up through flights: it earns 2 more points per dollar there, while the Gold earns 3 more per dollar at restaurants.

## The fee after credits

The fee gap is $570 a year. What matters is the credits you would use without changing your habits. For this reader:

| | Gold | Platinum |
|---|---|---|
| Annual fee | $325 | $895 |
| Resy, used fully by a weekly diner near eligible restaurants | $100 | $400 |
| Uber Cash, used every month | $120 | $200 |
| One two-night hotel stay in an Amex program | $0 | $300 |
| Checked bag fees on one airline | $0 | Up to $200 |
| A streaming service on the list | $0 | Up to $300 |
| Net cost if all of the above are used | $105 | $505 ahead |
| Net cost if only Resy and Uber are used | $105 | $295 |

So the answer turns on the travel side, not the dining side. A weekly diner who also uses the Platinum's hotel, airline and streaming credits comes out ahead on paper with the Platinum, and gets lounges as well, but earns fewer points on meals. A weekly diner who would use only the dining and Uber credits pays about $190 more a year for the Platinum and earns fewer points.

Each credit has conditions. See [the Resy credit](/amex-platinum-resy-credit-how-it-works/), [the Uber credit](/amex-platinum-uber-credit-worth-it/) and [what the Platinum credits are worth](/amex-platinum-credits-real-value/).

## What a few trips a year gets from the Platinum

Lounge access on three or four trips is six to eight visits. Guests at Centurion Lounges cost $50 per adult. The trip delay cover is stronger on the Platinum: up to $500 after 6 hours, against up to $300 after 12 hours on the Gold, according to One Mile at a Time.

## Who should skip each one

Skip the Gold if you rarely eat out or buy groceries on a card, or if you would not use Uber, Resy or the named dining partners. Then the $325 fee buys little.

Skip the Platinum if restaurants are your main spending and you would not use the hotel credit or the lounges. You would pay $895 for a card that earns 1 point per dollar on most of what you buy.

## Quick answers

**Which earns more points at restaurants, Amex Gold or Platinum?**
The Gold: 4 points per dollar on up to $50,000 a year. The Platinum earns 1 point per dollar.

**Does the Amex Gold have airport lounge access?**
No. Lounge access is a Platinum benefit.

**What are the annual fees?**
$325 for the Gold and $895 for the Platinum, as of November 2026.

## Sources

- [One Mile at a Time: Amex Gold Card review](https://onemileatatime.com/reviews/credit-cards/american-express/amex-gold-card/)
- [The Points Guy: Amex Gold Card review](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/reviews/amex-gold-card-review/)
- [The Points Guy: Amex Platinum review](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/reviews/amex-platinum-review/)
- [One Mile at a Time: Amex Platinum review](https://onemileatatime.com/news/amex-platinum-digital-entertainment-credit-improved/)
- [The Points Guy: Amex Uber Cash guide](https://thepointsguy.com/loyalty-programs/amex-platinum-uber-cash-credit/)
- [The Points Guy: Amex Platinum lounge access](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/american-express-platinum-lounge-access/)

# Amex Platinum or Hilton Honors Aspire for someone who stays at Hilton?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/amex-platinum-vs-hilton-honors-aspire/
Facts checked: 2026-11-21
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

For someone whose hotel nights are mostly at Hilton, the Hilton Honors Aspire gives more for less: a $550 fee, top-tier Diamond status, 14 points per dollar at Hilton and a free night each year. The $895 Platinum Card gives Hilton Gold status and only 1 point per dollar on most Hilton bills; its strengths are airport lounges and points that move to airlines.

This page is information, not financial advice. Terms change, so check Amex's pages before deciding.

## Side by side

| | Amex Platinum | Hilton Honors Aspire |
|---|---|---|
| Annual fee | $895 | $550 |
| Additional cards | $195 each | No fee |
| Hilton status | Gold | Diamond |
| Paying at a Hilton hotel | 1x Amex point; 5x only on prepaid stays booked through Amex Travel | 14x Hilton points |
| Flights | 5x booked direct or through Amex Travel | 7x Hilton points |
| US restaurants | 1x | 7x Hilton points |
| Everything else | 1x | 3x Hilton points |
| Hotel credits | Up to $600 a year, $300 each half-year, prepaid Fine Hotels + Resorts or The Hotel Collection | Up to $400 a year, $200 each half-year, at participating Hilton resorts |
| Free night | None | One each year; more after $30,000 and $60,000 of yearly spending |
| Flight credit | Up to $200 a year in fees on one airline, not tickets | Up to $50 a quarter on flights bought from airlines or Amex Travel |
| CLEAR+ credit | Up to $219 | Up to $219 |
| Airport lounges | Centurion Lounges, 10 Delta Sky Club visits a year, Priority Pass, Escape, Plaza Premium | None listed in the review read |
| Transfer partners | About 16 airlines; Hilton at 1:2, Marriott, Choice | None. Points stay in Hilton Honors |

A Hilton point and an Amex point are not worth the same. The Points Guy values a Hilton point at 0.4 cents and One Mile at a Time at about 0.5 cents; both put an Amex point near 1.7 to 2 cents. So 14 Hilton points are worth about 5.6 to 7 cents, and 5 Amex points about 8.5 to 10 cents.

## Gold against Diamond

Both statuses come with the fifth night free on award stays and space-available upgrades. The main differences:

- **Bonus points on paid stays:** 80% with Gold, 100% with Diamond.
- **Food:** Gold and Diamond both get a daily food and beverage credit at US hotels and breakfast at many hotels abroad. Diamond adds executive lounge access where a hotel has one. Sources disagree on whether Gold includes lounge access.
- **Upgrades:** both are subject to availability.

The page on [Platinum hotel status](/amex-platinum-hotel-status-marriott-hilton-gold/) covers what Gold gives in more detail.

## The sum for a Hilton stayer

Take $5,000 a year paid at Hilton hotels.

| | Amex Platinum | Hilton Aspire |
|---|---|---|
| Points earned | 5,000 Amex points | 70,000 Hilton points |
| As Hilton points | 10,000 (transfer at 1:2) | 70,000 |

On fees, start with the credits a Hilton stayer uses without changing habits.

- **Aspire:** $550, less $200 of flight credit used across four quarters, less $200 from one resort stay, leaves $150. The yearly free night then covers that if the room would have cost more than $150.
- **Platinum:** $895. No credit applies to a Hilton stay booked with Hilton. The $600 hotel credit needs a prepaid Fine Hotels + Resorts or Hotel Collection booking through Amex Travel.

The Aspire resort credit works only at Hilton properties on its resort list, not at every Hilton. A reader who never stays at a resort should leave that $400 out. The page on [Surpass against Aspire](/hilton-surpass-vs-aspire-amex/) compares the Aspire with the $150 Hilton card.

## Which pattern favors which card

- **Ten or more Hilton nights a year, some at resorts:** Aspire. Status, earning and credits all apply to those stays.
- **Flies often and wants lounges:** Platinum. No airport lounge access is listed for the Aspire in the review read.
- **Wants points for flights:** Platinum. Its points move to about 16 airline programs. Aspire points stay in Hilton Honors.
- **Splits hotel nights across Hilton, Marriott and independent luxury hotels:** Platinum, for Gold status at two chains and the $600 hotel credit.
- **Both:** the two fees total $1,445 a year. That fits only a reader who would use the lounges and the Hilton benefits fully.

## Who should skip it

- Skip the Aspire if you stay at Hilton fewer than a handful of nights a year. The $150 Surpass or no Hilton card costs less.
- Skip the Aspire if you would not use the quarterly flight credit. It is $50 at a time and unused amounts are lost.
- Skip the Platinum if Hilton stays are your main reason. It earns 1x there and gives the lower status.
- Skip both if you carry a balance. Interest costs more than either card returns.

Welcome offers on both cards vary by applicant and change, so they are left out of the sums. Amex generally allows one welcome offer per card in a lifetime; see [the once-per-lifetime rule](/amex-once-per-lifetime-welcome-offer-rule/).

## Quick answers

**Does the Amex Platinum give Hilton Diamond status?**
No. It gives Hilton Gold on enrollment. The Hilton Honors Aspire gives Diamond for as long as the card is held.

**Can Amex Platinum points become Hilton points?**
Yes, at 1:2. One thousand Amex points become 2,000 Hilton points.

**Does the Hilton Aspire include airport lounge access?**
None is listed in the September 2026 review read. A reader comment there says Priority Pass was removed; that is not confirmed.

- [The Points Guy: Hilton Surpass against Hilton Aspire](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/hotel/hilton/hilton-surpass-vs-hilton-aspire/)
- [AwardWallet: Hilton Honors Aspire](https://awardwallet.com/credit-cards/hilton-honors/hilton-aspire/)

# Amex Platinum or Chase Sapphire Reserve for a once-a-year Hawaii trip?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/amex-platinum-vs-sapphire-reserve-hawaii/
Facts checked: 2026-11-21
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

For one Hawaii trip a year, the Chase Sapphire Reserve is the closer fit of the two. It costs $100 less, its $300 travel credit works on any travel, and its points move to Hyatt 1:1. Neither card is an easy case for a single trip: both fees are high and lounge access in Hawaii is thin.

This page is information, not financial advice. Terms change, so check both issuers before deciding.

## Fee and main credits

| | Amex Platinum | Sapphire Reserve |
|---|---|---|
| Annual fee | $895 | $795 |
| Authorized user | $195 each | $195 each |
| Welcome offer seen today | Up to 175,000 points after $12,000 in 6 months | 100,000 points after $6,000 in 3 months |
| Flexible travel credit | None. Up to $200 a year in airline fees on one chosen airline, not tickets | Up to $300 a year on travel in general |
| Hotel credit | Up to $600 a year: $300 in each half, prepaid Fine Hotels + Resorts, The Hotel Collection or Airbnb Luxe | Up to $500 a year: $250 per prepaid stay at The Edit hotels, two-night minimum |
| Flights booked direct | 5x | 4x |
| Hotels booked direct | 1x | 4x |
| Dining | 1x | 3x |

Welcome offers change and vary by person. Amex states its offer as "up to", so the amount you are shown may be lower.

## How the credits fit one trip

The Amex hotel credit is split by half-year. One trip can use only one $300 half unless you book a second stay in the other half. The Hotel Collection and Airbnb Luxe need two nights.

The Reserve's hotel credit is $250 per stay. One Hawaii trip with two separate hotel stays of two nights or more, both at The Edit hotels, could use all $500. One stay uses $250.

Most other credits on both cards are monthly or quarterly and do nothing for the trip itself. Count them only if you already pay for those things. The Reserve's $300 travel credit is the one credit on either card that a once-a-year traveler will use without trying.

## Lounges at Honolulu and Maui

| Airport | Amex Platinum | Sapphire Reserve |
|---|---|---|
| Honolulu (HNL) | Amex lists Delta Sky Club (Terminal 2), IASS Hawaii Lounge (Terminal 2) and Hawaiian Airlines Premier Club (Terminal 1) | Chase lists one: IASS Hawaii Lounge (Terminal 2) |
| Maui (OGG) | Two Hawaiian Airlines Premier Clubs, through Priority Pass | The same two Hawaiian Airlines Premier Clubs, through Priority Pass |

- There is no Amex Centurion Lounge at either airport in Amex's lounge finder.
- The Delta Sky Club is only for Platinum holders flying Delta that day, and the card allows 10 visits a year.
- The IASS lounge has no food, according to Chase. Its Priority Pass hours are reported as 7:30 a.m. to 1:30 p.m. and 2 p.m. to 6 p.m., which misses evening flights home.
- Sources disagree on whether the Hawaiian Premier Club at Honolulu takes Priority Pass. Amex lists it; Chase's Honolulu guide does not. Check the Priority Pass app before you rely on it.
- At Maui the lounges offer snacks and drinks, entry starts 2 hours before departure, and they can turn people away when full.

The Platinum is ahead at Honolulu only if you fly Delta. Otherwise the cards are close to equal in Hawaii.

## Using points for Hawaii hotels

Here the cards differ most. Chase points from a Sapphire Reserve move to Hyatt at 1:1. Amex points do not move to Hyatt at all. The Amex hotel partners are Hilton at 1:2, Marriott at 1:1 and Choice at 1:1.

Hyatt prices rooms by category. Its top category runs from 35,000 to 75,000 points a night. Guides place several Hawaii resorts there, but sources conflict on some hotels after Hyatt's May 2026 chart change, so look up the exact hotel and dates on Hyatt's site before moving points. At those prices, 100,000 points covers one or two nights, not a week.

The Platinum does give Hilton Gold and Marriott Gold status, which helps if you pay cash at those chains.

## Who should get neither

- Anyone who takes one trip a year and would not use the monthly credits. A card with a fee under $100 costs far less to hold.
- Anyone who carries a balance.
- For the Reserve: anyone who has opened five or more personal cards in 24 months, since Chase generally declines them.

## Quick answers

**Which card has the lower fee?**
The Sapphire Reserve at $795. The Amex Platinum is $895.

**Is there a Centurion Lounge in Hawaii?**
Not at Honolulu or Maui, according to Amex's own lounge finder.

**Can I move Amex points to Hyatt?**
No. Hyatt is a Chase partner. From the Sapphire Reserve the rate is 1:1.

## Sources

- [NerdWallet: Amex Platinum fee rises to $895](https://www.nerdwallet.com/article/credit-cards/amex-platinum-hikes-fee-adds-hundreds-in-credits)

# How does the Amex Platinum Walmart+ credit work, and is the membership worth having?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/amex-platinum-walmart-plus-credit-how-it-works/
Facts checked: 2026-11-21
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

The Platinum Card refunds the cost of a monthly Walmart+ membership, $12.95 plus sales tax, each month you pay for it with the card, which Amex counts as up to $155 a year. Only the monthly plan is refunded, so the membership is free to hold but worth something only to people who order from Walmart or use its streaming choice.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## The rules

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Amount | Up to $12.95 a month plus applicable sales tax |
| Yearly figure | Up to $155 per calendar year |
| Plan | Monthly Walmart+ membership only |
| Payment | Charged to the Platinum Card |
| Enrollment | Required, according to The Points Guy |
| Excluded | Plus Ups (paid add-ons) and the annual plan |
| Per account | One credit; additional cardholders do not get their own |

The membership renews by itself every month. If you close the card or move the payment to another card, the charge continues and the refund stops. Cancel it in your Walmart account if you no longer want it.

## The monthly plan trap

Walmart+ is sold two ways: $12.95 a month or $98 a year. The annual plan is the lower-cost one for most shoppers, but the Amex credit does not cover it.

| Plan | Cost per year | Amex credit | Your cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| Monthly, paid with the Platinum Card | $155.40 plus tax | Refunded each month | $0 |
| Annual | $98 | None | $98 |

A cardholder who already pays for the annual plan would need to switch to monthly billing on the Platinum Card to get the credit.

A newer plan has the same limit. One source, Kudos, reports that Walmart launched "Walmart+ with Sam's Club Plus" on October 20, 2026, at $120 a year. It is an annual plan, so moving to it ends the Amex credits. This was found in one source only.

## What the membership includes

These perks are listed by The Points Guy:

- Free shipping on Walmart.com orders with no minimum.
- Free grocery delivery from a local store on orders of $35 or more. This is not offered where no Walmart store is near.
- Up to 10 cents off a gallon at Exxon, Mobil, Murphy, Walmart and Sam's Club fuel stations.
- A choice of Paramount+ Essential or Peacock Premium.
- Free returns from home.
- Burger King offers and Walmart Cash on travel booked through Walmart's travel site.

On the fuel discount, Upgraded Points gives 10 cents in its article and 5 cents in its own FAQ. Check the amount in the Walmart app.

The streaming choice can overlap with another benefit on the card. Paramount+ and Peacock are also on the list for the digital entertainment credit; see [what the digital entertainment credit covers](/amex-platinum-digital-entertainment-credit-what-counts/). Taking one through Walmart+ leaves that $25 a month free for something else.

## Is the membership worth having?

Since the card pays for it, the question is how much use you get, not whether to pay.

| Your situation | Fair value per year |
|---|---|
| You already pay $98 a year for Walmart+ | About $98 |
| You already pay $12.95 a month | About $155 |
| You do not have it, but would use the streaming service and some deliveries | What you would have paid for those elsewhere |
| A Walmart store is near and you fill up at the listed stations | Depends on gallons: 300 gallons a year at 10 cents is $30 |
| No Walmart delivery in your area and no interest in the streaming choice | $0 |

The yearly figure of $155 is the price of the monthly plan, not the saving. A person who was paying $98 saves $98.

Free grocery delivery has a floor. Orders under $35 do not qualify for it, and the card refunds only the membership fee.

## Not confirmed

- Walmart's own terms page for the benefit could not be read.
- How long the credit takes to appear. The Points Guy suggests contacting Amex if it has not posted after a few weeks.
- Current prices of Paramount+ Essential and Peacock Premium when bought alone.

## Who should skip it

Count this credit as $0 if:

- Walmart does not deliver to your address and you do not shop on Walmart.com.
- You already get the same streaming service another way.
- You prefer the Sam's Club bundle or another annual plan.
- You would not cancel the membership after closing the card.

To see this credit next to the others, see [what the credits are worth](/amex-platinum-credits-real-value/).

## Quick answers

**Does the Amex Platinum cover the annual Walmart+ plan?**
No. Only the monthly plan, $12.95 plus tax, is refunded. The $98 annual plan earns no credit.

**Is sales tax on the Walmart+ fee refunded too?**
Yes. The credit covers $12.95 plus applicable sales tax each month.

**Do additional cardholders get their own Walmart+ credit?**
No. There is one Walmart+ credit per card account.

## Sources

- [The Points Guy: Walmart+ and the Amex Platinum](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/american-express/walmart-plus-amex-platinum)
- [Upgraded Points: Amex Platinum Walmart+ credit](https://upgradedpoints.com/credit-cards/reviews/american-express-platinum-card/walmart-plus-credit/)
- [Kudos: Walmart+ with Sam's Club Plus and the Amex credit](https://www.joinkudos.com/blog/walmart-plus-sams-club-plus-amex-platinum-credit)
- [The Points Guy: authorized users on the Amex Platinum](https://thepointsguy.com/guide/why-add-authorized-users-amex-platinum/)

# What counts toward the Amex Platinum welcome-offer spending requirement, and what does not?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/amex-platinum-welcome-offer-spending-requirement/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

Ordinary purchases of goods and services count toward the Amex Platinum spending requirement, which is currently $12,000 in the first six months. The $895 annual fee, interest, gift cards, prepaid cards, person-to-person payments and other cash equivalents do not count, and refunds are taken back off your total.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## The requirement in numbers

| Item | Figure |
|---|---|
| Spending needed | $12,000 in eligible purchases |
| Time allowed | First six months of card membership |
| Average per month | $2,000 |
| Requirement before February 5, 2026 | $8,000 in six months |
| Annual fee (does not count) | $895 |

The points you receive vary by applicant. Read the requirement on your own offer screen, since terms can change.

## What counts and what does not

Amex's application terms would not load for this page, so the list of exclusions below comes from a January 2026 guide that quotes Amex's offer terms. Upgraded Points (April 2026) gives the same exclusions.

| Transaction | Counts? | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Everyday purchases: groceries, fuel, restaurants, travel, online shopping | Yes | General rule |
| Utility bills paid by card | Yes, reported | My Points Life |
| Tax payments through a card processor (fee of about 1.8% to 2%) | Yes, reported | My Points Life; One Mile at a Time says "if eligible" |
| Purchases by additional cardholders on your account | Yes | The Points Guy |
| The annual fee | No | One Mile at a Time, Upgraded Points |
| Interest, late fees and other fees | No | Amex terms as quoted |
| Gift cards | No | Amex terms as quoted; Upgraded Points |
| Buying or reloading prepaid cards | No | Amex terms as quoted |
| Person-to-person payments, including Amex Send & Split | No | Amex terms as quoted |
| Traveler's checks and other cash equivalents | No | Amex terms as quoted |
| Cash advances and balance transfers | No | My Points Life; Upgraded Points for balance transfers |

The terms exclude gift cards wherever they are bought, so do not plan on them.

## Refunds and statement credits

- **Refunds reduce your total.** The Points Guy states that a refunded amount is typically deducted from progress toward the requirement. A large return late in the six months can leave you short.
- **Refunds after the points arrive.** A search summary of that article says Amex can take back a welcome offer if a refund drops you under the requirement. Not confirmed on the page itself.
- **Card credits.** One guide reports that statement credits from card benefits, such as the airline fee credit, are treated as payments and do not reduce your progress. That is not confirmed by Amex.

A margin helps with both: aim a few hundred dollars over $12,000 so one return does not undo it.

## When the six months start, and when points arrive

- Amex's Gold Card terms, seen in a search result, count the six months from the date the account is opened. The Platinum terms were not read, so the exact start is not confirmed. Upgraded Points says the tracker in your account shows the deadline.
- The same Gold Card terms say points are credited within 8 to 12 weeks after the requirement is met. Upgraded Points reports that Membership Rewards welcome points tend to post within a few days. Neither timing is confirmed for the Platinum Card on an Amex page read today.
- A welcome offer tracker usually appears in the online account and the app, showing spending so far. Upgraded Points notes it can lag a few days and may not appear for every card.

## The sum to do first

Add up what you already put on cards in a normal six months.

| Your normal card spending per month | Six-month total | Reaches $12,000? |
|---|---|---|
| $1,500 | $9,000 | No, $3,000 short |
| $2,000 | $12,000 | Yes, with no margin for returns |
| $2,500 | $15,000 | Yes |

A planned large purchase can fill a gap. Spending you would not otherwise do is a cost, not a saving.

## Who should skip it

- Anyone whose normal card spending is well under $2,000 a month and who has no large planned purchase.
- Anyone who would carry a balance to get there. Interest does not count toward the requirement and can exceed the value of the points.
- Anyone who was counting on gift cards, prepaid cards or payments to friends to reach the total. Those are excluded.
- Anyone who has had the Platinum Card before. You may not be shown a welcome offer at all. See [the once-per-lifetime rule](/amex-once-per-lifetime-welcome-offer-rule/).

Related: [how to see your offer](/highest-amex-platinum-welcome-offer-how-to-check/).

## Quick answers

**Does the $895 annual fee count toward the spending requirement?**
No. Fees are not purchases, so the annual fee does not count.

**Do gift cards count toward the Amex spending requirement?**
No. Amex's offer terms, as quoted by reviewers, exclude gift cards, prepaid cards and other cash equivalents.

**Does an authorized user's spending count?**
Yes. The Points Guy reports that purchases on additional cards count toward the primary cardmember's welcome offer.

# Is the Amex Platinum worth its annual fee if you only fly 4 to 6 times a year?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/amex-platinum-worth-it-occasional-flyer/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

For most people who fly 4 to 6 times a year, the Amex Platinum is worth its $895 annual fee only if they would already spend money on the things its credits pay for. The lounges and travel perks alone do not cover the fee at that number of flights.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## What the fee buys

The card costs $895 a year. In return it gives statement credits on set things (hotels, Resy restaurants, Uber, streaming and more), airport lounge access, and hotel status with Hilton and Marriott.

The credits add up to a large number on paper. The 11 main yearly credits total $2,994. But most are split into monthly or quarterly pieces, several need enrollment, and each one only counts if you would have bought that thing anyway.

## What 4 to 6 flights a year gets you in lounges

Lounge access depends on which airports and airlines you use.

| Lounge type | What you get | Limit that matters for an occasional flyer |
|---|---|---|
| Centurion Lounges | Entry within 3 hours of departure | Guests cost $50 each ($30 for ages 2 to 17) unless you spend $75,000 a year on the card |
| Delta Sky Club | 10 visits a year | Only on a same-day Delta flight; basic economy tickets are excluded |
| Priority Pass Select | Lounge entry, up to two guests free where allowed | Needs enrollment; Priority Pass restaurants are not included |

At 4 to 6 round trips you have at most a dozen or so chances a year to use a lounge, and only where one exists at your airports. Ten Sky Club visits are enough for a Delta flyer at that pace. If you travel with a partner or children, the $50 Centurion guest fee changes the math fast. An additional Platinum card for a second adult costs $195 a year and gives that person their own lounge access.

## The credits an occasional flyer can realistically use

These are the credits that fit a person who takes a few trips a year:

| Credit | Amount per year | Catch |
|---|---|---|
| Hotel credit | Up to $600 ($300 each half-year) | Prepaid stays at Fine Hotels + Resorts or The Hotel Collection, booked through Amex Travel; two-night minimum for The Hotel Collection now and for both programs from January 1, 2027 |
| Airline fee credit | Up to $200 | One airline you pick; fees like checked bags, not tickets |
| Uber Cash | Up to $200 | $15 a month, plus $20 extra in December |
| Digital entertainment | Up to $300 | $25 a month, enrollment required |
| Resy restaurants | Up to $400 | $100 a quarter, enrollment required |

A person who uses the full hotel credit, the airline credit, Uber Cash and the streaming credit gets $1,300 back. That covers the fee with room to spare. A person who uses only the airline credit and one $300 hotel credit gets $500 back and pays $395 net for lounge visits and status.

## Who should not get it

- You fly 4 to 6 times a year from an airport with no lounge the card opens.
- You would have to change your habits to use the credits. A credit you force yourself to spend is not savings.
- You do not want to track monthly and quarterly credits. Unused pieces do not roll over.
- You mostly want points on everyday spending. Outside flights and prepaid hotels, the card earns 1 point per dollar.
- You fly one airline and mainly want free checked bags. An airline card such as the Delta SkyMiles Gold ($0 the first year, then $150) gives a free first checked bag on Delta for far less.

## About the welcome offer

Amex advertises the welcome offer as "as high as" a number and shows each applicant their own offer before they accept the card. Offers vary by applicant, so leave it out of your math. People who have had the card before are generally not eligible.

## Quick answers

**How many flights a year make the Amex Platinum worth it?**
There is no set number. It depends on how many of the credits you would use anyway and whether your airports have lounges the card opens.

**Can I bring my family into the lounge?**
At Centurion Lounges, guests cost $50 each, or $30 for ages 2 to 17, unless you spend $75,000 a year on the card. Priority Pass and Escape lounges allow two guests free where space allows.

**Do the credits make up for the $895 fee?**
Only the ones you would have paid for anyway. Add up those and compare the total with $895.

- [American Express: the $600 hotel credit](https://www.americanexpress.com/en-us/travel/get-inspired/Platinum-Card-600-Dollar-Hotel-Credit)
- [The Points Guy: Amex Platinum review](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/reviews/amex-platinum-review/)
