# What is the most practical way to use Amex points for flights to Hawaii?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/amex-points-to-hawaii-best-uses/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

The practical route is to move Membership Rewards points to an airline program that can book a seat to Hawaii: Delta itself, or a partner program such as Flying Blue or Avianca LifeMiles that books Delta or United flights for fewer miles. Paying with points through Amex Travel is simpler, but gives a flat 1 cent per point on flights.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## What Amex points cannot do

Amex has no transfer partner based in Hawaii. Hawaiian Airlines and Alaska share a program, Atmos Rewards, and it is not on Amex's partner list. United, American and Southwest are not Amex partners either. Of the large US airlines that fly to Hawaii, only Delta takes Amex points directly.

So most of the options below book one airline's seat with another airline's miles.

## The options side by side

Award prices change often. Each example carries the date of its source. Check the live price before moving points.

| Program (rate from Amex) | Flies you on | Example price, with date | Extra cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| Delta SkyMiles (1:1) | Delta | Seattle to Honolulu 19,200 miles one-way (The Points Guy, April 14, 2026) | Amex charges $0.0006 per point on transfers to US airlines, up to $99 |
| Flying Blue, Air France-KLM (1:1) | Delta | "As low as 35,000 miles round-trip" in economy (AwardWallet, June 28, 2026); Detroit to Honolulu 24,000 each way (Thrifty Traveler, May 2025) | Taxes not stated by either source |
| Avianca LifeMiles (1:1) | United | San Francisco to Maui 15,000 miles plus $17 one-way; United's own price for that flight was 24,000 miles (The Points Guy, April 14, 2026) | The $17 is taxes and fees |
| British Airways Avios (1:1) | American, Alaska | Sources disagree: about 13,000 Avios one-way from the West Coast in older guides; 20,000 to 22,000 on AwardWallet's current chart | Not confirmed |
| Amex Travel, pay with points | Any airline sold there | 1 cent per point, so a $500 fare costs 50,000 points (The Points Guy, August 24, 2026) | None |

Delta has no award chart. Its prices rise and fall with the cash fare, so the Seattle example is one day's price, not a rule. The 15% award discount some guides mention belongs to Delta's own credit cards, not to the Platinum Card.

## The transfer fee to Delta

Amex adds an excise tax offset fee when points go to a US airline. It is $0.0006 per point, capped at $99 per transfer.

| Points moved to Delta | Fee |
|---|---|
| 20,000 | $12 |
| 40,000 | $24 |
| 80,000 | $48 |

AwardWallet lists the fee for Delta and JetBlue only, not for foreign programs such as Flying Blue, LifeMiles or Avios.

## Transfer or Amex Travel?

Do one sum. Divide the cash fare, in cents, by the miles the award costs.

- If the answer is clearly above 1 cent per point, the transfer is the better use.
- If it is near or below 1 cent, pay with points through Amex Travel, or pay cash. The Platinum Card earns 5 points per dollar on flights bought directly from airlines or through Amex Travel.

Third-party sites value a transferred Amex point at about 1.7 to 2 cents. That is an average across many trips, and a Hawaii economy seat will not always reach it.

Three cautions:

- A transfer cannot be undone. Find the award seat first.
- Search for the seat in the program you plan to use, not only on the airline's own site. Each program sets its own price.
- Transfer bonuses come and go. In November 2026 AwardWallet listed a bonus to Avianca LifeMiles running through December 16, 2026. Check the current list.

## Protections when you book with miles

Amex's baggage insurance guide says tickets paid with airline frequent flyer miles do not qualify, while Pay with Points bookings do. That is one point in favor of Amex Travel for travelers checking costly gear. More in [what card insurance covers on a golf trip](/golf-trip-travel-insurance-credit-card/).

## Who should skip it

- Travelers who want Hawaiian Airlines or Southwest flights. Amex points do not reach either program.
- Anyone with fixed dates in a school holiday. Partner award seats are scarce then, and the flat 1 cent through Amex Travel may be all that is left.
- People holding the card mainly for Hawaii. See [what the Amex Platinum does for one Hawaii trip](/amex-platinum-hawaii-trip/).

## Quick answers

**Can Amex points be moved to Hawaiian Airlines?**
No. Hawaiian and Alaska's Atmos Rewards program is not an Amex transfer partner.

**What is an Amex point worth on a flight booked through Amex Travel?**
1 cent per point on flights, according to The Points Guy in August 2026.

**Is there a fee to move Amex points to Delta?**
Yes. $0.0006 per point, up to $99 per transfer.

- [AwardWallet: Amex transfer partners compared (June 28, 2026)](https://awardwallet.com/credit-cards/amex-membership-rewards/best-amex-transfer-partners)
- [The Points Guy: points and miles to Hawaii (April 14, 2026)](https://thepointsguy.com/loyalty-programs/points-and-miles-to-hawaii/)
- [Thrifty Traveler: Flying Blue prices on Delta flights (May 14, 2025)](https://thriftytraveler.com/news/points/air-france-klm-cuts-delta-award-rates/)
- [AwardWallet: Avios flights in North America](https://awardwallet.com/airlines/british-airways-club/avios-flights-north-america/)
- [The Points Guy: Amex Pay with Points (August 24, 2026)](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/american-express/amex-pay-with-points-guide/)

# Are Amex points or Chase points worth more?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/amex-points-vs-chase-points-which-are-worth-more/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

Published valuations put the two almost level: The Points Guy values an Amex point at 2.0 cents and a Chase point at 2.05 cents, and One Mile at a Time uses 1.7 cents for both. The real difference is at the bottom and at the edges: Chase points are worth 1 cent as cash against about 0.6 cents for Amex, while Amex has more airline partners and Chase has Hyatt.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## Side by side

| | Amex points (Membership Rewards) | Chase points |
|---|---|---|
| The Points Guy valuation, November 2026 | 2.0 cents | 2.05 cents |
| One Mile at a Time valuation | 1.7 cents | 1.7 cents |
| As cash or statement credit | About 0.6 cents | 1 cent |
| Flights through the card's travel site | 1 cent | 1 cent; up to 2 cents with a Points Boost on a Sapphire Reserve, up to 1.5 or 1.75 on a Sapphire Preferred |
| Most hotels through the travel site | About 0.7 cents | 1 cent; more with a Points Boost |
| Transfer partners | About 20 (16 airline programs, 3 or 4 hotel programs; counts differ) | 16 (12 airline, 4 hotel) |
| Partners at worse than 1 to 1 | Cathay Pacific and Emirates (5 to 4), JetBlue (250 to 200) | Hyatt from a Sapphire Preferred (4 to 3) |
| Fee to transfer | 0.06 cents per point to US airlines, up to $99 | None reported |

The valuations assume transfers to airline and hotel partners and a user who finds good awards. They are estimates, not rates. Details: [Amex point values](/amex-membership-rewards-points-value/) and [Chase Points Boost](/chase-points-boost-explained/).

## Partners only one of them has

| Only Amex | Only Chase | Both |
|---|---|---|
| ANA, Avianca LifeMiles, Delta, Emirates, Qatar Airways, Aeromexico | United, Southwest | Aer Lingus, Air Canada Aeroplan, Flying Blue, British Airways, Iberia, Cathay Pacific, JetBlue, Qantas, Singapore, Virgin Atlantic |
| Hilton, Choice | Hyatt, IHG, Wyndham | Marriott |

Chase added Cathay Pacific and Qantas on November 18, 2026, which narrowed Amex's lead in airline partners. Where both have a partner, Chase's ratio is the same or better: Cathay Pacific and JetBlue are 1 to 1 from Chase and 5 to 4 from Amex.

The values of the partners themselves are in [which Amex partners are worth it](/amex-transfer-partners-which-are-worth-it/) and [which Chase partners are worth it](/chase-transfer-partners-which-are-worth-it/).

## Which is worth more, by kind of traveler

**You want cash or simple bookings.** Chase. A point is 1 cent as cash and at least 1 cent on any Chase Travel booking. Amex points drop to 0.6 cents as a statement credit and about 0.7 cents on most Amex Travel hotels.

**You stay at Hyatt.** Chase, with a Sapphire Reserve. The Points Guy values a Hyatt point at 1.65 cents, and the Reserve transfers at 1 to 1. From a Sapphire Preferred the ratio is 4 to 3, which this page works out to about 1.24 cents per Chase point; see [the Hyatt change](/chase-to-hyatt-transfer-change-2026/). Amex's hotel partners are valued at 0.4 to 0.85 cents per partner point.

**You fly United or Southwest.** Chase. Neither is an Amex partner.

**You fly Delta.** Amex. Delta is not a Chase partner. The Points Guy values a SkyMile at 1.2 cents, so this is convenience more than high value.

**You want business class to Japan on ANA.** Amex has the direct route, ANA Mileage Club, at about 100,000 miles round trip in low season. Both programs reach ANA seats through Virgin Atlantic. See [points to Japan](/how-many-points-for-a-flight-to-japan/).

**You want Europe in business class.** Close to a tie. Flying Blue, Virgin Atlantic, Iberia and Aeroplan take both. Amex adds ANA and LifeMiles; Chase adds United. See [points to Europe](/how-many-points-for-a-flight-to-europe/).

## How much the gap matters in dollars

On 100,000 points:

| Use | Amex | Chase |
|---|---|---|
| Cash or statement credit | About $600 | $1,000 |
| Flights through the travel site | $1,000 | $1,000, or up to $2,000 with a Sapphire Reserve Points Boost |
| The Points Guy's valuation | $2,000 | $2,050 |
| One Mile at a Time's valuation | $1,700 | $1,700 |

The $400 gap in the first row is the firm difference. The rest depends on the award you find. The Points Guy also reports that 2-cent Boosts on the Reserve have become harder to find than at launch.

## Where sources disagree

- The Points Guy puts Chase 0.05 cents ahead; One Mile at a Time values the two the same.
- The top Points Boost on a Sapphire Preferred is given as 1.5 cents by some sources and 1.75 cents by others.
- Amex's partner count is 20 or 21 depending on the source.

## Who should skip both

- People who would redeem for cash. A 2% cash-back card pays more than 1 point per dollar at 1 cent.
- People who will not search for award seats. The 1.7 to 2 cent figures only apply to transfers.
- People who close cards often. Both programs can take points back when an account closes; see [whether points expire](/do-amex-and-chase-points-expire/).

## Quick answers

**Which point has the higher cash value?**
Chase, at 1 cent per point. Amex points are worth about 0.6 cents as a statement credit.

**Which has more transfer partners?**
Amex, with about 20 against Chase's 16. Chase is the only one of the two with Hyatt, United and Southwest.

**Are the 2-cent valuations guaranteed?**
No. They are estimates by The Points Guy that assume transfers to partners. One Mile at a Time uses 1.7 cents.

- [The Points Guy: Chase Points Boost](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/chase-points-boost)

# How do Amex referral offers work, and why does the page say "as high as" a number?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/amex-referral-offer-how-it-works/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

An Amex referral link is a personal link from an existing cardmember that takes you to a card application. The page says "as high as" because Amex sets a welcome offer for each applicant and shows you yours before you accept the card, so the number in the headline is the top of a range and not a promise.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## What happens when you use a referral link

1. A cardmember shares their personal link.
2. You open it. Amex says a referred friend "will typically be taken to a product page for the same American Express Card associated with the referral link."
3. You apply. Amex shows you the welcome offer you qualify for.
4. You decide whether to accept the card with that offer.
5. If you are approved through the link, the cardmember who referred you can earn a referral bonus.

You have to apply through that person's own link for the referral to count.

## Why it says "as high as"

For the Platinum Card, the offer is worded "As High As 175,000 points. Find Out Your Offer." New cardmembers may be eligible for up to that figure after spending $12,000 in the first six months. Many applicants are shown less.

What reviewers report about the process:

- You apply and see your offer amount, then choose to accept or not.
- One Mile at a Time reports "there won't be a hard pull unless you accept the offer", and that declining has no effect on your credit score.
- Some reader comments there say they saw a lower offer only after a hard credit check. That is not verified, but read each screen with care.

Nobody outside Amex can tell you what your offer will be. The spend requirement matters as much as the points: an offer that needs $12,000 of spending in six months is not useful if you would not normally spend that.

## Who is not eligible for a welcome offer

| Situation | What generally happens |
|---|---|
| You have or had the same card before | Not eligible. Amex generally allows one welcome offer per card in a lifetime |
| You upgrade or switch from another Amex card | Generally no welcome offer |
| You are an authorized user on someone else's card | You can still get the offer on your own account |

Amex may show a pop-up during the application saying you do not qualify for the offer.

## You can pick a different card

A referral link is not locked to one card. Amex says that from the page the link opens, a referred friend can look at other available American Express cards and choose a different one.

The card on the link may not fit you. Amex cards differ a lot:

| Card | Annual fee | Built for |
|---|---|---|
| Platinum Card | $895 | Frequent travelers who will use lounges and many credits |
| Delta SkyMiles Gold | $0 the first year, then $150 | Delta flyers who want a free first checked bag |
| Hilton Honors Surpass | $150 | Hilton guests; includes Hilton Honors Gold status |
| Marriott Bonvoy Brilliant | $650 | Marriott regulars; includes Platinum Elite status |

## Is a referral offer higher than the public one?

Not always. AwardWallet notes a referral offer "may not match other publicly available offers." It can be higher or lower. The Points Guy adds that referral offers "can also vary significantly from person to person, even among people with the same card."

Compare the offer you are shown through a referral link with the one on Amex's public page before you accept either.

## What the person who referred you gets

The cardmember who shared the link earns a referral bonus if you are approved. Three facts about that:

- The size of their bonus depends on their card and their current referral offer, not on which card you pick.
- Amex's page says a cardmember can earn a referral bonus up to five times per card account per calendar year. The Points Guy describes the yearly cap differently, as a points limit that varies by card.
- Referral bonuses are treated as taxable income for the person who receives them.

A person who sends you a referral link has a reason to want you to apply.

## Quick answers

**Will I get the full "as high as" amount?**
Maybe not. Offers vary by applicant, and Amex shows you yours before you accept the card.

**Can I choose a different Amex card from a referral link?**
Yes. Amex says referred friends can look at other available cards from the page the link opens.

**Does the person who referred me get something?**
Yes. If you are approved through their link, they can earn a referral bonus, up to five times a year per card according to Amex's page.

- [The Points Guy: Amex Platinum review](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/reviews/amex-platinum-review/)

# Which Amex transfer partners are worth using, and which rarely are?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/amex-transfer-partners-which-are-worth-it/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

Among Amex's roughly 20 transfer partners, Avianca LifeMiles, Virgin Atlantic, Air Canada Aeroplan, Flying Blue, ANA and the Avios programs are valued above the 1 cent a point is worth on Amex Travel flights. Hilton, Marriott, Choice and Emirates come out below 1 cent per Amex point, and Cathay Pacific and JetBlue sit close to it.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## The test: does it beat 1 cent?

An Amex point buys 1 cent of airfare through Amex Travel; see [what a Membership Rewards point is worth](/amex-membership-rewards-points-value/). A transfer makes sense only when the award returns more than that after taxes and fees. Transfers cannot be reversed.

Two things lower the return before you start. Some partners take points at worse than 1 to 1. And transfers to US airlines (Delta, JetBlue) carry a fee of 0.06 cents per point, up to $99.

## The partners, with The Points Guy's November 2026 values

The last column is this page's arithmetic: the value of one partner point times the ratio.

| Partner | Ratio (Amex : partner) | Value of one partner point | Per Amex point |
|---|---|---|---|
| Avianca LifeMiles | 1 : 1 | 1.65 cents | 1.65 cents |
| Virgin Atlantic Flying Club | 1 : 1 | 1.5 cents | 1.5 cents |
| Air Canada Aeroplan | 1 : 1 | 1.45 cents | 1.45 cents |
| Air France-KLM Flying Blue | 1 : 1 | 1.45 cents | 1.45 cents |
| British Airways, Iberia, Aer Lingus (Avios) | 1 : 1 | 1.35 cents | 1.35 cents |
| ANA Mileage Club | 1 : 1 | 1.3 cents | 1.3 cents |
| Qantas Frequent Flyer | 1 : 1 | 1.3 cents | 1.3 cents |
| Aeromexico Rewards | 1 : 1.6 | 0.8 cents | 1.28 cents |
| Singapore KrisFlyer | 1 : 1 | 1.25 cents | 1.25 cents |
| Delta SkyMiles | 1 : 1 | 1.2 cents | 1.2 cents, before the fee |
| JetBlue TrueBlue | 250 : 200 | 1.35 cents | 1.08 cents, before the fee |
| Cathay Pacific Asia Miles | 5 : 4 | 1.3 cents | 1.04 cents |
| Choice Privileges | 1 : 1 | 0.85 cents | 0.85 cents |
| Emirates Skywards | 5 : 4 | 1 cent | 0.8 cents |
| Hilton Honors | 1 : 2 | 0.4 cents | 0.8 cents |
| Marriott Bonvoy | 1 : 1 | 0.75 cents | 0.75 cents |

Qatar Airways Privilege Club is also a 1 to 1 partner; The Points Guy's list gives it no separate value. Etihad Guest was dropped on June 30, 2026. Cathay Pacific moved to 5 to 4 on March 1, 2026, and Emirates on September 16, 2025.

These are one site's averages, not prices. A single award can land well above or below them.

## Partners that tend to be worth it

- **ANA Mileage Club.** A round trip between the US and Europe on partner airlines is 55,000 miles in economy and 100,000 in business, per AwardWallet. Transfers take about two days, and ANA passes on surcharges from some airlines.
- **Avianca LifeMiles.** No fuel surcharges on partner awards, per AwardWallet and Frequent Miler.
- **Virgin Atlantic.** Economy between the US and London from 6,000 points one way, plus taxes and fees that The Points Guy puts near $165. It also books ANA flights; see [points to Japan](/how-many-points-for-a-flight-to-japan/).
- **Flying Blue.** From 25,000 miles one way in economy and 60,000 in business between the US and Europe; see [points to Europe](/how-many-points-for-a-flight-to-europe/).
- **Iberia.** Off-peak business class from New York or Boston to Madrid at 40,500 Avios one way, per The Points Guy.

## Partners that rarely are

- **Hilton, Marriott and Choice.** AwardWallet says hotel transfers rarely return more than about 1 cent per Amex point. Hilton's 1 to 2 ratio still comes to 0.8 cents.
- **Emirates.** The 5 to 4 ratio and high surcharges on its own flights.
- **Delta.** Prices move with the cash fare. AwardWallet found Los Angeles to Paris at 68,000 miles round trip in economy.

## Where sources disagree

- **Aeromexico.** The arithmetic above gives 1.28 cents. AwardWallet ranks it among the weaker airline partners and cites economy awards to Europe at 40,000 to 80,000 points.
- **Aer Lingus.** Valued with the other Avios programs, but AwardWallet does not recommend transfers to it for now because of booking problems.
- **Iberia's price.** One AwardWallet page still prints 34,000 Avios for the Madrid business award; The Points Guy and a newer AwardWallet page say 40,500.
- **Partner count.** CNBC Select counts 21, point.me 20. AwardWallet's table has 16 airline programs and four hotel programs.
- **Bonuses.** AwardWallet lists 30% to Virgin Atlantic through November 30, 10% to Avianca through December 16 and 35% to Marriott through December 10, 2026. Not confirmed on an Amex page.

## Who should skip transfers

- People who want cash or simple bookings. Amex Travel flights at 1 cent need no award search.
- People who mostly want hotel nights. Amex has no Hyatt transfer.
- Delta-only flyers expecting 2 cents a point.

For the Chase side, see [which Chase partners are worth it](/chase-transfer-partners-which-are-worth-it/).

## Quick answers

**Which Amex partners are not 1 to 1?**
Hilton (1 to 2), Aeromexico (1 to 1.6), Cathay Pacific and Emirates (5 to 4) and JetBlue (250 to 200).

**Is there a fee to transfer Amex points?**
Only to US airlines such as Delta and JetBlue: 0.06 cents per point, capped at $99 per transfer.

**How long do transfers take?**
Most are immediate, per AwardWallet. ANA takes about two days, and Iberia, Qatar, Singapore and Cathay Pacific up to a day.

# Are credit card welcome bonuses and referral bonuses taxable in the US?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/are-credit-card-welcome-bonuses-taxable/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

Generally, a welcome bonus you earn by meeting a spending requirement is treated as a rebate on your purchases and not as taxable income. A referral bonus, which you get without spending, is generally treated as taxable income, and the card issuer may report it to the IRS on Form 1099-MISC. This page states what sources say and is not tax advice.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## The general rule, by type of reward

| Reward | Tied to spending? | How sources describe the tax treatment |
|---|---|---|
| Points or cash back on purchases | Yes | Rebate, generally not income |
| Welcome bonus after a spending requirement | Yes | Rebate, generally not income |
| Referral bonus for referring a friend | No | Generally taxable income |
| Bonus for opening a bank account | No | Generally taxable income |

The Points Guy's tax guide puts the line at spending: rewards that need a purchase are generally not income, and bonuses received without spending are. Thrifty Traveler describes a welcome bonus tied to a spending requirement as "a rebate on spending rather than income."

The person who is referred does not owe tax on a welcome bonus they earn by spending, according to The Points Guy. The tax question sits with the person who made the referral.

## Where the rebate idea comes from

The IRS has long treated rewards earned on purchases as a reduction in the price paid. The Points Guy cites a 2010 IRS memorandum for cash back.

One court case marks the edge. In Anikeev v. Commissioner (US Tax Court, February 2021), rewards earned by buying money orders and reloading prepaid debit cards were held taxable, because those are cash equivalents and not products or services. Rewards on gift card purchases in the same case were not. The Points Guy's summary says ordinary purchases are not affected.

## Referral bonuses and Form 1099-MISC

| Item | What sources say |
|---|---|
| Amex | Sends Form 1099-MISC for referral bonuses, and counts each Membership Rewards point as 1 cent (AwardWallet, Thrifty Traveler) |
| Chase | Has sent 1099s for referral points, valued at 1 cent each (One Mile at a Time, 2020). A search summary of Chase's referral terms says the bonus may be taxable income to you |
| Where it goes on a return | Other income, Schedule 1, line 8z (The Points Guy) |
| No form received | The income is still reportable (The Points Guy, Thrifty Traveler) |

At 1 cent a point, 50,000 referral points would be reported as $500 of income.

## The reporting threshold changed for 2026

| Payments made in | Form 1099-MISC box 3 threshold | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 2025 and earlier | $600 | The Points Guy, Doctor of Credit |
| 2026 | $2,000 | IRS instructions for Forms 1099-MISC and 1099-NEC |
| 2027 on | $2,000, may be adjusted for inflation | IRS instructions |

The threshold decides when an issuer must send a form. It does not decide whether the income is taxable. Referral bonuses under the threshold are still income under the general rule above.

Some guides written early in 2026 still give $600, because they describe 2025 tax returns. Whether Amex and Chase will send forms only at $2,000 for 2026, or below it, is not confirmed.

## What this means for someone about to apply

- A welcome bonus earned by spending on a personal card is generally not something you report.
- If you later refer friends, the points you earn are generally income at about 1 cent each, in the year you receive them.
- Keep your own record of any referral points and the dates they posted.

State tax treatment was not researched for this page and is not confirmed.

## Who should skip relying on this page

- Anyone who earned referral or bank account bonuses this year. Check your own figures with a tax professional or the IRS instructions.
- Anyone meeting spending requirements with money orders, prepaid card reloads or similar cash equivalents. The Anikeev case treated those rewards as taxable, and card issuers generally do not count such transactions anyway.
- Anyone who received a 1099 that looks wrong. Ask the issuer what the form covers before you file.

For the rules on what counts as spending, see [the Amex Platinum requirement](/amex-platinum-welcome-offer-spending-requirement/) and [the Chase Sapphire requirement](/chase-sapphire-welcome-bonus-spending-requirement/). For how referrals work, see [Amex referral offers](/amex-referral-offer-how-it-works/) and [Chase Sapphire referral links](/chase-sapphire-preferred-referral-bonus-how-it-works/).

## Quick answers

**Do I pay tax on a credit card welcome bonus?**
Generally no, when you earned it by meeting a spending requirement. Sources describe it as a rebate on purchases.

**Are referral bonuses taxable?**
Generally yes. They are not tied to spending, and issuers such as Amex report them on Form 1099-MISC at 1 cent a point.

**What is the 1099-MISC threshold for 2026?**
The IRS instructions set it at $2,000 for tax years beginning after 2025. It was $600 before.

## Sources

- [IRS: Instructions for Forms 1099-MISC and 1099-NEC](https://www.irs.gov/instructions/i1099mec)
- [The Points Guy: guide to taxes on credit card rewards](https://thepointsguy.com/guide/complete-guide-to-paying-taxes-on-credit-card-rewards)
- [Thrifty Traveler: are credit card rewards taxable](https://thriftytraveler.com/guides/points/are-credit-card-rewards-taxable)
- [The Points Guy: the Anikeev Tax Court ruling](https://thepointsguy.com/news/tax-on-rewards-ruling)
- [AwardWallet: Amex Refer a Friend](https://awardwallet.com/credit-cards/amex-refer-a-friend/)
- [One Mile at a Time: Chase 1099s for referral bonuses](https://onemileatatime.com/chase-referral-1099/)
- [Doctor of Credit: which banks send 1099 forms](https://www.doctorofcredit.com/which-banks-send-out-tax-form-1099-discussion-post-for-2025-tax-forms/)

# Can two people in the same household each have a Rakuten account, and can one refer the other?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/can-two-people-in-one-household-have-rakuten-accounts/
Facts checked: 2026-11-27
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

Rakuten's terms limit each person to one account; they set no limit per household, so two adults at one address can each have their own. The referral terms describe referring friends and family and do not name household members as barred, but they ban self-referral and say accounts that share a name, address or email may be flagged.

This page is information, not financial advice. It was read on Rakuten's own pages on November 27, 2026. The terms carry the date October 23, 2026, and the referral program terms October 8, 2024. Neither document mentions households, so whether a same-address referral will be paid is not confirmed.

## What the terms say about accounts

- **One per person.** The terms say each person is limited to one account. The limit is on the person, not the address.
- **Each member must qualify alone.** At least 18, living in the 50 United States or Washington D.C., with an email address and password of their own.
- **PayPal cannot be shared.** One PayPal email address cannot be connected to more than one Rakuten account. Two people who both want PayPal need two PayPal accounts.
- **Checks go to a name.** A check is issued to the name and address in that member's Account Settings.

## What the referral terms say

Rakuten's program terms describe the program as a bonus for referring friends and family, and its FAQ says members can invite friends, family members and coworkers. The person referred must:

1. Be a real person and new to Rakuten.
2. Join through the referrer's link, or enter the referrer's Rakuten email on the join form.
3. Make purchases that earn cash back within 90 days of signing up. Amazon.com purchases do not count, other than music.amazon.com.
4. Be the individual who pays for those purchases.

The offer on Rakuten's referral page, as read on November 27, 2026, asks for qualifying purchases totaling at least $50 within 90 days, for sign-ups from October 1 to December 31, 2026. Amounts and requirements vary and change; the details are on [how the sign-up and referral bonuses work](/rakuten-50-bonus-how-it-works/).

## Where a shared home can cause trouble

The program terms list what is not allowed, including self-referral, making purchases on behalf of another person, buying under an account that is not yours, and creating fake accounts. They then say several accounts with matching details "may be flagged as fraudulent referrals."

| Shared detail | What Rakuten's terms say |
|---|---|
| Same name | Named as a detail that may be flagged |
| Same address | Named as a detail that may be flagged |
| Same email address | Named as a detail that may be flagged |
| Same payment method on orders | Named in the main terms as a detail that may be flagged |
| Same PayPal account | Not allowed on two accounts; also named as a flag |
| Same name on orders | Named in the main terms as a detail that may be flagged |
| Same device or internet connection | Not named. The terms add a catch-all for any other identifying feature, so it is not confirmed either way |
| Same household | Not mentioned in the terms read |

Flagged is not the same as banned. Two real people at one address share an address by definition, and the terms do not say that alone disqualifies a referral. What Rakuten does after a flag is at its discretion: the terms let it investigate referral activity, withhold or cancel a bonus, delay payment, take back rewards and close an account, and they say its decisions are final.

The practical reading: a referral inside a home is closest to what the terms allow when the new member is a different person, has their own email, pays for their own qualifying purchases with their own payment method, and is paid to their own name or PayPal account.

## What does not work

- **A second account for yourself.** That breaks the one-account rule and is self-referral.
- **Referring someone who already has an account**, including an old Ebates one. The referred person must be new.
- **Buying on the new member's behalf.** The terms require the new member to be the one who pays.
- **Taking both joining bonuses.** A new member gets one; see [welcome bonus or referral bonus](/rakuten-welcome-bonus-vs-referral-bonus/).

## Where Rakuten's pages disagree

The program terms and FAQ say the referral program is open to residents of the 50 states, D.C. and Canada. The current offer terms on the referral page, and the main terms, say the 50 states and D.C. only.

## Who should skip it

- A couple who shop from one login and one card. One account already earns the cash back on those orders; a second adds little beyond a one-time bonus that may be withheld.
- Anyone who would open the second account in another person's name but run it themselves.
- Anyone who would spend $50 they had not planned in order to reach a bonus.

If a second person does want their own account, the joining step is on [how to sign up for Rakuten](/how-to-sign-up-for-rakuten/).

## Quick answers

**Can a husband and wife both have Rakuten accounts?**
Yes, under the terms as written. The limit is one account per person, and each needs their own email.

**Can I refer my spouse to Rakuten?**
The terms do not bar it by name. Accounts sharing an address or payment method may be flagged, so payment is not confirmed.

**Can two Rakuten accounts use the same PayPal?**
No. The terms say one PayPal email address cannot be connected to more than one account.

## Sources

- [Rakuten: Terms and conditions](https://www.rakuten.com/help/article/terms-conditions)
- [Rakuten: Referral program terms](https://www.rakuten.com/help/article/referral-program-terms-360002101348)
- [Rakuten: Refer-a-friend program FAQ](https://www.rakuten.com/help/article/referafriend-program-faq-360002117087)
- [Rakuten: Refer-a-friend page](https://www.rakuten.com/referral)
- [Rakuten: How to join Rakuten](https://www.rakuten.com/help/article/how-to-join-rakuten-360002101108)
- [Rakuten: Choosing how you get paid](https://www.rakuten.com/help/article/choosing-how-you-get-paid-360002100828)

# What is Chase's 5/24 rule, and how do you count your cards?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/chase-5-24-rule-explained/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

The 5/24 rule is an unofficial Chase practice: if you have opened five or more personal credit cards, from any bank, in the past 24 months, Chase will generally decline you for most of its cards. To count, list every card on your credit report by its opening date and count the ones from the last 24 months, closed cards included.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## Where the rule comes from

Chase has never published it. The rule is pieced together from applicants' reported results, and guides such as The Points Guy's treat it as well established. Because it is unofficial, the details below are reported patterns, not Chase policy in writing.

It applies to most Chase cards, including both Sapphire cards, the Freedom cards, the Ink business cards, and Chase's airline and hotel cards.

## What counts and what does not

| Account | Counts toward 5/24? |
|---|---|
| Personal credit cards from any bank, opened in the past 24 months | Yes |
| Cards you opened and then closed in that time | Yes |
| Authorized user cards that show on your credit report | Yes, but see below |
| Store cards on a national network such as Visa or Mastercard | Yes |
| Store cards usable at one store only | Some reports say yes |
| Business cards from Discover and TD Bank | Yes |
| Most Capital One business cards | Yes (reported exceptions: Venture X Business, Spark Cash Plus) |
| Most other business cards, including Chase's own | No |
| Denied applications and credit inquiries | No |
| Auto loans, student loans, mortgages | No |
| Changing one card to another with the same bank | Usually no, unless it creates a new account |
| Charge cards | Not confirmed in the sources read |

The Points Guy's rule of thumb: if it is a credit card and it appears on your personal credit report, assume it counts.

One point that trips people up: Chase business cards do not add to your count, but you generally still need to be under 5/24 to be approved for one.

## Authorized user cards

If someone added you to their card in the past 24 months, it normally appears on your report, and Chase's system counts it. That can make you look over the limit when your own cards are under it.

Two things are reported to help:

- After a denial, call Chase's reconsideration line and point out which accounts are authorized user accounts. An agent may set them aside. This is manual and may not work.
- Ask to be removed as an authorized user at least a month before you apply, so the report has time to update.

## How to count your cards

1. Get your credit report. The Points Guy's guide suggests Experian's free report; be careful not to sign up for a paid plan by mistake.
2. Sort the accounts by date opened.
3. Count every credit card opened in the past 24 months. Include closed cards and authorized user cards. Leave out loans.
4. Add any Discover, TD Bank or Capital One business cards if they show on the report.
5. Four or fewer means you are under 5/24. Five or more means you are at or over it.

## When a card stops counting

A card drops off on the first day of the 25th month after it was opened, not on the exact anniversary. The Points Guy's example: if your fifth most recent card was opened in October 2024, the earliest day to apply is November 1, 2026.

| Fifth card opened | Earliest date under 5/24 |
|---|---|
| October 2024 | November 1, 2026 |
| January 2025 | February 1, 2027 |
| June 2025 | July 1, 2027 |

## Other limits reported alongside it

- Some applicants report Chase will not approve more than two new accounts within 30 days.
- Being under 5/24 does not mean approval. Credit score, income and existing debt still matter.
- Being under 5/24 does not make you eligible for a welcome bonus. The Sapphire cards have [separate bonus rules](/chase-sapphire-bonus-eligibility-2026/).

## Who should skip worrying about it

- Anyone who has opened one or two cards in two years. You are well under.
- Anyone who is far over 5/24 and has no wish to stop opening other cards for a long stretch. Other banks do not use this rule.
- Anyone thinking of opening cards only to collect bonuses. Each new account affects your credit, and bonuses change and vary by applicant.

## Quick answers

**Do business cards count toward 5/24?**
Most do not, including Chase's own. Business cards from Discover, TD Bank and most from Capital One are reported to count.

**Does a closed card still count?**
Yes. Chase looks at when the account was opened, not whether it is still open.

**Does a denied application count?**
No. Only opened accounts count, not inquiries.

## Sources

- [The Points Guy: guide to Chase's 5/24 rule](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/chase/ultimate-guide-chase-5-24-rule/)
- [Chase: Sapphire Preferred card page](https://creditcards.chase.com/rewards-credit-cards/sapphire/preferred)

# What is Chase Points Boost, and how much are Chase points worth now?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/chase-points-boost-explained/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

Points Boost is Chase's system for giving more than 1 cent per point on selected flights and hotels booked through Chase Travel. Without a Boost, a point is worth 1 cent there; with one, it is worth up to 2 cents on a Sapphire Reserve and up to 1.5 or 1.75 cents on a Sapphire Preferred.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## How it works

Points Boost started showing in Chase Travel on June 23, 2025. It replaced the old setup, where every booking through Chase Travel got the same fixed bonus.

Now the value depends on the booking. Chase marks some flights and hotels with a Boost, and the price in points is lower for those. The set of boosted bookings rotates, and Chase does not publish a list. You see the value only when you search.

What sources report about where Boosts show up:

- **Hotels:** most often at hotels in The Edit, Chase's own collection, and at other frequently booked hotels.
- **Flights:** more often on long-haul premium cabins with selected airlines. Boosts on domestic economy are uncommon. Basic economy is excluded.
- **Activities and cruises:** 1 cent per point, no Boost.

## Values by card

| Card | Base value in Chase Travel | Top Points Boost value | Old fixed rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sapphire Reserve | 1 cent | Up to 2 cents | 1.5 cents |
| Sapphire Preferred | 1 cent | Up to 1.5 cents on selected hotels and flights; up to 1.75 cents on some premium-cabin fares | 1.25 cents |
| Ink Business Preferred | 1 cent | Same as Sapphire Preferred | 1.25 cents |
| Freedom Unlimited, Freedom Flex | 1 cent | Up to 1.1 cents on selected hotels; no flights | 1 cent |

Sources do not fully agree on the Sapphire Preferred's top figure. The Points Guy, Upgraded Points and NerdWallet give 1.75 cents for some premium-cabin flights. Chase's own Reserve page describes Boosts as up to 1.5x or 2x depending on the card, and AwardWallet says the Preferred's maximum drops to 1.5 cents from December 2025. The safe reading: expect 1.5 cents at most on the Preferred, and treat 1.75 as an occasional result.

The Points Guy also reports that 2-cent Boosts on the Reserve have become harder to find than at launch.

## What happened to the old fixed rates

Before Points Boost, Sapphire Reserve points were worth a flat 1.5 cents on any Chase Travel booking, and Sapphire Preferred points a flat 1.25 cents. Those flat rates are being phased out.

| Who | Which points | What they get | Until |
|---|---|---|---|
| Reserve cardholders approved before June 23, 2025 | Points earned before October 26, 2025 | The higher of the Boost or 1.5 cents | October 26, 2027 |
| Preferred cardholders | Points earned before October 26, 2025 | The higher of the Boost or 1.25 cents | October 26, 2027 |
| Everyone | Points earned from October 26, 2025 | 1 cent, or the Boost when one is offered | No end date |

Two small points of disagreement: Upgraded Points applies the "approved before June 23, 2025" condition to the Preferred as well, and Doctor of Credit gives the end date as October 25, 2027. This wording was not found on a Chase page checked today, so confirm it in your own account.

## So what is a point worth?

It depends on what you do with it.

| Use | Value per point |
|---|---|
| Cash or statement credit | 1 cent or less |
| Chase Travel, no Boost | 1 cent |
| Chase Travel with a Boost | 1.1 to 2 cents, by card |
| Transfer to an airline or hotel partner | Varies; The Points Guy's September 2026 estimate is 2.05 cents, One Mile at a Time uses 1.7 cents |

The transfer figures are estimates that assume you find good award space. For simple economy flights through Chase Travel, plan on 1 cent.

One more change affects transfers: [the Hyatt rate from a Sapphire Preferred is now 4 to 3](/chase-to-hyatt-transfer-change-2026/), not 1 to 1.

## Who should skip it

- Anyone counting on a fixed bonus. A Boost may not exist for the flight or hotel you want, and then the points are worth 1 cent.
- Anyone who would pay a higher price in Chase Travel than booking direct just to get a Boost. Compare the cash prices first.
- Anyone who prefers plain cash back. At 1 cent a point, a cash back card with no annual fee may do as well.

## Quick answers

**Are Chase points still worth 1.25 or 1.5 cents?**
Only for points earned before October 26, 2025, and only until October 26, 2027. Newer points are worth 1 cent unless a Boost applies.

**Can I see which bookings have a Boost before I search?**
No. Chase does not publish a list. The value appears in the search results.

**Does the Sapphire Preferred get 2-cent Boosts?**
No. Two cents is the top value on the Reserve cards only.

## Sources

- [Chase: Sapphire Reserve card page](https://creditcards.chase.com/rewards-credit-cards/sapphire/reserve)
- [Upgraded Points: Chase Travel Points Boost](https://upgradedpoints.com/news/chase-travel-points-boost/)
- [The Points Guy: Chase Points Boost guide](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/chase-points-boost)
- [AwardWallet: Points Boost](https://awardwallet.com/credit-cards/chase-ultimate-rewards/points-boost/)

# What is the most practical way to use Chase points for a Hawaii trip?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/chase-points-to-hawaii-best-uses/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

For most travelers the practical use is the flight: move Chase points to United or Southwest at 1:1 when the award price is low, or book through Chase Travel when the cash fare is low. Hyatt hotels still work, but from a Sapphire Preferred each Hyatt point now costs one third more Chase points.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## The four options side by side

Award prices move daily. Each figure below is an example from the dated source, not a promise.

| Use | Rate from Chase | Example, with date | Main limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| United MileagePlus | 1:1 | Los Angeles to Honolulu 13,000 miles one-way; Denver 22,000; Chicago 25,000; each plus $5.60 (The Points Guy, June 16, 2026) | No fixed chart; checked bags cost extra |
| Southwest Rapid Rewards | 1:1 | Oakland to Honolulu from 16,500 points plus $5.60 one-way (The Points Guy, April 14, 2026) | Price follows the cash fare; bags now cost $45 and $55 |
| Chase Travel | 1 cent per point; up to 1.5 cents with Points Boost on a Sapphire Preferred (some sources report 1.75 on premium-cabin fares), up to 2 cents on a Sapphire Reserve | A $500 fare costs 50,000 points at 1 cent | Chase publishes no fixed list of boosted bookings |
| World of Hyatt | 4:3 from Sapphire Preferred; 1:1 from Sapphire Reserve | A 35,000-point night costs 46,667 Chase points from a Preferred | Few Hyatt hotels in Hawaii, mostly high categories |

## Flights: transfer or book through Chase Travel?

Do one sum before moving any points. Take the cash fare in cents and divide it by the points the award costs. That gives cents per point.

Two made-up fares show the range (they are illustrations, not quotes):

- If the cash fare were $400 and the award 13,000 United miles, that is about 3 cents per point.
- If the cash fare were $180 and the award 16,500 Southwest points, that is about 1.1 cents per point.

Then check the same flight in Chase Travel. Without a Points Boost, points are worth 1 cent each there. With a Boost, a Sapphire Preferred gets up to 1.5 cents on selected flights and hotels and, by some sources, up to 1.75 cents on premium-cabin fares. If the transfer gives fewer cents per point than Chase Travel does, book through Chase Travel.

Transfers go one way. Sources repeat the same advice: find the award seat first, then move the points.

## Hyatt: the 4:3 rate changes the sum

Since October 1, 2026, every Sapphire Preferred moves points to Hyatt at 4:3. Four Chase points become three Hyatt points. The Sapphire Reserve stays at 1:1.

| Hyatt price per night | Chase points from a Preferred | Chase points from a Reserve |
|---|---|---|
| 15,000 | 20,000 | 15,000 |
| 25,000 | 33,334 | 25,000 |
| 35,000 | 46,667 | 35,000 |
| 75,000 | 100,000 | 75,000 |

The two big Hawaii resorts, Andaz Maui and Grand Hyatt Kauai, are listed by most recent guides as Category 8, at 35,000 to 75,000 Hyatt points a night. Five nights at the lowest level would take 233,334 Chase points from a Preferred. See [what each Hyatt hotel in Hawaii costs in points](/hyatt-hotels-hawaii-points-cost/).

Hyatt can still beat 1 cent per point when the cash rate is high. One guide puts Grand Hyatt Kauai cash rates at $800 to $1,300 a night. But at 4:3 each Chase point buys 25% fewer Hyatt points than it did at 1:1.

## Other partners

British Airways Avios can book American and Alaska flights to Hawaii. Sources disagree on the price. Older guides give about 13,000 Avios one-way from the West Coast. AwardWallet's current chart shows 20,000 to 22,000. Check the live price before relying on it.

Alaska and Hawaiian's own program, Atmos Rewards, is not a Chase partner.

## Who should skip it

- Travelers with a small balance. Two round trips from the Midwest can take 100,000 United miles at the example prices above.
- Sapphire Preferred holders aiming at a Hyatt resort for a week. The 4:3 rate makes this costly.
- Anyone who finds a low cash fare. Paying cash and keeping the points can be the better sum.

A [Sapphire Preferred for one trip a year](/chase-sapphire-preferred-one-trip-a-year/) is covered separately.

## Quick answers

**Do Chase points transfer to Hawaiian Airlines?**
No. Hawaiian's program, Atmos Rewards, is not on Chase's partner list. United and Southwest are.

**Is the Chase to Hyatt rate still 1:1?**
Only from a Sapphire Reserve. From a Sapphire Preferred it has been 4:3 since October 1, 2026.

**Can a transfer be undone?**
No. Find the award seat first, then move the points.

- [The Points Guy: points and miles to Hawaii (April 14, 2026)](https://thepointsguy.com/loyalty-programs/points-and-miles-to-hawaii/)
- [Chase: Sapphire Preferred card page](https://creditcards.chase.com/rewards-credit-cards/sapphire/preferred)
- [Chase: Sapphire Reserve card page](https://creditcards.chase.com/rewards-credit-cards/sapphire/reserve)

# What does an authorized user cost on the Sapphire Preferred and the Reserve, and what do they get?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/chase-sapphire-authorized-user-cost-and-benefits/
Facts checked: 2026-11-21
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

An authorized user costs nothing on the Sapphire Preferred and $195 a year each on the Sapphire Reserve. On both cards they earn points at the card's rates into the primary cardholder's balance; on the Reserve they also get their own airport lounge access, but not a second set of the card's credits.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## Side by side

| | Sapphire Preferred | Sapphire Reserve |
|---|---|---|
| Fee per authorized user | $0 | $195 a year |
| Primary cardholder's fee | $95 | $795 |
| Earning rates | Same as the primary card | Same as the primary card |
| Where points go | Primary cardholder's account | Primary cardholder's account |
| Airport lounges | None | Own Priority Pass with two free guests; Sapphire Lounges; select Air Canada lounges |
| Travel and rental car cover | Yes, per One Mile at a Time | Yes, same as the primary cardholder |
| DashPass | Can activate on their own DoorDash account | Can activate, with the monthly promos |
| Extra statement credits | None | None |
| Welcome bonus of their own | No | No |

## What both cards share

Chase's terms say an authorized user has the same charging privileges as the primary cardmember but is not financially responsible. The primary cardmember owes every dollar an authorized user spends.

One Mile at a Time reports, for the Reserve:

- There is typically no credit check to add someone.
- The card usually appears on the authorized user's own credit report, which can help build a history.
- It also counts as one of their cards under [Chase's 5/24 rule](/chase-5-24-rule-explained/).
- Their spending counts toward the primary cardholder's welcome bonus requirement.
- The new card is mailed to the primary cardholder.

Being an authorized user does not stop someone from later opening the same card in their own name.

Chase's minimum age for an authorized user is not confirmed.

## What $195 buys on the Reserve

The main gain is lounge access when the authorized user travels without the primary cardholder. Chase's terms give each cardholder, primary or authorized, a Priority Pass membership with two free guests and $27 for each extra guest. Air Canada lounge access covers the cardholder and one guest. Details are on the [Reserve lounge access page](/chase-sapphire-reserve-lounge-access/).

## What $195 does not buy

No second set of credits. One Mile at a Time lists the travel credit, dining credit, The Edit credit and Global Entry credit as one per account. An authorized user's spending can use up those credits, but the totals do not grow. Whether an authorized user's card can trigger the StubHub, Lyft and Peloton credits is not confirmed.

Whether Chase refunds part of the $195 when an authorized user is removed mid-year is not confirmed.

## The lounge sum

The primary cardholder already brings two guests free. So an authorized user card adds lounge access only in two cases: the person flies without the primary cardholder, or the group is larger than three.

| Authorized user's solo lounge visits a year | Cost per visit at $195 |
|---|---|
| 2 | $97.50 |
| 5 | $39 |
| 10 | $19.50 |

For a couple who always fly together, the second card adds no lounge access the first card did not already give.

The other route is a second Reserve account at $795, with its own credits and its own shot at a welcome bonus. That is a separate decision with a hard credit check; an authorized user card is $600 less and carries no credits.

## On the Preferred

Because it is free, the question is only whether you want the person spending on your account. Reasons people add one: pooling a household's dining and travel spending into one points balance, or giving a family member a card with no foreign transaction fee for a trip. The Apple TV offer on the Preferred is for the primary cardholder, per The Points Guy.

An older snippet on one site says Preferred authorized users cost $195 and get Priority Pass. Chase's pages and that site's current article say free, with no lounges.

## Who should skip it

- Couples who always travel together on a Reserve. The primary card's two free guests cover the lounge.
- Anyone who would add a person they cannot trust with their credit line. The primary cardholder pays the bill.
- Anyone planning their own Chase applications soon. An authorized user card can count toward 5/24.
- Anyone hoping for a second $300 travel credit or dining credit. It does not come with the card.

## Quick answers

**Is an authorized user free on the Sapphire Preferred?**
Yes. Chase charges no fee for authorized users on the Preferred.

**Do Reserve authorized users get their own Priority Pass?**
Yes. Chase's terms give each authorized user a membership with two free guests per visit.

**Do authorized users get their own $300 travel credit?**
No. The credits are per account, and an authorized user's spending draws on the same totals.

## Sources

- [Chase: Sapphire offer and benefit terms](https://www.chase.com/personal/credit-cards/offerdetails/chasesapphire)
- [One Mile at a Time: Sapphire Reserve authorized user cost and benefits](https://onemileatatime.com/reviews/credit-cards/chase/chase-sapphire-reserve-authorized-user/)
- [Chase: DashPass terms for Sapphire and Sapphire Preferred](https://chase.com/digital/resources/terms-of-use/sapphire-doordash)
- [The Points Guy: a college student as a Sapphire Preferred authorized user](https://thepointsguy.com/guide/reasons-why-college-student-authorized-user-chase-sapphire-preferred/)
- [Chase: Sapphire Lounge access](https://www.chase.com/sapphire-cards/lounges)

# Can you get a Sapphire welcome bonus if you had a Sapphire card before? The 2026 rules

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/chase-sapphire-bonus-eligibility-2026/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

It depends on which card. Under the rules in force since January 2026, you can earn the welcome bonus on each Sapphire card once in your lifetime, so a past Sapphire Preferred does not block a first Sapphire Reserve bonus, and the reverse. A second bonus on the same card is not available, no matter how long ago the first one was.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## The rule by situation

| Your history | Sapphire Preferred bonus | Sapphire Reserve bonus |
|---|---|---|
| Never had either card | Possible | Possible |
| Earned the Preferred bonus before | No | Possible |
| Earned the Reserve bonus before | Possible | No |
| Earned both before | No | No |
| Hold a Preferred now, never had a Reserve | No (you already have the card) | Possible |
| Held a card before but never earned its bonus | Unclear, see below | Unclear, see below |

"Possible" is not a promise. You still have to be approved, and Chase decides bonus eligibility at the time you apply. Welcome offers also change and vary by applicant.

## How the rules got here

| Period | Rule |
|---|---|
| Before June 2025 | You could earn a Sapphire bonus again 48 months after your last one |
| June 2025 to January 2026 | One bonus per card for life, and holding one Sapphire card blocked a first bonus on the other |
| From January 22, 2026 | One bonus per card for life; holding or having held the other card no longer blocks it |

The Points Guy dates the latest change to January 22, 2026. A CNBC Select summary gives January 25. The 48-month reset is gone under either date.

## The unclear case: you held the card but got no bonus

The Points Guy's January 2026 news piece frames the test as whether you ever earned the bonus on that card. Chase's own card pages word it more broadly:

> "The new cardmember bonus may not be available to you if you previously held this card." (Chase)

A later Points Guy article, from July 2026, also says former cardholders may be ineligible even if they never earned a bonus. So if you once held a Sapphire card through a product change, with no bonus, do not assume you qualify. The two readings conflict, and Chase's wording leaves it room to say no.

Chase's page adds that it may look at how many cards you have opened and closed.

## The pop-up that tells you

Chase now shows a notice during the application if you would not receive the bonus. As The Points Guy describes it, the message says you may be approved for the card but will not get the bonus. You then choose:

- Cancel the application. The Points Guy reports this has no effect on your credit score.
- Continue and take the card without the bonus.

Keep a record of the offer terms shown when you apply.

## Other things that can stop you

- **You already have that card open.** Chase's Reserve page says the card is not available to someone who currently holds it.
- **The 5/24 rule.** If you opened five or more personal cards at any bank in the past 24 months, Chase generally declines the application. See [how to count your cards](/chase-5-24-rule-explained/).
- **A past bonus still counts after you close or downgrade.** Closing the card does not reset anything.
- **Product changes carry no bonus.** Switching an existing Chase card to a Sapphire is not a new account and normally comes with no welcome offer.

How these rules treat the Sapphire Reserve for Business was not confirmed in the sources read.

## Who should skip it

- Anyone who already earned the bonus on the card they are looking at. The card may still suit you, but work out the sums without a bonus.
- Anyone at or over 5/24. An application is likely to be declined.
- Anyone who would have to spend more than usual to meet a spending requirement. A bonus does not make up for purchases you would not otherwise make, or for interest on a balance.
- Anyone waiting for the old 48-month clock. It no longer exists.

## Quick answers

**I got the Sapphire Preferred bonus in 2019. Can I get it again?**
No. Each card's bonus is now once per lifetime, and the 48-month reset ended in June 2025.

**I have a Sapphire Preferred. Can I get the Sapphire Reserve bonus?**
Yes, if you never earned the Reserve bonus and Chase approves you. Holding the Preferred has not blocked it since January 2026.

**Will Chase tell me before I apply whether I get the bonus?**
Chase shows a notice during the application if you will not receive it, and you can cancel at that point.

## Sources

- [The Points Guy: Sapphire bonus eligibility changes 2026](https://thepointsguy.com/news/chase-sapphire-bonus-eligibility-changes-2026)
- [The Points Guy: the Sapphire bonus eligibility pop-up](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/chase-sapphire-preferred-lifetime-bonus-popup/)
- [Chase: Sapphire Preferred card page](https://creditcards.chase.com/rewards-credit-cards/sapphire/preferred)
- [Chase: Sapphire Reserve card page](https://creditcards.chase.com/rewards-credit-cards/sapphire/reserve)
- [CNBC Select: Sapphire welcome bonus rules](https://www.cnbc.com/select/chase-sapphire-welcome-bonus-rules-what-to-know/)
- [The Points Guy: guide to Chase's 5/24 rule](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/chase/ultimate-guide-chase-5-24-rule/)

# Chase Sapphire Preferred hotel credit: how it works and what bookings count

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/chase-sapphire-preferred-50-hotel-credit-how-it-works/
Facts checked: 2026-11-23
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

The Sapphire Preferred's $50 hotel credit no longer exists in that form: Chase doubled it to $100 on June 15, 2026. It is a statement credit of up to $100 each account anniversary year for hotel stays booked and paid for through Chase Travel with the card, and it does not apply to hotels booked anywhere else.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## What changed in June 2026

| | Before June 15, 2026 | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Amount | Up to $50 | Up to $100 |
| Period | Account anniversary year | Account anniversary year |
| Annual fee | $95 | $95 |
| Activation | None | None |

The Points Guy reports that existing cardholders who had already used $50 got another $50 from June 15. Some older articles still show the $50 figure.

## What counts

- **A hotel stay bought through Chase Travel.** Chase's terms name "hotel accommodation purchases" made through Chase Travel. A hotel booked on the hotel's own site or another travel site does not count.
- **Paid with the card.** One Mile at a Time notes that you must choose to pay with the card at checkout. If you pay with points, the credit does not apply.
- **Prepaid.** Chase's announcement says the credit needs a prepaid booking through Chase Travel. Chase's terms page does not repeat that word, so treat prepaid as the safe choice.
- **Any length of stay.** Upgraded Points reports no minimum stay and no set list of hotels.

A stay that costs less than $100 uses part of the credit. Upgraded Points says the rest can go toward a later booking in the same account year. Its example is $79 on one stay and $21 on the next.

## What does not count

- Flights, rental cars and other travel in Chase Travel.
- Hotels booked outside Chase Travel.
- Whether vacation rentals in Chase Travel count is not confirmed.
- Whether a booking made on an authorized user's card triggers the credit is not confirmed for this card.

## When the year starts and ends

The credit follows your account, not the calendar. Chase's terms define the year as running from the account open date through the first statement date after the account anniversary, and then every 12 billing cycles. Unused credit does not carry over.

## When the credit shows up

The price is not reduced at booking. You pay in full and the credit arrives later. Sources disagree on how long that takes:

| Source | Stated timing |
|---|---|
| Chase's terms | Within 3 business days, up to 4 weeks |
| One Mile at a Time | Within two days of the purchase posting |
| Upgraded Points | 1 to 2 billing cycles |

Chase can take the credit back if the booking is canceled, returned or changed, or if you close the account within 90 days of receiving it.

## The costs that do not show on the statement

- **No points on the credited part.** The first $100 of Chase Travel hotel purchases each year earns no points. The rest of the booking earns 5x.
- **Hotel loyalty.** Chase Travel is a third-party booking channel. At the large chains, such bookings generally earn no hotel points and no elite benefits. The Points Guy notes some listings carry a loyalty tag, but points are not guaranteed.
- **Price.** Rates in Chase Travel can be higher than the hotel's own rate or a member rate. A $100 credit on a stay that costs $40 more than booking direct is worth $60.

A simple check: price the same room and dates on the hotel's site. Subtract any difference from $100. That is what the credit is worth to you on that stay.

## The sum against the fee

Used in full on a stay you would have booked anyway at the same price, the credit is $100 against a $95 fee. Used on a pricier rate, or on a stay you would not have taken, it is worth less. How this fits with the rest of the card's first year is on the [first-year plan page](/chase-sapphire-preferred-first-year-plan/).

## Who should skip it

- Anyone with hotel elite status who would lose upgrades, breakfast or night credits by booking through a third party.
- Anyone who rarely pays for hotels, or who stays in vacation rentals booked direct.
- Anyone who finds the same room cheaper elsewhere by close to $100.
- Anyone who needs a pay-at-hotel rate. The credit is described as needing a prepaid booking.

## Quick answers

**Is the Sapphire Preferred hotel credit $50 or $100?**
It is up to $100 per account anniversary year. Chase raised it from $50 on June 15, 2026.

**Does a hotel booked directly with the hotel count?**
No. Only hotel stays bought through Chase Travel with the card count.

**Does the credit roll over?**
No. It resets each account anniversary year and unused credit is lost.

## Sources

- [Chase: Meet the New Chase Sapphire Preferred (June 15, 2026)](https://media.chase.com/news/Meet-the-New-Chase-Sapphire-Preferred)
- [Chase: Sapphire offer and benefit terms](https://www.chase.com/personal/credit-cards/offerdetails/chasesapphire)
- [Chase: how to use the Sapphire Preferred hotel credit](https://chase.com/personal/credit-cards/education/rewards-benefits/how-to-use-the-sapphire-preferred-hotel-credit)
- [One Mile at a Time: Sapphire Preferred hotel credit](https://onemileatatime.com/reviews/credit-cards/chase/chase-sapphire-preferred-hotel-credit/)
- [Upgraded Points: Sapphire Preferred hotel credit](https://upgradedpoints.com/credit-cards/reviews/chase-sapphire-preferred-card/hotel-credit/)
- [The Points Guy: Sapphire Preferred hotel credit](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/chase/chase-sapphire-preferred-hotel-credit/)
- [The Points Guy: Sapphire Preferred refresh, June 2026](https://thepointsguy.com/news/chase-sapphire-preferred-refresh-2026/)

# How does the Sapphire Preferred 10% anniversary points bonus work?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/chase-sapphire-preferred-anniversary-points-bonus/
Facts checked: 2026-11-21
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

The Sapphire Preferred's 10% anniversary points bonus has ended: people who applied on or after June 15, 2026 never get it, and for earlier cardholders it stopped counting purchases after October 1, 2026. Chase says the last bonuses will be awarded by January 31, 2027, and in its place the card gained new 3x categories and a larger hotel credit.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## How the bonus worked

Each account anniversary, Chase added points equal to 10% of the dollars you spent on purchases in the year before. It was based on spending, not on the points earned in bonus categories. The Points Guy describes it as adding 0.1 points per dollar.

| Yearly spending | Anniversary bonus | Value at 1 cent a point |
|---|---|---|
| $10,000 | 1,000 points | $10 |
| $20,000 | 2,000 points | $20 |
| $50,000 | 5,000 points | $50 |

The $20,000 and $50,000 rows match the examples given by Thrifty Traveler. The other figures follow the same rule.

## The end dates

| Who | What happens |
|---|---|
| Applied on or after June 15, 2026 | No anniversary bonus at all |
| Applied before June 15, 2026 | Purchases through October 1, 2026 still count |
| Final payout | Chase: all bonuses earned are awarded by January 31, 2027 |

Chase's wording, in its June 15 announcement: "The 10% Anniversary Bonus will be discontinued."

Whether the final bonus arrives on your own anniversary or as one deposit for everyone is not confirmed. AwardWallet says it is posted in early 2027. If you had the card before June 15, 2026 and spent on it up to October 1, look for a line in your points activity by the end of January 2027.

## What replaced it

Chase did not swap the bonus for one thing. The same June 2026 refresh made these changes, with the fee still $95:

| Change | Detail |
|---|---|
| Gas and EV charging | 3x, up from 1x |
| Vacation homes at brands such as Airbnb and Vrbo | 3x |
| Hotel credit | Up to $100 a year on Chase Travel hotel stays, up from $50 |
| Global Entry, TSA PreCheck or NEXUS | Credit up to $120 every four years |
| Hyatt transfers | Now 4 Chase points to 3 Hyatt points, down from 1:1 |

The hotel credit has its own page: [how the $100 hotel credit works](/chase-sapphire-preferred-50-hotel-credit-how-it-works/). The Hyatt change is on the [Hyatt transfer page](/chase-to-hyatt-transfer-change-2026/).

## Did you come out ahead or behind?

Compare what the bonus paid you with what the new terms pay. Two illustrations, not typical results:

| | Reader A | Reader B |
|---|---|---|
| Yearly spending on the card | $15,000 | $40,000 |
| Old bonus lost | 1,500 points | 4,000 points |
| Gas spending | $2,000 | $0 |
| Extra points from 3x gas (2 more per dollar) | 4,000 points | 0 |
| Extra hotel credit, if used | $50 | $0 |
| Net | Ahead by 2,500 points and $50 | Behind by 4,000 points |

A reader who buys gas on the card and books one hotel a year through Chase Travel is ahead. A reader with high spending in categories that earn 1x, who does not use the hotel credit, is behind.

The sum leaves out the Hyatt change. Someone who moved many points to Hyatt each year loses more from the 4:3 ratio than from the bonus.

## What to do about it

Nothing needs to be done to receive the final bonus. Three things are worth checking:

1. Your points activity in early 2027, if you held the card before June 15, 2026.
2. Whether gas or EV charging should move to this card now that it earns 3x.
3. Whether everyday 1x spending would earn more on a no-fee card. See [pairing the Preferred with Freedom cards](/chase-sapphire-preferred-with-freedom-cards-combine-points/).

## Who should skip it

This is no longer a reason to choose or keep the card.

- Anyone comparing cards from an old review that lists the 10% bonus should strike it from the sum.
- Anyone who kept the card mainly for the bonus on heavy 1x spending should rerun the numbers; a 1.5% card may return more on that spending.
- New applicants get nothing from it and should not count it.

## Quick answers

**Does the Sapphire Preferred still have the 10% anniversary bonus?**
No. Chase ended it in 2026. Purchases after October 1, 2026 earn no anniversary bonus.

**When is the last anniversary bonus paid?**
Chase says all bonuses earned are awarded by January 31, 2027. The exact posting date per account is not confirmed.

**Was the bonus 10% of points or 10% of spending?**
It was 10% of the dollars spent on purchases, so $20,000 of spending gave 2,000 points.

- [Thrifty Traveler: Sapphire Preferred anniversary bonus ending](https://thriftytraveler.com/news/credit-card/chase-sapphire-preferred-anniversary-bonus-ending/)
- [The Points Guy: Sapphire Preferred refresh, June 2026](https://thepointsguy.com/news/chase-sapphire-preferred-refresh-2026/)

# What credit score do you need for the Chase Sapphire Preferred?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/chase-sapphire-preferred-credit-score-needed/
Facts checked: 2026-11-22
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

Chase does not publish a minimum credit score for the Sapphire Preferred. Sources that track approvals report a FICO score of about 670 as the low end and 700 or higher as the usual range, and Chase also weighs income, recent card openings and the credit it has already given you.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## What Chase says

Chase's card page gives no score, no income figure and no minimum credit line. It says only that the card is subject to credit approval. The Points Guy states it directly:

> "Chase doesn't publish a minimum credit score requirement." (The Points Guy)

Every number below is a report from a named source, not a Chase rule and not a promise of approval.

## What named sources report

| Source | Figure reported | Date of article |
|---|---|---|
| The Points Guy | FICO of about 700 or higher | July 2026 |
| CNBC Select | At least 670; above 700 gives better odds | October 2026 |
| Upgraded Points | Wait for at least 670; most cardholders at 720 or higher | July 2025 |
| Motley Fool Money | Most approved applicants above 700; 680 to 699 approved less often | August 2025 |
| FinanceBuzz | Good to excellent credit, with good starting at 670 | November 2026 |

The sources differ on where the line sits, 670 or 700, and none claims a cutoff. Upgraded Points notes approvals with scores in the 600s and denials with scores in the 800s. A score in the reported range does not mean approval.

## What else Chase looks at

- **Cards opened in the past 24 months.** Chase generally declines applicants who opened five or more personal cards at any bank in that time, whatever their score. This is unofficial; see [how the 5/24 rule counts cards](/chase-5-24-rule-explained/).
- **Income.** Chase states no minimum. Upgraded Points suggests at least $30,000 a year, its own view.
- **Debt against income.** Motley Fool Money says a low ratio helps.
- **Length of credit history.** Upgraded Points and Motley Fool Money both suggest two years or more.
- **Credit Chase already gives you.** The Points Guy says Chase may limit the total credit it extends across your cards.
- **Recent applications.** CNBC Select lists them as a factor. Each application also adds a hard inquiry; see [what an application does to a score](/does-applying-for-a-travel-card-hurt-credit-score/).
- **Whether you already hold the card.** Approval and the welcome offer are separate questions. The offer has [its own eligibility rules](/chase-sapphire-bonus-eligibility-2026/), and offers vary by applicant and change.

## The Visa Signature credit line

FinanceBuzz and Upgraded Points both report that an approved Sapphire Preferred comes with a credit limit of at least $5,000, and FinanceBuzz ties that to the card being a Visa Signature. Chase's public card page does not state this figure, so it is reported, not confirmed by Chase.

If the report holds, Chase has to be willing to extend $5,000, which depends on income and on your existing Chase credit lines.

## Checking before you apply

Chase has a page that checks for preapproved offers. You enter basic details such as name and address. Chase says filling out the form does not affect your credit score, while an application does. The page does not say an offer guarantees approval.

## If Chase says no

A denial comes with a notice giving the reasons. The Points Guy and AwardWallet both describe calling Chase's reconsideration line to ask for a second look.

| Point | What is reported |
|---|---|
| Result | Not guaranteed, per both sources |
| Too much total credit | An agent may move or lower credit on an existing Chase card (The Points Guy, AwardWallet) |
| 5/24 | Agents generally cannot override it (The Points Guy, AwardWallet) |
| Phone number | AwardWallet lists 888-270-2127 for personal cards; another listing differs, so check your denial notice |

## Who should skip it for now

- Anyone at or over 5/24. A high score does not get around it.
- Anyone with a FICO score well under 670. Every source read puts the reported range above that.
- Anyone with a credit history shorter than about two years, going by the two sources that give a figure.
- Anyone who would carry a balance. Interest outweighs points.

## Quick answers

**Is there a minimum credit score for the Sapphire Preferred?**
Chase publishes none. Named sources report roughly 670 as the low end and 700 or more as typical.

**Does a score above 700 mean approval?**
No. Chase also looks at recent card openings, income and existing Chase credit, and denials with high scores are reported.

**Does checking for a preapproved offer affect my credit score?**
Chase says filling out its form does not. Submitting an application does.

## Sources

- [Chase: Sapphire Preferred card page](https://creditcards.chase.com/rewards-credit-cards/sapphire/preferred)
- [Chase: check for preapproved offers](https://creditcards.chase.com/check-for-preapproved-offers)
- [The Points Guy: credit score needed for the Sapphire Preferred](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/chase/credit-score-needed-for-chase-sapphire-preferred/)
- [CNBC Select: Sapphire Preferred credit score](https://www.cnbc.com/select/chase-sapphire-preferred-card-credit-score/)
- [Upgraded Points: Sapphire Preferred credit score requirements](https://upgradedpoints.com/credit-cards/reviews/chase-sapphire-preferred-card/credit-score-requirements)
- [Motley Fool Money: Sapphire Preferred credit score](https://www.fool.com/money/credit-cards/chase/chase-sapphire-preferred-card-review/chase-sapphire-preferred-credit-score)
- [FinanceBuzz: Sapphire Preferred common questions](https://financebuzz.com/chase-sapphire-preferred-common-questions)
- [AwardWallet: credit card reconsideration calls](https://awardwallet.com/credit-cards/reconsideration-call/)
