# What DoorDash and DashPass benefits come with the Sapphire Preferred, and what are they worth?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/chase-sapphire-preferred-doordash-dashpass-benefit/
Facts checked: 2026-11-21
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

The Sapphire Preferred comes with a free DashPass membership, which runs until December 31, 2029 if you activate it before then, plus $10 off one non-restaurant DoorDash order each month. At face value that is up to $240 a year, but it is worth only what you already spend on DoorDash delivery fees and grocery or convenience orders.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## The two parts

| Part | What you get | Limits |
|---|---|---|
| DashPass | $0 delivery fee and reduced service fees on eligible orders | Order must meet the minimum subtotal shown in the app; activate by 12/31/2029 |
| Monthly promo | $10 off one non-restaurant order per calendar month | Grocery, convenience and similar orders; subtotal only; no rollover |

Chase puts the value of DashPass at $120 a year. DoorDash's help page, seen in a search summary, gives the current paid price as $9.99 a month.

## How long DashPass lasts

Chase's terms say the membership runs "from activation until December 31, 2029 or for 12 months, whichever is longer." Activate in 2026 and it lasts about three years. Activate in late 2029 and it lasts 12 months from that date.

Sources disagree on the activation deadline. Chase's terms, Chase's Preferred update page and DoorDash all say December 31, 2029. A search summary of an older Chase page gave December 31, 2027. The 2029 date is on the pages read in full today.

After the free period, DoorDash's help page says a membership renews at the monthly rate then in force. Set a reminder if you do not want to pay for it.

## How to turn it on

1. Add the Sapphire Preferred as a payment method in the DoorDash or Caviar app. A digital wallet such as Apple Pay does not qualify.
2. Tap the activation button.
3. Pay with that same card at checkout to get the monthly promo.

Authorized users can add their card and activate too. Chase's terms say everyone on the account shares one membership period, which starts when the first person activates.

If you already pay for DashPass, DoorDash says the Chase membership replaces it and the billing stops. It does not mention a refund of past charges.

## The $10 monthly promo

- It applies to one order a month from a non-restaurant store on DoorDash, such as a grocery or convenience store.
- It comes off the subtotal. Fees, taxes and tip are still charged.
- Unused value is gone at the end of the month.
- Gift cards are excluded, and alcohol orders may be restricted.
- Chase sets no separate minimum order for the promo, but DoorDash's own order minimums apply.

Restaurant orders get the DashPass fee savings but not this promo. The Sapphire Reserve has a larger set of DoorDash promos, covered in [the Reserve credits page](/chase-sapphire-reserve-credits-real-value/).

## What it is worth to you

Use last year's DoorDash history, not a guess.

| Reader | DashPass | Monthly promo | Yearly total |
|---|---|---|---|
| Never uses DoorDash | $0 | $0 | $0 |
| Already pays for DashPass, no grocery orders | $120 | $0 | $120 |
| Orders restaurant delivery twice a month, no DashPass today | Fee savings on about 24 orders | $0 | Depends on the fees saved |
| Already pays for DashPass and orders groceries on DoorDash monthly | $120 | $120 | $240 |

Two cautions on the sums:

- Prices for items on delivery apps can be higher than in the store. A $10 promo on a grocery order that costs $8 more than a store trip, plus tip, saves little.
- A promo that leads to an order you would not have placed is spending, not saving.

This benefit sits beside the card's other perks in the [first-year plan](/chase-sapphire-preferred-first-year-plan/).

## Who should skip it

- Anyone who does not use DoorDash. The benefit has no cash value.
- Anyone outside DoorDash's delivery area, or whose local non-restaurant stores are not on the app.
- Anyone who would order more delivery only because of the promo.
- Anyone weighing the $95 fee mainly on this perk. It is a discount inside one app, not money back.

## Quick answers

**Does the $10 promo work on restaurant orders?**
No. On the Sapphire Preferred it applies to one non-restaurant order a month, such as grocery or convenience.

**Does the unused $10 roll over?**
No. Chase's terms say the monthly discount does not roll over into a later month.

**Do authorized users get DashPass too?**
Yes. Each adds the card in the app and activates; everyone on the account shares the same membership period.

## Sources

- [Chase: DashPass terms for Sapphire and Sapphire Preferred](https://chase.com/digital/resources/terms-of-use/sapphire-doordash)
- [Chase: Sapphire offer and benefit terms](https://www.chase.com/personal/credit-cards/offerdetails/chasesapphire)
- [DoorDash help: DashPass for Chase card members](https://help.doordash.com/consumers/s/article/Chase-Partnership)
- [Chase: Meet the New Chase Sapphire Preferred (June 15, 2026)](https://media.chase.com/news/Meet-the-New-Chase-Sapphire-Preferred)
- [Chase: Sapphire Preferred update page](https://www.chase.com/travel/guide/tips/preferred-update)

# Is the Chase Sapphire Preferred a sensible first travel card, and what credit do you need?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/chase-sapphire-preferred-first-travel-card/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

It can be, for someone who already has good credit, at least a year or two of credit history, and one or more trips a year. Chase publishes no minimum score; guides suggest 670 to 700 or higher. It is a poor first credit card of any kind, because approval is harder with a thin credit file.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## What credit you need

Chase does not publish a cutoff. Guides differ:

| Source | Suggested score | Other advice |
|---|---|---|
| Upgraded Points (July 2025) | At least 670 | About 2 years of good history; income of $30,000 or more |
| NerdWallet (search summary) | At least 690 | Not read in full |
| The Points Guy (July 2026) | At least 700 | Average account age over one year; balances under about 20% of limits |

Upgraded Points notes people have been approved with scores in the 600s and denied with scores in the 800s. Chase also looks at income, debt and account age.

Upgraded Points reports a minimum credit limit of $5,000 for new cardholders, which is why very low incomes are a hurdle.

## The other approval rule

Chase generally declines applicants who have opened five or more personal credit cards, from any bank, in the past 24 months. A first-time travel card applicant is rarely near that number, but authorized-user cards can count. See [the 5/24 rule](/chase-5-24-rule-explained/).

If you are declined, Chase must tell you why. The Points Guy notes you can call Chase's reconsideration line and ask for a second look; it does not always work.

## What you pay and what you get

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Annual fee | $95, charged in the first year too |
| Foreign transaction fee | None |
| Earning | 5 points per dollar on Chase Travel; 3 on dining and some other categories; 2 on other travel; 1 elsewhere |
| Hotel credit | Up to $100 per account year on hotel stays bought through Chase Travel |
| Travel protections | Trip cancellation, trip delay, baggage and primary rental car cover |
| Points | Worth 1 cent as cash; more on some Chase Travel bookings; transferable to 14 airline and hotel programs |

Welcome offers vary by applicant and change over time. The public offer checked on this date required $5,000 of purchases in the first 3 months. Only count an offer if that spending is already in your budget.

## The sums for a beginner

The fee is $95 a year. Ways it can be covered:

- **One hotel stay through Chase Travel.** The credit of up to $100 offsets the fee, if the Chase Travel price is as low as booking direct.
- **Points on ordinary spending.** $400 a month on dining earns 14,400 points a year, worth $144 as cash at 1 cent each. A 2% cash back card with no fee would pay $96 on the same spending, so the card's edge on that spending is $48.
- **Protections.** [Primary rental car cover](/chase-sapphire-preferred-rental-car-insurance/) and [trip insurance](/chase-sapphire-preferred-travel-insurance/) have value only if you rent cars or prepay trips.

If you take no trips in a year and book no hotel through Chase Travel, the points on everyday spending have to carry the whole fee. A worked year is on the [first-year plan page](/chase-sapphire-preferred-first-year-plan/).

## Why it is a common first travel card

- The fee is low for a card with transferable points and primary rental car cover.
- Points can be used simply, as cash or through Chase Travel, before you learn transfers.
- The Points Guy says approval is generally easier than for the Sapphire Reserve.

## Limits a beginner should know

- No airport lounge access.
- No medical cover abroad.
- Transfers to Hyatt are now 4 Chase points for 3 Hyatt points.
- Chase may not give the new cardmember bonus to someone who has held the card before. See [bonus eligibility](/chase-sapphire-bonus-eligibility-2026/).

## Who should skip it

- Anyone with no credit history, or less than a year of it. The Points Guy suggests building credit with a starter card first.
- Anyone with a score well under 670.
- Anyone who carries a balance month to month.
- Anyone who does not travel at least [once a year](/chase-sapphire-preferred-one-trip-a-year/). A no-fee cash back card is simpler.
- Anyone who has opened five or more cards in the past 24 months.

## Quick answers

**What credit score do I need for the Sapphire Preferred?**
Chase publishes no minimum. Guides suggest at least 670 to 700, and approval also depends on income and history.

**Can the Sapphire Preferred be my first credit card ever?**
It is unlikely to be approved with no credit history. Guides suggest a year or two of on-time payments on another card first.

**Is the $95 fee waived in the first year?**
No. The fee is charged in the first year.

## Sources

- [The Points Guy: credit score needed for the Sapphire Preferred](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/chase/credit-score-needed-for-chase-sapphire-preferred/)
- [Upgraded Points: Sapphire Preferred credit score requirements](https://upgradedpoints.com/credit-cards/reviews/chase-sapphire-preferred-card/credit-score-requirements)
- [NerdWallet: things to know before getting the Sapphire Preferred](https://www.nerdwallet.com/travel/learn/things-you-should-know-before-getting-the-chase-sapphire-preferred)
- [Chase: Sapphire Preferred card page](https://creditcards.chase.com/rewards-credit-cards/sapphire/preferred)

# What should you do in the first year with a Sapphire Preferred to get your $95 back?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/chase-sapphire-preferred-first-year-plan/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

One step covers the fee: book a hotel stay of $100 or more through Chase Travel, and the card's yearly hotel credit returns up to $100 against the $95 annual fee. Everything else in the first year, such as the DoorDash promos, the Apple TV offer and the points you earn, is on top of that.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## The first-year checklist

| Step | What you get back | Deadline or limit |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Book one hotel stay through Chase Travel | Up to $100 statement credit | Once each account anniversary year; posts automatically |
| 2. Meet the spending requirement with normal spending | The welcome offer shown when you applied | Public offer today asks for $5,000 in the first 3 months |
| 3. Activate DashPass | DashPass for 12 months (Chase states a $120 value) | Activate by 12/31/2029 |
| 4. Use the DoorDash monthly promo, if you already order there | $10 off one non-restaurant order a month | Expires each month; non-restaurant orders only |
| 5. Activate Apple TV | At least 12 months (Chase states a $180 value) | Activate by 12/31/2026 |
| 6. Pay a Global Entry, TSA PreCheck or NEXUS fee with the card | Up to $120 credit | Once every four years |
| 7. Decide where the points go | 1 cent each or more | No deadline while the account is open |

## Step 1: the hotel credit

This is the step that settles the question. Notes on using it:

- The booking must be made through Chase Travel and paid with the card.
- The first $100 of hotel spending that the credit covers earns no points.
- Compare the Chase Travel price with the hotel's own price for the same room. If Chase Travel is $40 more, the credit is really worth $60 to you.

The credit was $50 until a June 2026 refresh raised it to $100, so older articles may still show $50.

## Step 2: the spending requirement

Welcome offers change and vary by applicant, so go by the terms shown on your own application. The public offer today is 75,000 points after $5,000 in purchases in the first three months, with points posting six to eight weeks after you qualify.

$5,000 in three months is about $1,667 a month. If that is more than you normally put on a card, the offer is not a reason to spend more.

If you held a Sapphire Preferred before, check [the bonus eligibility rules](/chase-sapphire-bonus-eligibility-2026/) first.

## Steps 3 to 6: the partner perks

Count these only if you would pay for the thing anyway.

- **DashPass** lowers delivery fees. It has value only if you already order from DoorDash.
- **The $10 monthly promo** is for non-restaurant orders, such as grocery or convenience. Twelve uses is $120 a year, but an unused month is lost.
- **Apple TV** needs activation by December 31, 2026. Note when the free period ends.
- **Global Entry:** pay the application fee with the card and the credit posts.

The 10% anniversary points bonus that older guides mention was removed in June 2026.

## Step 7: where the points go

| Use | Value per point |
|---|---|
| Cash or statement credit | 1 cent or less |
| Chase Travel, ordinary booking | 1 cent |
| Chase Travel with [Points Boost](/chase-points-boost-explained/) | Up to 1.5 cents; some sources say up to 1.75 cents on certain premium-cabin fares |
| Transfer to most airline and hotel partners | 1 point to 1 mile or point; value depends on the booking |
| Transfer to Hyatt | [4 Chase points to 3 Hyatt points](/chase-to-hyatt-transfer-change-2026/) since 2026 |

Day to day, the card earns 5x on Chase Travel, 3x on dining, gas stations, EV charging, selected streaming and online grocery, 2x on other travel and 1x elsewhere.

Transfers cannot be undone.

## The sum

The $95 fee less the $100 hotel credit leaves you $5 ahead. If you were going to pay for Global Entry anyway, add $120. Points and any welcome offer come on top.

## Who should skip it

- Anyone who would not book a hotel through Chase Travel at least once a year. Without the credit, the card costs $95.
- Anyone who carries a balance month to month.
- Anyone who has opened five or more personal cards in 24 months. Chase generally declines them under [the 5/24 rule](/chase-5-24-rule-explained/).
- Anyone who wants lounge access. That comes with the Sapphire Reserve only.

## Quick answers

**Is the $95 fee waived in the first year?**
No. It is charged in year one.

**Does the hotel credit work if I book directly with the hotel?**
No. The stay must be booked through Chase Travel.

**Do I need to use every perk to come out ahead?**
No. The hotel credit alone covers the fee if you would have booked that stay anyway.

## Sources

- [Chase: Sapphire Preferred card page](https://creditcards.chase.com/rewards-credit-cards/sapphire/preferred)
- [One Mile at a Time: Sapphire Preferred review and 2026 changes](https://onemileatatime.com/chase-sapphire-card-limited-time-perks/)
- [The Points Guy: Chase Sapphire Preferred review](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/chase-sapphire-preferred-review)
- [The Points Guy: Chase Points Boost guide](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/chase-points-boost)
- [AwardWallet: Chase to Hyatt transfer ratios](https://awardwallet.com/credit-cards/chase-ultimate-rewards/chase-to-hyatt-transfer/)

# Can Chase Sapphire Preferred points pay for a Disney trip, and how far do they go?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/chase-sapphire-preferred-for-disney-trip/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

Partly. Sapphire Preferred points can pay for flights and for hotels near the Disney parks, either through Chase Travel or by transfer to an airline or hotel program. Park tickets are the weak spot: Chase Travel is reported not to sell tickets to the US Disney parks, so points cover them only as cash back at 1 cent each.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## What points are worth here

| Way to use points | Value per point | Works for |
|---|---|---|
| Statement credit or cash | 1 cent | Anything, including park tickets |
| Chase Travel, no Points Boost | 1 cent | Flights, hotels, rental cars |
| Chase Travel with Points Boost | Up to 1.5 cents on selected hotels and flights | Only the bookings Chase marks |
| Transfer to Hyatt | 4 Chase points become 3 Hyatt points | Hyatt hotels near the parks |
| Transfer to Southwest, United or Marriott | 1:1 | Flights to Orlando or Anaheim, Marriott hotels |

Chase does not publish which bookings get a Points Boost. See [how Points Boost works](/chase-points-boost-explained/).

## How far a balance goes

| Points | As cash (1 cent) | Chase Travel with a 1.5-cent Boost |
|---|---|---|
| 25,000 | $250 | $375 |
| 50,000 | $500 | $750 |
| 75,000 | $750 | $1,125 |
| 100,000 | $1,000 | $1,500 |

A $300 hotel night costs 30,000 points at 1 cent and 20,000 points with a 1.5-cent Boost. A family's park tickets for several days usually cost more than the hotel, and tickets get the 1-cent rate.

## Hotels

**Through Chase Travel.** AwardWallet reports that the Swan, Swan Reserve and Dolphin hotels at Walt Disney World can be booked with points, and that Disney's own resorts appear only occasionally. A booking made this way earns no Marriott stay credit or elite perks, and resort fees still apply.

The card's hotel credit of up to $100 per account year applies to hotel stays bought through Chase Travel, so it can come off one of these bookings.

**By transfer to Hyatt.** AwardWallet names Hyatt Regency Grand Cypress and Hyatt Place Lake Buena Vista near Walt Disney World, and Hyatt House, Hyatt Place and Hyatt Regency Orange County near Disneyland. Hyatt waives resort fees on award nights.

In April 2025 the Grand Cypress cost 12,000 to 18,000 Hyatt points a night. At the Sapphire Preferred's 4:3 rate that would be 16,000 to 24,000 Chase points. Hyatt changed its award chart in May 2026, and the hotel's current price is not confirmed. The [Hyatt transfer change](/chase-to-hyatt-transfer-change-2026/) explains the 4:3 rate.

**By transfer to Marriott.** The Swan and Dolphin are Marriott hotels. Upgraded Points gives two different starting prices in the same article, about 40,000 and about 50,000 Marriott points a night, and Marriott does not waive the resort fee on award nights. Compare the Chase Travel price first.

## Park tickets

Sources disagree on whether Chase Travel sells them:

- Upgraded Points (June 2026) says Chase Travel does not sell tickets to US Disney parks, though it lists overseas parks.
- AwardWallet (April 2025) says Chase Travel sometimes sells Walt Disney World and Disneyland admission, usually at higher prices than Disney or other sellers.

Check Chase Travel before counting on it. Otherwise, pay for tickets with the card and redeem points as a statement credit at 1 cent each.

## What the card earns on Disney spending

| Purchase | Reported rate |
|---|---|
| Tickets bought alone from Disney | 1 point per dollar; they code as entertainment |
| A Disney package with lodging and tickets, booked direct | 2 points; it codes as travel |
| Food at the US parks | 3 points, as dining |
| Hotels or activities bought through Chase Travel | 5 points |

How a ticket reseller codes on this card is not confirmed.

## Insurance on a park trip

The card's trip cancellation cover applies to prepaid travel paid with the card. Standalone theme park tickets that are not part of a travel package are reported as excluded. Details are on the [travel insurance page](/chase-sapphire-preferred-travel-insurance/).

## Who should skip it

- Anyone whose main cost is park tickets. A flat cash back card pays the same or more on tickets.
- Anyone set on a Disney-owned resort. They are rarely bookable with Chase points.
- Anyone who would not otherwise spend enough to build a useful balance.

## Quick answers

**Can I buy Disney park tickets with Chase points?**
Not reliably through Chase Travel for the US parks; sources disagree. You can pay with the card and redeem points as a statement credit at 1 cent each.

**Can I book a Disney hotel with Sapphire Preferred points?**
The Swan, Swan Reserve and Dolphin are reported as bookable in Chase Travel. Disney-owned resorts appear only occasionally.

**Do Disney tickets earn bonus points on the card?**
Tickets bought alone are reported to earn 1 point per dollar. A package with lodging earns 2 points as travel.

## Sources

- [Upgraded Points: Sapphire Preferred and theme park tickets](https://upgradedpoints.com/news/chase-sapphire-preferred-card-theme-park-tickets)
- [AwardWallet: using Chase points for a Disney World resort](https://awardwallet.com/blog/how-to-use-ultimate-rewards-points-for-a-disney-world-resort)
- [The Points Guy: credit cards for Disney trips](https://thepointsguy.com/guide/best-credit-cards-disney)
- [Upgraded Points: Disney World with points](https://upgradedpoints.com/travel/disney-world-for-cheap-with-points/)
- [Chase: Sapphire Preferred card page](https://creditcards.chase.com/rewards-credit-cards/sapphire/preferred)

# Is the Chase Sapphire Preferred a good card to use abroad?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/chase-sapphire-preferred-foreign-transaction-fees-abroad/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

For purchases, yes. The Sapphire Preferred charges no foreign transaction fee, runs on the Visa network, and carries trip and rental car protections that apply outside the United States. It is a poor way to get cash, it has no lounge access, and it does not pay medical bills abroad.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## The fee, in numbers

Many US cards add about 3% to each purchase made in a foreign currency. The Sapphire Preferred adds nothing, according to Chase's card page.

| Spending abroad | Card with a 3% foreign fee | Sapphire Preferred |
|---|---|---|
| $1,000 | $30 in fees | $0 |
| $3,000 | $90 in fees | $0 |
| $5,000 | $150 in fees | $0 |

The card's annual fee is $95. A card with no annual fee and no foreign fee would save the same amounts, so the foreign fee alone does not justify the $95.

## Acceptance

The card is a Visa Signature card, per FinanceBuzz, and Visa is widely accepted worldwide. FinanceBuzz also reports that you do not need to tell Chase before you travel.

Whether the card works with a PIN at unattended machines, such as some train ticket kiosks and fuel pumps in Europe, is not confirmed. Search summaries describe it as a chip-and-signature card. Carry a second way to pay.

## Three ways it can still cost you

**Paying in dollars at the terminal.** Some foreign terminals offer to charge you in US dollars. That is dynamic currency conversion: the merchant sets the exchange rate, and Wise notes the rate can be inflated. Choosing the local currency leaves the conversion to Visa.

**Cash from an ATM.** A cash withdrawal on the card is a cash advance. Wise reports the fee as $10 or 5% of each transaction, whichever is greater, plus any fee from the ATM owner. A $400 withdrawal costs $20 before interest. A debit card is the usual tool for cash.

**Cash-like purchases.** Buying foreign currency or traveler's checks does not count as a purchase and earns no points.

## What you earn abroad

| Purchase | Points per dollar |
|---|---|
| Travel booked through Chase Travel | 5 |
| Dining | 3 |
| Other travel, such as trains, taxis and hotels booked direct | 2 |
| Everything else | 1 |

Chase's summary puts no US-only limit on the dining or travel categories. No source read for this page states in so many words that foreign restaurants earn 3 points, and the rate depends on how the merchant is coded. Gas, online grocery and streaming categories have their own exclusions.

## Protections that travel with you

These apply when the trip or rental is paid with the card. Limits and exclusions are on the [travel insurance page](/chase-sapphire-preferred-travel-insurance/).

- Trip cancellation and interruption, up to $10,000 per traveler
- Trip delay, up to $500 per traveler after 12 hours or an overnight stay
- Baggage delay, up to $100 a day for 5 days
- Lost luggage, up to $3,000 per traveler, with reported sub-limits of $500 for jewelry and watches and $500 for cameras and electronics
- [Primary rental car cover](/chase-sapphire-preferred-rental-car-insurance/) for damage to the car, in the United States and some countries abroad

The card also has a travel and emergency assistance line. FinanceBuzz describes it as a referral service: it helps you find a doctor, a lawyer or a translator, and you pay for whatever you use.

## What it lacks abroad

- **Medical cover.** No emergency medical expense benefit is listed for this card.
- **Liability cover in a rental car.** The rental benefit covers the car, not other people or property.
- **Airport lounges.** None are included. The [Sapphire Reserve](/sapphire-preferred-vs-reserve-light-traveler/) has them, at a much higher fee.

The card also has a credit of up to $120 every four years for a Global Entry, TSA PreCheck or NEXUS application fee, which helps on the way home.

## Who should skip it

- Anyone who mainly needs cash abroad. Use a debit card with low ATM fees.
- Anyone who wants medical cover from a card. Buy a travel medical policy.
- Anyone who travels abroad rarely and would not use the card's other features. A no-annual-fee card without a foreign fee saves the same 3%.
- Anyone who wants lounge access.

## Quick answers

**Does the Sapphire Preferred charge a foreign transaction fee?**
No. Chase's card page lists no foreign transaction fee on purchases made outside the United States.

**Should I pay in dollars or the local currency?**
The local currency. When a terminal converts to dollars for you, the merchant picks the rate, and it can be worse than Visa's.

**Can I use it at an ATM abroad?**
Yes, but it is a cash advance. The reported fee is $10 or 5%, whichever is greater, plus ATM owner fees.

## Sources

- [Chase: Sapphire Preferred card page](https://creditcards.chase.com/rewards-credit-cards/sapphire/preferred)
- [Wise: Chase Sapphire foreign transaction fee guide](https://wise.com/us/blog/chase-sapphire-foreign-transaction-fee)
- [FinanceBuzz: using the Sapphire Preferred internationally](https://financebuzz.com/using-chase-sapphire-preferred-internationally)
- [Chase: how Sapphire rental car insurance works](https://www.chase.com/personal/credit-cards/education/basics/chase-sapphire-rental-car-insurance-guide)

# Is the Chase Sapphire Preferred worth it if you take one big trip a year?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/chase-sapphire-preferred-one-trip-a-year/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

For most people who take one real trip a year, yes. The card costs $95 a year, and a single hotel booking through Chase Travel returns up to $100, so the fee can be covered by one stay. If you would never book a hotel through Chase's site, the answer gets weaker.

This page is information, not financial advice. Card terms change, so check the issuer's page before you decide.

## The yearly sums

| Item | Amount |
|---|---|
| Annual fee | $95, charged in year one too |
| Hotel credit | Up to $100 each account year, on hotel stays bought through Chase Travel |
| Fee left over if you use the whole credit | $0 |
| Fee left over if you never use it | $95 |

The credit posts by itself. The first $100 of those hotel purchases earns no points.

One catch. A hotel booked through Chase Travel is a third-party booking. Your trip has to include at least one hotel night you are happy to book that way. If your one trip is a week in a rented house or with family, the credit may go unused.

## What you earn the rest of the year

Points come from ordinary spending, not only from the trip.

| Spending | Points per dollar |
|---|---|
| Chase Travel bookings | 5 |
| Dining, gas stations, EV charging, selected vacation homes, selected streaming, online grocery | 3 |
| Other travel | 2 |
| Everything else | 1 |

Online grocery leaves out Walmart, Target and wholesale clubs. There is no foreign transaction fee, which matters if the trip is abroad.

## What the points are worth

Through Chase Travel a point is worth 1 cent as the base. On selected bookings Chase marks up the value, which it calls Points Boost. On this card that can reach 1.5 cents on some hotels and flights. Some sources also report 1.75 cents on premium-cabin airfare, and others say 1.5 cents is now the top; [the Points Boost page](/chase-points-boost-explained/) sets out the disagreement. Chase does not publish a fixed list, so you cannot plan around it.

You can also move points to 14 airline and hotel programs. United and Southwest transfer 1:1. Hyatt changed in 2026: from a Sapphire Preferred, 4 Chase points now become 3 Hyatt points. Older articles that call Hyatt a 1:1 partner for this card are out of date.

## The welcome offer

The public offer on Chase's page today is 75,000 points after $5,000 in purchases in the first 3 months. At the 1-cent base that is $750 of travel through Chase Travel. Moved to Hyatt at 4:3 it becomes 56,250 Hyatt points.

Welcome offers change and can differ by person and by link. Treat the number as today's, not a promise.

$5,000 in 3 months is a real hurdle. If that is more than you normally spend, the bonus is not a reason to get the card.

## The protection a single big trip needs

This is the quiet reason the card suits a once-a-year traveler. When the trip is paid with the card, Chase lists:

- Trip cancellation or interruption: up to $10,000 per traveler, $20,000 per trip.
- Trip delay: up to $500 per traveler after more than 12 hours or an overnight stay.
- Rental car: primary cover up to $60,000 for theft and collision.
- Delayed bags: up to $100 a day for 5 days. Lost bags: up to $3,000 per traveler.

Restrictions apply, and the full terms are in Chase's benefits guide.

## Who should skip it

- People who carry a balance. Interest will cost more than any points return.
- People who have opened five or more personal cards in the past 24 months. Chase generally declines them under its unofficial "5/24" practice.
- People who already earned this card's bonus. Chase now gives the bonus once per person per Sapphire card.
- People who want lounge access. This card has none.
- People who want plain cash back and will not book through Chase Travel or learn transfers.

## Quick answers

**Does one trip a year cover the $95 fee?**
It can. One Chase Travel hotel stay of $100 or more returns up to $100 in statement credit each account year.

**Can I still move points to Hyatt at 1:1?**
Not from this card. Since 2026 the Sapphire Preferred rate is 4:3. The Sapphire Reserve keeps 1:1.

**Can I get the bonus if I had the card years ago?**
Only if you never earned the bonus on it. The old 48-month wait no longer exists. Chase shows a notice before the credit check if you will not get it.

## Sources

- [Chase: Sapphire Preferred card page](https://creditcards.chase.com/rewards-credit-cards/sapphire/preferred)
- [The Points Guy: Chase Sapphire Preferred review](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/chase-sapphire-preferred-review)
- [One Mile at a Time: Sapphire Preferred review and 2026 changes](https://onemileatatime.com/chase-sapphire-card-limited-time-perks/)
- [AwardWallet: Chase to Hyatt transfer ratios](https://awardwallet.com/credit-cards/chase-ultimate-rewards/chase-to-hyatt-transfer/)
- [NerdWallet: Sapphire Preferred and Points Boost](https://www.nerdwallet.com/article/credit-cards/chase-sapphire-preferred-rolls-out-points-boost-hikes-bonus)
- [The Points Guy: Chase's 5/24 rule](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/chase/ultimate-guide-chase-5-24-rule/)
- [The Points Guy: Sapphire bonus eligibility changes 2026](https://thepointsguy.com/news/chase-sapphire-bonus-eligibility-changes-2026)

# How do purchase protection and extended warranty work on the Chase Sapphire Preferred?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/chase-sapphire-preferred-purchase-protection-extended-warranty/
Facts checked: 2026-11-21
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

Purchase protection on the Sapphire Preferred covers a new item against theft or damage for 120 days from purchase, up to $500 per item and $50,000 per account. Extended warranty adds one year to a manufacturer's warranty of three years or less, up to $10,000 per item and $50,000 per account.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## The two benefits side by side

| | Purchase protection | Extended warranty |
|---|---|---|
| What it covers | Theft of, or accidental damage to, a new item | A failure the original warranty would have covered |
| Time window | 120 days from the purchase date | One extra year after the warranty ends, up to four years from purchase |
| Limit per item or claim | $500 | $10,000 |
| Limit per account | $50,000 | $50,000 |

The item has to be paid for with the card or its points. The extended warranty figures come from Chase's own guide. The purchase protection figures come from Upgraded Points (updated October 6, 2026) and The Points Guy (June 23, 2026), which agree on 120 days and $500. Chase's Guide to Benefits governs. It was not read directly for this page.

## What purchase protection pays

The benefit administrator chooses to repair the item, replace it or pay you back. The payment is capped at what you charged or at $500, whichever is lower. A $1,200 laptop stolen in month two would bring $500 at most.

Upgraded Points lists these exclusions: used items, antiques and collectibles; vehicles; computer software; medical equipment; perishables; cash, gift cards and tickets; items bought for resale or commercial use; items that "mysteriously disappear"; items in the hands of a shipper or airline; jewelry and watches in checked baggage; and items never delivered. The Points Guy also names animals.

## What extended warranty pays

Chase's guide says the benefit adds one year to a United States manufacturer's warranty of three years or less. Cover ends four years after the purchase date.

The payment is the lowest of the repair cost, the replacement cost or the amount charged, up to $10,000 per item.

Chase's guide excludes motorized vehicles and their parts, items bought for resale or for professional or commercial use, rented or leased items, computer software, medical equipment, and used or pre-owned items.

## How to claim

1. Report the loss or failure to the benefit administrator within 90 days. Upgraded Points gives the phone number as 888-320-9656.
2. For theft, file a police report. Upgraded Points says within 48 hours.
3. Return the claim form and papers within 120 days.

Chase and Upgraded Points name these papers: the card statement, the itemized store receipt, proof of any other payment method, the original warranty for a warranty claim, a repair estimate or paid repair bill, and a police, fire or insurance report for theft or damage.

## Where sources disagree

- **Lost items.** The Points Guy says the cover applies to items that are lost, damaged or stolen. Upgraded Points says theft and accidental damage, and lists items that mysteriously disappear as excluded. Do not count on cover for an item you misplaced.
- **Warranty length.** Chase says warranties of three years or less qualify. Upgraded Points says under three years.

Not confirmed: whether a gift is covered for the person who receives it, whether the benefit pays only after other insurance, and any yearly cap beyond the $50,000 per account.

## How the Reserve differs

| | Sapphire Preferred | Sapphire Reserve |
|---|---|---|
| Annual fee | $95 | $795 |
| Purchase protection per item | $500 | $10,000 |
| Extended warranty | Same | Same |
| Return protection | Not listed | 90 days, $500 per item, $1,000 per 12 months |

The Reserve figures are from Chase's guide. The fee comparison is on the [Preferred against Reserve page](/sapphire-preferred-vs-reserve-light-traveler/). Trip cover is on the [travel insurance page](/chase-sapphire-preferred-travel-insurance/).

## Who should skip relying on it

- Anyone buying items well over $500, such as a high-end phone or laptop. Most of the loss stays with you.
- Anyone buying used or refurbished goods.
- Anyone who does not keep receipts and warranty papers.

## Quick answers

**Does Sapphire Preferred purchase protection cover a cracked phone screen?**
Accidental damage in the first 120 days is covered, up to $500 per item. After 120 days it is not.

**Does the extended warranty apply to a five-year warranty?**
No. Chase's guide limits it to warranties of three years or less.

**Is there a fee or sign-up for either benefit?**
No sign-up is named in any source read. The item has to be paid for with the card or its points.

## Sources

- [Chase: extended warranty protection with Chase Sapphire](https://www.chase.com/personal/credit-cards/education/basics/extended-warranty-protection-with-chase-sapphire)
- [Upgraded Points: Chase purchase protection benefits](https://upgradedpoints.com/credit-cards/chase-price-and-purchase-protection-benefits/)
- [The Points Guy: lesser-known Sapphire Preferred benefits](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/chase-sapphire-preferred-lesser-known-benefits-2026/)
- [Chase: Sapphire Preferred card page](https://creditcards.chase.com/rewards-credit-cards/sapphire/preferred)
- [Chase: Sapphire Reserve card page](https://creditcards.chase.com/rewards-credit-cards/sapphire/reserve)

# How does a Chase Sapphire refer-a-friend link work for the person applying?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/chase-sapphire-preferred-referral-bonus-how-it-works/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

A Chase Sapphire refer-a-friend link is a personal link from a cardholder that opens a standard Chase application showing a stated welcome bonus. You get that bonus if you are approved, are eligible for it and meet its spending requirement, and the cardholder who shared the link earns points from Chase.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## What happens, step by step

1. A Sapphire cardholder gets a personal link from Chase and shares it.
2. You open it. The page states the welcome bonus and its spending requirement.
3. You apply. Chase runs its normal credit check.
4. If approved, you earn the bonus by meeting the spending requirement in the stated time.
5. The cardholder who referred you earns points from Chase once you are approved.

Since May 2026 a cardholder with either Sapphire card can refer a friend to the Sapphire Preferred or the Sapphire Reserve, according to Upgraded Points. Before that, a link covered only the referrer's own card.

## What the offer was on November 20, 2026

| Route | Sapphire Preferred bonus stated | Spending requirement | Annual fee |
|---|---|---|---|
| Referral page | 75,000 points | $5,000 in the first 3 months | $95 |
| Chase public page | 75,000 points | $5,000 in the first 3 months | $95 |

The two matched on that date. That is a snapshot and not a promise: Chase's own page says "Offers may vary depending on where you apply," for example online or in a branch, and can change over time. Read the figure on the page you apply from. More on the differences: [referral against public and in-branch offers](/chase-sapphire-referral-vs-public-offer/).

Unlike Amex, Chase states one figure on the page for every applicant.

## Rules that still apply to you

A referral link changes where you start the application. No source read says it changes Chase's rules, and Chase's eligibility wording is general.

| Rule | What it means |
|---|---|
| Already have the card | Chase says the card is unavailable if you currently have it open |
| Had the card or its bonus before | The bonus may not be available. Each Sapphire card's bonus is once per lifetime |
| 5/24 | Five or more personal cards opened in 24 months, at any bank, generally means a denial |
| Credit check | Applying adds a hard inquiry whether or not you are approved |
| Spending requirement | No bonus unless you meet it in time |

Details: [Sapphire bonus eligibility](/chase-sapphire-bonus-eligibility-2026/), [the 5/24 rule](/chase-5-24-rule-explained/), [what counts toward the spending requirement](/chase-sapphire-welcome-bonus-spending-requirement/) and [what an application does to your credit score](/does-applying-for-a-travel-card-hurt-credit-score/).

Chase now shows a notice during the application if you would be approved without the bonus. The Points Guy reports you can cancel at that point.

## What the person who referred you gets

The cardholder earns bonus points from Chase for each friend approved through their link, up to a yearly cap. Sources differ on the per-friend figure, and Chase's own referral page sits behind a sign-in, so the current amount is not confirmed here.

The person sharing the link has a reason to want you to use it. You pay nothing extra, and your bonus is not reduced by theirs.

Referral points are generally treated as taxable income for the person who receives them. See [whether card bonuses are taxable](/are-credit-card-welcome-bonuses-taxable/).

## What a referral link does not do

- It does not raise your approval odds.
- It does not waive the $95 annual fee.
- It does not always carry the highest offer available that day. In mid-2026 referral links showed a higher bonus than the public page for about a week; in 2021 they showed a lower one for several weeks, as reported by Doctor of Credit and Frequent Miler.

## Who should skip it

- Anyone who has earned the bonus on the same Sapphire card before.
- Anyone at or over 5/24.
- Anyone who would need to spend more than usual to reach $5,000 in three months, or who would carry a balance to do it.
- Anyone about to apply for a mortgage or car loan, where a new inquiry and account can matter.

For whether the card itself fits, see [Sapphire Preferred on one trip a year](/chase-sapphire-preferred-one-trip-a-year/).

## Quick answers

**Is the bonus through a Sapphire referral link the same as on Chase's website?**
On November 20, 2026 both showed 75,000 points after $5,000 in three months. They have differed at times, so compare on the day.

**Does using a referral link cost me anything?**
No. The cardholder's points come from Chase, not from your bonus.

**Can I use a referral link if I had a Sapphire card before?**
You can apply, but the bonus may not be available if you held that card or earned its bonus before.

## Sources

- [Chase: Sapphire Preferred card page](https://creditcards.chase.com/rewards-credit-cards/sapphire/preferred)
- [Upgraded Points: Chase expands Sapphire referrals](https://upgradedpoints.com/news/chase-expands-sapphire-card-referral-program/)
- [The Points Guy: Sapphire Preferred referral](https://thepointsguy.com/news/chase-sapphire-preferred-referral)
- [Upgraded Points: Sapphire referral limit](https://upgradedpoints.com/news/chase-increases-sapphire-annual-referral-bonus-limit/)
- [Doctor of Credit: Sapphire Preferred 100,000-point offer timeline](https://doctorofcredit.com/chase-sapphire-preferred-100000-points-offer)
- [Frequent Miler: referral links with lower offers (2021)](https://frequentmiler.com/friends-dont-let-friends-get-inferior-offers/)
- [The Points Guy: the Sapphire bonus eligibility pop-up](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/chase-sapphire-preferred-lifetime-bonus-popup/)

# Does the Chase Sapphire Preferred cover a rental car, and what does primary coverage leave out?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/chase-sapphire-preferred-rental-car-insurance/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

Yes. The Sapphire Preferred gives primary cover for theft of, or damage to, the rental car itself, up to $60,000, when you pay for the whole rental with the card and decline the rental company's collision damage waiver. It leaves out liability for other people and property, injuries, your belongings and several kinds of vehicle.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## What "primary" means

Primary cover pays first. You do not have to claim on your own auto policy before the card's benefit pays, so a claim need not touch your insurer. Secondary cover pays only what your own insurer does not.

One exception: for New York residents renting inside the United States, the cover is secondary to personal auto insurance.

## What it pays for

Chase's own guide lists these costs, capped at the car's actual cash value:

- Theft of the rental car
- Damage to the rental car
- Valid loss-of-use charges from the rental company
- Administrative fees
- Reasonable towing after a covered theft or damage

## The conditions

| Condition | Detail |
|---|---|
| Payment | The full rental is charged to the card. Chase points can be used toward it. |
| Waiver | Decline the rental company's collision damage waiver. Accepting it cancels the card benefit. |
| Driver | The cardmember is the primary driver on the rental agreement. |
| Length | Fewer than 31 consecutive days. |
| Vehicle value | List price of $125,000 or less, per Chase's card page. |
| Place | The United States and some countries abroad. |

A rental booked through Chase Travel with points keeps the cover, according to AwardWallet.

## What primary coverage leaves out

**Liability.** The benefit covers the car you rented. It does not pay for damage to another car or to property, and it does not pay for anyone's injuries. Upgraded Points lists liability as an exclusion. Check whether your own auto policy extends liability to a rental, especially abroad.

**Your belongings.** Valuables left in the car and lost or damaged are excluded.

**Some vehicles and rentals.** Chase's guide excludes:

- Expensive and exotic vehicles
- Vehicles more than 10 years old
- Motorcycles, mopeds and electric scooters
- Rented moving trucks and vans
- Large passenger vans
- Peer-to-peer rentals such as Turo
- Hourly rentals

**Some driving.** Driving off-road can void the cover.

## Where sources disagree

- **Van size.** Chase's guide excludes vans with more than nine passengers. Upgraded Points, summarizing the Guide to Benefits, says passenger vans that seat more than 12. If you plan to rent a van for a group, confirm with the benefit administrator first.
- **Countries.** Chase says the cover applies in the United States and "some countries abroad" and tells travelers to confirm the destination before leaving. Third-party guides say most countries. The list of countries is not confirmed on any page read for this article.

Chase's Guide to Benefits governs. It was not read directly for this page.

## If something happens

Chase's guide names these papers for a claim:

- A copy of the rental agreement
- A card statement showing the rental was paid in full with the card or points
- A repair estimate, an accident report form and photographs
- A police report for vandalism or carjacking

The claim deadline for this benefit is not confirmed. AwardWallet reports 20 days to give notice and 90 days to send documents for Chase's travel benefits in general, so report a loss right away.

## The sums

If you would otherwise buy the rental company's waiver, the saving is that daily price times your rental days, set against the card's $95 annual fee. The saving is zero if you would decline the waiver anyway and rely on your own policy, though primary cover still keeps a claim off that policy.

The other trip protections on the card are on the [travel insurance page](/chase-sapphire-preferred-travel-insurance/).

## Who should skip relying on it

- Anyone with no liability cover for the trip. The card does not supply it.
- Anyone renting for 31 days or more.
- Anyone renting through a car-sharing service, by the hour, or renting a moving truck.
- Anyone renting a luxury or exotic car, or a large van.
- New York residents with personal auto insurance who want primary cover inside the United States.
- Anyone who cannot put the whole rental on the card.

## Quick answers

**Does the Sapphire Preferred cover liability in a rental car?**
No. It covers theft of and damage to the rental car itself. Damage to other cars or property and injuries are outside the benefit.

**Do I need to decline the rental company's insurance?**
You need to decline its collision damage waiver, because accepting it cancels the card's cover. Liability insurance is a separate product and a separate decision.

**Does it cover Turo?**
No. Chase's guide excludes peer-to-peer rentals, and Upgraded Points names Turo as excluded.

## Sources

- [Chase: how Sapphire rental car insurance works](https://www.chase.com/personal/credit-cards/education/basics/chase-sapphire-rental-car-insurance-guide)
- [Chase: Sapphire Preferred card page](https://creditcards.chase.com/rewards-credit-cards/sapphire/preferred)
- [Upgraded Points: Sapphire Preferred travel insurance benefits](https://upgradedpoints.com/credit-cards/reviews/chase-sapphire-preferred-card/travel-insurance-benefits)
- [AwardWallet: Chase Sapphire travel insurance](https://awardwallet.com/credit-cards/chase-ultimate-rewards/chase-sapphire-travel-insurance/)
- [AwardWallet: using Chase points near the Disney parks](https://awardwallet.com/blog/how-to-use-ultimate-rewards-points-for-a-disney-world-resort)

# What travel insurance comes with the Sapphire Preferred, and what does it not cover?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/chase-sapphire-preferred-travel-insurance/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

The Sapphire Preferred includes trip cancellation and interruption cover, trip delay, baggage delay, lost luggage and primary rental car damage cover when you pay for the trip with the card. It does not pay medical bills abroad, it does not cover pre-existing conditions, and it does not pay out if you simply decide not to go.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## What is included

| Protection | Limit | When it applies |
|---|---|---|
| Trip cancellation and interruption | Up to $10,000 per traveler, $20,000 per trip, $40,000 per 12 months | Prepaid, non-refundable costs lost for a listed reason |
| Trip delay | Up to $500 per traveler | Delay of more than 12 hours, or an overnight stay |
| Baggage delay | Up to $100 a day for 5 days | Bags more than 6 hours late |
| Lost luggage | Up to $3,000 per traveler | Lost or damaged by the carrier; pays after the carrier does |
| Rental car collision damage | Up to $60,000 | Theft or collision damage to the rental car |
| Travel accident | Up to $500,000 on a common carrier | Accidental death or dismemberment |
| Emergency evacuation | Up to $100,000 | Trips of 5 to 60 days, more than 100 miles from home, arranged in advance by the administrator |

The first six limits are on Chase's card page. The 12-month cap, the evacuation conditions and the exclusions below come from Upgraded Points and AwardWallet summaries of Chase's Guide to Benefits, which governs and was not read directly for this page.

Some or all of the trip must be charged to the card or paid with Chase points. Cover extends to the cardholder and immediate family.

## Trip cancellation: the listed reasons

This cover pays only for reasons on Chase's list. Reported examples:

- Injury, illness or death of you, a traveling companion or an immediate family member
- Severe weather or a named storm
- Jury duty or a subpoena
- Your home or lodging becoming uninhabitable
- A quarantine ordered by a physician

## What it does not cover

| Not covered | Detail |
|---|---|
| Change of plans | Deciding not to go, money trouble, or work obligations are not listed reasons |
| Pre-existing conditions | Any condition with advice, diagnosis or treatment in the 60 days before your first trip payment |
| Medical bills abroad | No emergency medical expense benefit is listed for this card |
| Long trips | Trips over 60 days |
| Late pregnancy | Travel after 26 weeks |
| A travel company going out of business | Excluded |
| Standalone tickets | Theme park, museum or golf bookings that are not part of a travel package |

The medical gap matters most. The evacuation benefit moves you to care; it does not pay for the care.

## Trip delay details

The delay has to come from a covered cause: equipment failure, weather, a strike or a hijacking. It pays for meals, lodging, toiletries and medication that the carrier does not cover. Keep receipts.

## Rental car cover

"Primary" means you claim on the card first, not on your own auto insurer. Pay for the whole rental with the card and decline the rental company's collision damage waiver.

Limits to know:

- Rentals of 31 consecutive days or fewer.
- Most vehicles with a list price of $125,000 or less. Excluded: antique cars, cargo vans, trucks other than pickups, motorcycles, limousines, RVs, and passenger vans that seat more than 12.
- Car-sharing such as Turo is excluded, according to Upgraded Points.
- **Liability is not covered.** Damage to other cars or property and injuries to anyone are outside this benefit. So are your belongings in the car.
- For New York residents, cover inside the United States is secondary to personal auto insurance.

## Who should skip relying on it

- Anyone traveling abroad without other medical cover.
- Anyone with a health condition treated in the past 60 days that could affect the trip.
- Anyone who wants to be able to cancel for any reason.
- Anyone on a trip longer than 60 days, or renting a car for more than 31 days.
- Anyone whose trip costs well over $10,000 per person.

In these cases a separate travel insurance policy is the usual answer. The card's cover is a base for an ordinary [one-trip-a-year traveler](/chase-sapphire-preferred-one-trip-a-year/), not a full policy.

## Quick answers

**Does the Sapphire Preferred cover medical bills overseas?**
No emergency medical benefit is listed for this card. It includes emergency evacuation with conditions, not treatment costs.

**Is the rental car cover primary?**
Yes, for theft and collision damage up to $60,000, except for New York residents renting inside the United States. Liability is not included.

**Do I have to pay for the whole trip with the card?**
For trip cancellation, some or all of the trip must be on the card or paid with Chase points. For the rental car cover, pay for the whole rental with the card.

## Sources

- [Chase: Sapphire Preferred card page](https://creditcards.chase.com/rewards-credit-cards/sapphire/preferred)
- [Upgraded Points: Sapphire Preferred travel insurance benefits](https://upgradedpoints.com/credit-cards/reviews/chase-sapphire-preferred-card/travel-insurance-benefits)
- [AwardWallet: Chase Sapphire travel insurance](https://awardwallet.com/credit-cards/chase-ultimate-rewards/chase-sapphire-travel-insurance/)

# Chase Sapphire Preferred or Amex Green: which mid-fee travel card fits?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/chase-sapphire-preferred-vs-amex-green/
Facts checked: 2026-11-21
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

For a new applicant the choice is made already: Amex stopped taking applications for the Green Card in July 2026, and the $95 Sapphire Preferred is open. The Green Card, now named the Classic Green Card, still exists at $150 for current holders and as a downgrade from an Amex Gold or Platinum card, and it earns more on travel booked direct.

This page is information, not financial advice. Terms change, so check each issuer's pages before deciding.

## What happened to the Green Card

- Amex told cardholders in June 2026 that the card would be renamed the Classic Green Card on August 20, 2026, according to a U.S. News report.
- The application page came off Amex's site in late July 2026. An earlier fact check on this site recorded July 23, from Upgraded Points.
- Upgraded Points, updated October 28, 2026, says the card is closed to new applicants and can be reached only by product change from a Gold or Platinum card.
- Amex has not said what replaces it. Reports of a new Green card with a fee of $195 to $250 are rumor and not confirmed. No launch was found as of November 21, 2026.

## Side by side

| | Chase Sapphire Preferred | Amex Classic Green |
|---|---|---|
| Open to new applicants | Yes | No; product change only |
| Annual fee | $95 | $150 |
| Main credit | Up to $100 each account year on Chase Travel hotel stays | Up to $219 a calendar year for CLEAR+ |
| Travel booked direct | 2x | 3x |
| Transit (trains, rideshare, tolls, parking) | Not confirmed | 3x |
| Travel through the issuer's portal | 5x on Chase Travel | 3x, as travel |
| Dining | 3x | 3x worldwide |
| Gas, streaming, online grocery | 3x | No bonus listed |
| Everything else | 1x | Not confirmed in the pages read |
| Lounge access | None | None |
| Rental car cover | Primary | One Mile at a Time says the card has none |
| Trip delay | Up to $500 per traveler after 12 hours | Up to $300 per trip after 12 hours |
| Trip cancellation | Up to $10,000 per traveler | Not confirmed |
| Transfer partners | 16 programs: United, Southwest, Hyatt (at 4:3) and others | About 16 airlines, Delta included; Hilton, Marriott, Choice |
| Foreign transaction fee | None | None |

## The fee sum

- **Preferred:** $95. One hotel stay of $100 or more booked through Chase Travel returns $100, which puts the card at minus $5 for the year.
- **Classic Green:** $150. CLEAR+ costs $219 a year, and the credit covers it. For a reader who would pay for CLEAR+ anyway, $150 minus $219 is minus $69. For a reader who would not, the credit is worth nothing and the fee stays $150.

The gap between the fees is $55.

## The points sum

Take $5,000 a year of flights and hotels booked direct, and $4,000 of dining.

| | Sapphire Preferred | Classic Green |
|---|---|---|
| Travel booked direct, $5,000 | 10,000 points | 15,000 points |
| Dining, $4,000 | 12,000 points | 12,000 points |
| Total | 22,000 points | 27,000 points |

The Green earns 5,000 more points on that pattern. If the same travel were booked through Chase Travel, the Preferred would earn 25,000 on it and come out ahead. Add $3,000 of gas and streaming, and the Preferred earns 9,000 points on spending where no Green bonus is listed.

The Points Guy valued an Amex point at 2.0 cents and a Chase point at 2.05 cents in November 2026, so the two are close; the page on [Amex points against Chase points](/amex-points-vs-chase-points-which-are-worth-more/) explains where they differ.

## Which pattern favors which card

- **New to both issuers:** Preferred. It is the one that can be applied for.
- **Holds an Amex Platinum or Gold and wants a lower fee:** Classic Green is one way down. It keeps Membership Rewards points alive at $150 a year. See [Platinum downgrade options](/amex-platinum-downgrade-or-cancel-options/).
- **Pays for CLEAR+ and books travel direct:** Classic Green. The credit covers the fee and travel earns 3x.
- **Rents cars or wants trip cancellation cover:** Preferred. Its [rental car insurance](/chase-sapphire-preferred-rental-car-insurance/) is primary.
- **Wants Hyatt, United or Southwest:** Preferred. Amex points do not move to those programs.
- **Wants Delta:** Classic Green. Chase points do not move to Delta.

A reader weighing an Amex card against the Preferred who cannot get the Green may want the [Amex Gold comparison](/amex-gold-vs-chase-sapphire-preferred/) instead.

## Who should skip it

- Skip the Classic Green if you do not use CLEAR+. Without that credit it costs $55 more than the Preferred and has thinner travel cover.
- Skip waiting for a new Green card as a plan. Its terms and date are not confirmed.
- Skip the Preferred if most of your travel spending is booked direct and you want Amex partners such as Delta.
- Skip both if you carry a balance. Interest costs more than either card returns.

Welcome offers vary by applicant and change. A product change to the Classic Green generally does not come with a welcome offer.

## Quick answers

**Can you still apply for the Amex Green Card?**
No. Applications closed in July 2026. It is available only by product change from an Amex Gold or Platinum card, according to Upgraded Points.

**What is the Amex Green Card's annual fee now?**
$150, under the name Classic Green Card. A higher fee on a future replacement is rumor only.

**Which card earns more on travel?**
The Classic Green earns 3x on travel booked direct against the Preferred's 2x. The Preferred earns 5x through Chase Travel.

# Chase Sapphire Preferred or a Bilt card for a renter?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/chase-sapphire-preferred-vs-bilt/
Facts checked: 2026-11-21
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

A renter who would put most everyday spending on the card earns more with a Bilt card, because rent itself earns up to 1.25 points per dollar. A renter who spends little on the card, or who wants strong trip and rental car cover, is closer to the Sapphire Preferred, since Bilt's rent points shrink to 250 a month when other spending is low.

This page is information, not financial advice. Terms change, so check each issuer's pages before deciding.

## What a Bilt card is now

The Wells Fargo Bilt Mastercard ended on February 6, 2026. Three cards replaced it the next day, serviced by Cardless and issued by Column N.A.: Bilt Blue ($0), Bilt Obsidian ($95) and Bilt Palladium ($495). A person can be the primary holder of one Bilt card.

## Side by side

| | Chase Sapphire Preferred | Bilt Blue | Bilt Obsidian |
|---|---|---|---|
| Annual fee | $95 | $0 | $95 |
| Rent or mortgage | No reward | Up to 1.25x | Up to 1.25x |
| Dining | 3x | 1x | 3x on dining or groceries, one chosen for the year |
| Travel | 2x; 5x through Chase Travel | 1x | 2x |
| Everything else | 1x; 3x on gas, streaming, online grocery | 1x | 1x |
| Main credit | Up to $100 a year on Chase Travel hotels | None | Up to $100 a year on Bilt Travel hotels, $50 each half-year, two-night stays |
| Lounge access | None | None | None |
| Transfer partners | 16 programs: United, Southwest, Hyatt at 4:3 | 18 airlines and 7 hotel programs: United, Southwest, Alaska's Atmos Rewards, Hyatt at 1:1 until December 31, 2026 | Same as Blue |
| Foreign transaction fee | None | None | None |

The $495 Palladium earns 2x on everyday purchases and adds Priority Pass, a $400 hotel credit and $200 of Bilt Cash a year. From January 15, 2027 Bilt replaces those two with $600 of Bilt Cash, and the Obsidian's hotel credit becomes $100 of Bilt Cash.

## How rent earns points

Bilt gives two options, and a cardholder can switch between them month to month.

**Housing-only.** The rate on rent depends on other card spending that month, as a share of the rent:

| Other spending as a share of rent | Points per dollar of rent |
|---|---|
| Under 25% | 250 points flat |
| 25% | 0.5 |
| 50% | 0.75 |
| 75% | 1 |
| 100% or more | 1.25 |

**Bilt Cash.** Everyday purchases earn 4% in Bilt Cash on top of points. Each $30 of Bilt Cash turns into 1,000 points on rent, up to 1 point per dollar. Bilt Cash now expires 12 months after it is earned.

Sources disagree on a fee. AwardWallet's January 2026 guide says a cardholder short on Bilt Cash can pay a 3% fee to earn the full rate. The Points Guy's Obsidian review says neither option carries a transaction fee.

Cards opened from January 1, 2027 get the housing-only option alone. Anyone with a card opened by December 31, 2026 can keep the Bilt Cash option by opting out before the card anniversary.

## The sum for a renter

Take rent of $2,000 a month and $1,500 a month of other spending, $500 of it on dining. That is 75% of rent, so rent earns 1x under housing-only.

| Per year | Sapphire Preferred | Bilt Blue | Bilt Obsidian |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rent, $24,000 | 0 | 24,000 | 24,000 |
| Dining, $6,000 | 18,000 | 6,000 | 18,000 |
| Other, $12,000 | 12,000 | 12,000 | 12,000 |
| Total points | 30,000 | 42,000 | 54,000 |
| Annual fee | $95 | $0 | $95 |

Now cut the other spending to $400 a month, 20% of rent. Rent earns 250 points a month, 3,000 a year, and the Bilt advantage mostly disappears.

The Preferred figures leave out gas, streaming and Chase Travel bonuses, which would raise its total for a reader with that spending.

## Which pattern favors which card

- **Card spending near or above the rent each month:** a Bilt card. Rent earns 1 to 1.25 points per dollar, on a $0 card if wanted.
- **Card spending under a quarter of the rent:** the Preferred, or no change. Bilt pays 250 points a month at that level.
- **Wants Hyatt at 1:1:** Bilt, but only through December 31, 2026. From January 1, 2027 Bilt moves to 4:3, the same as the Preferred.
- **Wants Alaska or Hawaiian miles:** Bilt. Chase has no Atmos Rewards transfer.
- **Wants trip cancellation cover of up to $10,000 per traveler and primary rental car cover:** the Preferred. See its [travel insurance](/chase-sapphire-preferred-travel-insurance/). The Bilt pages read list trip delay cover on the Obsidian and rental cover on the Blue without amounts.
- **Does not want to track tiers, Bilt Cash and yearly rule changes:** the Preferred. Its rates do not depend on a monthly ratio.

## Who should skip it

- Skip a Bilt card for rent points if you would not move your everyday spending to it.
- Skip the Bilt Cash option if a 12-month expiry on credits would catch you out.
- Skip the Preferred if rent is your largest bill and you want it to earn. The Preferred has no rent reward.
- Skip both if you carry a balance. Interest costs more than either card returns.

Welcome offers vary by applicant and change, so they are left out of the sums.

## Quick answers

**Does the Sapphire Preferred earn points on rent?**
It has no rent reward. Whether a landlord takes cards, and at what fee, depends on the landlord.

**Is there still a no-annual-fee Bilt card?**
Yes. The Bilt Blue has no annual fee and earns up to 1.25 points per dollar on rent, depending on other spending.

**Do Bilt points transfer to Hyatt at 1:1?**
Yes until December 31, 2026. The Points Guy reports the rate drops to 4:3 on January 1, 2027.

- [The Points Guy: Bilt tiers for rent and mortgage points](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/bilt-2-0-new-tiers-points-rent-mortgage)
- [The Points Guy: Bilt Obsidian review](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/reviews/bilt-obsidian-card-review/)

- [AwardWallet: Chase to Hyatt transfers](https://awardwallet.com/credit-cards/chase-ultimate-rewards/chase-to-hyatt-transfer/)

# Chase Sapphire Preferred or Capital One Venture: which fits a few trips a year?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/chase-sapphire-preferred-vs-capital-one-venture/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

Both cards cost $95 a year, so the choice comes down to where the money goes. The Venture earns more for someone whose spending is mostly general purchases, and the Sapphire Preferred earns more for someone whose dining and similar spending is larger than everything else, and it has stronger trip protection.

This page is information, not financial advice. Terms change, so check each issuer's pages before deciding.

## Side by side

| | Sapphire Preferred | Capital One Venture |
|---|---|---|
| Annual fee | $95 | $95 |
| Yearly credit | Up to $100 on hotels booked through Chase Travel | None |
| Portal bookings | 5x on Chase Travel | 5x on hotels, vacation rentals and rental cars in Capital One Travel |
| Dining | 3x | 2x |
| Gas, EV charging, selected streaming, online grocery | 3x | 2x |
| Flights and hotels booked direct | 2x | 2x |
| Everything else | 1x | 2x |
| Global Entry or TSA PreCheck credit | Up to $120 every four years | Up to $120 |
| Airport lounges | None | None |
| Foreign transaction fee | None | None |
| Simple travel redemption | 1 cent a point in Chase Travel, more on Points Boost fares | 1 cent a mile against any travel purchase from the past 90 days |
| Transfer partners | 14, including United, Southwest and Hyatt | 15+, including Flying Blue, Air Canada and Wyndham; JetBlue is the only US airline |

Hyatt transfers from the Preferred are now 4 Chase points to 3 Hyatt points. The other Chase partners are 1 to 1. Most Capital One partners are 1 to 1, with JetBlue at 5 to 3.

## The plain sum

Call dining and the other 3x categories D, direct travel T, and everything else O.

- Preferred: 3 points on D, 2 on T, 1 on O.
- Venture: 2 miles on all three.

Travel booked direct is a tie. The Preferred gains 1 point per dollar on D and loses 1 per dollar on O. So the Preferred earns more only when D is larger than O.

| Yearly spending | Preferred | Venture |
|---|---|---|
| $5,000 dining and gas, $3,000 travel, $16,000 other | 37,000 points | 48,000 miles |
| $10,000 dining and gas, $3,000 travel, $11,000 other | 47,000 points | 48,000 miles |
| $13,000 dining and gas, $3,000 travel, $8,000 other | 53,000 points | 48,000 miles |

A reader whose general spending is larger than restaurants, gas, streaming and online grocery together earns more with the Venture. Add up last year's statements to see which side is bigger.

## What the Preferred adds back

- **The hotel credit.** Up to $100 a year on a hotel booked through Chase Travel. A reader who would book one hotel night that way gets the fee back.
- **Trip protection.** Trip cancellation and interruption up to $10,000 per traveler, trip delay up to $500 after 12 hours, and primary rental car cover. The page on [Sapphire Preferred travel insurance](/chase-sapphire-preferred-travel-insurance/) has the limits and exclusions. The Venture reviews read list travel accident insurance and lost luggage cover, and no trip cancellation or delay cover.
- **United, Southwest and Hyatt.** Capital One miles cannot go to any of the three.

## What the Venture adds back

- **Redemption without a portal.** Buy any flight, hotel or rental anywhere, then use miles to wipe the charge at 1 cent each within 90 days.
- **One rate to remember.** 2x on everything means no tracking of categories.
- **Hertz Five Star status**, with enrollment.

## Which pattern favors which card

- **Two or three trips, booked wherever is cheapest, most spending on general purchases:** Venture.
- **Eats out often, drives a lot, or flies United or Southwest:** Sapphire Preferred.
- **Rents cars or books costly nonrefundable trips:** Sapphire Preferred, for the cover.
- **Wants the least effort:** Venture.

## Who should skip both

- Anyone who carries a balance month to month.
- Anyone who wants cash, not travel. Venture miles are worth about half a cent as cash, and Chase points 1 cent.
- For the Preferred: anyone who has opened five or more personal cards in 24 months. See [Chase's 5/24 rule](/chase-5-24-rule-explained/).

Welcome offers on both cards vary and change. Both issuers also limit repeat bonuses, so read the offer terms.

## Quick answers

**Which card earns more on groceries bought in a store?**
The Venture, at 2x. The Preferred gives 3x only on online grocery orders, and 1x in the store.

**Does either card include lounge access?**
No. Neither card has airport lounge access today.

**Is the Venture's rental car cover primary?**
Not confirmed in the sources read. The Sapphire Preferred's cover is primary.

## Sources

- [Chase: Sapphire Preferred card page](https://creditcards.chase.com/rewards-credit-cards/sapphire/preferred)
- [Capital One: Venture card page](https://www.capitalone.com/credit-cards/venture/)
- [The Points Guy: Capital One Venture review](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/capital-one-venture-card-review)
- [AwardWallet: Capital One Venture card](https://awardwallet.com/credit-cards/capital-one-rewards/venture-card)
- [The Points Guy: Capital One transfer partners](https://thepointsguy.com/loyalty-programs/capital-one-transfer-partners/)
- [The Points Guy: Chase Sapphire Preferred review](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/chase-sapphire-preferred-review)
- [AwardWallet: Chase to Hyatt transfer ratios](https://awardwallet.com/credit-cards/chase-ultimate-rewards/chase-to-hyatt-transfer/)

# Chase Sapphire Preferred or Citi Strata Premier: which $95-class card fits?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/chase-sapphire-preferred-vs-citi-strata-premier/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

Both cards cost $95 a year. The Citi Strata Premier earns more for someone with large supermarket and airfare spending, and the Sapphire Preferred fits someone who wants stronger trip protection or points that move to United, Southwest and Hyatt.

This page is information, not financial advice. Terms change, so check each issuer's pages before deciding.

## Side by side

| | Sapphire Preferred | Citi Strata Premier |
|---|---|---|
| Annual fee | $95 | $95 |
| Portal bookings | 5x on Chase Travel | 10x on hotels, car rentals and attractions in Citi Travel |
| Restaurants | 3x | 3x |
| Supermarkets, in store | 1x | 3x |
| Online grocery | 3x, not Walmart, Target or wholesale clubs | Not listed separately |
| Gas and EV charging | 3x | 3x |
| Flights booked direct | 2x | 3x |
| Hotels booked direct | 2x | 3x |
| Selected streaming | 3x | 1x |
| Everything else | 1x | 1x |
| Yearly hotel benefit | Up to $100 in credits on Chase Travel hotels | $100 off one Citi Travel hotel stay of $500 or more |
| Airport lounges | None | None |
| Foreign transaction fee | None | None |
| Trip cancellation cover | Up to $10,000 per traveler | Up to $5,000 per trip (one source) |
| Rental car cover | Primary | Secondary at home, primary abroad |
| US airline partners | United, Southwest, JetBlue | American, JetBlue |
| Hotel partners | Hyatt (4 points to 3), IHG, Marriott, Wyndham | Wyndham, Choice, Accor and others; no Hyatt |

The Strata Premier's hotel benefit comes off the price at booking, once per calendar year, and needs a $500 stay before taxes and fees. The Preferred's credit has no stated minimum and runs on the account anniversary year.

## The plain sum

The two cards tie on restaurants, gas and everything else. They differ in four places:

- **Supermarkets in store:** Strata Premier earns 2 more points per dollar.
- **Flights and hotels booked direct:** Strata Premier earns 1 more per dollar.
- **Streaming:** Sapphire Preferred earns 2 more per dollar.
- **Online grocery:** Sapphire Preferred earns 3x; Citi's 3x covers supermarkets and the sources read do not say how online orders are treated.

| Yearly spending | Preferred | Strata Premier |
|---|---|---|
| $6,000 supermarkets | 6,000 | 18,000 |
| $3,000 flights booked direct | 6,000 | 9,000 |
| $1,500 hotels booked direct | 3,000 | 4,500 |
| $4,000 restaurants | 12,000 | 12,000 |
| $600 streaming | 1,800 | 600 |
| $10,000 everything else | 10,000 | 10,000 |
| Total | 38,800 | 54,100 |

On that household the Strata Premier earns about 15,000 more points a year, nearly all of it from supermarkets. Take the supermarket line away and the gap falls to about 3,300.

## What a point can do

Points are only worth what they can be used for.

- **Chase:** 1 cent as cash or in Chase Travel, up to 1.5 cents on Points Boost bookings (some sources report 1.75). Partners include United, Southwest and Hyatt, which no Citi card reaches.
- **Citi:** 1 cent toward travel or gift cards. Partners include American Airlines at 1 to 1, which no Chase card reaches, plus Flying Blue, Turkish, Singapore, Virgin Atlantic and others.

A reader who flies American should weigh that partner heavily. A reader who stays at Hyatt or flies United or Southwest has the same reason to look at Chase.

## Trip protection

The Sapphire Preferred's cover is stronger on paper: trip cancellation up to $10,000 per traveler, trip delay up to $500 after 12 hours, and primary rental car cover in the US. Frequent Miler lists the Strata Premier at up to $5,000 per trip for cancellation, $500 for trip delay, and rental cover that is secondary in the US. Those Citi amounts come from one source. The [Sapphire Preferred travel insurance page](/chase-sapphire-preferred-travel-insurance/) has the Chase limits.

## Which pattern favors which card

- **Large in-store supermarket bill, flies American:** Citi Strata Premier.
- **Books airfare direct several times a year:** Citi Strata Premier, 3x against 2x.
- **Rents cars in the US, or books costly nonrefundable trips:** Sapphire Preferred.
- **Wants Hyatt, United or Southwest:** Sapphire Preferred.
- **Books hotel stays under $500 through a card portal:** Sapphire Preferred; Citi's $100 needs a $500 stay.

## Who should skip both

- Anyone who carries a balance month to month.
- Anyone who wants cash back with no points to manage.
- For the Preferred: anyone with five or more new personal cards in 24 months; see [Chase's 5/24 rule](/chase-5-24-rule-explained/).
- For the Strata Premier: anyone counting on a repeat welcome bonus. Sources disagree on Citi's rule. Upgraded Points describes a 48-month wait, while One Mile at a Time says it is now once in a lifetime. Read the offer terms.

Welcome offers on both cards vary and change, so they are not in these sums.

## Quick answers

**Which card earns more on groceries?**
The Strata Premier, 3x at supermarkets. The Sapphire Preferred earns 3x only on online grocery orders and 1x in store.

**Can either card transfer points to American Airlines?**
The Citi Strata Premier can, at 1 to 1. Chase has no American Airlines transfer.

**Is the $100 hotel benefit the same on both?**
No. Chase's is a statement credit on Chase Travel hotels. Citi's is $100 off one Citi Travel stay of $500 or more.

- [Upgraded Points: Citi Strata Premier review](https://upgradedpoints.com/credit-cards/reviews/citi-strata-premier-card/)
- [Frequent Miler: Citi Strata Premier review](https://frequentmiler.com/citi-strata-premier-credit-card-review/)

- [The Points Guy: Chase Points Boost](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/chase-points-boost)
