# Chase Sapphire Preferred or Freedom Unlimited: is the annual fee worth paying over the no-fee card?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/chase-sapphire-preferred-vs-freedom-unlimited/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

The $95 Sapphire Preferred is worth paying for if you will use its $100 hotel credit, spend abroad, or move points to airline and hotel programs. If you want cash back and travel little, the no-fee Freedom Unlimited returns more, because it pays 1.5% on ordinary purchases where the Preferred pays 1 point.

This page is information, not financial advice. Terms change, so check Chase's pages before deciding.

## Side by side

| | Sapphire Preferred | Freedom Unlimited |
|---|---|---|
| Annual fee | $95 | $0 |
| Chase Travel bookings | 5x | 5% |
| Dining | 3x | 3% |
| Drugstores | 1x | 3% |
| Gas, EV charging, selected streaming, online grocery | 3x | 1.5% |
| Travel booked direct | 2x | 1.5% |
| Everything else | 1x | 1.5% |
| Yearly credit | Up to $100 on Chase Travel hotels | None |
| Foreign transaction fee | None | 3% |
| Airport lounges | None | None |
| Transfer partners | 14 airline and hotel programs | None when held alone |
| Value of a point | 1 cent as cash; up to 1.5 cents on Points Boost bookings (some sources report 1.75); more through some partners | 1 cent as cash |
| Trip cancellation cover | Up to $10,000 per traveler | Up to $1,500 per traveler (one source) |
| Rental car cover | Primary | Not confirmed |

The Freedom Unlimited is sold as a cash back card, but it earns the same kind of Chase points. One percent equals one point.

## The plain sum

Take a household that puts $20,000 a year on one card: $4,000 dining, $2,000 travel booked direct, $14,000 everything else.

| | Sapphire Preferred | Freedom Unlimited |
|---|---|---|
| Dining, $4,000 | 12,000 | 12,000 |
| Travel, $2,000 | 4,000 | 3,000 |
| Everything else, $14,000 | 14,000 | 21,000 |
| Total points | 30,000 | 36,000 |
| As cash at 1 cent | $300 | $360 |
| After the annual fee | $205 | $360 |

Taken as cash, the Freedom Unlimited is ahead by $155. For the Preferred to draw level, its 30,000 points have to be worth $455, which is about 1.5 cents each.

Now add the hotel credit. A reader who books one hotel a year through Chase Travel gets up to $100 back, which leaves the Preferred $5 short on fees. Its points then need to be worth about 1.2 cents each to match. Points Boost bookings and transfers to partners can reach that. Cash cannot.

If part of the "everything else" is gas, streaming or online grocery, the Preferred earns 3x there and the gap narrows.

## Three things that tip it toward the Preferred

- **Spending abroad.** The Freedom Unlimited adds 3% to purchases in foreign currency. On $3,200 abroad that is $96, the whole Preferred fee.
- **Transfers.** Only the Preferred, the Reserve or the Ink Business Preferred can send points to United, Southwest, Hyatt and the other partners. Hyatt is now 4 Chase points to 3 from the Preferred; see [the Hyatt transfer change](/chase-to-hyatt-transfer-change-2026/).
- **Trip cover.** The Preferred's trip cancellation, trip delay and primary rental car cover are stronger. The limits are on the [travel insurance page](/chase-sapphire-preferred-travel-insurance/).

## Holding both

One person can hold both cards and move Freedom Unlimited points into the Sapphire Preferred account. Those points then transfer to partners like any others. In the example above, that would mean 1.5 points on the $14,000 of general spending and 2x on travel, for 37,000 points a year that can all go to partners, for one $95 fee.

That only pays if the points are used for travel. A reader who would cash out at 1 cent gains nothing from the second card.

## Which pattern favors which card

- **No trips abroad, wants cash back, pays for travel rarely:** Freedom Unlimited.
- **One or more hotel stays a year and some spending abroad:** Sapphire Preferred.
- **Collects points for flights or Hyatt stays:** Sapphire Preferred, or both cards together.
- **Large drugstore spending:** Freedom Unlimited, at 3%.

## Who should skip the fee

- Anyone who redeems for cash every time. The Preferred's extra value comes from travel use.
- Anyone who would not book a hotel through Chase Travel. Without the $100 credit the fee is a full $95 each year.
- Anyone carrying a balance. Interest outweighs rewards on either card.
- Anyone with five or more new personal cards in 24 months is generally declined for both; see [Chase's 5/24 rule](/chase-5-24-rule-explained/).

Welcome offers on both cards vary and change, so they are left out of the sums. A [first-year plan for the Preferred](/chase-sapphire-preferred-first-year-plan/) covers the early months.

## Quick answers

**Does the Freedom Unlimited earn more than the Sapphire Preferred on ordinary purchases?**
Yes. It earns 1.5 points per dollar where the Preferred earns 1.

**Can Freedom Unlimited points transfer to airlines?**
Not from that card alone. They can after being moved to a Sapphire Preferred, Sapphire Reserve or Ink Business Preferred held by the same person.

**How much spending abroad cancels out the $95 fee?**
About $3,200 a year. The Freedom Unlimited's 3% foreign transaction fee on that amount is $96.

## Sources

- [Chase: Freedom Unlimited card page](https://creditcards.chase.com/cash-back-credit-cards/freedom/unlimited)
- [Chase: Sapphire Preferred card page](https://creditcards.chase.com/rewards-credit-cards/sapphire/preferred)
- [One Mile at a Time: Chase Freedom Unlimited review](https://onemileatatime.com/reviews/credit-cards/chase/chase-freedom-unlimited/)
- [The Points Guy: Chase Sapphire Preferred review](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/chase-sapphire-preferred-review)
- [The Points Guy: Chase Points Boost](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/chase-points-boost)
- [AwardWallet: Chase to Hyatt transfer ratios](https://awardwallet.com/credit-cards/chase-ultimate-rewards/chase-to-hyatt-transfer/)

# Chase Sapphire Preferred or a Southwest Rapid Rewards card for a Southwest flyer?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/chase-sapphire-preferred-vs-southwest-rapid-rewards-priority/
Facts checked: 2026-11-21
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

A Southwest flyer who checks bags gets more from a Southwest Rapid Rewards card, because every Southwest card waives the first bag fee for up to nine people on a reservation. A Southwest flyer who travels with a carry-on, or who also flies other airlines, gets more from the $95 Sapphire Preferred, whose points move to Southwest at 1:1.

This page is information, not financial advice. Terms change, so check Chase's pages before deciding.

## Side by side

| | Chase Sapphire Preferred | Southwest Rapid Rewards Priority |
|---|---|---|
| Annual fee | $95 | $229 |
| Yearly points or credit | Up to $100 each account year on Chase Travel hotel stays | 7,500 points each account anniversary |
| Southwest flights | 2x | 4x |
| Dining | 3x | 2x |
| Gas stations | 3x | 2x |
| Chase Travel bookings | 5x | No bonus |
| Everything else | 1x | 1x |
| Checked bag on Southwest | No benefit | First bag free for the cardholder and up to 8 others on the reservation |
| Seats | No benefit | Preferred seat at booking; Extra Legroom seat within 48 hours of departure, when available |
| Boarding | No benefit | Group 5 |
| Lounge access | None | None |
| Where the points go | 16 transfer partners, Southwest included | Southwest Rapid Rewards only |
| Foreign transaction fee | None | None |

Chase's page for the Priority card no longer lists the $75 Southwest travel credit or the upgraded boardings that some older reviews still describe.

## The other two Southwest cards

| | Plus | Premier | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|
| Annual fee | $99 | $149 | $229 |
| Southwest flights | 2x | 3x | 4x |
| Anniversary points | 3,000 | 6,000 | 7,500 |
| Seat selection | Standard seat, within 48 hours | Preferred seat, within 48 hours | Preferred seat at booking; Extra Legroom within 48 hours |
| Free first bag, up to 9 people | Yes | Yes | Yes |

This table comes from a Points Guy comparison dated February 2026. The Plus at $99 costs $4 more than the Preferred and carries the same bag benefit as the Priority.

## The bag sum

Southwest charges $45 for a first checked bag on Basic, Choice and Choice Preferred fares booked since April 9, 2026. Sources disagree here: one February 2026 comparison still prints $35, and two later pages give $45.

- One traveler, one round trip: $90.
- A family of four, one round trip: 4 x $90 = $360.

For the Priority, the 7,500 anniversary points are worth about $94 at The Points Guy's 1.25 cents a point. $229 minus $94 leaves about $135, which is one and a half solo round trips of bag fees. A family of four passes the full $229 on one trip.

For the Plus, 3,000 points are worth about $38. $99 minus $38 leaves about $61, less than one solo round trip with a bag.

## The points sum

Take $2,500 a year of Southwest fares and $3,000 of dining.

| | Sapphire Preferred | Priority |
|---|---|---|
| Southwest fares, $2,500 | 5,000 points | 10,000 points |
| Dining, $3,000 | 9,000 points | 6,000 points |
| Anniversary | 0 | 7,500 points |
| Total | 14,000 points | 23,500 points |

The Priority earns more Southwest points. Chase points can do more: they move to Southwest at 1:1 and also to United, Hyatt and 13 other programs. The Points Guy valued Chase points at 2.05 cents and Southwest points at 1.25 cents in November 2026.

## Which pattern favors which card

- **Checks bags on Southwest, alone, twice a year or more:** a Southwest card. The Plus covers its fee on the first round trip.
- **Family or group on one reservation:** a Southwest card. One trip for four saves $360 in bag fees.
- **Wants a seat picked at booking or more legroom:** the Priority. The Plus and Premier open seat selection only within 48 hours of departure.
- **Carry-on only, a few Southwest flights a year:** the Preferred. Without bags the Priority's $229 has to come back from 7,500 points and seat selection.
- **Working toward the Companion Pass:** a Southwest card. Each one adds 10,000 qualifying points a year toward the 135,000 needed, and card spending counts.
- **Flies several airlines or wants trip insurance:** the Preferred, for its [travel insurance](/chase-sapphire-preferred-travel-insurance/) and wider partners.

Whether points moved from Chase to Southwest count toward the Companion Pass is not confirmed in the sources read.

## Who should skip it

- Skip a Southwest card if you fly Southwest once a year with no checked bag.
- Skip the Priority if the bag benefit is all you want. The $99 Plus has the same one.
- Skip the Preferred if nearly all your travel is Southwest with bags. It has no Southwest benefit beyond points.
- Skip both if you carry a balance. Interest costs more than either card returns.

Welcome offers vary by applicant and change, so they are left out of the sums. Chase limits the Southwest card bonus to people who do not hold a personal Southwest card and have not had a Southwest card bonus in 24 months.

## Quick answers

**Do Sapphire Preferred points transfer to Southwest?**
Yes, at 1:1. Southwest award prices follow the cash fare of the flight.

**Do all Southwest cards include a free checked bag?**
Yes, according to The Points Guy's comparison: the first bag for the cardholder and up to eight others on the reservation.

**Does either card include airport lounge access?**
No lounge access is listed for the Sapphire Preferred or for the Southwest Priority on Chase's pages.

## Sources

- [Chase: Southwest Rapid Rewards Priority card page](https://creditcards.chase.com/travel-credit-cards/southwest/priority)
- [The Points Guy: Southwest Priority review](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/reviews/southwest-priority-credit-card-review/)
- [The Points Guy: comparing Southwest credit cards](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/airlines/southwest-airlines/comparing-southwest-credit-cards)
- [One Mile at a Time: Southwest Priority review](https://onemileatatime.com/reviews/credit-cards/chase/southwest-priority/)
- [AwardWallet: Southwest baggage fees](https://awardwallet.com/airlines/southwest-rapid-rewards/southwest-baggage-fees/)
- [Chase: Sapphire Preferred card page](https://creditcards.chase.com/rewards-credit-cards/sapphire/preferred)
- [The Points Guy: monthly valuations](https://thepointsguy.com/loyalty-programs/monthly-valuations/)

# Chase Sapphire Preferred or United Explorer for someone who mostly flies United?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/chase-sapphire-preferred-vs-united-explorer/
Facts checked: 2026-11-21
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

A United flyer who checks a bag on two round trips a year saves more in bag fees than the United Explorer's $150 fee. A United flyer who travels with a carry-on gets little from the Explorer and more from the $95 Sapphire Preferred, whose points move to United at 1:1 and to 15 other programs.

This page is information, not financial advice. Terms change, so check Chase's pages before deciding.

## Side by side

| | Chase Sapphire Preferred | United Explorer |
|---|---|---|
| Annual fee | $95 | $0 the first year, then $150 |
| Main credits | Up to $100 each account year on Chase Travel hotel stays | Rideshare up to $60, Instacart up to $120 (through 2027), JSX up to $100, United Hotels up to $100 a year |
| United flights | 2x | 3x from the card, on top of the miles the fare earns |
| Chase Travel bookings | 5x | No bonus |
| Dining | 3x | 2x |
| Hotels booked direct | 2x | 2x |
| Everything else | 1x; 3x on gas, streaming, online grocery | 1x |
| Checked bag on United | No benefit | First bag free for the cardholder and one companion |
| Boarding | No benefit | Group 2 |
| Lounge access | None | Two one-time United Club passes a year |
| Where the points go | 16 transfer partners, United included | United MileagePlus only |
| Trip cancellation cover | Up to $10,000 per traveler | Up to $1,500 per person (one source) |
| Foreign transaction fee | None | None |

Both cards are issued by Chase. Each earns its own kind of point: the Preferred earns Chase points, which can become United miles, and the Explorer earns United miles, which cannot become anything else.

## The bag sum

United charges $45 for a first checked bag paid in advance, or $50 within 24 hours of departure, on tickets bought since April 3, 2026.

- One traveler, one round trip: $90.
- Two travelers on one reservation, one round trip: $180.
- Explorer fee from the second year: $150.

Two solo round trips with a checked bag ($180), or one round trip with a companion ($180), cover the fee. Two rules apply: the ticket has to be bought with the Explorer, and the cardholder's MileagePlus number has to be on the reservation. Only flights operated by United or United Express count.

## The points sum

Take $3,000 a year of United fares and $3,000 of dining.

| | Sapphire Preferred | United Explorer |
|---|---|---|
| United fares, $3,000 | 6,000 points | 9,000 miles |
| Dining, $3,000 | 9,000 points | 6,000 miles |
| Total | 15,000 points | 15,000 miles |

The totals match, but the points differ. Chase points can move to United at 1:1, so 15,000 of them can be 15,000 United miles, or they can go to Hyatt, Southwest or an airline with a lower award price for the same trip. The Points Guy valued Chase points at 2.05 cents and United miles at 1.2 cents in November 2026; One Mile at a Time uses 1.3 cents for United. Explorer cardholders do see lower award prices on some United flights, according to One Mile at a Time.

## Which pattern favors which card

- **Checks a bag on United at least twice a year, or travels with a companion who does:** Explorer. The bag saving alone passes $150.
- **Travels carry-on only:** Preferred. Without bags, the Explorer's fee has to come back from two club passes and credits for rideshare, Instacart and JSX.
- **Flies United and other airlines:** Preferred. Its 2x covers every airline and its trip cover is higher.
- **Chasing United status:** Explorer. It earns 1 Premier Qualifying Point per $20 spent, up to 1,000 a year. The Preferred earns none.
- **Spends $10,000 a year on one card:** the Explorer adds $100 of United TravelBank cash at that level.

Holding both costs $245 a year from the second year. Chase's 5/24 rule applies to both; see [how the 5/24 rule works](/chase-5-24-rule-explained/).

## Who should skip it

- Skip the Explorer if you fly United once a year without a bag. The fee is $150 from year two.
- Skip the Preferred if all you want is cheaper United flights with bags. It has no United benefit beyond points.
- Skip both if you carry a balance. Interest costs more than either card returns.

Welcome offers vary by applicant and change, so they are left out of the sums. Sources disagree on the Explorer's public offer today: Chase's own page showed one figure in its headline and another in its terms.

## Quick answers

**Do Sapphire Preferred points transfer to United?**
Yes, at 1:1 in 1,000-point steps. Transfers cannot be reversed.

**Does the Sapphire Preferred give a free checked bag on United?**
No. Among these two cards only the United Explorer does, for the cardholder and one companion on the same reservation.

**Does the United Explorer include United Club access?**
Only two one-time passes a year, added to the MileagePlus account. It is not a club membership.

## Sources

- [Chase: United Explorer card page](https://creditcards.chase.com/travel-credit-cards/united/united-explorer)
- [One Mile at a Time: United Explorer review](https://onemileatatime.com/reviews/credit-cards/chase/united-explorer-card/)
- [Chase: Sapphire Preferred card page](https://creditcards.chase.com/rewards-credit-cards/sapphire/preferred)
- [The Points Guy: Sapphire Preferred review](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/chase-sapphire-preferred-review)
- [The Points Guy: monthly valuations](https://thepointsguy.com/loyalty-programs/monthly-valuations/)
- [Good Morning America: airline bag fee increases](https://www.goodmorningamerica.com/travel/story/american-airlines-alaska-airlines-join-carriers-raising-bag-131890702)
- [The Points Guy: credit cards with free checked bags](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/credit-cards-with-free-checked-baggage/)

# Chase Sapphire Preferred or Wells Fargo Autograph Journey: which $95 card fits?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/chase-sapphire-preferred-vs-wells-fargo-autograph-journey/
Facts checked: 2026-11-21
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

Both cards cost $95 a year, and the Wells Fargo Autograph Journey earns more points on flights and hotels booked directly, at 4x and 5x against the Sapphire Preferred's 2x. The Preferred fits a reader who wants points that move to United, Southwest and Hyatt, or primary rental car cover in the United States.

This page is information, not financial advice. Terms change, so check each issuer's pages before deciding.

## Side by side

| | Chase Sapphire Preferred | Wells Fargo Autograph Journey |
|---|---|---|
| Annual fee | $95 | $95 |
| Main credit | Up to $100 each account year on hotel stays booked through Chase Travel | $50 each year after a first airline purchase of $50 or more |
| Hotels booked direct | 2x | 5x |
| Flights booked direct | 2x | 4x |
| Issuer travel portal | 5x on Chase Travel | No separate portal rate listed |
| Dining | 3x | 3x |
| Other travel | 2x | 3x |
| Gas, streaming, online grocery | 3x | 1x |
| Everything else | 1x | 1x |
| Lounge access | None | None |
| Transfer partners | 16 programs, with United, Southwest, JetBlue, Hyatt (4:3), Marriott, IHG | About 11 programs, with Flying Blue, British Airways, Avianca, Virgin Atlantic, JetBlue, Choice, Wyndham |
| Rental car cover | Primary | Secondary in the US, primary abroad |
| Trip cancellation | Up to $10,000 per traveler, $20,000 per trip | Up to $15,000 |
| Trip delay | Up to $500 per traveler after 12 hours | Not listed on Wells Fargo's page |
| Cell phone protection | Not listed | Up to $1,000 per claim, $25 deductible |
| Foreign transaction fee | None | None |

Sources disagree on the Wells Fargo partner list. AwardWallet's May 2026 table shows nine airline programs and two hotel programs. The Points Guy's March 2025 review lists seven programs, without Cathay Pacific, JetBlue or Wyndham. Wells Fargo's card page names none, so check the list in a Wells Fargo account before counting on a partner.

## The fee sum

- **Autograph Journey:** $95 minus the $50 airline credit is $45. The credit posts after one airline purchase of $50 or more, booked anywhere.
- **Preferred:** $95 minus the $100 hotel credit is minus $5. The credit works only on a hotel stay booked through Chase Travel.

A reader who buys one plane ticket a year uses the Wells Fargo credit without trying. A reader who would not book a hotel through Chase's portal should count the Preferred at the full $95.

## The points sum

Take $4,000 a year of airfare and $3,000 of hotels, both booked direct, plus $4,000 of dining.

| | Sapphire Preferred | Autograph Journey |
|---|---|---|
| Airfare, $4,000 | 8,000 | 16,000 |
| Hotels, $3,000 | 6,000 | 15,000 |
| Dining, $4,000 | 12,000 | 12,000 |
| Total points | 26,000 | 43,000 |

The Autograph Journey is 17,000 points ahead on that pattern. Two things narrow the gap.

First, booking the same travel through Chase Travel earns 5x on the Preferred: 35,000 points on the $7,000, for a total of 47,000. Portal bookings can cost hotel loyalty benefits, so this is a trade.

Second, the points are not equal. Both are worth 1 cent as a statement credit. Above that, value depends on partners. Chase points move to United, Southwest and Hyatt; none of those is in either Wells Fargo partner list read. The Points Guy valued Chase points at 2.05 cents in November 2026 and Wells Fargo points at 1.6 cents in March 2025.

Add $3,000 a year of gas and streaming and the Preferred earns 9,000 points on it; the Autograph Journey earns 3,000.

## Which pattern favors which card

- **Books flights and hotels direct and redeems for statement credits or simple travel:** Autograph Journey. It earns two to two and a half times as much on that spending.
- **Wants to fly on United or Southwest points, or stay at Hyatt:** Preferred.
- **Rents cars in the US:** Preferred. Its [rental car cover](/chase-sapphire-preferred-rental-car-insurance/) is primary, so a claim does not go through personal auto insurance first.
- **Pays a phone bill and wants the phone covered:** Autograph Journey.
- **Uses Flying Blue, Avios or Virgin Atlantic:** either. Both issuers transfer to those programs.
- **Has opened five or more cards in two years:** Chase generally declines under its [5/24 rule](/chase-5-24-rule-explained/). Wells Fargo's approval rules were not checked for this page.

The [Citi Strata Premier comparison](/chase-sapphire-preferred-vs-citi-strata-premier/) and the [Capital One Venture comparison](/chase-sapphire-preferred-vs-capital-one-venture/) cover two other cards at this fee.

## Who should skip it

- Skip the Autograph Journey if your plan depends on a specific US airline or hotel partner. Its list is shorter and sources do not agree on it.
- Skip the Preferred if you book travel direct, redeem for cash value and never transfer points. It earns fewer points on that spending.
- Skip both if you take one trip a year and spend little on dining. A no-fee card costs less.
- Skip both if you carry a balance. Interest costs more than either card returns.

Welcome offers vary by applicant and change, so they are left out of the sums.

## Quick answers

**Which card earns more on hotels and flights?**
The Autograph Journey on direct bookings: 5x on hotels and 4x on airlines against 2x. The Preferred earns 5x only through Chase Travel.

**Do Wells Fargo points transfer to United, Southwest or Hyatt?**
No, not in the partner lists read. Chase points transfer to all three.

**Does the Autograph Journey include airport lounge access?**
No. Neither card includes lounge access.

## Sources

- [AwardWallet: Wells Fargo Autograph Journey](https://awardwallet.com/credit-cards/wells-fargo-rewards/autograph-journey/)
- [The Points Guy: Wells Fargo Autograph Journey review](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/reviews/wells-fargo-autograph-journey-card-review/)

# Does pairing a Sapphire Preferred with Freedom cards make sense, and how do you combine the points?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/chase-sapphire-preferred-with-freedom-cards-combine-points/
Facts checked: 2026-11-21
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

Pairing a Sapphire Preferred with a no-fee Freedom card makes sense for people who transfer points to airlines or hotels, because Freedom points can be moved to the Preferred for free and sent to partners from there. Since October 2025 the move no longer raises what the points are worth on ordinary Chase Travel bookings, so for someone who takes points as cash the pairing adds little.

This page is information, not financial advice. For choosing one card over the other, see [Sapphire Preferred or Freedom Unlimited](/chase-sapphire-preferred-vs-freedom-unlimited/).

## Why people pair them

Each card earns more than the other in some places. All of it is the same kind of Chase point.

| Spending | Sapphire Preferred | Freedom Unlimited | Freedom Flex |
|---|---|---|---|
| Dining | 3x | 3% | 3% |
| Gas, EV charging, online grocery, selected streaming | 3x | 1.5% | 1% |
| Travel booked direct | 2x | 1.5% | 1% |
| Drugstores | 1x | 3% | 3% |
| Rotating quarterly categories | 1x | 1.5% | 5% on up to $1,500 a quarter, after activating |
| Everything else | 1x | 1.5% | 1% |
| Annual fee | $95 | $0 | $0 |
| Transfers to partners | Yes | Not alone | Not alone |

One percent on a Freedom card equals one point.

## How to combine points

Chase's own guide says there is no minimum and no fee, and no points are lost.

1. Sign in to the Chase account and open the rewards section for the card that holds the points.
2. Open Rewards details, then Combine points.
3. Pick the card to move from and the card to move to.
4. Enter the amount, review and submit. Chase may ask for a security code.

Between your own cards the move is instant, per The Points Guy. Only the primary cardholder can do it.

**Another person.** Chase lets you share with one person at the same address: "you can only designate one person to share points with." The first link is set up by phone. Chase may suspend or close accounts for misuse, such as selling points.

**Undoing it.** Chase's guide says a transfer cannot be undone. AwardWallet says points can be moved straight back between your own cards. Treat a move to another person as final.

**If the option is missing.** One site reports that some people lost the online option in late 2025 and had a phone agent move the points.

## What changed in 2025

Before, points held on a Sapphire Preferred were worth a fixed 1.25 cents each toward any Chase Travel booking. Moving Freedom points over raised their value by a quarter at once.

That ended with Points Boost. Frequent Miler reports that points earned on, or combined to, a Sapphire card from October 26, 2025 follow the new rules: 1 cent as the base, more only on bookings marked with a Boost. On the Preferred a Boost goes up to 1.5 cents, or 1.75 on some premium-cabin fares; sources differ on that top figure. Details are on the [Points Boost page](/chase-points-boost-explained/). Chase's own wording for that rule was not found, so the date rests on third-party reports.

So the reason to combine now is transfers to partners, plus the occasional Boost. One more change: from the Preferred, Hyatt is 4 Chase points to 3, not 1:1. See [the Hyatt transfer change](/chase-to-hyatt-transfer-change-2026/).

## The sum

Take $12,000 a year of spending that earns 1x on the Preferred.

| | Preferred alone | Moved to Freedom Unlimited |
|---|---|---|
| Points on $12,000 | 12,000 | 18,000 |
| Extra points | | 6,000 |
| Extra value at 1 cent | | $60 |
| Extra value at 2.05 cents (The Points Guy's valuation, which assumes partner transfers) | | $123 |

A Freedom Flex user who fills every quarter earns 5 points on $6,000 a year in place of 1: 24,000 extra points. That takes activating each quarter and spending in the listed categories.

Costs to set against it:

- A second card is a new account with a hard credit check, and it counts toward [5/24](/chase-5-24-rule-explained/).
- The Freedom Unlimited charges a 3% foreign transaction fee. Keep it at home.

## Who should skip it

- Anyone who redeems points as cash. Points are worth 1 cent on either card, so the Preferred's $95 fee buys nothing in the pairing; a Freedom card alone does the job.
- Anyone who does not want to track categories across several cards.
- Anyone saving 5/24 slots for other applications.
- Anyone whose spending is mostly dining, gas and travel. The Preferred already earns 3x or 2x there.

## Quick answers

**Can Freedom points be transferred to airlines and hotels?**
Not directly. Move them to a Sapphire Preferred, Sapphire Reserve or Ink Business Preferred first, then transfer.

**Is there a fee or a minimum to combine Chase points?**
No. Chase says there is no fee and no minimum amount.

**Does moving points to the Preferred still make them worth 1.25 cents?**
No. Since October 26, 2025, newly earned or combined points get 1 cent, or more only on Points Boost bookings.

- [The Points Guy: transferring Chase points between accounts](https://thepointsguy.com/loyalty-programs/transfer-ultimate-rewards-points-between-accounts/)

# Is the Chase Sapphire referral offer the same as the public or in-branch offer?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/chase-sapphire-referral-vs-public-offer/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

Often, but not always. On November 20, 2026 the Sapphire Preferred referral page and Chase's public page showed the same bonus, 75,000 points after $5,000 of purchases in three months. The two have differed for days or weeks in the past, and no current in-branch offer could be confirmed.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## The three routes on November 20, 2026

| Route | Sapphire Preferred bonus | Spending requirement | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Chase public page | 75,000 points | $5,000 in 3 months | Confirmed on Chase's page |
| Referral link | 75,000 points | $5,000 in 3 months | Confirmed on that date |
| Chase branch | Not confirmed | Not confirmed | No source read lists a branch offer this month |

For the Sapphire Reserve, the public page and the referral page both showed 100,000 points, and the public page states $6,000 of purchases in three months.

Chase itself says offers are not uniform. Its card page states: "Offers may vary depending on where you apply," for example online or in a branch, and they can change over time.

## Times the routes did not match

| When | Public page | Referral links | Branch | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2021 | 100,000 points | 80,000 for several weeks | Not covered | Frequent Miler |
| 2023 | 60,000 points | 60,000 points | 90,000 after $6,000 in 6 months | Frequent Miler |
| March 2024 | Lower than branch (figure not given) | Not covered | 70,000 in two steps | Danny the Deal Guru |
| June 15 to July 30, 2026 | 100,000 after $5,000 | 100,000 from June 16 | Not covered | Doctor of Credit |
| July 30 to early August 2026 | 75,000 | 100,000 for about one more week | Not covered | Doctor of Credit |

Three patterns come out of this:

- Referral links usually follow the public offer, sometimes a day late.
- When an offer ends, referral links have lagged in either direction. In 2021 they were lower. In summer 2026 they stayed higher for about a week.
- Branch offers have at times been higher than online.

Sources disagree by one day on when the 2026 referral offer ended: Frequent Miler lists August 5, Doctor of Credit August 6.

Frequent Miler also reported that in 2021 Chase would not match applicants who had used the lower referral offer to the higher public one. Do not count on a match after the fact.

## About branch offers

A branch offer is one a Chase banker can submit for you in person. What sources say:

- Past branch offers sometimes had a higher points figure, a longer spending window, or a second step that needed more spending.
- A Frequent Miler post, seen in a search summary, says the annual fee has been waived for the first year more often on branch offers than online. Not confirmed for 2026.
- No source read lists a Sapphire branch offer for November 2026. Frequent Miler's card page lists only the 75,000-point offer.

Asking a banker what the branch offer is does not involve a credit check. Applying does.

## How to compare on the day

1. Open Chase's public Sapphire page. Note the points, the spending requirement, the time allowed and the annual fee.
2. Open the referral page. Note the same four things.
3. If you bank with Chase, ask at a branch what its offer is before you apply anywhere.
4. Compare whole offers, not only points, and keep a copy of the terms you apply under.

## What is the same on every route

- **Bonus eligibility.** One bonus per Sapphire card per lifetime. See [the 2026 eligibility rules](/chase-sapphire-bonus-eligibility-2026/).
- **5/24.** See [how to count your cards](/chase-5-24-rule-explained/).
- **The credit check.** Each application adds a hard inquiry.
- **What counts as spending.** See [the spending requirement](/chase-sapphire-welcome-bonus-spending-requirement/).

No source read says a referral or branch application is exempt from these. That is not confirmed as a stated Chase rule.

For how a referral link works step by step, see [the refer-a-friend page](/chase-sapphire-preferred-referral-bonus-how-it-works/).

## Who should skip it

- Anyone who already earned the bonus on that Sapphire card. No route brings it back.
- Anyone at or over 5/24. The route does not change the likely denial.
- Anyone waiting for a higher offer who needs the card's travel protections for a trip soon. Past higher offers were short and their dates were not announced far ahead.
- Anyone who would have to stretch to meet a larger spending requirement.

No offer amount is promised here. Offers change.

## Quick answers

**Is the Sapphire referral bonus higher than the public bonus?**
Not as of November 20, 2026, when both showed 75,000 points on the Preferred. It has been higher and lower at times.

**Are Chase branch offers higher than online offers?**
Sometimes in the past. No branch offer for November 2026 was confirmed in the sources read.

**Will Chase match a higher offer after I apply?**
Do not plan on it. Frequent Miler reported Chase declining to match in 2021.

## Sources

- [Chase: Sapphire Preferred card page](https://creditcards.chase.com/rewards-credit-cards/sapphire/preferred)
- [Chase: Sapphire Reserve card page](https://creditcards.chase.com/rewards-credit-cards/sapphire/reserve)
- [Doctor of Credit: Sapphire Preferred 100,000-point offer timeline](https://doctorofcredit.com/chase-sapphire-preferred-100000-points-offer)
- [Frequent Miler: Sapphire Preferred offer page](https://frequentmiler.com/csp/)
- [Frequent Miler: referral links with lower offers (2021)](https://frequentmiler.com/friends-dont-let-friends-get-inferior-offers/)
- [Frequent Miler: 2023 in-branch offer](https://frequentmiler.com/chase-sapphire-preferred-90k-offer-in-branch-starting-3-19/)
- [Danny the Deal Guru: 2024 in-branch offer](https://dannydealguru.com/chase-sapphire-preferred-70k-bonus-available-in-branch/)

# What counts toward the Chase Sapphire Reserve's $300 travel credit, and when does it reset?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/chase-sapphire-reserve-300-travel-credit-what-counts/
Facts checked: 2026-11-21
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

Any purchase that Chase codes as travel counts, including airfare, hotels, car rentals, trains, taxis, tolls and parking, with no sign-up and no booking site required. The credit resets each account anniversary year, not on January 1, and the part of a purchase it covers earns no points.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## What counts

Chase's terms say the credit applies to "purchases made in the travel category". Chase's category list names these merchants:

- Airlines
- Hotels, motels and timeshares
- Car rental agencies
- Cruise lines
- Travel agencies and discount travel sites
- Campgrounds
- Passenger trains, buses, taxis, limousines and ferries
- Toll bridges and highways
- Parking lots and garages

Chase's guide gives taxi fares and highway tolls as examples, and The Points Guy says everyday parking can qualify. One Mile at a Time (June 2, 2026) says rideshare and subway fares count too. Rideshare is not named on Chase's own list.

## What does not count

Chase's category list leaves out sightseeing, excursions and tourist attractions; in-flight goods and services; purchases on board a cruise ship; merchants inside hotels and airports; RV and boat rentals; public campgrounds; rentals for hauling; and gift card merchants or merchants that sell points or miles. The Points Guy adds theme park tickets bought from the park and ski lift tickets.

The merchant's code decides, not what you bought. Chase's terms say it does not determine whether a merchant bills a purchase under the right category.

## How it is applied

The credit posts by itself as a statement credit. It can be spread over many purchases or used on one.

| Purchases | Credit |
|---|---|
| $270 airfare, then $180 hotel | $270, then $30 |
| One $500 car rental | $300 |

Both examples are Chase's.

## When it resets

The credit runs on the account anniversary year, not the calendar year. Chase's terms define the first year as the account open date through the first statement date after the anniversary. After that, each year is the next 12 monthly billing cycles.

For an account opened March 10, 2026, the first credit year ends on the first statement date after March 10, 2027.

The Points Guy reports one exception: accounts opened before May 21, 2017 get the credit by calendar year, starting after the December statement closes. That is not confirmed on a Chase page read for this article.

## Do the purchases earn points?

No, not on the part the credit covers. Chase's card page says purchases that qualify will not earn points.

| Purchase | Credit | Earns points on |
|---|---|---|
| $300 flight booked with the airline | $300 | $0 |
| $1,000 flight booked with the airline | $300 | $700 |

The card earns 8 points per dollar through Chase Travel and 4 points per dollar on flights and hotels booked direct. So a credit used on a direct flight gives up 4 points per dollar on that $300, or 1,200 points.

## Where sources disagree

- **Posting time.** Chase's guide says a credit may appear within a few days and can take one to two billing cycles to show on a statement. The Points Guy says a couple of days.
- **Refunds.** One Mile at a Time says a refunded purchase should reverse the credit, which then applies to a later travel purchase, and that some readers report no reversal.

Not confirmed: whether Airbnb and other vacation rentals count, whether an authorized user's purchases draw on the same $300, and whether a Chase Travel booking uses this credit before the card's separate hotel credits.

## The sums

Used in full, the credit brings the $795 fee down to $495. Whether the remaining credits cover that gap is a separate question, answered on the [page about what the Reserve credits are really worth](/chase-sapphire-reserve-credits-real-value/).

## Who should skip counting on it

- Anyone who spends under $300 a year on travel, parking, tolls and transit combined.
- Anyone whose travel spending is mostly tours, attractions and theme park tickets. Those do not code as travel.
- Anyone weighing the card on this credit alone. The [Sapphire Preferred at $95](/sapphire-preferred-vs-reserve-light-traveler/) costs far less.

## Quick answers

**Does the Sapphire Reserve travel credit reset on January 1?**
No. It resets on the account anniversary year. The Points Guy reports that accounts opened before May 21, 2017 follow the calendar year.

**Do I need to book through Chase Travel?**
No. Chase's guide says there is nothing to activate and no specific booking site to use.

**Do parking and tolls count?**
Yes. Chase's travel category includes parking lots, garages, toll bridges and highways.

## Sources

- [Chase: Sapphire Reserve card page and terms](https://creditcards.chase.com/rewards-credit-cards/sapphire/reserve)
- [Chase: how the Sapphire Reserve travel credit works](https://www.chase.com/personal/credit-cards/education/rewards-benefits/chase-sapphire-reserve-travel-credit-how-it-works)
- [Chase: rewards category list](https://www.chase.com/personal/credit-cards/rewards-category-faq)
- [The Points Guy: Sapphire Reserve annual travel credit](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/chase/chase-sapphire-reserve-annual-travel-credit/)
- [One Mile at a Time: Sapphire Reserve travel credit](https://onemileatatime.com/guides/chase-sapphire-reserve-travel-credit/)

# What are the Sapphire Reserve credits really worth if you only count the ones you would use anyway?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/chase-sapphire-reserve-credits-real-value/
Facts checked: 2026-11-22
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

At face value the Sapphire Reserve's recurring credits add up to about $2,384 a year against a $795 fee, before counting the DashPass membership and the Global Entry credit. Count only what you would have paid for anyway and most people land far lower, often between $300 and $900, so the card pays for itself only for those who already spend in several of its categories.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## Every credit, with amount and cadence

| Credit | Amount | Cadence | Limits |
|---|---|---|---|
| Travel credit | Up to $300 | Each account anniversary year | Automatic on travel purchases; those purchases earn no points |
| The Edit hotels | Up to $500 | Calendar year, $250 per booking | Prepaid stays of two nights or more at hotels in Chase's The Edit collection |
| Dining | Up to $300 | $150 January to June, $150 July to December | Only restaurants in Sapphire Reserve Exclusive Tables on OpenTable |
| StubHub and viagogo | Up to $300 | $150 per half-year, through 12/31/2027 | Activation needed; no gift cards |
| DoorDash promos | Up to $420 | $35 a month, through 12/31/2029 | $15 off one restaurant order, two $10 off non-restaurant orders; unused promos expire at month end |
| DashPass | Chase's stated value $120 | 12 months | Activate by 12/31/2029 |
| Lyft | Up to $120 | $10 a month, through 9/30/2027 | Rides only; not tips, taxes or fees |
| Peloton | Up to $120 | $10 a month, through 12/31/2027 | Eligible memberships; activation needed |
| Apple TV and Apple Music | Chase's stated value $324 | Yearly | Activate by 6/22/2027 |
| Global Entry, TSA PreCheck or NEXUS | Up to $120 | Once every four years | About $30 a year |

Several reports also describe a one-time 2026 credit of up to $250 for a prepaid two-night stay at selected hotel brands in Chase Travel. It is not on Chase's public card page today, so treat the details as not confirmed and check your account.

## Why face value is the wrong number

A credit is worth its full amount only if it replaces money you were going to spend anyway. Three things shrink it:

- **Narrow lists.** The dining credit works at a set list of restaurants, not at any restaurant. The Edit credit works at a set collection of hotels, and needs a prepaid stay of two nights.
- **Use it or lose it.** The half-year and monthly credits do not roll over. A missed month of Lyft or DoorDash is gone.
- **Spending you would not have done.** A hotel in The Edit can cost more than the hotel you would have picked.

## Add up your own number

Go down the list and write a dollar figure next to each line. Use last year's real spending, not what you hope to do.

1. **Travel credit.** If you spend $300 a year on any travel, write $300. Most cardholders can.
2. **The Edit.** Write $250 for each two-night prepaid stay you would book at one of these hotels at the price Chase shows. If you are not sure, write $0.
3. **Dining.** Check the Exclusive Tables list for your city. Write $150 per half-year only if you would eat at one of those restaurants anyway.
4. **StubHub.** Write what you spent on resale tickets last year, up to $150 per half.
5. **DoorDash.** Write $15 for each month you already order restaurant delivery, and $10 or $20 for each month you already order groceries or convenience items there.
6. **Lyft and Peloton.** Write $10 for each month you already pay for them.
7. **Apple.** Write what you pay now for Apple TV and Apple Music. If you pay for neither, write $0.
8. **Global Entry.** Write $30.

Add the lines up and subtract $795.

## Two sample totals

These are illustrations, not typical results.

| Reader | What they count | Total | Against $795 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Uses travel credit only | $300 | $300 | Short by $495 |
| Adds Apple subscriptions, Lyft ten months, one Edit stay | $300 + $324 + $100 + $250 | $974 | Ahead by $179 |

Points and [airport lounge access](/chase-sapphire-reserve-lounge-access/) are separate from this sum. Count them only if you would use them.

## Who should skip it

- Anyone whose honest total is under $795 and who does not value the lounges or the higher earning rates enough to cover the gap.
- Anyone who does not want to track monthly and half-year deadlines.
- Anyone who carries a balance. Interest will outweigh any credit.
- Light travelers. The [Sapphire Preferred at $95](/sapphire-preferred-vs-reserve-light-traveler/) asks for much less.

## Quick answers

**Does the $300 travel credit alone justify the fee?**
No. It brings the cost down to $495. The remaining credits, points and lounges have to cover that.

**Do the credits roll over if I miss one?**
No. Monthly and half-year credits expire at the end of each period.

**Are all the credits permanent?**
No. Lyft ends 9/30/2027, StubHub and Peloton end 12/31/2027, and the DoorDash benefits run through 12/31/2029 unless Chase extends them.

## Sources

- [Chase: Sapphire Reserve card page](https://creditcards.chase.com/rewards-credit-cards/sapphire/reserve)
- [The Points Guy: Sapphire changes in January 2026, including The Edit credit](https://thepointsguy.com/news/chase-sapphire-bonus-eligibility-changes-2026)
- [Frequent Miler: 2026 credit for select Chase Travel hotels](https://frequentmiler.com/new-sapphire-reserve-benefit-for-2026-a-250-credit-for-select-chase-travel%E2%84%A0-hotels/)
- [Doctor of Credit: The Edit credit change and one-time hotel credit](https://www.doctorofcredit.com/chase-sapphire-reserve-enhances-500-the-edit-credit-adds-one-time-250-hotel-credit/)

# How does the Sapphire Reserve dining credit (Exclusive Tables) work, and which restaurants count?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/chase-sapphire-reserve-dining-credit-how-it-works/
Facts checked: 2026-11-21
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

The Sapphire Reserve dining credit pays back up to $150 from January to June and up to $150 from July to December when you pay with the card at a restaurant in the Sapphire Reserve Exclusive Tables list on OpenTable. Only those restaurants count, reported at roughly 360 to 400 in about 50 US cities and metro areas, so the credit is worth nothing in a city without one.

This page is information, not financial advice. The card's other credits are on [the full credits page](/chase-sapphire-reserve-credits-real-value/); this page covers only dining.

## The rules

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Amount | Up to $150 January 1 to June 30; up to $150 July 1 to December 31 |
| Cards | Personal Sapphire Reserve and J.P. Morgan Reserve; not the Sapphire Reserve for Business |
| Trigger | Pay with the card at a participating restaurant |
| Split | Can be spread over several meals and restaurants in a half-year |
| Rollover | None |
| Points | The Points Guy reports 3x on the whole bill, credited part included |

Chase's own example: $80 at one restaurant in February and $70 at another in May fill the first half-year's $150.

## Which restaurants count

Only restaurants in the Exclusive Tables program. Chase does not publish a count and says the list can change.

- The Points Guy reports figures from 362 to 397 restaurants, in about 50 US cities and metro areas listed by OpenTable.
- Thrifty Traveler counted 51 locations and found three participating restaurants in the Twin Cities.
- Chase has city guides for New York, Los Angeles, Chicago, San Francisco, Philadelphia, Houston, Las Vegas and San Diego.
- Restaurants in OpenTable's wider Visa Dining Collection do not count unless they carry the Sapphire Reserve badge.

The current list is at opentable.com/sapphire-reserve-exclusive-tables, or through the benefits section of the Chase account.

## Do you have to book through OpenTable?

The credit comes from paying with the card at a listed restaurant. The Points Guy states that a reservation made through Exclusive Tables is not required.

The program also holds back prime-time tables for cardholders. To see and book those, you add the Reserve to an OpenTable account and pass an eligibility check; Chase's terms say new cardmembers may wait up to four business days. Whether that link is also needed for the credit itself is not confirmed. Linking the card costs nothing, so doing it removes the doubt.

## What does not count

Chase's terms exclude:

- Gift cards and merchandise.
- Orders through delivery platforms.
- Purchases run through a third-party payment processor. The charge must be identifiable as made directly with the restaurant.

Two gray areas. The Points Guy reports cases where a restaurant gift card did trigger the credit, which conflicts with the terms; do not rely on it. Thrifty Traveler says takeout is unclear and that some people report credits posting with Apple Pay or Google Pay.

## When the credit posts

| Source | Stated timing |
|---|---|
| Chase's terms | Within 3 business days, up to 4 weeks |
| The Points Guy | One or two billing cycles |
| Thrifty Traveler | Six to eight weeks |

Each period ends at 11:59 PM Eastern on its last day. A meal on June 29 or December 30 that the restaurant processes late can land in the next period. Chase can reverse a credit if the charge is refunded or changed, or if the account closes within 90 days.

## What it is worth

These are mostly sit-down restaurants where a dinner for two can pass $150. The Points Guy's writer spent about $196 on one visit. So the usual result is $150 off a meal that costs more, twice a year.

| Reader | Honest yearly value |
|---|---|
| No listed restaurant within reach | $0 |
| One listed restaurant you would visit once a year anyway | $150 |
| Listed restaurants you already eat at in both halves of the year | $300 |
| Would go only to use the credit, $200 bill each time | $300 back on $400 of new spending |

The last row is a cost of $100, not a gain of $300.

## Who should skip it

- Anyone living far from the listed cities. Check the list before counting a dollar of this credit.
- Anyone who rarely eats at restaurants in this price range.
- Anyone who mostly orders delivery. Delivery platforms are excluded.
- Anyone who will not track two deadlines a year.

For a different dining credit with a wider restaurant list, see [how the Amex Platinum Resy credit works](/amex-platinum-resy-credit-how-it-works/).

## Quick answers

**Does any restaurant on OpenTable count?**
No. Only restaurants in the Sapphire Reserve Exclusive Tables list count.

**Does unused credit from January to June carry into July?**
No. Each half-year's $150 expires at the end of its period.

**Does delivery from a listed restaurant count?**
Not through a delivery platform. Chase's terms exclude those orders.

## Sources

- [Chase: Sapphire offer and benefit terms](https://www.chase.com/personal/credit-cards/offerdetails/chasesapphire)
- [Chase: how to use the dining credit with Exclusive Tables](https://www.chase.com/personal/credit-cards/education/basics/how-to-use-dining-credit-chase-sapphire-reserve-exclusive-tables)
- [Chase: guide to Sapphire Reserve Exclusive Tables](https://www.chase.com/personal/credit-cards/education/basics/guide-to-chase-sapphire-reserve-exclusive-tables)
- [The Points Guy: Sapphire Reserve Exclusive Tables guide](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/chase-sapphire-reserve-exclusive-tables-guide/)
- [Thrifty Traveler: Sapphire Reserve dining credit](https://thriftytraveler.com/guides/credit-card/sapphire-reserve-dining-credit/)

# Sapphire Reserve Exclusive Tables: what the Chase program is and how to book it

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/chase-sapphire-reserve-exclusive-tables-how-it-works/
Facts checked: 2026-11-26
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

Sapphire Reserve Exclusive Tables is a Chase program on OpenTable that sets aside prime-time reservations and special events at selected restaurants for Sapphire Reserve cardholders. You book it by adding an eligible card to a free OpenTable account, passing an eligibility check, and reserving through OpenTable's website or app.

This page is information, not financial advice. It covers the reservation side of the program. The $150 half-year statement credit tied to the same restaurants has its own page: [how the Sapphire Reserve dining credit works](/chase-sapphire-reserve-dining-credit-how-it-works/).

## What the program is

Chase's benefit terms describe "exclusive access to primetime reservations and special events" at participating restaurants in select cities, offered through OpenTable. Chase's guide says the restaurants were chosen by The Infatuation, Chase and OpenTable together.

It is a booking benefit, not a discount. Nothing in Chase's terms lowers the bill, and you pay the restaurant as any guest would. Chase's guide calls making a reservation through the program complimentary, so there is no booking fee from Chase.

| Fact | Detail | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Where it is booked | OpenTable website, mobile app, or the benefit page on OpenTable | Chase terms |
| Runs through | June 30, 2030 | Chase terms |
| Restaurants | Not published by Chase; reported at 362 to 397 | The Points Guy |
| Cities | About 50 US cities and metro areas | The Points Guy, citing OpenTable |
| Fee to book | None from Chase | Chase guide |
| Wait for new cardmembers | Up to 4 business days after account opening | Chase terms |

## Which cards qualify

Chase's terms name three US-issued cards.

| Card | Reservation access | Dining statement credit |
|---|---|---|
| Chase Sapphire Reserve | Yes | Yes |
| J.P. Morgan Reserve | Yes | Yes |
| Sapphire Reserve for Business | Yes | No |
| Chase Sapphire Preferred | No | No |

Chase's guide says authorized users on an eligible account can also make reservations through the program. The Sapphire Preferred is not named in the terms. For how the two personal cards differ, see [Sapphire Preferred or Reserve for a light traveler](/sapphire-preferred-vs-reserve-light-traveler/).

## How to book

Chase's terms set out four steps.

1. Go to OpenTable.com or open the OpenTable app.
2. Sign in, or create a free OpenTable account.
3. Complete the eligibility check that verifies the card.
4. Add the eligible card to the OpenTable account.

After that, The Points Guy reports that a "Sapphire Reserve Exclusive Tables" banner appears on OpenTable's home page and leads to the held tables. Chase's account pages also link to OpenTable from the card's benefits section. A linked card does not need to be linked again unless it is removed.

OpenTable checks eligibility when the card is verified and then again once every 24 hours when you visit. A card that fails the first check can be stored and granted access later if it becomes eligible.

## How it relates to the dining credit

The two share a restaurant list and a name, but they are separate benefits.

- **Exclusive Tables** is about getting a table. It is used on OpenTable.
- **The dining credit** is about paying. Chase says the credit comes from paying with the card at a restaurant in the program.

The Points Guy states that a reservation made through Exclusive Tables is not required for the credit. The same guide also says the card must first be connected to OpenTable to activate the credit, while Chase's own article ties the credit only to paying with the card at a listed restaurant. Whether the link is strictly required for the credit is not confirmed. The dollar rules, exclusions and posting times are on the dining credit page, and the yearly sums are on [what the Reserve credits are worth](/chase-sapphire-reserve-credits-real-value/).

## Limits

- **Only listed restaurants.** Other OpenTable restaurants are not part of the program.
- **Held tables are not guaranteed.** Chase's terms say inventory not booked before the reservation day and time may be released to general OpenTable users. How many tables each restaurant holds is not confirmed.
- **Some bookings need the card.** Where a restaurant asks for card details or prepayment, the terms say the eligible Chase card stored in the OpenTable account must be used.
- **Coverage is uneven.** One Points Guy writer in a midsize city reported three nearby restaurants. Thrifty Traveler counted three in the Twin Cities.
- **Events.** Prices and how often special events run are not confirmed.
- **Responsibility.** The terms say OpenTable and Chase are not responsible for the dining experience itself.
- **Card status.** If the eligible card is no longer stored in the OpenTable account, a new eligibility check may be required.

OpenTable's own program page could not be loaded on November 26, 2026, so the city list here rests on The Points Guy's reading of it.

## Who should skip it

- Anyone in a city with no listed restaurant. The program has nothing to book there except on trips.
- Anyone who rarely eats at reservation-driven, higher-priced restaurants.
- Anyone holding only the Sapphire Preferred. It is not an eligible card.
- Anyone weighing the Reserve's annual fee on this benefit alone. Access to a table has no fixed dollar value; count the dining credit only if you would eat at a listed restaurant anyway.

## Quick answers

**Is Sapphire Reserve Exclusive Tables the same as the dining credit?**
No. Exclusive Tables is reservation access; the credit is a separate statement credit at the same restaurants.

**Where do you book Exclusive Tables?**
On OpenTable's website or app, after adding an eligible Reserve card to your OpenTable account.

**Does the Sapphire Reserve for Business get Exclusive Tables?**
Yes for reservation access. It does not get the dining statement credit.

## Sources

- [Chase: Sapphire offer and benefit terms](https://www.chase.com/personal/credit-cards/offerdetails/chasesapphire)
- [Chase: guide to Sapphire Reserve Exclusive Tables](https://www.chase.com/personal/credit-cards/education/basics/guide-to-chase-sapphire-reserve-exclusive-tables)
- [Chase: how to use the dining credit with Exclusive Tables](https://www.chase.com/personal/credit-cards/education/basics/how-to-use-dining-credit-chase-sapphire-reserve-exclusive-tables)
- [The Points Guy: Sapphire Reserve Exclusive Tables guide](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/chase-sapphire-reserve-exclusive-tables-guide/)
- [Thrifty Traveler: Sapphire Reserve dining credit](https://thriftytraveler.com/guides/credit-card/sapphire-reserve-dining-credit/)

# Which airport lounges does the Sapphire Reserve get you into, and what are the guest rules?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/chase-sapphire-reserve-lounge-access/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

The Sapphire Reserve gets you into Chase's own Sapphire Lounges at eight US airports, a partner lounge at Washington Dulles, more than 1,300 Priority Pass lounges worldwide, and some Air Canada lounges. You can bring two guests free to Sapphire and Priority Pass lounges; each extra guest is $27 a visit. Priority Pass airport restaurants are not included.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## Chase Sapphire Lounges by location

Chase's lounge page lists these as open today:

| Airport | Where | Hours on Chase's page |
|---|---|---|
| Boston (BOS) | Terminal B, near gate B40 | 5 a.m. to 11 p.m. |
| Dallas Fort Worth (DFW) | Terminal D, near gate D25 | 5 a.m. to 10 p.m. |
| Las Vegas (LAS) | Terminal 1, near gate C23 | 4:30 a.m. to 11 p.m. |
| New York JFK | Terminal 4, near gate A2 (run with Etihad) | 5 a.m. to 10 p.m. |
| New York LaGuardia (LGA) | Terminal B | 4:30 a.m. to 9:30 p.m. |
| Philadelphia (PHL) | Terminal D/E connector | 5 a.m. to 10 p.m. |
| Phoenix (PHX) | Terminal 4, near gate D11 | 4:30 a.m. to 10:30 p.m. |
| San Diego (SAN) | Terminal 2, near gates 46 and 47 | 5 a.m. to 10 p.m. |
| Washington Dulles (IAD) | Etihad Lounge, Concourse A, near gate A14 | 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. |

Los Angeles (LAX) is marked "coming soon" with no date. Upgraded Points also names Seattle, and AwardWallet mentions Miami as not confirmed; neither is on Chase's page. Sources count eight or nine lounges depending on how the two Etihad partner lounges are treated.

## The other lounges

- **Priority Pass:** more than 1,300 lounges worldwide. Since October 25, 2025, cardmembers are enrolled automatically. The digital card is in the Chase Mobile app under More, then Airport lounges.
- **Air Canada Maple Leaf Lounges and Air Canada Cafés:** with the Reserve card and a same-day boarding pass on a Star Alliance airline. Some lounges are excluded.

## Guest and entry rules

| Rule | Sapphire Lounges | Priority Pass lounges | Air Canada lounges |
|---|---|---|---|
| Free guests | 2 | 2 | 1 |
| Extra guests | $27 each per visit | $27 each per visit | $59 each per visit |
| What to show | Physical Reserve card and boarding pass | Digital or physical Priority Pass card and boarding pass | Reserve card and Star Alliance boarding pass |
| Authorized users | Own access | Own membership, with two guests each | Included |

Other rules on Chase's pages:

- Entry is within three hours of your scheduled departure. Several sites report that this is five hours for a connecting flight since August 2026; that detail was not confirmed on Chase's page.
- Lounges can refuse entry when full.

## What is not included

**Priority Pass restaurants.** Since July 1, 2024, Priority Pass memberships that come from Chase cards no longer include the meal credit at airport restaurants, cafés and markets. AwardWallet's September 2026 guide confirms this is still the case. Some other non-lounge experiences remain, such as certain spas, gaming lounges and the first hour at Minute Suites.

**The Sapphire Preferred.** The $95 card has no lounge access at all.

## A recent change that affects crowding

On August 15, 2026, the Sapphire Lounges left the Priority Pass and LoungeKey networks. People whose Priority Pass comes from another bank's card can no longer use them. Reserve cardholders keep full access with their card. Guides written before August still describe the old rule of one free visit a year.

## What it is worth

Count the airport visits you make in a year where a lounge in this network is in your terminal, and multiply by what you would otherwise spend there on food and drinks. Six visits at $25 each is $150. Set that beside [the credits you would really use](/chase-sapphire-reserve-credits-real-value/) and the $795 fee.

## Who should skip it

- Anyone who flies fewer than four or five times a year. See [Preferred or Reserve for a light traveler](/sapphire-preferred-vs-reserve-light-traveler/).
- Anyone whose home airport has no lounge in the network, or only one in the wrong terminal.
- Anyone who mainly wanted the Priority Pass restaurant credit. It is gone on Chase cards.
- Families of five or more. The third guest onward costs $27 each, every visit.

## Quick answers

**How many guests can I bring with a Sapphire Reserve?**
Two free at Sapphire Lounges and Priority Pass lounges. Each extra guest is $27 per visit.

**Does the Sapphire Reserve Priority Pass work at airport restaurants?**
No. Chase removed that on July 1, 2024.

**Do authorized users get lounge access?**
Yes on the personal Reserve. Each authorized user gets their own access and can bring two guests. The card costs $195 a year per authorized user.

# How does the Chase Sapphire Reserve StubHub credit work, and what counts?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/chase-sapphire-reserve-stubhub-credit-how-it-works/
Facts checked: 2026-11-22
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

The Sapphire Reserve pays back up to $150 from January to June and up to $150 from July to December on purchases made directly with StubHub or viagogo, through December 31, 2027. You activate it once in your Chase account before buying, and whatever you do not use in a half-year is gone.

This page is information, not financial advice. The card's other credits are on [the full credits page](/chase-sapphire-reserve-credits-real-value/); this page covers only StubHub.

## The rules

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Amount | Up to $150 January 1 to June 30; up to $150 July 1 to December 31 |
| End date | Through December 31, 2027 |
| Cards | Personal Sapphire Reserve and J.P. Morgan Reserve; Chase's terms do not name the Sapphire Reserve for Business |
| Activation | One time, on chase.com or in the Chase app |
| Minimum purchase | None |
| Split | Can be spread over several purchases in a half-year |
| Rollover | None |
| Authorized users | Their purchases on the account count toward the same $150 |

## Activation

Chase's terms call for a one-time activation. Chase's own guide says purchases made before activation do not qualify. AwardWallet describes the path as Benefits and travel, then Benefits, then the StubHub credit tile.

Doctor of Credit mentions reader reports of a credit after late activation. That conflicts with Chase's guide.

## What counts

- Tickets bought on stubhub.com, viagogo.com or either app, paid with the card. Chase's guide names sports, concerts and theater.
- viagogo counts the same way as StubHub and shares the same $150 limit.
- Parking passes sold on StubHub: not confirmed. Chase's terms do not mention them.

## What does not count

- Gift cards. Chase's terms exclude them.
- Events in the United Kingdom. Chase's terms say these are sent to stubhub.co.uk, a separate company, and do not qualify.
- A purchase that is later returned, canceled or changed. Chase can take the credit back, and can also do so if the account closes within 90 days of a credit.

## Do fees and taxes count?

Chase's terms do not say. Doctor of Credit reports that they do, with the example of a $130 ticket that comes to $151 after fees and receives the full $150. AwardWallet's examples also use order totals. Treat this as reported, not as written policy.

## When the credit posts

| Source | Stated timing |
|---|---|
| Chase's terms | Within 3 business days, up to 4 weeks |
| Chase's guide | One to two billing cycles |
| The Points Guy | Reports of about a day |
| Doctor of Credit | Most within a few days |

Each period ends at 11:59 PM Eastern on its last day. The Points Guy reports a June 30 purchase that posted July 1 and was counted in the second half.

Thrifty Traveler says the purchase earns the card's usual 1 point per dollar.

## The sums for one ticket purchase a year

These are resale sites, so a ticket can cost more than its face price, and fees are added.

| Reader | Yearly value |
|---|---|
| Buys no resale tickets | $0 |
| One purchase a year, $150 or more | $150 |
| One purchase a year, $90 | $90 |
| One purchase in each half, $150 or more each time | $300 |
| Buys only to use the credit, $200 each half | $300 back on $400 of new spending |

Someone who buys once a year gets at most half the listed $300. The last row is a cost of $100, not a gain of $300.

## Who should skip it

- Anyone who does not go to ticketed events. This credit is then worth $0 toward the $795 fee.
- Anyone who buys from the venue or team at face price and would pay more on a resale site.
- Anyone going to events in the United Kingdom only.
- Anyone who will not track two deadlines a year.

For a credit on the same half-year schedule, see [how the dining credit works](/chase-sapphire-reserve-dining-credit-how-it-works/).

## Quick answers

**Does viagogo count as well as StubHub?**
Yes. Chase's terms cover purchases made directly with either one, under the same $150 limit.

**Does unused credit from January to June carry into July?**
No. Each half-year's $150 expires at the end of its period.

**Do StubHub gift cards trigger the credit?**
No. Chase's terms exclude gift cards.

## Sources

- [Chase: Sapphire Reserve card page](https://creditcards.chase.com/rewards-credit-cards/sapphire/reserve)
- [Chase: Sapphire offer and benefit terms](https://www.chase.com/personal/credit-cards/offerdetails/chasesapphire)
- [Chase: how to use the StubHub credit](https://www.chase.com/personal/credit-cards/education/rewards-benefits/how-to-use-the-$300-stubhub-credit-with-chase-sapphire-reserve)
- [The Points Guy: StubHub credit examples](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/chase-sapphire-reserve-stubhub-credit-examples/)
- [Doctor of Credit: the StubHub credit on the Sapphire Reserve](https://doctorofcredit.com/maximizing-the-stubhub-300-credit-on-chase-sapphire-reserve-card)
- [AwardWallet: Sapphire Reserve StubHub credit](https://awardwallet.com/credit-cards/chase-ultimate-rewards/sapphire-reserve-stubhub-credit/)
- [Thrifty Traveler: Sapphire Reserve StubHub credit](https://thriftytraveler.com/guides/credit-card/chase-sapphire-reserve-stubhub-credit/)

# How does the Sapphire Reserve credit for The Edit hotels work, and what are the catches?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/chase-sapphire-reserve-the-edit-credit-how-it-works/
Facts checked: 2026-11-21
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

The Sapphire Reserve gives up to $250 back on a prepaid stay of two nights or more at a hotel in Chase's The Edit collection, on up to two separate bookings per calendar year, for $500 in total. The catches are the two-night minimum, the need to prepay, hotel prices that often run $500 a night or more, and the fact that one booking can never earn more than $250.

This page is information, not financial advice. The Reserve's other credits are on [the full credits page](/chase-sapphire-reserve-credits-real-value/); this page covers only The Edit.

## The rules

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Amount | Up to $250 per booking, up to $500 per calendar year |
| Period | January 1 to December 31; both credits usable at any time since 1/1/2026 |
| Stay | Two nights or more |
| Payment | Prepaid "Pay Now" rate through Chase Travel, on the Reserve |
| Who can book | The cardmember or an authorized user; one $500 cap per account |
| Points | The credited part earns none; the rest earns 8x |

Before 2026 the credit was split by half-year.

## What comes with an Edit stay

The Points Guy lists the on-property benefits as daily breakfast for two, a $100 property credit per booking, a room upgrade and early check-in or late checkout when available, and Wi-Fi where offered. Upgraded Points notes that back-to-back bookings at the same hotel get one set of benefits, not two.

The Points Guy puts the collection at more than 1,000 properties; Thrifty Traveler counted 1,371 in November 2025 and notes the list rotates.

## The catches

**Price.** These are upscale hotels. Thrifty Traveler's examples run from about $500 to over $600 a night. NerdWallet, seen in a search summary, found only about a third of the rates it checked were under $500 a night.

**Prepaying.** The credit needs a Pay Now rate. Cancellation terms vary by hotel and rate and were not read for this page; check them before paying. Chase can reverse the credit if the booking is canceled, returned or changed, or if the account closes within 90 days of the credit.

**Two bookings, not one.** A single $900 stay earns $250, not $500.

**The portal price.** The Points Guy notes prices in Chase Travel may be higher than booking direct. Compare the same room and dates on the hotel's site.

**Hotel loyalty.** Thrifty Traveler says hotel points and elite night credits are earned in most cases. The Points Guy notes exceptions, such as Small Luxury Hotels bookings earning no Hilton points.

**Timing.** The price is not cut at booking. Chase's terms say the credit posts within 3 business days and may take up to 4 weeks. The Points Guy says up to eight weeks. A purchase delayed in processing near December 31 can fall into the next year.

Whether a stay paid with points triggers the credit is not confirmed.

## A sample sum

An illustration, not a typical result:

| | Two nights at $450 a night |
|---|---|
| Prepaid price | $900 |
| Edit credit | $250 |
| Net cost | $650 |
| Points on the $650 at 8x | 5,200 |
| On-property | Breakfast for two, $100 property credit |

If you would have paid $900 for that hotel anyway, the credit is worth the full $250. If you would have stayed somewhere for $300 a night, you spent $50 more than planned to use it.

## Stacking in 2026

Through December 31, 2026, the Reserve also has a one-time credit of up to $250 for prepaid stays of two nights or more at selected brands in Chase Travel: IHG, Montage, Pendry, Omni, Virgin Hotels, Minor Hotels and Pan Pacific. The Points Guy reports both credits can apply to one reservation when a hotel qualifies for each. Upgraded Points describes that second credit as annual; the other sources say it is one-time and ends this year.

## Who should skip it

- Anyone who would not pay $400 or more a night for a hotel. Count this credit as $0 when adding up the card.
- Anyone who takes one-night stays, or needs flexible, pay-at-hotel rates.
- Anyone whose usual destinations have no Edit hotels. Search Chase Travel first.
- Anyone who gets more from booking direct with elite status than from the breakfast and property credit here.

## Quick answers

**Can one stay use the full $500?**
No. Each booking gets up to $250. The full $500 takes two separate prepaid stays of two nights or more.

**Does the credit follow the calendar year or the account year?**
The calendar year, January 1 to December 31. Unused credit does not carry over.

**Do authorized users get their own $500?**
No. Their bookings can trigger the credit, but the account has one $500 cap.

## Sources

- [Chase: Sapphire offer and benefit terms](https://www.chase.com/personal/credit-cards/offerdetails/chasesapphire)
- [The Points Guy: stacking the Sapphire Reserve hotel credits](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/stacking-chase-sapphire-reserve-hotel-credits-the-edit/)
- [The Points Guy: Sapphire Reserve credit for The Edit](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/chase-sapphire-reserve-the-edit-credit/)
- [Thrifty Traveler: The Edit by Chase Travel](https://thriftytraveler.com/guides/credit-card/the-edit-by-chase-travel/)
- [Upgraded Points: Sapphire Reserve hotel credit updates for 2026](https://upgradedpoints.com/news/chase-sapphire-reserve-hotel-credit-updates-2026/)
- [NerdWallet: Sapphire Reserve hotel credit for The Edit](https://www.nerdwallet.com/article/travel/chase-sapphire-reserve-the-edit-hotel-credit)
