# Chase Sapphire Reserve or Capital One Venture X: which premium card costs less to keep?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/chase-sapphire-reserve-vs-capital-one-venture-x/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

The Venture X costs less to keep. After its $300 travel credit and 10,000 anniversary miles its $395 fee nets to about zero, while the Sapphire Reserve's $795 fee nets to $495 after its $300 travel credit, and the rest has to come from narrower credits.

This page is information, not financial advice. Terms change, so check each issuer's pages before deciding.

## Side by side

| | Sapphire Reserve | Capital One Venture X |
|---|---|---|
| Annual fee | $795 | $395 |
| Authorized user | $195 each, with lounge access | Free; $125 each for lounge access |
| Travel credit | Up to $300 a year on any travel purchase | Up to $300 a year, Capital One Travel bookings only |
| Other main credits | The Edit hotels $500, dining $300, StubHub $300, Lyft $120, DoorDash promos, Peloton $120, Apple TV and Music | 10,000 miles each account anniversary |
| Portal bookings | 8x on Chase Travel | 10x hotels and rental cars, 5x flights and vacation rentals |
| Flights and hotels booked direct | 4x | 2x |
| Dining | 3x | 2x |
| Everything else | 1x | 2x |
| Lounges | Sapphire Lounges, 1,300+ Priority Pass lounges, some Air Canada lounges | Capital One Lounges and Landings, 1,300+ Priority Pass lounges |
| Lounge guests | Two free; extra guests $27 each | $45 per adult at Capital One Lounges, $35 at Priority Pass |
| Transfer partners | 14, including United, Southwest and Hyatt at 1 to 1 | 15+; JetBlue is the only US airline, no Hyatt |

Credit amounts are "up to" figures. The Reserve's dining and StubHub credits are split by half-year, and its Lyft and Peloton credits are monthly.

## The cost to keep each card

**Venture X:** $395, minus $300 of travel booked through Capital One Travel, minus 10,000 miles worth $100 against travel. That is minus $5 from the second year. The miles arrive at the first anniversary.

**Sapphire Reserve:** $795 minus $300 is $495. The travel credit is the easy one, since it applies to travel purchases in general, with no portal needed. To clear the other $495 a reader needs some of these, at prices they would have paid anyway:

| Reserve credit | Yearly amount | Limit |
|---|---|---|
| The Edit hotels | $500 | $250 per prepaid stay of two nights or more, Chase's own hotel list |
| Dining | $300 | Restaurants in the Exclusive Tables list on OpenTable only |
| StubHub | $300 | Through the end of 2027 |
| Lyft | $120 | $10 a month, through September 2027 |

The page on [what the Reserve credits are worth](/chase-sapphire-reserve-credits-real-value/) goes through each one.

## Where the Reserve earns the difference back

- **Guests in lounges.** The Reserve admits two guests free. Since February 1, 2026 the Venture X charges for each one. A couple with one child making four lounge visits a year pays about $280 in guest fees on the Venture X: $35 per guest at Priority Pass lounges, or $45 per adult and $25 per child at Capital One's own.
- **Travel booked direct.** $10,000 of flights and hotels booked with the airline or hotel earns 40,000 points on the Reserve and 20,000 miles on the Venture X.
- **Hyatt, United and Southwest.** The Reserve transfers to all three at 1 to 1. Capital One miles go to none of them.
- **Points Boost.** Reserve points can be worth up to 2 cents on selected Chase Travel bookings. See [how Points Boost works](/chase-points-boost-explained/).

## Where the Venture X stays ahead

- **General spending.** $30,000 of purchases outside travel and dining earns 60,000 miles on the Venture X and 30,000 points on the Reserve.
- **A solo traveler.** No guest fees to pay, and the same Priority Pass network.
- **Low effort.** One portal booking a year covers the fee. Nothing is monthly.

## Which pattern favors which card

- **One traveler, a few trips, mixed spending:** Venture X.
- **Family or couple using lounges together:** Sapphire Reserve, if the guest fees and credits used add up to more than the $400 fee gap.
- **Hyatt stays on points, or heavy direct airfare:** Sapphire Reserve.
- **Would not change where they eat or stay to use credits:** Venture X.

## Who should skip both

- Anyone who carries a balance.
- Anyone who visits a lounge once or twice a year. A $95 card costs less; see [Preferred or Reserve for a light traveler](/sapphire-preferred-vs-reserve-light-traveler/).
- For the Venture X: anyone unwilling to book through a card portal, since both of its fee offsets depend on travel.
- For the Reserve: anyone with five or more new personal cards in 24 months, whom Chase generally declines.

Welcome offers on both cards vary and change, so they are not in these sums.

## Quick answers

**Which card is cheaper after the travel credit?**
The Venture X. It nets to about zero with the anniversary miles; the Reserve nets to $495 before its other credits.

**Which card is kinder to guests in lounges?**
The Sapphire Reserve. Two guests enter free. The Venture X charges $35 to $45 per adult guest.

**Do both cards use Priority Pass?**
Yes, both include a Priority Pass membership with 1,300+ lounges. Priority Pass restaurants are not included on the Reserve.

## Sources

- [Chase: Sapphire Reserve card page](https://creditcards.chase.com/rewards-credit-cards/sapphire/reserve)
- [Chase: Sapphire lounges](https://www.chase.com/sapphire-cards/lounges)
- [Capital One: Venture X card page](https://www.capitalone.com/credit-cards/venture-x/)
- [The Points Guy: Capital One Venture X review](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/reviews/capital-one-venture-x-card-review/)
- [One Mile at a Time: Capital One Venture X review](https://onemileatatime.com/reviews/credit-cards/capital-one/capital-one-venture-x-card/)
- [One Mile at a Time: Venture X lounge access changes](https://onemileatatime.com/news/capital-one-venture-x-lounge-access-changes/)
- [The Points Guy: Capital One transfer partners](https://thepointsguy.com/loyalty-programs/capital-one-transfer-partners/)
- [AwardWallet: Chase to Hyatt transfer ratios](https://awardwallet.com/credit-cards/chase-ultimate-rewards/chase-to-hyatt-transfer/)

# Chase Sapphire Reserve or Citi Strata Elite: which premium card costs less to keep?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/chase-sapphire-reserve-vs-citi-strata-elite/
Facts checked: 2026-11-21
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

On the fee alone the Citi Strata Elite costs less, at $595 a year against $795, but the Sapphire Reserve's $300 credit works on any travel and brings it to $495. The Strata Elite gets to $295 only with a two-night hotel stay booked through Citi Travel, so it is the cheaper card to keep for readers who would make that booking anyway.

This page is information, not financial advice. Terms change, so check each issuer's pages before deciding.

## Side by side

| | Chase Sapphire Reserve | Citi Strata Elite |
|---|---|---|
| Annual fee | $795 | $595 |
| Authorized user | $195 each | $75 each |
| Travel credit | Up to $300 each account year on any travel | None on travel in general |
| Hotel credit | Up to $500 a calendar year: $250 per prepaid two-night stay at The Edit hotels | Up to $300 off one stay of two nights or more through Citi Travel, once a calendar year |
| Other credits | Dining $300, StubHub $300, DoorDash promos up to $35 a month, Lyft $120, Peloton $120, Apple TV and Apple Music | Splurge credit $200 on two chosen brands; Blacklane car service $100 each half-year |
| Portal bookings | 8x through Chase Travel | 12x on hotels, car rentals and attractions and 6x on flights through Citi Travel |
| Flights and hotels booked direct | 4x | 1.5x |
| Dining | 3x | 3x; 6x on Friday and Saturday from 6 PM to 6 AM Eastern |
| Everything else | 1x | 1.5x |
| Lounges | Sapphire Lounges at eight US airports; 1,300+ Priority Pass lounges | 1,500+ Priority Pass lounges; four Admirals Club passes a calendar year |
| Lounge guests | Two free; $27 each after that | Two with Priority Pass |
| Transfer partners | 16 programs, with United, Southwest and Hyatt at 1:1 | American Airlines at 1:1, JetBlue, Virgin Atlantic, Cathay Pacific, EVA, Choice and others |
| Global Entry or TSA PreCheck | Up to $120 every four years | Up to $120 every four years |

The two issuers print different Priority Pass lounge counts, 1,300+ and 1,500+. The Splurge credit brands are 1stDibs, American Airlines, Best Buy, Future Personal Training and Live Nation.

## The Strata Elite sum

- Fee: $595.
- Hotel benefit: $300, taken off the price when a two-night stay is booked through Citi Travel. Leaves $295.
- Splurge credit: $200, for example on American Airlines or Best Buy purchases. Leaves $95.
- Blacklane: $200 in two halves. Leaves minus $105, but only for a reader who would hire a chauffeured car twice a year.

Citigold clients get a further $145 credit each year, which brings the starting fee to $450.

A reader who uses the hotel benefit and the Splurge credit, and ignores Blacklane, keeps the card for $95 a year.

## The Reserve sum

- Fee: $795.
- Travel credit: $300, applied to any travel charge. Leaves $495.
- The Edit: $250 per prepaid two-night stay, up to two a year. One stay leaves $245; two leave minus $5.
- Dining: $150 in each half of the year at Exclusive Tables restaurants on OpenTable. Used in full with one Edit stay, it leaves minus $55.

A reader who uses only the travel credit keeps the card for $495 a year. The page on [what the Reserve credits are worth](/chase-sapphire-reserve-credits-real-value/) goes through each one.

## Which spending pattern favors which card

| Pattern | Lower cost to keep |
|---|---|
| Books one two-night hotel stay a year through Citi Travel | Strata Elite, at $295 against $495 |
| Would never book through Citi Travel or use the Splurge brands | Reserve, at $495 against $595 |
| Books two luxury hotel stays a year and eats at listed restaurants | Reserve, at about minus $305 on paper |
| Shops at Best Buy or flies American, books one portal hotel | Strata Elite, at $95 |
| Adds two authorized users | Strata Elite: $150 against $390 |

Earning also differs:

- **Flights and hotels booked direct:** Reserve, at 4x against 1.5x. On $8,000 a year that is 32,000 points against 12,000.
- **Everyday spending outside travel and dining:** Strata Elite, at 1.5x against 1x. On $20,000 that is 30,000 points against 20,000.
- **Flies American:** Strata Elite. Of these two, only Citi moves points to American AAdvantage, and the card adds four Admirals Club passes.
- **Flies United or Southwest, or stays at Hyatt:** Reserve. None of the three is a Citi partner in the lists read.
- **Uses lounges at Boston, Dallas Fort Worth, JFK, LaGuardia, Las Vegas, Philadelphia, Phoenix or San Diego:** Reserve, for its own lounges. Citi has none. See [Reserve lounge access](/chase-sapphire-reserve-lounge-access/).

Trip delay, trip cancellation and rental car cover amounts for the Strata Elite were not confirmed in the pages read, so travel insurance is left out of this comparison.

## Who should skip both

- Anyone who carries a balance. Interest costs more than either card returns.
- Anyone who travels once or twice a year. The $95 [Sapphire Preferred or Citi Strata Premier](/chase-sapphire-preferred-vs-citi-strata-premier/) costs less.
- For the Strata Elite: anyone who books hotels direct for loyalty benefits and would not use Citi Travel.
- For the Reserve: anyone who would use only the travel credit and rarely sees a lounge. $495 a year is the cost.

The [Venture X comparison](/chase-sapphire-reserve-vs-capital-one-venture-x/) covers a third premium card at $395. Welcome offers on both cards vary by applicant and change, so they are left out of the sums.

## Quick answers

**Which card has the lower annual fee?**
The Citi Strata Elite, at $595 against $795 for the Sapphire Reserve.

**Does the Strata Elite have a general travel credit like the Reserve's $300?**
No. Its $300 hotel benefit applies only to one stay of two nights or more booked through Citi Travel.

**Do Citi points transfer to American Airlines?**
Yes, at 1:1 from the Strata Elite. Chase points do not transfer to American.

- [The Points Guy: Citi Strata Elite review](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/reviews/citi-strata-elite-review)

# Can you upgrade a Sapphire Preferred to a Reserve or downgrade to a Freedom card, and what happens to points and the bonus?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/chase-sapphire-upgrade-downgrade-product-change/
Facts checked: 2026-11-21
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

Yes: after a year with the card, Chase lets a Sapphire Preferred holder switch to a Sapphire Reserve, or down to a Freedom Flex or Freedom Unlimited, without a new application. A product change pays no welcome bonus on the new card, and after a downgrade to a Freedom card your points can no longer move to airline and hotel partners unless you hold another card that allows it.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## The two directions

| | Upgrade to Reserve | Downgrade to a Freedom card |
|---|---|---|
| Wait | At least a year with the Preferred (Chase) | Typically 12 months (The Points Guy) |
| Other condition | Credit limit of at least $10,000 | Options vary by account |
| How | Online (24 to 48 hours), phone or branch | Phone; ask for a "product change" |
| Annual fee after | $795 | $0 |
| Welcome bonus on the new card | No | No |
| Credit check | Not stated by Chase | Generally none |
| Transfer partners | Kept; Hyatt becomes 1:1 | Lost unless another eligible card is held |

The Points Guy adds that the card number, credit line and due date typically stay the same. A product change is usually not reported as a new account, so it does not add to your [5/24 count](/chase-5-24-rule-explained/).

## Upgrading: the bonus you give up

Chase's own page says people who switch from the Preferred are not eligible for the Reserve's new-cardmember offer. That offer goes only to new accounts.

This matters more since two rule changes:

- Since the 2025 relaunch, Chase lets one person hold both Sapphire cards.
- Since January 2026, holding a Preferred does not block a first bonus on the Reserve.

So there are two routes to a Reserve. Offers vary by applicant and change.

| | Product change | New application |
|---|---|---|
| Welcome bonus | None | Possible, if you never had the Reserve's bonus |
| Hard credit check | Generally none | Yes |
| Counts toward 5/24 | Usually not | Yes |
| Preferred account | Becomes the Reserve | Stays open, $95 a year, unless changed later |

The rules on who can get a bonus are on the [Sapphire bonus eligibility page](/chase-sapphire-bonus-eligibility-2026/). Chase's wording says a bonus may not be available to someone who previously held the card, and sources differ on whether a Reserve held through an upgrade would count against a later Reserve bonus.

## Downgrading: what happens to points

The guides read treat the points as staying with the account through a product change. A Chase page saying so was not found, so that is not confirmed.

What changes is what the points can do. The Freedom cards earn the same kind of Chase points, but alone they cannot send them to airline or hotel programs. The Points Guy advises transferring or redeeming before a downgrade, unless you keep another card that can transfer.

Three ways people handle it:

1. Transfer to a partner first. Transfers cannot be reversed.
2. Move the points to another transfer-capable card of yours or a household member's. See [how combining points works](/chase-sapphire-preferred-with-freedom-cards-combine-points/).
3. Accept 1 cent a point as cash back on the Freedom card.

In Chase Travel, the Freedom cards get Points Boost of up to 1.1 cents on selected hotels, against up to 1.5 cents (some sources say 1.75) on the Preferred.

## The annual fee

Sources disagree on refunds.

- The Points Guy's August 2026 guide says Chase may prorate or refund part of the fee if you downgrade shortly after it posts.
- The Points Guy's June 2025 article says not to expect a prorated refund on a downgrade, and that Chase typically refunds the fee only if you cancel within 30 days of it posting.
- Doctor of Credit also reports the 30-day window for cancellations.

Ask the agent what will be refunded before you agree.

## Other things that change

- **The earned bonus.** A welcome bonus you already earned on the Preferred still counts as earned after a downgrade, so the card's once-per-lifetime bonus is used. Whether Chase takes back a bonus after a very early downgrade is not confirmed.

Which cards a Reserve can be downgraded to is not confirmed.

## Who should skip it

- Anyone eligible for a Reserve welcome bonus who is under 5/24. An upgrade gives that bonus up.
- Anyone with a points balance meant for Hyatt or airline transfers who is about to downgrade with no other transfer-capable card.

## Quick answers

**Do you get the Reserve welcome bonus when upgrading from the Preferred?**
No. Chase says cardmembers who switch are not eligible for the new-cardmember offer.

**Do points disappear after a downgrade to a Freedom card?**
The guides say they stay with the account, but they can no longer be transferred to partners from that card.

**How long must you hold the Preferred before changing it?**
Chase says at least a year before an upgrade. Downgrades typically need 12 months too.

## Sources

- [Chase: switching from Sapphire Preferred to Sapphire Reserve](https://www.chase.com/personal/credit-cards/education/chase-cards/upgrading-to-sapphire-reserve-from-sapphire-preferred)
- [The Points Guy: how to downgrade a Chase credit card](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/chase/downgrade-chase-credit-card/)
- [The Points Guy: canceling the Sapphire Reserve and fee refunds](https://thepointsguy.com/news/cancel-chase-sapphire-reserve-card)
- [Doctor of Credit: annual fee refund rules by issuer](https://doctorofcredit.com/annual-fee-refund-rules-for-each-card-issuer)
- [Chase: Sapphire offer and benefit terms](https://www.chase.com/personal/credit-cards/offerdetails/chasesapphire)
- [The Points Guy: Sapphire bonus eligibility changes in 2026](https://thepointsguy.com/news/chase-sapphire-bonus-eligibility-changes-2026)
- [The Points Guy: Chase 5/24 rule guide](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/chase/ultimate-guide-chase-5-24-rule/)
- [The Points Guy: the Sapphire bonus pop-up and past bonuses](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/chase-sapphire-preferred-lifetime-bonus-popup/)

# What counts toward the Chase Sapphire welcome-bonus spending requirement, and when do the points post?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/chase-sapphire-welcome-bonus-spending-requirement/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

Purchases of products and services made by you or an authorized user count toward the Chase Sapphire spending requirement. The annual fee, interest, balance transfers, cash advances and cash-like transactions such as money orders do not. Chase asks you to allow 6 to 8 weeks after qualifying for the points to post, though reviewers report they often arrive when the next statement closes.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## The requirement on November 20, 2026

| Card | Public bonus stated | Purchases needed | Time allowed | Annual fee |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sapphire Preferred | 75,000 points | $5,000 | First 3 months from account opening | $95 |
| Sapphire Reserve | 100,000 points | $6,000 | First 3 months | $795 |

These are the offers on Chase's pages on that date. Offers change, and the bonus may not be available to you. See [who is eligible](/chase-sapphire-bonus-eligibility-2026/).

On average that is about $1,667 a month for the Preferred and $2,000 a month for the Reserve.

## What counts and what does not

Chase's Sapphire Preferred page defines purchases as when "you, or an authorized user" use the card to buy products and services.

| Transaction | Counts? |
|---|---|
| Everyday purchases of products and services | Yes |
| Purchases by an authorized user on your account | Yes |
| The annual fee and any other fee | No |
| Interest | No |
| Balance transfers | No |
| Cash advances | No |
| Traveler's checks, foreign currency, money orders | No |
| Other cash-like transactions | No |
| Unauthorized or fraudulent charges | No |
| Gift card purchases | Not confirmed |

Chase's list of cash-like transactions is longer than the part read for this page, so read the offer details on the application for the full wording. Whether a gift card bought at a store counts is not confirmed in the terms read. Do not build a plan on it.

Purchases covered by a card credit, such as the Preferred's hotel credit, are a separate question from the bonus. Chase's terms say the first $100 of those hotel purchases earns no points. Whether they still count toward the $5,000 is not confirmed.

## Refunds

The Points Guy states that a refunded amount is typically deducted from progress toward a spending requirement. One Mile at a Time gives the same warning. A return near the end of the three months can leave you short, so a small margin over the target helps.

## When the three months start

Chase's wording is the first 3 months from account opening. That points to the day the account is opened and not the day the card arrives in the mail. No source read spells out the exact day, so ask Chase for your deadline.

## When the points post

| Source | Timing |
|---|---|
| Chase's terms | Allow 6 to 8 weeks after qualifying |
| Upgraded Points (August 2026) | Often when the statement closes after you qualify; one editor's points posted about three weeks after qualifying |
| Same source | Qualifying just before a statement closes can push the bonus to the following statement |

Chase's terms add that the account must be open and not in default when the bonus is paid.

The 6 to 8 weeks matter if you want the points for a specific trip. Count back from the date you need to book: time to reach the spending, plus up to 8 weeks.

## The sum to do first

| Your normal card spending per month | Three-month total | Reaches $5,000 (Preferred)? | Reaches $6,000 (Reserve)? |
|---|---|---|---|
| $1,000 | $3,000 | No, $2,000 short | No, $3,000 short |
| $1,500 | $4,500 | No, $500 short | No, $1,500 short |
| $1,700 | $5,100 | Yes, with little margin | No, $900 short |
| $2,100 | $6,300 | Yes | Yes, with little margin |

Count only spending you would do anyway, or a large purchase you had already planned. Adding an authorized user at no fee on the Preferred lets a household member's purchases count on the same account.

## Who should skip it

- Anyone whose normal spending will not reach the figure in three months without extra purchases.
- Anyone who would carry a balance to get there. Interest does not count, and it can cost more than the points are worth.
- Anyone relying on balance transfers, cash advances or money orders. None of them count.
- Anyone who needs the points sooner than the spending time plus 8 weeks.
- Anyone who has already earned that card's bonus. See [the eligibility rules](/chase-sapphire-bonus-eligibility-2026/).

Related: [a first-year plan for the Sapphire Preferred](/chase-sapphire-preferred-first-year-plan/) and [how a referral link works](/chase-sapphire-preferred-referral-bonus-how-it-works/).

## Quick answers

**Does the annual fee count toward the Sapphire spending requirement?**
No. Chase's terms exclude fees of any kind, including the annual fee.

**Do authorized user purchases count?**
Yes. Chase defines purchases as those made by you or an authorized user on the account.

**How long until the bonus points show up?**
Chase says to allow 6 to 8 weeks after qualifying. Reviewers report they often post when the next statement closes.

## Sources

- [Chase: Sapphire Preferred card page](https://creditcards.chase.com/rewards-credit-cards/sapphire/preferred)
- [Chase: Sapphire Reserve card page](https://creditcards.chase.com/rewards-credit-cards/sapphire/reserve)
- [Upgraded Points: when the Sapphire Preferred bonus posts](https://upgradedpoints.com/news/when-does-chase-sapphire-preferred-sign-up-bonus-post/)
- [The Points Guy: how refunds affect a welcome bonus](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/refunds-hurting-sign-up-bonus)
- [One Mile at a Time: do annual fees count toward minimum spend](https://onemileatatime.com/do-annual-fees-count-towards-credit-card-minimum-spend/)

# Did Chase change the Hyatt transfer rate, and which Sapphire card still transfers 1:1?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/chase-to-hyatt-transfer-change-2026/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

Yes. From a Sapphire Preferred, 4 Chase points now become 3 World of Hyatt points, where it used to be 1 for 1. The Sapphire Reserve still transfers to Hyatt at 1:1.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## What changed and when

| Date | What happened |
|---|---|
| June 15, 2026 | New Sapphire Preferred cardholders approved from this date got the 4:3 Hyatt rate from the start |
| September 30, 2026 | Last day of 1:1 for existing Sapphire Preferred cardholders |
| October 1, 2026 | Existing Sapphire Preferred cardholders moved to 4:3 |

The Ink Business Preferred and the older Ink Plus moved to 4:3 as well.

Only Hyatt changed. Reports say the other airline and hotel partners still transfer 1:1 from the Preferred, including United and Southwest.

## Which card gets which rate

| Card | Chase points to Hyatt points |
|---|---|
| Sapphire Preferred | 4 to 3 |
| Ink Business Preferred | 4 to 3 |
| Sapphire Reserve | 1 to 1 |
| Sapphire Reserve for Business | 1 to 1 |
| J.P. Morgan Reserve | 1 to 1 |

Chase's public Sapphire Preferred page lists World of Hyatt as a partner but does not show the ratio. The figures here come from The Points Guy, AwardWallet and NerdWallet, which agree with each other.

## What it costs in points

At 4:3, the same Hyatt night takes one third more Chase points.

| Hyatt points needed | From a Sapphire Reserve | From a Sapphire Preferred |
|---|---|---|
| 12,000 | 12,000 | 16,000 |
| 25,000 | 25,000 | 33,334 |
| 40,000 | 40,000 | 53,334 |
| 60,000 | 60,000 | 80,000 |

The Preferred figures are the Hyatt amount multiplied by four thirds. The minimum transfer size and step were not confirmed in the sources read, so the amount you must send may round up further.

Another way to look at it: a Chase point moved to Hyatt from a Preferred is now worth 75% of what it was. If you valued a Hyatt point at 2 cents, a Preferred point sent there is worth 1.5 cents. That is the same as the usual top [Points Boost value](/chase-points-boost-explained/) on the Preferred, so the gap between transferring and booking through Chase Travel is smaller than it was.

## If you hold both cards

Chase lets you move points between your own cards. If you have a Sapphire Reserve as well as a Preferred, you can move the Preferred's points into the Reserve account and transfer to Hyatt from there at 1:1. Both AwardWallet and The Points Guy describe this.

That only helps if the Reserve makes sense for you on its own. The Reserve costs $795 a year against $95 for the Preferred. The $700 gap is a lot to pay for a transfer rate. As a rough test, at 2 cents per Hyatt point you would need to move more than 140,000 points a year to Hyatt before the better rate alone covered $700. Most people will decide on [the Reserve's credits](/chase-sapphire-reserve-credits-real-value/) and not on this.

## Things to know before any Hyatt transfer

- Transfers cannot be reversed. Once points are in Hyatt, they stay there.
- Transfers are instant in most cases, so there is rarely a reason to move points before you have found a room.
- Hyatt points expire after 24 months with no qualifying activity.
- Hyatt changed its award chart in May 2026. Each category now has five price levels, so the same hotel can cost very different amounts on different nights. Check the price for your dates first.

## Who should skip it

- Sapphire Preferred holders who rarely stay at Hyatt. Other partners still transfer 1:1, and Chase Travel with a Boost may come close.
- Anyone thinking of the Reserve only for the Hyatt rate, unless they move a large number of points each year.
- Anyone with no specific booking in mind. Moving points on a guess locks them into one program.

## Quick answers

**Is the Sapphire Preferred to Hyatt rate still 1:1?**
No. It has been 4:3 since October 1, 2026, and since June 15, 2026 for cards opened from that date.

**Did other Chase partners change too?**
Reports say no. Only Hyatt moved, and only from the Preferred and Ink cards listed above.

**Can I get 1:1 by moving points to a Reserve first?**
Yes, if the Reserve account is yours. Points moved there transfer to Hyatt at 1:1.

## Sources

- [The Points Guy: Chase to Hyatt ratio change on October 1](https://thepointsguy.com/news/chase-hyatt-transfer-ratio-change-october-1/)
- [AwardWallet: Chase to Hyatt transfer ratios](https://awardwallet.com/credit-cards/chase-ultimate-rewards/chase-to-hyatt-transfer/)
- [NerdWallet: Sapphire Preferred Hyatt transfer changes](https://www.nerdwallet.com/travel/news/chase-sapphire-preferred-hyatt-transfer-changes)
- [AwardWallet: Hyatt transfer rate change news](https://awardwallet.com/news/chase-ultimate-rewards/hyatt-transfer-rate-devaluation/)
- [AwardWallet: World of Hyatt award charts](https://awardwallet.com/hotels/world-of-hyatt/award-charts/)
- [Chase: Sapphire Preferred card page](https://creditcards.chase.com/rewards-credit-cards/sapphire/preferred)

# Which Chase transfer partners are worth using, and which rarely are?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/chase-transfer-partners-which-are-worth-it/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

Of Chase's 16 transfer partners, Hyatt, Virgin Atlantic, Air Canada Aeroplan, Flying Blue and the Avios programs are the ones published valuations put clearly above the 1 cent a point is worth in Chase Travel. Marriott, IHG and Wyndham are valued below 1 cent, so a transfer to them usually loses value unless a bonus is running.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## The test: does it beat 1 cent?

A Chase point is worth 1 cent toward any booking in Chase Travel, and more on some bookings; see [how Points Boost works](/chase-points-boost-explained/). A transfer is worth doing only when the award you book returns more than that. Transfers cannot be reversed.

Transfers are 1 to 1 in blocks of 1,000 points. The one exception is Hyatt from a Sapphire Preferred or Ink Business Preferred, which is 4 to 3; see [the Hyatt change](/chase-to-hyatt-transfer-change-2026/). You need a Sapphire Preferred, Sapphire Reserve, Ink Business Preferred or Sapphire Reserve for Business to transfer at all.

Cathay Pacific Asia Miles and Qantas Frequent Flyer were added on November 18, 2026, which brought the count to 16.

## The partners, with The Points Guy's November 2026 values

| Partner | Ratio | Value of one partner point | What that gives per Chase point |
|---|---|---|---|
| World of Hyatt (from Sapphire Reserve) | 1 : 1 | 1.65 cents | 1.65 cents |
| World of Hyatt (from Sapphire Preferred) | 4 : 3 | 1.65 cents | About 1.24 cents |
| Virgin Atlantic Flying Club | 1 : 1 | 1.5 cents | 1.5 cents |
| Air Canada Aeroplan | 1 : 1 | 1.45 cents | 1.45 cents |
| Air France-KLM Flying Blue | 1 : 1 | 1.45 cents | 1.45 cents |
| British Airways, Iberia, Aer Lingus (Avios) | 1 : 1 | 1.35 cents | 1.35 cents |
| JetBlue TrueBlue | 1 : 1 | 1.35 cents | 1.35 cents |
| Cathay Pacific Asia Miles | 1 : 1 | 1.3 cents | 1.3 cents |
| Qantas Frequent Flyer | 1 : 1 | 1.3 cents | 1.3 cents |
| Singapore KrisFlyer | 1 : 1 | 1.25 cents | 1.25 cents |
| Southwest Rapid Rewards | 1 : 1 | 1.25 cents | 1.25 cents |
| United MileagePlus | 1 : 1 | 1.2 cents | 1.2 cents |
| Marriott Bonvoy | 1 : 1 | 0.75 cents | 0.75 cents |
| IHG One Rewards | 1 : 1 | 0.6 cents | 0.6 cents |
| Wyndham Rewards | 1 : 1 | 0.55 cents | 0.55 cents |

These are one site's estimates of an average, not prices. A single award can come out far above or below them. The 4 to 3 Hyatt figure is this page's arithmetic: 1.65 cents times three quarters.

## Partners that tend to be worth it

- **Hyatt.** It has a fixed award chart, and AwardWallet puts standard rooms from 3,500 points a night at the lowest category. From a Sapphire Preferred the 4 to 3 ratio cuts the return by a quarter.
- **Virgin Atlantic.** The Points Guy reports economy between New York and London from 6,000 points plus about $165 in taxes and fees, and business class from 29,000 points plus about $700 in surcharges one way. The cash part is large; count it.
- **Flying Blue.** Business class between the US and Europe starts at 60,000 miles one way, with taxes and fees near $600 in Flying Blue's own example.
- **Iberia.** Off-peak business class from New York or Boston to Madrid is 40,500 Avios one way, per The Points Guy and AwardWallet.
- **United and Southwest.** Lower values per point, but simple to use on US flights. AwardWallet lists United domestic awards from 5,000 miles one way.

## Partners that rarely are

- **Marriott, IHG and Wyndham.** At 0.55 to 0.75 cents, the same points buy more as a plain Chase Travel booking. AwardWallet says of IHG that transfers are generally not a good deal.
- **Singapore KrisFlyer** adds fuel surcharges on some flights, and transfers take a day or two, so a seat can go while you wait.

## Where sources disagree

- **Wyndham.** The Points Guy values a point at 0.55 cents. AwardWallet's users report 1.33 cents on average, and more at some all-inclusive resorts.
- **Marriott.** The Points Guy says 0.75 cents; AwardWallet's users average 0.93 cents.
- **Transfer bonuses.** AwardWallet lists bonuses now: 30% to the Avios programs through December 1, 40% to Virgin Atlantic through December 30, 80% to IHG and 30% to Wyndham through December 3, 2026. These were not confirmed on a Chase page. With an 80% bonus, IHG comes to about 1.08 cents per Chase point at The Points Guy's value. Check the transfer screen for the ratio that applies to you.

## Who should skip transfers

- People who will not search for award seats before moving points.
- People who mostly book hotels other than Hyatt.
- Sapphire Preferred holders eyeing Hyatt who have not redone the sums at 4 to 3.

For the Amex side, see [which Amex partners are worth it](/amex-transfer-partners-which-are-worth-it/).

## Quick answers

**How many transfer partners does Chase have?**
Sixteen as of November 18, 2026: twelve airline programs and four hotel programs, per AwardWallet.

**Is every Chase transfer 1 to 1?**
Yes, except Hyatt from a Sapphire Preferred or Ink Business Preferred, which is 4 to 3.

**Can a transfer be undone?**
No. Sources agree that transfers are final, so find the award seat or room first.

## Sources

- [The Points Guy: monthly valuations, November 2026](https://thepointsguy.com/loyalty-programs/monthly-valuations/)
- [The Points Guy: Chase transfer partners](https://thepointsguy.com/loyalty-programs/chase-ultimate-rewards-transfer-partners/)
- [The Points Guy: Chase adds Cathay Pacific and Qantas](https://thepointsguy.com/news/chase-cathay-pacific-qantas-transfer-partners)
- [AwardWallet: Chase adds Qantas and Cathay](https://awardwallet.com/news/chase-ultimate-rewards/chase-adds-qantas-cathay-transfer-partners/)
- [AwardWallet: Chase transfer partners](https://awardwallet.com/credit-cards/chase-ultimate-rewards/chase-transfer-partners/)
- [The Points Guy: Flying Blue award fare changes](https://thepointsguy.com/news/flying-blue-award-fare-changes/)

# Delta SkyMiles Gold, Platinum or Reserve Amex: which one fits someone who flies Delta 4 to 8 times a year?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/delta-gold-vs-platinum-vs-reserve-amex/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

At 4 to 8 Delta flights a year, the Gold card ($150 after a free first year) fits most people who check a bag, because the bag benefit is the same on all three cards. The Platinum ($350) makes sense mainly if you will use its yearly companion certificate, and the Reserve ($650) mainly if you want Delta Sky Club visits.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## The three cards side by side

| | Gold | Platinum | Reserve |
|---|---|---|---|
| Annual fee | $0 the first year, then $150 | $350 | $650 |
| First checked bag free on Delta | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Second checked bag free, domestic | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Miles on Delta purchases | 2 per dollar | 3 per dollar | 3 per dollar |
| Companion certificate | No | Yes, Delta Main | Yes, up to Delta First |
| Delta Sky Club | No | No | 15 visits per Medallion Year |
| Delta Stays credit | Up to $100 a year | Up to $150 a year | Up to $200 a year |
| Resy restaurant credit | No | Up to $10 a month | Up to $20 a month |
| Rideshare credit | Up to $10 a month, after first renewal | Up to $10 a month | Up to $10 a month |
| Status boost | No | 2,500 MQDs, plus 1 per $20 spent | 2,500 MQDs, plus 1 per $10 spent |

All three give 15% off award flights on Delta and cover the cardmember plus up to eight companions on the same reservation for bags.

## What 4 to 8 flights is worth in bags

Delta's first checked bag costs $45 each way on domestic and short-haul international routes for tickets bought on or after April 8, 2026.

| One-way flights a year | One person, one bag | Two people, one bag each |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | $180 | $360 |
| 6 | $270 | $540 |
| 8 | $360 | $720 |

That saving is identical on Gold, Platinum and Reserve. If bags are the reason for the card, the extra fee on the higher cards buys nothing more. The [Gold bag sums are worked out here](/delta-skymiles-gold-amex-free-checked-bag-math/).

## When the Platinum's extra $200 pays off

The Platinum costs $200 a year more than the Gold. What it adds:

- A companion certificate each year after renewal. You buy one adult round trip in Delta Main and the second traveler pays only taxes and fees, which run $22 to $250. Basic fares are excluded, and The Points Guy reports it books only into certain fare classes, so not every flight qualifies.
- Up to $120 a year at US Resy restaurants and up to $120 a year on rideshare, both paid monthly.
- $50 more Delta Stays credit, and a Global Entry or TSA PreCheck fee credit every four years.

If you take one round trip a year with another person and the second ticket would cost more than about $200 plus the taxes, the certificate covers the fee gap. The certificate arrives after the first renewal, so the first year does not include one.

Sources do not agree on where the Platinum certificate works. The Points Guy says all 50 states plus the Caribbean, Central America and Mexico. One Mile at a Time says the lower 48 states plus select Caribbean and Central American routes. Delta's own June 2026 release says domestic, Caribbean and Central American flights. Check the certificate terms before planning a Hawaii or Alaska trip around it.

## When the Reserve's $650 pays off

The Reserve adds 15 Delta Sky Club visits per Medallion Year when you fly Delta, Centurion Lounge access when the Delta flight is booked with the card, a companion certificate that also works in Delta First, Premium Select and Comfort, and up to $240 a year at Resy restaurants.

At 4 to 8 flights a year you would use at most 8 of the 15 lounge visits, fewer if a round trip has no time for a lounge. The fee is $300 more than the Platinum. Lounge visits, the wider certificate and the larger restaurant credit together would need to be worth that to you.

## A plain way to choose

- You fly alone or mostly check bags: Gold.
- You take at least one paid round trip a year with a companion and would use restaurant or rideshare credits monthly: Platinum.
- You want a lounge on most trips and will use a First or Comfort companion ticket: Reserve.

## Who should skip all three

- People who fly Delta once a year or less.
- People who never check a bag and travel alone.
- Medallion members and first class passengers, who already get free bags.
- People who want points that work on many airlines. These cards earn Delta miles only.

Welcome offers vary and change. Having or having had a higher Delta card can make you ineligible for a lower card's offer. See [the once per lifetime rule](/amex-once-per-lifetime-welcome-offer-rule/).

## Quick answers

**Is the free checked bag different on the three cards?**
No. All three give a free first checked bag on Delta flights and a free second bag on domestic Delta flights.

**Does the Gold card include lounge access or a companion certificate?**
No. Sky Club visits come only with the Reserve, and the companion certificate only with the Platinum and Reserve.

**Do I get a companion certificate in the first year?**
No. Delta says the certificate comes each year after the card renews.

# How many Delta flights does it take for the SkyMiles Gold Amex checked-bag benefit to cover the annual fee?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/delta-skymiles-gold-amex-free-checked-bag-math/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

Four one-way Delta flights with one checked bag, which is two round trips, cover the Delta SkyMiles Gold Amex's $150 annual fee for a solo traveler. Two people checking a bag each on the same reservation cover it in one round trip.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## The numbers behind the answer

- The card's annual fee is $0 in the first year, then $150.
- Delta's first checked bag costs $45 each way on domestic and short-haul international routes, for tickets bought on or after April 8, 2026. Before that it was $35.
- The card makes the first checked bag free on Delta flights.

$150 divided by $45 is 3.3. So the fourth one-way flight with a checked bag is the one that puts you past the fee.

| One-way flights with a bag | One traveler | Two travelers | Family of four |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | $45 | $90 | $180 |
| 2 (one round trip) | $90 | $180 | $360 |
| 4 (two round trips) | $180 | $360 | $720 |
| 6 (three round trips) | $270 | $540 | $1,080 |
| 8 (four round trips) | $360 | $720 | $1,440 |

Figures in the table are bag fees avoided, before the $150 fee. In the first year there is no fee, so any checked bag is a saving.

At the old $35 bag fee the same sum came to five one-way flights. The April 2026 price rise shortened it to four.

## Who is covered

The benefit covers the cardmember and up to eight companions traveling on the same reservation. Two details decide whether it works on a given trip:

- The cardmember's SkyMiles number has to be on the reservation.
- The ticket does not have to be bought with the card, according to One Mile at a Time.

Companions booked on a separate reservation are not covered. A family that books in two parts may get the free bag on only one of them.

## The second bag

Since June 4, 2026, the card also gives a free second checked bag on domestic Delta-operated flights. Delta charges $55 for a second bag, so a traveler who checks two bags on a domestic flight avoids $100 each way. For that traveler, one round trip ($200) is more than the annual fee.

The free second bag is for domestic flights only. The free first bag applies on Delta flights worldwide.

## What can shrink the saving

- **You may already get free bags.** Medallion members and first class passengers do not pay for the first bag, so the card adds nothing for bags on those trips.
- **Long-haul international trips.** Delta did not change bag fees on long-haul international flights in April 2026. Check the fee for your own route before counting on $45.
- **Basic fares.** Whether the free bag applies on Delta's lowest fares is not confirmed in the sources read for this page. Check Delta's terms before you book one.
- **Carry-on only.** If you travel with a carry-on, the bag benefit is worth nothing to you.
- **Other airlines.** The benefit is described for Delta flights. Whether a flight operated by a partner airline counts is not confirmed.

## What else the $150 buys

The bag is the main reason to hold this card, but it is not the only feature:

- 2 miles per dollar on Delta purchases, at restaurants and at US supermarkets; 1 mile elsewhere.
- 15% off award flights on Delta booked on delta.com or in the Fly Delta app.
- Up to $100 a year back on prepaid Delta Stays bookings.
- Up to $10 a month back on US rideshare with select providers, after the card's first renewal. Enrollment is required.
- A $200 Delta flight credit after $10,000 of purchases in a calendar year.
- Zone 5 boarding and 20% back on inflight purchases.

The card has no lounge access and no companion certificate. For those, see [how Gold, Platinum and Reserve compare](/delta-gold-vs-platinum-vs-reserve-amex/).

## Who should skip it

- People who fly Delta with a checked bag fewer than four one-way flights a year, alone.
- People who pack carry-on only.
- People with Medallion status, who already check a bag for free.
- People who fly several airlines and would rarely be on Delta.

Welcome offers on this card vary by applicant and change, and are not part of the sums above.

## Quick answers

**How many round trips cover the $150 fee?**
Two round trips with one checked bag each way for one traveler, or one round trip for two travelers on the same reservation.

**Do I have to pay for the flight with the card?**
One Mile at a Time reports that you do not, but your SkyMiles number must be on the reservation.

**Is a second checked bag free too?**
Yes on domestic Delta-operated flights, since June 4, 2026. On other routes only the first bag is free.

## Sources

- [One Mile at a Time: Delta SkyMiles Gold review](https://onemileatatime.com/reviews/credit-cards/american-express/delta-skymiles-gold-amex-card/)
- [The Points Guy: Delta raises checked bag fees](https://thepointsguy.com/news/delta-air-lines-hikes-checked-bag-fees/)
- [Delta News Hub: SkyMiles card changes, June 4, 2026](https://news.delta.com/more-travel-value-added-delta-skymiles-cards-no-increase-annual-fees.md)
- [Delta: SkyMiles American Express personal cards](https://www.delta.com/us/en/skymiles/airline-credit-cards/american-express-personal-cards)

# Do Amex and Chase points expire, and what happens if you close the card?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/do-amex-and-chase-points-expire/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

Amex Membership Rewards points and Chase points do not expire while the card account stays open and in good standing. They are lost when you close the last card tied to that points balance, so use them or move them before you close it; sources do not agree on whether you get any days of grace afterward.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## The rules side by side

| | Amex points (Membership Rewards) | Chase points |
|---|---|---|
| Expire with time or inactivity | No | No |
| Close one card, keep another in the same points balance | Points stay | Points stay if you move them to the open card first |
| Close the last card holding the points | Points forfeited | Points forfeited |
| Days to redeem after closing | Sources disagree: none, or 30 | Sources disagree: none stated by Chase, or 30 |
| Late payment | Points earned in that billing period can be forfeited; a $35 fee reinstates them after you pay | All points lost if the minimum payment is 60 days late |
| Issuer closes the account for misuse | Points forfeited | Points forfeited |

Sources: Chase's own guide, AwardWallet (February 2026 for Chase), The Points Guy, View from the Wing and One Mile at a Time (October 2026 for Amex).

## Chase: what the bank says

Chase's guide says points do not expire as long as the card account is open. In Chase's words: "Inactivity won't cause your Chase points to disappear from your account."

On closing, the same guide says that if you close the card before redeeming or transferring, you no longer have those points. It adds that points are forfeited if Chase closes the account for missed payments, program misuse or other reasons in the agreement.

Before closing a Chase card you can:

- Move the points to another of your own Chase cards that earns the same points.
- Move them to a household member's card. AwardWallet says a member of your household; The Points Guy says a spouse or domestic partner.
- Transfer them to an airline or hotel partner. That is final, and the points then follow that program's rules.
- Change the card to a no-fee Chase card instead of closing it. The Points Guy notes that if the new card cannot transfer to partners, you should transfer first.

## Amex: what changed in October 2026

Amex points do not expire from inactivity, per AwardWallet, which quotes Amex's FAQ that points can be forfeited as the program terms describe.

Until October 2026, a new Amex card joined your existing points balance on its own. View from the Wing and One Mile at a Time report that Amex changed its terms that month: a newly opened US card now gets its own rewards account, and the balances combine only after the accounts are linked. Existing cards were not changed.

Why it matters when closing a card: View from the Wing reads Amex's terms as forfeiting a rewards account's balance when the last card linked to that account is canceled. Another Amex card under the same login does not protect the points unless it is linked to the same rewards account. Its example: closing a new, unlinked Platinum Card could forfeit the points earned on it even though a Gold Card stays open.

Before closing an Amex card:

- Check the links under Manage Connections on the Amex site or app, or call the number on the card.
- Confirm the combined balance shows on a card you are keeping.
- Or redeem or transfer the points first.

Amex's terms document did not load as readable text, so the forfeiture wording was not confirmed on Amex's own page.

## Where sources disagree

- **Days after closing an Amex card.** AwardWallet says you have 30 days to use the points. The Points Guy (2024) says they are forfeited at once when your only Membership Rewards card closes, with a 30-day window only if you keep another Amex card that does not earn these points. View from the Wing (October 2026) describes forfeiture on canceling the last linked card, a 90-day window for cardholders with a New York billing address, and up to 30 days for a last linked Corporate Card.
- **Days after closing a Chase card.** Chase's guide mentions no window. AwardWallet and The Points Guy say there are 30 days if the account is in good standing.

The safe reading for both: treat the points as gone on the day the last card closes.

## Points you have already transferred

Miles and hotel points that have reached an airline or hotel account are no longer the bank's. Closing the card does not remove them. They can expire under that program's own rules; Hyatt points, for example, expire after 24 months with no qualifying activity.

A transfer made only to rescue points locks them into one program; see [Amex or Chase points, which are worth more](/amex-points-vs-chase-points-which-are-worth-more/).

## Who does not need to worry, and who should skip closing

- If you keep at least one card on the same points balance open and pay on time, nothing here applies.
- If the annual fee is the reason, ask about a lower-fee card in the same program before closing.
- If you opened an Amex card in or after October 2026, check the link before closing any older card.
- If you would transfer points in a hurry with no trip in mind, compare [which Chase partners](/chase-transfer-partners-which-are-worth-it/) and [which Amex partners](/amex-transfer-partners-which-are-worth-it/) hold their value.

## Quick answers

**Do Chase points expire?**
No, not while the card account is open. Chase says inactivity does not remove them.

**Do Amex points expire?**
No, not from inactivity. They can be forfeited when the last linked card closes or after a late payment.

**Do I lose miles already moved to an airline when I close the card?**
No. They sit in the airline's program and follow its expiry rules.

## Sources

- [Chase: Do credit card points expire?](https://chase.com/personal/credit-cards/education/rewards-benefits/do-credit-card-points-expire)
- [AwardWallet: Do Chase points expire?](https://awardwallet.com/credit-cards/chase-ultimate-rewards/do-chase-points-expire/)
- [AwardWallet: Do Amex points expire?](https://awardwallet.com/credit-cards/amex-membership-rewards/do-amex-points-expire/)
- [View from the Wing: Amex stops automatically pooling new card points](https://viewfromthewing.com/?p=258466)
- [One Mile at a Time: Amex stops automatically pooling points on new cards](https://onemileatatime.com/news/amex-stops-automatically-pooling-membership-rewards-points-new-cards/)
- [The Points Guy: Do you keep your points when you cancel a card?](https://thepointsguy.com/loyalty-programs/debunking-credit-card-myths-do-you-keep-your-points-and-miles-when-you-cancel-a-credit-card/)
- [The Points Guy: Downgrading a Chase card](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/chase/downgrade-chase-credit-card/)
- [AwardWallet: Chase to Hyatt transfers](https://awardwallet.com/credit-cards/chase-ultimate-rewards/chase-to-hyatt-transfer/)

# How much does applying for a travel card affect your credit score, and for how long?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/does-applying-for-a-travel-card-hurt-credit-score/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

For most people, one credit card application lowers a FICO score by fewer than five points, according to FICO. The hard inquiry counts in FICO scores for 12 months and stays on your credit report for two years, and the new account also lowers the average age of your accounts.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## The numbers

| Item | FICO | VantageScore |
|---|---|---|
| Typical drop from one hard inquiry | Less than five points | Five to 10 points |
| How long the inquiry is counted in the score | 12 months | Up to 24 months |
| How long the effect usually lasts | A few months | A few months |
| How long the inquiry stays on the report | Two years | Two years |

The FICO figures come from myFICO. The VantageScore figures come from Experian. FICO adds that the drop can be larger for people with a short credit history.

Sources disagree on one point: a credit expert quoted by CNBC Select says both scoring models ignore inquiries after one year, while Experian says VantageScore can count them for 24 months.

## Three things an application changes

**1. A hard inquiry.** Applying for a card puts a hard inquiry on your report whether or not you are approved. FICO says inquiries play "a minor part in only 10%" of the score, the part called new credit.

**2. A new account.** If approved, the new card lowers the average age of your accounts. Length of credit history is 15% of a FICO score. No source read gives a point figure for this, and it depends on how many accounts you have and how old they are.

**3. More available credit.** How much of your available credit you use is part of the amounts-owed category, which is 30% of a FICO score. A new credit line can lower that share if your balances stay the same. It raises it if you run up the new card.

| FICO score category | Weight | Affected by a new card? |
|---|---|---|
| Payment history | 35% | Only by how you pay afterward |
| Amounts owed | 30% | Yes, either way |
| Length of credit history | 15% | Yes, lower average age |
| New credit | 10% | Yes, the inquiry and new account |
| Credit mix | 10% | Usually little |

## Card applications are not grouped

For mortgages, auto loans and student loans, several inquiries in a short window are counted as one. Experian says that does not apply to credit cards: each card application is counted separately, however close together they are.

An older Experian article says several inquiries close together can have a larger effect, and suggests waiting six months to a year between applications.

## Looking at an offer is not always an application

| Action | Type of check |
|---|---|
| Checking your own credit report or score | Soft, no effect |
| Mailed preapproved offers | Soft, no effect |
| Seeing your Amex welcome offer before accepting | Reported as soft by The Points Guy and others |
| Accepting an Amex card after seeing the offer | Hard inquiry |
| Submitting a Chase Sapphire application | Hard inquiry |
| Canceling at Chase's notice that you will not get the bonus | No effect, per The Points Guy |

More on the Amex process: [how to check which offer you are shown](/highest-amex-platinum-welcome-offer-how-to-check/). For Chase, see [how a referral link works](/chase-sapphire-preferred-referral-bonus-how-it-works/).

## Other effects that are not about the score

- Chase generally declines applicants who opened five or more personal cards in 24 months. Each new card, from any bank, counts toward that. See [the 5/24 rule](/chase-5-24-rule-explained/).
- Payment history is the largest part of the score at 35%. It depends on paying on time once you have the card.

## Who should skip a new application for now

- Anyone applying for a mortgage, car loan or other large loan in the next several months. A few points can matter at a rate cutoff. Experian's six-to-twelve-month spacing is a cautious guide.
- Anyone with a thin or short credit history. FICO says the effect of an inquiry is larger for them.
- Anyone with several recent card applications.
- Anyone who expects to carry a balance on the new card. Amounts owed is 30% of a FICO score against 10% for new credit, and interest can outweigh a welcome offer.

A small score effect says nothing about whether a card is worth its fee. For that, see [Amex Platinum for an occasional flyer](/amex-platinum-worth-it-occasional-flyer/) or [Sapphire Preferred on one trip a year](/chase-sapphire-preferred-one-trip-a-year/).

## Quick answers

**How many points does a credit card application cost?**
FICO says less than five points for most people. Experian puts the typical VantageScore drop at five to 10 points.

**How long does a hard inquiry stay on my credit report?**
Two years. FICO scores count it for only the first 12 months.

**Does being denied hurt more than being approved?**
The inquiry is the same either way. A denial adds no new account, so it does not change the average age of your accounts.

## Sources

- [myFICO: credit checks and inquiries](https://www.myfico.com/credit-education/credit-reports/credit-checks-and-inquiries)
- [myFICO: what is in your credit score](https://www.myfico.com/credit-education/whats-in-your-credit-score)
- [Experian: how long hard inquiries stay on your report](https://www.experian.com/blogs/ask-experian/how-long-do-hard-inquiries-stay-on-your-credit-report/)
- [Experian: hard pulls on credit card applications](https://www.experian.com/blogs/ask-experian/is-there-a-hard-pull-on-credit-cards-if-i-apply/)
- [Chase: how hard and soft inquiries affect your score](https://www.chase.com/personal/credit-cards/education/credit-score/how-hard-soft-inquiries-affect-credit-score)
- [CNBC Select: how applying for new credit affects your score](https://www.cnbc.com/select/how-applying-for-new-credit-impacts-credit-score/)
- [The Points Guy: Amex Platinum current offer](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/amex-platinum-current-offer/)
- [The Points Guy: the Sapphire bonus eligibility pop-up](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/chase-sapphire-preferred-lifetime-bonus-popup/)

# Does Chase Sapphire rental car insurance cover Turo?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/does-chase-sapphire-rental-car-insurance-cover-turo/
Facts checked: 2026-11-27
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

No. The Sapphire Preferred Guide to Benefits excludes a vehicle rented through a car sharing company and any vehicle not rented from a commercial rental agency, and Chase's own guide for both Sapphire cards says peer-to-peer rentals are not covered. Turo's help center says the same from its side.

This page is information, not financial advice. The sources were read on November 27, 2026. The Guide to Benefits governs any claim, and the benefit administrator decides it.

## What Chase's wording says

Chase's Guide to Benefits for the Sapphire Preferred (form BGC11387, describing the benefit in effect as of October 1, 2024) was read directly for this page. Its Auto Rental Coverage section lists two exclusions that matter here:

- Vehicles that are not rented from a Rental Agency.
- A rental vehicle rented through "a car sharing company that allows individuals to rent out their own vehicle."

The guide defines a Rental Agency as a commercial rental company, licensed under the laws of the place it operates, whose primary business is renting automobiles. A private owner listing a car on an app does not fit that definition.

Chase's web guide to Sapphire rental coverage, which covers both the Preferred and the Reserve, says peer-to-peer and hourly car rentals are not covered. It does not name Turo. Whether Chase has issued a newer Preferred guide than the one read is not confirmed, and the Sapphire Reserve Guide to Benefits was not read directly.

## What Turo says

Turo's help article on credit card coverage, updated May 4, 2026, says it is very unlikely that a card covers damage to a car booked through Turo, because Turo is a peer-to-peer car sharing platform and not a rental car company. It tells guests to read their card's terms and ask the issuer.

## Turo, a rental agency, and Turo's own plans

| | Traditional rental agency | Turo, relying on a Sapphire card | Turo with a Turo protection plan |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sapphire Preferred damage and theft cover | Primary, up to $60,000, when the rental company's waiver is declined | Excluded by the Guide to Benefits | Not from the card |
| Sapphire Reserve damage and theft cover | Primary, up to $75,000, per Chase's web guide | Not covered, per Chase's web guide | Not from the card |
| Most you pay Turo for physical damage | Not applicable | With protection declined: all of it, plus claim fees | $0 on Premier, $500 on Standard, $3,000 on Minimum |
| Liability to others | Not part of the card benefit | State minimum through Turo, secondary to your own policy | State minimum; optional extra liability up to $300,000 in some states |

The plan figures are from Turo's help page for US guests, updated October 21, 2026. Turo says its protection plans are contracts with Turo, not insurance. On the Standard and Minimum plans, the limit does not apply to mechanical and interior damage. Premier is not offered to drivers under 21 or on some higher-value cars. Plan prices are shown at checkout and are not confirmed here.

Getaround, Zipcar and other services are not named in the Chase guide. The car sharing exclusion is written by type of company, and Chase's web guide separately excludes hourly rentals. How the administrator treats each service is not confirmed.

## Where sources disagree

- **Commercial hosts.** The Points Guy, in an article published June 17, 2021, reported that a Chase benefits specialist said a Turo booking might not be excluded when the car comes from a commercial rental company and the rental contract names that company. The written guide read for this page has no such carve-out: it excludes a car rented through a car sharing company without regard to who the host is. Upgraded Points, updated September 16, 2026, lists car sharing rentals such as Turo as excluded.
- **Rental length.** Chase's web guide says fewer than 31 consecutive days; the Guide to Benefits says up to 31.
- **Old vehicles.** The web guide excludes vehicles more than 10 years old; the Guide to Benefits excludes antique cars, defined as over 20 years old or out of production for 10 years.

A phone answer is not a written term. The guide lists 1-800-350-1362 for coverage questions before a trip.

## The sums

Because the card pays nothing on Turo, the choice is between a Turo protection plan, your own auto policy if it extends to car sharing, or carrying the risk. With protection declined, Turo says you owe all physical, mechanical and interior damage costs plus fees. The card's benefit has no value in this sum, so compare the Turo price plus a plan against a rental agency's price with the agency's waiver declined.

More on the benefit is on [Sapphire Preferred rental car insurance](/chase-sapphire-preferred-rental-car-insurance/), [Sapphire Preferred travel insurance](/chase-sapphire-preferred-travel-insurance/) and, for another issuer's rule, [Amex Platinum rental car cover](/amex-platinum-rental-car-status-and-insurance/).

## Who should skip relying on it

- Anyone booking Turo and planning to decline Turo's protection because of a Sapphire card.
- Anyone renting by the hour from any service.
- Anyone counting on the card for liability. It covers neither liability nor injuries, on Turo or anywhere else.
- Anyone whose own auto policy excludes car sharing. Ask the insurer before the trip.

## Quick answers

**Does the Chase Sapphire Preferred cover Turo?**
No. Its Guide to Benefits excludes vehicles rented through a car sharing company where individuals rent out their own cars.

**Does the Chase Sapphire Reserve cover Turo?**
Chase's web guide for both Sapphire cards says peer-to-peer rentals are not covered. The Reserve's own benefits guide was not read.

**Should I buy Turo's protection plan if I have a Sapphire card?**
The card will not pay for damage to a Turo car. Without a plan, Turo says you owe all damage costs.

## Sources

- [Chase: Sapphire Preferred Guide to Benefits (PDF)](https://static.chasecdn.com/content/services/structured-document/document.en.pdf/card/benefits-center/product-benefits-guide-pdf/BGC11387_v2.pdf)
- [Chase: how Sapphire rental car insurance works](https://www.chase.com/personal/credit-cards/education/basics/chase-sapphire-rental-car-insurance-guide)

# Do you need a credit card or bank account to join Rakuten?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/does-rakuten-need-a-credit-card-to-join/
Facts checked: 2026-11-27
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

No. Rakuten's terms ask for an email address and a password to open an account, and no credit card, debit card or bank account. A card is asked for only if you choose to link one for in-store offers, and a mailing address is asked for before Rakuten will pay you.

This page is information, not financial advice. It covers what Rakuten asks for and when, as read on its own pages on November 27, 2026; its terms and privacy policy carry the date October 23, 2026. The joining steps are on [how to sign up for Rakuten](/how-to-sign-up-for-rakuten/) and the costs are on [is Rakuten free](/is-rakuten-free/).

## What Rakuten asks for, and when

| Information | To join | To be paid | Only if you opt in |
|---|---|---|---|
| Email and password, or a Facebook, Google or Apple sign-in | Yes | Yes | |
| Credit or debit card | No | No | Yes, to link a card for in-store and dining offers |
| Bank account | No | No | Not asked for on the pages read |
| Mailing address | No | Yes | |
| PayPal email | No | Only if you pick PayPal | |
| Social Security number | Not mentioned | Not mentioned | Not mentioned |

The terms add that you may choose to give more information to use certain offers and services. That is a choice, not a condition of membership.

## When a card does come up

The one place Rakuten asks for a card number is card linking. It is a separate, optional feature with its own terms: you enroll a card, add a store's offer, and pay in the store with that card. Rakuten's help center says most Visa and Mastercard credit and debit cards and most American Express cards can be linked, so even this step does not need a credit card.

Rakuten's linked-cards article says it will never charge a linked card and will never ask for the card's CVV. The in-store terms say the card network may share the merchant name, location, date and amount of purchases at participating merchants, and that a card can be removed at any time. The steps are on [linking a card for in-store cash back](/rakuten-link-card-for-in-store-cash-back/).

Shopping online through Rakuten does not need a linked card. You pay the store, with whatever payment method the store accepts.

## What you need to get paid

The terms list four conditions for payment: an active account, a valid email address, a password and a physical address. Then you pick a method.

| Method | What Rakuten needs |
|---|---|
| Check | The name and mailing address in Account Settings |
| PayPal | A valid PayPal email that is not used on another Rakuten account |
| Bilt Points, Samsung Cash or Amex points | An account with that program, linked to Rakuten |

No listed method is a direct deposit, so Rakuten does not ask for bank account or routing numbers. A check is deposited at your own bank; a PayPal balance is handled under PayPal's own rules. The trade-offs are on [check or PayPal](/rakuten-big-fat-check-vs-paypal/).

The minimum is small but real. The terms say, "The minimum payout amount for Rewards is $5.01." The help page says $5 or more. A smaller balance carries over to the next payment date.

## Does joining affect your credit

The terms and the privacy policy do not mention a credit check, a credit report or a Social Security number for membership, and the sign-up asks for nothing a credit check would need. Whether Rakuten ever asks for more to verify a member is not confirmed.

The Rakuten American Express Card is a different thing: a credit card with its own application. It is not needed for membership, and its application terms were not read for this page.

## Who can join, and what is collected

Members must be at least 18 and live in the 50 United States or Washington D.C., and each person is limited to one account. Whether the join form also asks for a name or phone number is not confirmed; the help pages do not list its fields.

Not asking for a card does not mean collecting little. The privacy policy lists name, postal and email address, phone number, and payment account details among the information Rakuten may hold when you provide them, along with shopping activity. See [the extension and your privacy](/rakuten-browser-extension-safe-privacy/).

Joining bonuses also need purchases, not a card on file; see [how the sign-up and referral bonuses work](/rakuten-50-bonus-how-it-works/).

## Who should skip it

- Anyone under 18 or living outside the 50 states and Washington D.C.
- Anyone who will not give a mailing address. Rakuten's terms make it a condition of payment.
- Anyone with neither a PayPal account nor a way to deposit a paper check, unless one of the points options fits.
- Anyone who does not want card purchases shared with Rakuten: skip card linking and shop online only.

## Quick answers

**Do you need a credit card to join Rakuten?**
No. The terms ask for an email address and a password. A card is linked only for optional in-store offers.

**Does Rakuten need your bank account?**
No. Payment goes by check, PayPal or a points program. No direct deposit option is listed.

**Does joining Rakuten affect your credit score?**
Rakuten's terms and privacy policy mention no credit check for membership. Anything beyond that is not confirmed.

## Sources

- [Rakuten: Terms and conditions](https://www.rakuten.com/help/article/terms-conditions)
- [Rakuten: How to join Rakuten](https://www.rakuten.com/help/article/how-to-join-rakuten-360002101108)
- [Rakuten: What are linked cards?](https://www.rakuten.com/help/article/what-are-linked-cards-360002118187)
- [Rakuten: In-store cash back terms and conditions](https://www.rakuten.com/help/article/in-store-cash-back-terms-conditions-115013738007)
- [Rakuten: Choosing how you get paid](https://www.rakuten.com/help/article/choosing-how-you-get-paid-360002100828)
- [Rakuten: When will I get paid?](https://www.rakuten.com/help/article/when-will-i-get-paid-360002117667)
- [Rakuten: Privacy policy](https://www.rakuten.com/help/article/privacy-policy)

# Does Rakuten give cash back on Amazon?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/does-rakuten-work-on-amazon/
Facts checked: 2026-11-21
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

Not in the usual way. On November 21, 2026 Rakuten listed Amazon with no percentage rate, only a flat $5 on each of the first three eligible Amazon orders for members in their first 60 days. Longer-standing members saw no ongoing Amazon rate on that page.

This page is information, not financial advice. Offers change daily, so read the Amazon page on Rakuten on the day you shop.

## What was listed on November 21, 2026

| Item | What Rakuten's Amazon page said |
|---|---|
| Rate | $5 per order, not a percentage |
| How many orders | The first 3 eligible Amazon orders |
| Who | Members within their first 60 days |
| Deadline | Purchases within 60 days of signing up |
| How to shop | Rakuten browser extension, Rakuten app or Samsung Wallet Perks |
| Counts toward the welcome or referral bonus | No |

The page also says the offer can be changed at any time.

One thing stands out in the terms: "Amazon is not a partner of Rakuten." Rakuten says the offer comes from Rakuten alone and that it is not affiliated with, sponsored by or endorsed by Amazon. At most stores, the store pays Rakuten a commission and Rakuten shares it. Here the wording says the reward is Rakuten's own.

## Where sources differ

- **Minimum order.** A search summary of Rakuten's Amazon page says each order must be $25 or more, and that the 60-day rule applies to sign-ups on or after January 23, 2026. The page as read on November 21 showed neither. Treat the $25 minimum as possible and check the terms shown to your account.
- **The Rakuten website.** The terms name the extension, the app and Samsung Wallet Perks. They do not name a click from rakuten.com. Whether that route counts is not confirmed.
- **Older statements.** A search summary of an older Rakuten help article said cash back at Amazon ended in March 2020. That article no longer loads. Earlier Amazon offers reported by Frequent Miler were targeted and have expired.

## What does not earn

The terms exclude:

- Subscriptions and digital purchases
- Gift cards and vouchers, both buying and redeeming them, and store credit
- Orders using a voucher or promo code not featured on Rakuten
- Orders placed through Add to Delivery, Auto Buy or Rufus AI
- Amazon Pharmacy, Amazon Health urgent care and the Amazon FSA/HSA Store

## The sums

Three orders at $5 each is $15 in total. That is the ceiling of the offer as listed.

| Order size | Reward | As a share of the order |
|---|---|---|
| $25 | $5 | 20% |
| $100 | $5 | 5% |
| $500 | $5 | 1% |

So the offer is worth most on small orders. After the third order, or after day 60, the page showed nothing further for Amazon itself.

The Amazon orders do not count toward Rakuten's welcome bonus. That bonus needs spending at other stores; see [how the Rakuten bonus works](/rakuten-50-bonus-how-it-works/).

## Related listings

A few Amazon-owned services had their own listings that day, each with separate terms that were not read for this page:

| Listing | Seen November 21, 2026 |
|---|---|
| Amazon Music | $4 |
| Amazon Business | $10 |
| Woot | Up to 6% |

Amazon-brand devices sold by other stores may also be excluded there. Kohl's listing on Rakuten, for one, excludes Amazon products.

## Who should skip it

- You joined Rakuten more than 60 days ago. Nothing was listed for you at Amazon on the day checked.
- Your Amazon spending is mostly subscriptions, digital items or gift cards. Those are excluded.
- You use Auto Buy or add items to an existing Prime delivery. Those orders are excluded.
- You plan to count Amazon orders toward the welcome bonus. They do not count.

## Quick answers

**Does Rakuten pay a percentage back at Amazon?**
No percentage was listed on November 21, 2026. The listing was a flat $5 on each of a new member's first three eligible orders.

**Can a long-time member earn at Amazon?**
Not from the Amazon listing seen that day. It was limited to members in their first 60 days.

**Do Amazon gift cards earn the $5?**
No. The terms exclude buying and redeeming gift cards and vouchers.

## Sources

- [Rakuten: Amazon store page](https://www.rakuten.com/shop/amazon)
- [Rakuten: Kohl's store page](https://www.rakuten.com/kohls.com)
- [Rakuten: How does Rakuten work?](https://www.rakuten.com/help/article/how-does-rakuten-work-360002117047)
- [Frequent Miler: earlier targeted Amazon offer, now expired](https://frequentmiler.com/rakuten-offering-rewards-for-amazon-purchases-targeted/)
