# Is booking a Hawaii resort through Amex Fine Hotels + Resorts worth it?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/fine-hotels-resorts-hawaii-worth-it/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

It is usually worth it for a short stay at a resort you were going to book anyway, provided the Amex Travel rate is close to the hotel's own rate. The fixed perks, a $100 property credit and up to $300 back from the Platinum Card, do not grow with the length of the stay, so they matter less on a week.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## What a Fine Hotels + Resorts booking includes

Amex lists these benefits for Platinum Card members who book through Amex Travel:

| Benefit | Amex's terms | Certain or not |
|---|---|---|
| Daily breakfast for two | Every morning of the stay | Certain |
| Property credit | $100 per stay toward eligible charges, which vary by hotel | Certain, but sometimes food and drink only |
| Late checkout | Guaranteed 4 p.m. | Certain |
| Early check-in | Noon, when available | Not guaranteed |
| Room upgrade | On arrival, when available; some room types excluded | Not guaranteed |

On November 20, 2026, Amex Travel listed 25 Fine Hotels + Resorts properties in Hawaii, on Oahu, Maui, Kauai, the Big Island and Lanai. Examples are Halekulani, Andaz Maui, Grand Hyatt Kauai and Mauna Lani.

## The Platinum hotel credit on top

The Platinum Card gives up to $300 back each half-year, up to $600 per calendar year, on prepaid Fine Hotels + Resorts bookings made through Amex Travel and paid with the card.

- One stay in one half of the year uses one $300 credit.
- From January 1, 2027, a Fine Hotels + Resorts booking needs at least two nights to earn the credit. Until then one night qualifies.
- Only "Book and Pay Today" earns the credit and 5 points per dollar. "Book and Pay at Check-in" does not.

## What it adds up to on a short stay

The fixed part is simple: $100 at the hotel plus up to $300 back from the card is up to $400 per stay. Breakfast for two is extra value, but only what you would have paid for breakfast anyway.

| Stay length | Fixed value ($100 + $300) | Fixed value per night |
|---|---|---|
| 1 night (through 2026) | $400 | $400 |
| 2 nights | $400 | $200 |
| 5 nights | $400 | $80 |
| 7 nights | $400 | $57 |

Set that against Hawaii prices. One guide puts Grand Hyatt Kauai cash rates at $800 to $1,300 a night. At $800, the fixed $400 is a quarter of a two-night bill and under a tenth of a seven-night bill.

## When a direct or other booking is cheaper

Check these before paying:

- **The rate itself.** AwardWallet notes that Amex Travel prices "can vary widely" from booking direct. Compare the total with taxes and fees for the same room and dates.
- **Member, resident or package rates.** A hotel's member, resident or package rates may not appear on Amex Travel. Whether the rates match is not confirmed for any Hawaii hotel.
- **Resort fees.** No source read says whether Fine Hotels + Resorts rates include Hawaii resort fees, or whether the $300 credit applies to them. Not confirmed.
- **Points.** Paying with Membership Rewards points through Amex Travel gives about 0.7 cents per point on prepaid hotels, per The Points Guy.
- **Hyatt points.** Andaz Maui and Grand Hyatt Kauai can also be booked with World of Hyatt points. See [what Hyatt hotels in Hawaii cost in points](/hyatt-hotels-hawaii-points-cost/).

A simple test: take the Amex Travel total, subtract $300 if the credit is unused, subtract $100 only if you would spend it at the hotel anyway, and subtract what breakfast would have cost you. If the result is below the cheapest direct total, the booking wins.

## Splitting a longer stay

Two separate bookings in the same half-year still earn one $300 credit, because the cap is per half-year. Two bookings charged in different half-years can each earn up to $300. The exact dates of each half-year were not confirmed on Amex's page.

## Who should skip it

- Travelers who normally rent a condo or pick mid-priced hotels. Paying several hundred dollars more per night to collect $400 leaves you worse off.
- Anyone who finds a much lower direct or package rate.
- Anyone counting on the upgrade. It is given only when available.

See also [the Amex Platinum for a Hawaii trip](/amex-platinum-hawaii-trip/).

## Quick answers

**Does Fine Hotels + Resorts include breakfast in Hawaii?**
Yes. Amex lists daily breakfast for two on every Fine Hotels + Resorts stay.

**Can one Hawaii stay earn both $300 hotel credits?**
Not as one booking. The credit is up to $300 per half-year.

**Does the $100 property credit cover golf or spa?**
It depends on the hotel. Eligible charges vary by property, and some limit the credit to food and drink.

## Sources

- [American Express: Fine Hotels + Resorts benefits and value](https://www.americanexpress.com/en-us/travel/get-inspired/great-value-hotels-fhr/)
- [American Express: the $600 hotel credit](https://www.americanexpress.com/en-us/travel/get-inspired/Platinum-Card-600-Dollar-Hotel-Credit)
- [American Express: Hawaii hotels in Fine Hotels + Resorts and The Hotel Collection](https://www.americanexpress.com/en-us/travel/discover/property-results/dt/3/d/Hawaii)
- [AwardWallet: Amex Fine Hotels + Resorts (August 13, 2026)](https://awardwallet.com/credit-cards/amex-membership-rewards/amex-fine-hotels-and-resorts/)
- [The Points Guy: Amex Pay with Points (August 24, 2026)](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/american-express/amex-pay-with-points-guide/)
- [Elevate Miles: Grand Hyatt Kauai on points (September 8, 2026)](https://elevatemiles.com/grand-hyatt-kauai-on-points-the-hyatt-award-worth-planning-a-trip-around/)

# Fine Hotels + Resorts or The Hotel Collection: which uses the Amex Platinum hotel credit better?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/fine-hotels-resorts-vs-hotel-collection/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

The Hotel Collection usually costs less, so the $300 half-year credit covers a larger share of the bill. Fine Hotels + Resorts gives more at the hotel, mainly daily breakfast for two and a guaranteed 4 p.m. checkout, and until January 1, 2027 it is the only one of the two that works for a one-night stay.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## The credit both programs share

The Platinum Card gives up to $300 back each half-year, $600 per calendar year, on a prepaid booking made through Amex Travel and paid with the card. Both programs qualify. A booking must use the prepaid, pay-today rate; a pay-at-the-hotel rate earns no credit. Prepaid bookings also earn 5 points per dollar.

One trip in one half of the year can use one $300 piece, not both.

## Side by side

| | Fine Hotels + Resorts | The Hotel Collection |
|---|---|---|
| Size | Over 1,900 hotels | More than 1,300 hotels |
| Price level | Higher | Generally lower |
| Minimum stay for the credit today | None | 2 nights |
| Minimum stay for the credit from January 1, 2027 | 2 nights | 2 nights |
| Daily breakfast for two | Yes | No |
| Credit to spend at the hotel | $100 per stay, use varies by hotel | Up to $100 per stay, use varies by hotel |
| Room upgrade | When available | When available |
| Noon check-in | When available | When available |
| 4 p.m. checkout | Guaranteed | When available |
| Wi-Fi | Included | Not listed |
| Who can book | Platinum and Centurion cardholders | Also Gold cardholders |

Benefit lists are from AwardWallet (August 2026) and The Points Guy (July 2026). Amex's own program page would not load for this check.

## The January 2027 change

Today, a single night at a Fine Hotels + Resorts hotel can earn the credit. Amex's hotel credit page states: "Effective January 1, 2027, Fine Hotels + Resorts bookings will require a minimum two-night stay". After that date both programs need two nights.

This matters for the sums. At a hotel that charges $500 a night, one night with a $300 credit costs $200 before taxes. Two nights with the same credit cost $700. From 2027 the one-night use is gone.

The sources describe the two-night rule only for the statement credit. Whether it also applies to the breakfast and $100 hotel credit on a one-night stay is not confirmed.

## Which uses the $300 better

It depends on what you want the credit to do.

**To pay as little as possible.** The Hotel Collection tends to win. Its hotels are generally cheaper, so a two-night stay can land closer to $300. The Points Guy gives an example of a two-night stay that cost $577, or $277 after the credit.

**To get the most at the hotel.** Fine Hotels + Resorts gives breakfast for two each morning and a checkout you can count on. Amex puts the average value of the program's benefits at $550 per stay, based on two-night stays. That is Amex's own figure, and it assumes you would have paid for those things.

**For one night, through December 31, 2026.** Only Fine Hotels + Resorts works.

Before booking, compare the Amex Travel price with the price elsewhere. AwardWallet notes that Amex Travel prices can differ from the hotel's own price, sometimes by a lot. A $300 credit on a rate that is $150 higher is a $150 credit.

## Limits that apply to both

- The hotel must be in one of the two programs. Most ordinary hotels are not.
- Hotel loyalty points and elite perks are not guaranteed on these bookings. A Points Guy writer reports usually receiving them at The Hotel Collection hotels, but that is one person's experience.

## Who should skip it

Leave the hotel credit out of your sums on the $895 fee if:

- You normally book budget or mid-priced hotels. A credit that moves you to a $350-a-night hotel raises your spending.
- Your trips are single nights, from 2027 on.
- You book with hotel points, or need a refundable pay-later rate.
- You take one trip a year. Then the credit is worth $300 to you, not $600.

For a worked example on one destination, see [the Hawaii trip page](/amex-platinum-hawaii-trip/).

## Quick answers

**Does The Hotel Collection include free breakfast?**
No. Breakfast for two is a Fine Hotels + Resorts benefit. The Hotel Collection gives up to $100 to spend at the hotel.

**Can a one-night stay earn the Amex Platinum hotel credit?**
Only at Fine Hotels + Resorts, and only until January 1, 2027. After that both programs need two nights.

**Can you use the whole $600 on one stay?**
No. It comes as up to $300 in each half of the year, so one stay uses one piece.

## Sources

- [American Express: the $600 hotel credit](https://www.americanexpress.com/en-us/travel/get-inspired/Platinum-Card-600-Dollar-Hotel-Credit)
- [AwardWallet: Amex Fine Hotels + Resorts](https://awardwallet.com/credit-cards/amex-membership-rewards/amex-fine-hotels-and-resorts)
- [The Points Guy: The Hotel Collection guide](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/american-express-the-hotel-collection-guide/)
- [American Express: Platinum hotel programs](https://www.americanexpress.com/en-us/travel/platinum-card-hotel-programs/)

# What does it cost to fly with golf clubs on US airlines, and which cards cover the fee?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/flying-with-golf-clubs-airline-fees/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

On the major US airlines a golf bag is charged as an ordinary checked bag: about $45 each way as your first bag and $55 as your second, as of the April 2026 fee increases. The Amex Platinum's airline fee credit can repay checked bag fees on one chosen airline, and airline credit cards waive the first bag.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## Fees and golf bag rules by airline

Bag fees rose in April 2026. Older tables showing $30 or $35, or free bags on Southwest, are out of date. Fees are one-way, for standard economy fares.

| Airline | First / second bag | Golf bag rule | Weight and size | Case rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Delta | $45 / $55 | One golf bag at standard baggage charges: one set of clubs, balls and tees, one pair of shoes | Over 50 lb pays an excess weight fee. Over 115 linear inches or 100 lb is not accepted | Hard-shell case, or soft travel bag after signing a limited release |
| United | $45 / $55 prepaid; $50 / $60 within 24 hours of departure | One set of clubs counts toward the checked bag allowance. No oversize fee on the golf bag | Overweight charges may apply | United says it is not liable for damage unless the clubs are in a hard-sided case |
| American | $45 / $55 prepaid; $50 / $60 at the airport | One golf bag with up to 14 clubs, 12 balls and one pair of shoes, at the standard fee | Standard fee applies up to 50 lb and 126 inches | Not confirmed |
| Southwest | $45 / $55 | Standard and overweight fees apply. Oversize fees are waived | Over 100 lb or 115 inches cannot be checked | Hooded or soft-sided bags travel with a limited release of liability |
| Alaska and Hawaiian | $45 / $55, including mainland to Hawaii. $30 / $40 between the islands | Standard fees apply. Oversize or overweight fee waived for golf clubs | Other items packed in the case can still trigger an overweight fee | Soft or hard case made for the equipment |

Notes on the table:

- American charges $55 and $65 on domestic Basic Economy tickets, less $5 if prepaid.
- Delta's and Southwest's pages were read in full. The United, American and Alaska rules come from search summaries of their pages.
- Overweight fee amounts were not confirmed for any airline.

## What a round trip costs

| How the clubs travel | Each way | Round trip |
|---|---|---|
| Golf bag is your only checked bag | $45 | $90 |
| Suitcase first, golf bag second | $45 + $55 = $100 | $200 |

## Card benefits that cover the fee

| Benefit | What is confirmed | What is not |
|---|---|---|
| Amex Platinum airline fee credit | Up to $200 per calendar year on one airline chosen in advance: Alaska, American, Delta, JetBlue, Southwest or United. Checked bag fees count, and AwardWallet lists oversized baggage charges too | No source names golf bags or overweight fees. Whether a fee on a Hawaiian-operated flight counts when Alaska is the chosen airline is not confirmed |
| Sapphire Reserve travel credit | Up to $300 per account year on any purchase the card categorizes as travel | Chase's page does not name bag fees |
| Sapphire Preferred | No bag fee benefit found | |
| Airline credit cards | First checked bag free on United Explorer, Citi / AAdvantage Platinum Select, Delta SkyMiles Gold, Atmos Rewards Ascent and Southwest Rapid Rewards cards | Rules on companions and paying with the card differ |

With the Platinum credit, the airline can be changed once a year, by January 31. It does not cover tickets or award taxes.

A free first bag helps most when the golf bag is the only checked bag. With a suitcase too, the golf bag becomes the second bag at $55.

Damage and loss are a separate question. See [what card insurance covers on a golf trip](/golf-trip-travel-insurance-credit-card/).

## Who should skip it

- Golfers taking one short trip a year. Compare $90 to $200 in bag fees with renting clubs at the course or shipping them. Neither price was checked for this page.
- Travelers with a heavy staff bag. Over 50 lb, Delta, United, American and Southwest can add an overweight fee, and no card benefit here is confirmed to cover it.

See also [the Amex Platinum for golfers](/amex-platinum-for-golfers/).

## Quick answers

**Do airlines charge extra for golf clubs?**
Not on these five. A golf bag is charged as a standard checked bag if it stays within the weight limit.

**Does Southwest still fly golf bags free?**
No. Since April 9, 2026 the first bag is $45 and the second $55 on most fares.

**Does the Amex Platinum airline credit cover a golf bag fee?**
It covers checked bag fees on your one chosen airline. No source names golf bags, but airlines charge them as checked bags.

- [Chase: how the Sapphire Reserve travel credit works](https://www.chase.com/personal/credit-cards/education/rewards-benefits/chase-sapphire-reserve-travel-credit-how-it-works)
- [The Points Guy: credit cards with free checked bags (updated November 18, 2026)](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/credit-cards-with-free-checked-baggage/)

# Does credit card travel insurance cover a golf trip?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/golf-trip-travel-insurance-credit-card/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

Partly. The Sapphire cards and the Amex Platinum can pay when the trip itself is canceled, cut short or delayed, and when checked clubs are lost or damaged, up to set limits. No source read shows any of them paying for a round that is rained out while the trip goes ahead.

This page is information, not financial advice.

Each card's Guide to Benefits is the binding document. Read the current one before a trip.

## What each card covers

| Problem | Sapphire Preferred / Reserve | Amex Platinum |
|---|---|---|
| Rained-out round, lost green fees | Not confirmed as covered. Chase's summary covers a trip canceled or cut short by sickness, severe weather or other covered situations | Not confirmed as covered. Amex's guide covers a trip canceled or interrupted by weather that stops a prudent person from traveling |
| Clubs lost or damaged by the airline | Up to $3,000 per traveler. A lower limit for sporting equipment is not confirmed | Up to $2,000 per person for checked bags, but sporting equipment is capped at $1,000 per person |
| Clubs arrive late | Up to $100 a day for 5 days once bags are more than 6 hours late, for essential purchases | No baggage delay benefit found in Amex's baggage guide |
| Flight canceled or badly delayed | Up to $500 per traveler after more than 12 hours (Preferred) or 6 hours (Reserve), or an overnight stay | Up to $500 per trip after more than 6 hours; 2 claims per 12 months |
| Whole trip canceled for a covered reason | Up to $10,000 per traveler, $20,000 per trip | Up to $10,000 per trip, $20,000 per card per 12 months |

## Rained-out rounds

Both issuers' trip cancellation cover is about the trip, not one activity inside it. Weather counts when it stops you from traveling or forces you home. No page read lists green fees or tee times as a covered loss.

That is "not confirmed" in both directions, and the full Chase guide was not read. If prepaid golf is a large part of the cost, ask the benefits administrator first.

## Lost or damaged clubs

**Chase Sapphire.** Chase's summary gives up to $3,000 per traveler for bags that are lost, damaged or stolen. The cover is secondary: you claim from the airline first. Sources disagree on any lower limit for clubs. AwardWallet lists $500 for valuables such as jewelry and electronics and does not mention sporting equipment. Another comparison shows $1,000 for jewelry, sporting equipment or electronics. Treat the limit for clubs as not confirmed.

**Amex Platinum.** Amex's Baggage Insurance Plan guide, revised April 19, 2024, lists sporting equipment as a high-risk item. The guide says: "Any High Risk Items are subject to $1,000 maximum per Covered Person." Total loss on one trip is capped at $3,000 per person. New York residents have different limits.

If a set of clubs is worth more than $1,000, the gap is yours on the Platinum Card.

Delta and Southwest carry a soft golf bag only under a limited release of liability. Whether a card pays after the airline refuses on those grounds is not confirmed.

## How you paid matters

| Card | What must be charged to the card |
|---|---|
| Sapphire cards | The trip booked with the card, through Chase Travel, or with Chase points. One writer reports an award flight qualified when the taxes and fees were paid with the card |
| Amex Platinum, baggage | The entire fare. Pay with Points bookings count. Tickets paid with airline frequent flyer miles do not |
| Amex Platinum, trip cancellation | Round-trip travel with the full transportation cost on the card. Sources disagree on award tickets |

## Late clubs and canceled flights

Chase's baggage delay benefit repays essential purchases. Sources give clothing and toiletries as examples. Whether rental clubs count is not confirmed.

Trip delay cover repays meals and a hotel. No source shows it paying for a missed round.

## Who should skip relying on it

- Anyone whose clubs are worth far more than $1,000. Card limits may not cover them. Other insurance was not checked for this page.
- Golfers with large prepaid, non-refundable golf packages. Card cover for the golf itself is not confirmed.
- Travelers who booked with airline miles and hold only the Amex Platinum.

Fees for checking the clubs are in [flying with golf clubs](/flying-with-golf-clubs-airline-fees/).

## Quick answers

**Does card insurance refund green fees if it rains?**
No source read shows that. The cover is for a canceled, interrupted or delayed trip.

**Are golf clubs covered if the airline loses them?**
Yes, within limits. Amex caps sporting equipment at $1,000 per person. The Chase limit for clubs is not confirmed.

**Which card covers clubs that arrive late?**
The Sapphire cards list baggage delay cover after 6 hours. None was found in Amex's baggage guide.

# Which Hawaii airport lounges can you get into with the Amex Platinum or Sapphire Reserve?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/hawaii-airport-lounges-by-card/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

Both cards get you into lounges at Honolulu and Maui, mostly through Priority Pass, and neither opens a lounge at Kona or Lihue. The Amex Platinum adds the Delta Sky Club in Honolulu when you fly Delta that day.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## One table: airport by card

Lounge lists change. Each row shows what the card issuer's own pages listed on November 20, 2026, unless noted.

| Airport | Amex Platinum | Chase Sapphire Reserve |
|---|---|---|
| Honolulu (HNL) | IASS Hawaii Lounge, Terminal 2 (Priority Pass). Delta Sky Club, Terminal 2 near gate F1, on a same-day Delta flight. Hawaiian Airlines Premier Club, Terminal 1 near gate A18, listed by Amex's lounge finder | IASS Hawaii Lounge, Terminal 2 (Priority Pass). Hawaiian Airlines Premier Club: not confirmed |
| Kahului, Maui (OGG) | Two Hawaiian Airlines Premier Club lounges (Priority Pass) | The same two Hawaiian Airlines Premier Club lounges (Priority Pass) |
| Kona (KOA) | None found | None found |
| Lihue, Kauai (LIH) | None found | None found |

Neither issuer has its own lounge in Hawaii. Amex's lounge finder shows no Centurion Lounge at Honolulu or Maui, and Chase's Honolulu and Maui guides list only Priority Pass lounges.

## Honolulu in detail

**IASS Hawaii Lounge.** Terminal 2, Garden Court. This is the one lounge both cards clearly open. Upgraded Points gives Priority Pass hours of 7:30 a.m. to 1:30 p.m. and 2 p.m. to 6 p.m. Chase's guide says it has no food. Amex's page says "Access is not guaranteed and is subject to space availability."

**Delta Sky Club.** Platinum only, and only with a same-day Delta flight. Basic economy tickets do not qualify. Each visit uses one of the card's 10 Sky Club visits per year.

**Hawaiian Airlines Premier Club, Terminal 1.** Here the sources disagree. Amex's US lounge finder lists it for Platinum holders, up to 3 hours before departure, space permitting. A lounge directory says it rejoined Priority Pass on November 24, 2025. But Chase's Honolulu guide lists only the IASS lounge, and Upgraded Points names IASS as the one Priority Pass lounge at the airport. For Sapphire Reserve holders, access is not confirmed. Check the Priority Pass app on the day.

**Hawaiian Plumeria Lounge.** Not open to either card. It left Priority Pass on April 1, 2025. Some older guides, including one Chase page, still list it. A $40 day pass is sold at the desk.

## Maui in detail

Both cards open the two Hawaiian Airlines Premier Club lounges at Kahului through Priority Pass. One is across from gate 17 and one is opposite gate 15.

- Entry starts 2 hours before departure.
- Amex lists the South lounge for domestic flights only.
- Amex also lists an adults-only rule for the South lounge, with an exception for children under 2.
- Chase describes snacks and drinks, not meals.
- Either lounge can turn people away when full.

## Kona and Lihue

Each airport has one lounge, a Hawaiian Airlines Premier Club. A lounge site that last checked Lihue on October 28, 2026 says entry there is for Hawaiian and Alaska premium-cabin passengers and certain Atmos Rewards members, with no day pass, and that Priority Pass is not accepted.

"None found" is the honest wording. Amex's lounge finder would not load results for either airport, and no Chase page for them was found.

## Rules that apply to both cards

| Rule | Amex Platinum | Sapphire Reserve |
|---|---|---|
| Priority Pass setup | Must enroll first | Physical card or Priority Pass digital card needed |
| Guests | Two free where the lounge takes guests | Two free; more at $27 each |
| Priority Pass restaurants | Not included | Not stated in the pages read |
| When full | Entry can be refused | Entry can be refused |

## Who should skip it

Lounge access in Hawaii is thin. A traveler flying home from Kona or Lihue gets nothing from either card at the airport. A traveler flying Hawaiian from Honolulu's Terminal 1 may get nothing from the Sapphire Reserve. If lounges are the main reason for paying $795 or $895 a year, a Hawaii trip does not support it. See [how the two cards compare for Hawaii](/amex-platinum-vs-sapphire-reserve-hawaii/).

## Quick answers

**Is there a Centurion Lounge or Chase Sapphire Lounge in Hawaii?**
No Centurion Lounge appears in Amex's lounge finder for Hawaii, and Chase's Hawaii guides list only Priority Pass lounges.

**Which lounge in Honolulu takes Priority Pass?**
The IASS Hawaii Lounge in Terminal 2. Whether the Hawaiian Airlines Premier Club in Terminal 1 also does is disputed between sources.

**Can either card get me into a lounge at Kona or Lihue?**
No access was found for either card at either airport.

# For one week in Hawaii, which travel card comes closest to paying for itself?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/hawaii-trip-which-card-pays-for-itself/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

Counting only what one Hawaii trip returns, the Chase Sapphire Preferred is the only one of the three that covers its own fee: a $100 hotel credit against a $95 fee. The Sapphire Reserve comes back about $245 short and the Amex Platinum about $415 short, so both need their other credits to break even.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## The assumptions

Change any of these and the sums change.

- Two travelers, one trip in the year, flying from the mainland in economy.
- One checked bag each, both ways, at $45 a bag. That is $180 in bag fees.
- Five hotel nights, booked as one prepaid stay through the card's travel site, at a hotel in that card's program.
- Counted: statement credits the trip itself triggers.
- Not counted: welcome offers, which vary by applicant and change; points earned; lounge visits; insurance; credits for things outside the trip, such as dining or streaming.

## The worked example

| | Sapphire Preferred | Sapphire Reserve | Amex Platinum |
|---|---|---|---|
| Annual fee | $95 | $795 | $895 |
| Hotel credit used | $100 (Chase Travel hotel stay) | $250 (The Edit, prepaid, two nights or more) | $300 (Fine Hotels + Resorts or The Hotel Collection, prepaid) |
| Travel or airline credit used | None | $300 (any travel purchase) | $180 of the $200 airline fee credit, for the bag fees |
| Total credits from the trip | $100 | $550 | $480 |
| Credits minus fee | +$5 | -$245 | -$415 |
| Bag fees still paid by you | $180 | $180 (the $300 credit is already used in full) | $0 if both bags are on the one chosen airline |

Each premium card's hotel program also gives a $100 property credit and daily breakfast for two. If you would spend that $100 at the hotel anyway, the gaps shrink to about -$145 for the Reserve and -$315 for the Platinum.

## What sits behind each number

**Sapphire Preferred.** The $100 credit applies each account anniversary year to hotel stays bought through Chase Travel. The card has no bag fee benefit and no lounge access.

**Sapphire Reserve.** The $300 travel credit applies to any purchase the card categorizes as travel, so airfare or the hotel will use it in full. The Edit credit is up to $250 per prepaid booking with a two-night minimum, up to $500 a calendar year. Chase's travel guides name Hawaii hotels in The Edit, including The Royal Hawaiian. The full list was not read.

**Amex Platinum.** The hotel credit is up to $300 per half-year, so one stay uses one of the two. The airline fee credit works on one airline chosen in advance from Alaska, American, Delta, JetBlue, Southwest and United. Whether it applies to a bag fee on a Hawaiian-operated flight is not confirmed.

## What the trip does not show

Three things the table leaves out can matter more than the credits.

- **Hotel price.** The Reserve and Platinum credits only work at higher-priced hotels in each program. Booking a much dearer room to collect $300 costs more than it returns.
- **Lounges.** Both premium cards open lounges at Honolulu and Maui and none at Kona or Lihue. See [Hawaii lounges by card](/hawaii-airport-lounges-by-card/).
- **Points.** All three earn extra points on travel booked through their own travel sites. The value depends on what you spend.

## How the premium cards close the gap

| Card | Gap after the trip | Other yearly credits that could close it |
|---|---|---|
| Sapphire Reserve | $245 | A second $250 Edit stay; up to $300 dining; up to $300 StubHub; Lyft, DoorDash, Peloton and Apple credits |
| Amex Platinum | $415 | The second $300 hotel credit; up to $400 Resy; up to $300 digital entertainment; up to $200 Uber Cash; other listed credits |

A credit only counts if you would have bought the thing anyway. That question is worked through in [what the Platinum credits are worth](/amex-platinum-credits-real-value/) and [Preferred or Reserve for a light traveler](/sapphire-preferred-vs-reserve-light-traveler/).

## Who should skip which card

- One trip a year and no use for dining, ride or streaming credits: skip both premium cards. The sums above do not close.
- Condo or vacation rental instead of a hotel: none of the three hotel credits applies as assumed here.
- Flying home from Kona or Lihue and hoping for a lounge: neither premium card opens one there.

## Quick answers

**Which card pays for itself on one Hawaii trip?**
On trip credits alone, only the Sapphire Preferred: $100 back against a $95 fee.

**How far short is the Amex Platinum on one trip?**
About $415 under these assumptions: $480 in trip credits against an $895 fee.

**Do any of these cards include free checked bags?**
No. The Platinum's airline fee credit and the Reserve's travel credit can repay bag fees, within their rules.

- [Chase: Sapphire Reserve card page](https://creditcards.chase.com/rewards-credit-cards/sapphire/reserve)
- [Chase: how the Sapphire Reserve travel credit works](https://www.chase.com/personal/credit-cards/education/rewards-benefits/chase-sapphire-reserve-travel-credit-how-it-works)

# How do you check which Amex Platinum welcome offer you are shown, and why do people see different numbers?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/highest-amex-platinum-welcome-offer-how-to-check/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

You see your own Amex Platinum welcome offer by starting an application: Amex shows the points figure before you accept the card, and reviewers report no hard credit check up to that point. People see different numbers because Amex sets the offer for each applicant, so the headline of as high as 175,000 points is a ceiling and not a promise.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## Ways to check, side by side

| Route | What it shows | Credit check | Status in November 2026 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Amex public page | Your own offer, after you enter your details | Soft check to show the offer, per The Points Guy | Confirmed |
| A referral link | Your own offer, the same way | Same process reported | Confirmed; can differ from the public route |
| CardMatch tool | Targeted offers from several banks, sometimes Amex | Soft check | Whether it shows a Platinum offer now is not confirmed |
| Mail or email from Amex | A targeted offer, if you get one | None to receive it | Depends on being targeted |
| Private (incognito) window or another browser | The same public page | None to view | Not confirmed to change the offer |
| Prequalification page | Not described in any source read | Not confirmed | Not confirmed |

## The Amex application

The Points Guy describes the process this way: you submit an application, Amex generally runs a soft credit check, and your own welcome offer appears. You then accept or decline.

- If you decline, One Mile at a Time and Upgraded Points both report no effect on your credit score.
- If you accept, Amex may run a hard inquiry and opens the account.

Write down the points figure and the spending requirement from the offer screen, or save a copy of it.

A referral link leads to the same kind of application, and its number can match, beat or trail the public route. See [referral against public offer](/amex-platinum-referral-vs-public-offer/).

## CardMatch

CardMatch is a third-party tool that asks for your name, address and the last four digits of your Social Security number, then lists card offers you may be matched with. One Mile at a Time reports it uses only a soft check.

Its limits: that page was last updated in 2022, when it showed no targeted Platinum offer. No source read confirms a Platinum offer in CardMatch this month.

## Mail and email offers

Upgraded Points and The Points Guy both suggest opting in to Amex marketing messages, in your Amex account settings, to have a chance at a targeted offer. One Mile at a Time calls larger targeted offers rare. You cannot request one.

## Private windows and other browsers

This is the least certain route. Frequent Miler wrote in 2025 that some referral links showed the top offer only when opened "in certain ways or in certain browsers."

No 2026 article read for this page confirms that a private window changes the Platinum offer. Since Amex now sets the figure after you enter your details, the browser may matter less than it once did. Treat it as unproven.

## Why the numbers differ

- **Amex sets the offer per applicant.** Amex does not publish how. Upgraded Points names credit score, income and existing Amex cards as likely factors; that is the site's reading, not Amex's statement.
- **Your history with the card.** If you have or had the Platinum Card, you may be shown no welcome offer at all. See [the once-per-lifetime rule](/amex-once-per-lifetime-welcome-offer-rule/).
- **The route.** Referral links and targeted mailers can carry different offers from the public page.
- **The date.** Offers change. The spending requirement rose from $8,000 to $12,000 in February 2026.

## Who should skip it

- Anyone who has held the Platinum Card before. Checking is harmless, but the likely answer is no offer.
- Anyone who cannot reach $12,000 of normal spending in six months. The points figure does not matter if the requirement is out of reach. See [what counts toward it](/amex-platinum-welcome-offer-spending-requirement/).
- Anyone planning a mortgage or car loan soon. Viewing an offer is reported as a soft check, but accepting adds a hard inquiry and a new account. See [how an application affects your score](/does-applying-for-a-travel-card-hurt-credit-score/).
- Anyone who would not keep the card at $895 a year without the welcome offer.

## Quick answers

**Can I see my Amex Platinum offer without a hard credit check?**
Reviewers report yes. Amex shows the offer after a soft check, and a hard inquiry follows only if you accept.

**Does a private browser window show a higher offer?**
Not confirmed. Older reports say browsers sometimes mattered for referral links. No 2026 source read confirms it for the Platinum Card.

**Why did someone else get a higher number than I did?**
Amex sets each applicant's offer. Card history, credit profile, the route used and the date can all differ.

- [The Points Guy: Amex Platinum current offer](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/amex-platinum-current-offer/)
- [Upgraded Points: Amex Platinum welcome offer news](https://upgradedpoints.com/news/amex-platinum-up-to-175k-bonus/)
- [One Mile at a Time: Amex Platinum welcome offer](https://onemileatatime.com/reviews/credit-cards/american-express/amex-platinum-card-bonus/)

# Hilton Honors Surpass or Aspire: which Amex is worth it for two or three Hilton stays a year?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/hilton-surpass-vs-aspire-amex/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

For two or three Hilton stays a year, the Surpass ($150) is the easier card to earn back, because its Hilton credits can cover most of the fee on those stays. The Aspire ($550) comes out ahead only if you will use its yearly free night at a hotel you would otherwise pay well for, plus its resort or flight credits.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## The two cards side by side

| | Surpass | Aspire |
|---|---|---|
| Annual fee | $150 | $550 |
| Hilton status | Gold | Diamond |
| Points at Hilton | 12 per dollar | 14 per dollar |
| Hilton credit | Up to $50 a quarter ($200 a year), any Hilton property | Up to $200 each half-year ($400 a year), participating Hilton resorts only |
| Free night | Only after $15,000 of purchases in a calendar year | One each year, no spend needed |
| Flight credit | None | Up to $50 a quarter ($200 a year) |
| CLEAR+ credit | None | Up to $219 a year |
| Car rental status | National Emerald Club Executive | National Emerald Club Executive |

Enrollment is needed for some benefits. Unused credits do not carry over to the next quarter or half-year.

## The Surpass sum for two or three stays

The Surpass credit is paid by quarter. Each quarter in which you spend at least $50 directly with a Hilton property gives $50 back.

| Hilton stays, each in a different quarter | Credit used | Fee left to cover |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | $50 | $100 |
| 2 | $100 | $50 |
| 3 | $150 | $0 |
| 4 | $200 | $50 ahead |

Two stays in the same quarter count once. Three summer stays in July and August use one $50 credit, not three.

What is left of the fee has to come from Gold status and points. One Mile at a Time lists Gold benefits as breakfast or a daily food and beverage credit, bonus points and room upgrades when available. The free night on this card needs $15,000 of card spending in a calendar year, so an occasional guest who uses the card only at hotels will not earn it.

## The Aspire sum for two or three stays

The Aspire costs $400 more. What it adds for a light traveler:

- **One free night a year.** It arrives in the first card year and after each renewal, and must be used within one year of issue. Its value is the price of the room you use it on.
- **Resort credit, up to $200 per half-year.** It applies only at participating Hilton resorts. A city hotel or a roadside Hampton Inn does not count. Both halves need a resort stay to get the full $400.
- **Flight credit, up to $50 a quarter.** It applies to flights bought from an airline or through Amex Travel. Four separate quarters with a flight purchase are needed for the full $200.
- **CLEAR+ credit, up to $219.** Worth that only if you would pay for CLEAR+.
- **Diamond status** in place of Gold.

Three example years:

| Your year | Aspire value used | Against the $550 fee |
|---|---|---|
| Two city stays, one flight purchase, free night used on a $250 room | $50 + $250 = $300 | $250 short |
| One resort stay, flights in two quarters, free night on a $300 room | $200 + $100 + $300 = $600 | $50 ahead |
| Resort stays in both halves, flights in four quarters, free night on a $400 room | $400 + $200 + $400 = $1,000 | $450 ahead |

The room prices are examples to show the sum, not quotes.

Sources differ on what Hilton points are worth: The Points Guy says 0.4 cents each, One Mile at a Time about 0.5 cents. At two or three stays a year, the two extra points per dollar on the Aspire add only a few dollars.

## How to decide

Ask three questions about the next 12 months:

1. Will at least one stay be at a Hilton resort? If no, the resort credit is worth nothing.
2. Is there a night you would otherwise pay $300 or more for, where you could use the free night?
3. Will you buy airfare in several different quarters?

Two or three "yes" answers point to the Aspire. One or none points to the Surpass.

## Who should skip both

- People whose two or three hotel stays a year are spread across different chains.
- People who stay only at low-priced Hilton brands, where a free night and elite status save little.
- People who do not want to track quarterly and half-year credits.
- People who would put less than $50 a quarter on a Hilton bill.

Welcome offers vary by applicant and change. The Points Guy notes that moving from the Surpass to the Aspire by upgrade may not come with a welcome offer.

## Quick answers

**Does the Surpass come with a free night every year?**
No. The Surpass free night is earned only after $15,000 of purchases in a calendar year. The Aspire gives one each year.

**Can the Aspire resort credit be used at any Hilton?**
No. It applies to charges made directly with participating Hilton resorts, up to $200 in each half of the year.

**Which status does each card give?**
The Surpass gives Hilton Honors Gold. The Aspire gives Diamond.

## Sources

- [The Points Guy: Hilton Surpass vs. Hilton Aspire](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/hotel/hilton/hilton-surpass-vs-hilton-aspire/)
- [AwardWallet: Hilton Honors Aspire](https://awardwallet.com/credit-cards/hilton-honors/hilton-aspire/)
- [One Mile at a Time: Hilton Surpass review](https://onemileatatime.com/reviews/credit-cards/american-express/hilton-surpass-card-worth-it/)

# How does Rakuten work, step by step?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/how-does-rakuten-work-step-by-step/
Facts checked: 2026-11-27
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

Rakuten works in six steps: you create a free account, click through Rakuten to a store, and buy as usual; the store pays Rakuten a commission, Rakuten passes part of it to you as cash back, and confirmed cash back is paid four times a year once you have about $5. Every step below was re-read on Rakuten's help pages on November 27, 2026.

This page is information, not financial advice. Still deciding? See [is Rakuten free](/is-rakuten-free/) and [is Rakuten legit, and how it makes money](/is-rakuten-legit-how-it-makes-money/). What each bonus asks you to spend is on [how the sign-up and referral bonuses work](/rakuten-50-bonus-how-it-works/).

## Step 1: Create an account

Rakuten says joining is free. You sign up with an email and password, or with a Facebook, Google or Apple account. Its terms say members must be at least 18 and live in the 50 states or Washington D.C., and each person may have one account. No card is needed to join. What the form asks for is on [how to sign up for Rakuten](/how-to-sign-up-for-rakuten/), and the two kinds of bonus are compared on [welcome bonus or referral bonus](/rakuten-welcome-bonus-vs-referral-bonus/).

## Step 2: Start a shopping trip

A "shopping trip" is Rakuten's name for the click that takes you from Rakuten to a store. Each trip gets a unique number, which Rakuten uses to verify the purchase with the store. Rakuten's help page says purchases earn cash back "only if you start a Shopping Trip with Rakuten." A trip stays in your account history for up to three months, even if you buy nothing.

There are five ways to earn; the first three start a trip with a click, and the last two use a linked card.

| Way to shop | How the trip starts | Where it works |
|---|---|---|
| Rakuten.com | Pick the store on the site and click through | Computer or phone browser |
| Browser extension | Click the activate button when it appears on a store's site | Desktop Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari; Safari on iPhone |
| Mobile app | Tap the store in the app | iOS and Android |
| In a physical store | Link a payment card, add the store's offer, pay with that card | Participating stores |
| At a restaurant | Link a card once and pay with it | 22,000+ restaurants, at 5%, per Rakuten |

A pop-up confirms that cash back is active. You need a new trip for every purchase, and the browser window you buy in must be the one that opened from Rakuten. Rakuten's pages differ on how many stores take part: its main help page says 3,500+, its extension page over 3,700. Rates differ by store and change daily; this morning's are on [Rakuten rates today, by store](/rakuten-cash-back-rates-today-by-store/).

For how the two main tools differ, see [the app and the extension compared](/rakuten-app-vs-browser-extension/). Card linking has its own rules; see [how in-store cash back works](/rakuten-in-store-cash-back-how-it-works/) and [which cards can be linked](/rakuten-link-card-for-in-store-cash-back/).

## Step 3: Buy at the store

You check out on the store's own website and pay the store, not Rakuten. Rakuten's example: spend $100 at a store offering 5% and you earn $5. Taxes and shipping do not earn cash back, most gift cards are excluded, and each store lists its excluded items. Orders finished by phone or chat do not qualify.

Rakuten's checklist for an order that tracks:

- Activate before adding anything to the cart.
- Check out in the tab that opened from Rakuten.
- Use only coupon codes listed on Rakuten.
- Accept the store's cookies, and turn off ad blockers, VPNs and cookie blockers.
- Keep the order. Returned or canceled orders do not earn.

## Step 4: The store pays Rakuten, and Rakuten shares it

The store reports the order to Rakuten and pays it a commission for sending the shopper. Rakuten keeps a portion and gives the rest to you as cash back. What share Rakuten keeps is not confirmed; its page says only that it shares part. The business side is covered in [how Rakuten makes money](/is-rakuten-legit-how-it-makes-money/).

## Step 5: Processing, pending, confirmed

| Status | What it means | Typical time, per Rakuten |
|---|---|---|
| Processing | Rakuten is waiting for the store to send the order details | 24 to 48 hours |
| Pending | The store has reported the order; its return period is running | 3 to 17 weeks overall; 3 to 14 weeks for online and in-store shopping |
| Confirmed | The amount is in your confirmed balance | Included in the next payment |
| Ineligible | The order did not qualify | Returns, exclusions, coupon codes not found on Rakuten |

Other kinds of purchase run on their own clocks. Rakuten's payment page says dining is confirmed within 3 to 5 days, and travel typically within 45 to 120 days after the booking is complete. Its terms say travel rewards typically are not confirmed until after the travel itself. See [how long a purchase takes to show up](/rakuten-how-long-until-purchase-shows-up/), and if nothing appears, [what to do when cash back did not track](/rakuten-missing-cash-back-what-to-do/). The terms give 90 days from the purchase to report it.

## Step 6: Get paid

Rakuten pays on February 15, May 15, August 15 and November 15. Each payment covers the cash back confirmed before that date. Bonuses are confirmed together with the purchase that earned them.

The minimum is about $5. Rakuten's help page says $5 or more; its terms say $5.01. A smaller balance carries over to the next date.

Rakuten's payment page lists PayPal, check, Bilt points and Samsung Cash. Its home page lists PayPal, Bilt points and check. Eligible American Express card members can take Membership Rewards points instead. A check or PayPal payment needs a mailing address on the account. The payment page also offers a faster route: a confirmed balance of at least $5 can be redeemed for a gift card, within limits. Worked dates are in [when Rakuten pays](/rakuten-when-do-you-get-paid/).

## Who should skip it

- You want the saving at checkout. Rakuten pays months later; a lower price or a coupon is money today.
- You do not want a company recording where you shop. See [what the extension collects](/rakuten-browser-extension-safe-privacy/).
- You always use coupon codes from other sites. Codes not listed on Rakuten can void the cash back.
- You shop online once or twice a year. The balance may sit under the minimum for a long time.

## Quick answers

**Do you pay Rakuten anything?**
No. Rakuten says joining is free. Its income is the commission stores pay for each sale.

**Do you have to click through Rakuten every time?**
Yes. Each purchase needs its own shopping trip, started from the site, app or extension.

**How often does Rakuten pay?**
Four times a year: February 15, May 15, August 15 and November 15, with about $5 confirmed.

# How does TopCashback work, step by step, for a first purchase?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/how-does-topcashback-work-step-by-step/
Facts checked: 2026-11-25
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

TopCashback works in three steps: find the store on TopCashback, click the pink "Get Cash Back" button, and buy on the store's site as usual. Its Getting Started page says the purchase shows in your account within about seven days, and takes one to three months on average to become money you can withdraw.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## The three steps

From TopCashback's Getting Started page, read on November 25, 2026:

1. **Search.** Log in and find the store or service. The page says cash back is offered at more than 7,000 stores.
2. **Select.** Click the pink "Get Cash Back" button. The store's website opens in a new tab.
3. **Buy.** Shop in that new tab as you normally would. The value of the purchase is recorded in your account.

Behind those steps, the help page explains, the click tells the store that TopCashback sent you. The store pays TopCashback a commission, and TopCashback passes it to you. Tracking is done with cookies and happens in the background; nothing about cash back appears on the store's own pages.

## The timeline of a first purchase

| When | What happens | What you see |
|---|---|---|
| Day 0 | You click through and buy | Nothing yet |
| Within about 7 days | The store reports the sale | Cash back shows as "In Progress" |
| 1 to 3 months, on average | The store confirms the sale and pays TopCashback | Cash back turns "Available" |
| When you ask | You cash out | Payment "within a couple of working days" |

All of the figures are TopCashback's own. The one-to-three-month step is an average; each store sets its own period, and travel bookings wait until the trip is over.

## Set up payment details early

One detail on the Getting Started page is easy to miss: after you add new payment details, TopCashback disables payments for 72 hours as a security measure. Its tip is to add your details before you are ready to cash out, so the hold has passed by the time you need it.

Payment methods listed are PayPal, Venmo, bank transfer and more than 30 gift cards. More on each is on [how TopCashback pays](/topcashback-how-to-cash-out-and-when/).

## Coupons: the rule that catches people

The Getting Started page says only coupon codes "listed and authorized by TopCashback" work together with cash back. They are in the Special Deals and Coupons section of each store's page on TopCashback. A code from another site can cancel the cash back for that order.

## What can go wrong

TopCashback's help page lists the usual reasons a purchase does not track:

- A coupon code TopCashback did not list.
- An ad blocker.
- Buying in a different tab from the one that opened after the click.
- Clicking another cash back or coupon site afterward.

If a purchase has not shown after seven days, the Getting Started page says to contact customer service.

## How much is realistic

TopCashback's help pages say members earn $450 a year on average, and that those members shop through the site at least twice a month. The figure is the company's own and how it is calculated is not stated. What one person earns depends on what they buy and each store's rate, and rates change. A person who shops online a few times a year should expect far less than the average.

Cash back is a share of money already spent. Buying something extra to earn it costs more than it returns.

## Ways to start a purchase

| Tool | Where it works | Page |
|---|---|---|
| Website | Any browser | This page |
| Browser extension | Desktop only | [How the extension works](/topcashback-browser-extension-how-it-works/) |
| App | iPhone, iPad, Android | [How the app works](/topcashback-app-how-it-works/) |

## Who should skip it

- You want the money within days. The store's confirmation takes one to three months on average.
- You rely on coupon codes from other sites. They can cancel the cash back.
- You keep an ad blocker on for every site.
- You shop online rarely. The amounts will be small.

For what the company is and how it earns, see [is TopCashback legit](/is-topcashback-legit-how-it-makes-money/). For the larger US site's version of the same steps, see [how Rakuten works](/how-does-rakuten-work-step-by-step/).

## Quick answers

**How long does TopCashback take to show a purchase?**
Up to seven days to appear as "In Progress," by its Getting Started page.

**How long until TopCashback cash back is available?**
One to three months on average after it shows, because the store has to confirm the sale and pay TopCashback first.

**Can I use a coupon code with TopCashback?**
Only codes listed on TopCashback's own page for that store. Other codes can cancel the cash back.

## Sources

- [TopCashback: Getting Started](https://www.topcashback.com/getting-started/)
- [TopCashback: How does TopCashback work?](https://www.topcashback.com/help/how-we-work/)

# How many Amex or Chase points does a round trip to Europe cost?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/how-many-points-for-a-flight-to-europe/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

Through airline partners, a round trip from the US to Europe starts at about 12,000 to 55,000 Amex or Chase points in economy and about 81,000 to 120,000 in business class, at each program's lowest published price. Taxes and surcharges run from about $100 to more than $1,000 on top, and the low prices are not offered on every date.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## Lowest published prices, round trip

One-way prices from the sources are doubled here. "Both" means Amex and Chase points transfer to the program.

| Program (who can transfer) | Economy | Business | Cash on top, per sources |
|---|---|---|---|
| Virgin Atlantic, own flights to London (both) | From 12,000 East Coast, 18,000 West Coast | From 58,000; price moves with demand | About $160 out and $250 to $300 back in economy; about $700 each way in business |
| Virgin Atlantic, on Air France or KLM (both) | 24,000 East Coast, 30,000 Central and West | Not confirmed | Not confirmed |
| Aer Lingus Avios, Northeast to Dublin (both) | 26,000 off-peak, 40,000 peak | Not confirmed | Under $120 each way |
| Iberia Avios, New York or Boston to Madrid (both) | 32,000 off-peak | 81,000 off-peak | About $125 |
| Flying Blue, Air France and KLM (both) | 50,000 | 120,000 | 237 euros each way in economy and $608 each way in business, in Flying Blue's examples |
| United MileagePlus (Chase only) | About 52,000 to 54,000 | 160,000 on United, 176,000 on partners | Not confirmed |
| ANA Mileage Club, partner airlines (Amex only) | 55,000 | 100,000 | Varies by airline; none on United or Air Canada |
| Air Canada Aeroplan (both) | 65,000 to 85,000 by distance | 150,000 on trips of 4,001 to 6,000 miles each way | No fuel surcharges on partners |
| Avianca LifeMiles (Amex only) | 70,000 to 96,000 | 138,000 to 186,000 | No fuel surcharges |

Sources and dates: Frequent Miler (September 2026) for Virgin Atlantic, United, ANA and Avianca; The Points Guy (September 2026) for Iberia, Aer Lingus and Flying Blue; Air Canada's chart notice for Aeroplan, effective June 1, 2026; AwardWallet for ANA round trips.

## What the table leaves out

**Fare types.** Since September 8, 2026, Flying Blue sells Light, Standard and Flex awards. The 25,000 and 60,000 one-way prices are Light fares. Light economy has no checked bag, no changes and no refunds. Standard starts at 30,000 in economy and 75,000 in business.

**Surcharges.** A Virgin Atlantic business round trip at 58,000 points can carry about $1,400 in surcharges, by The Points Guy's one-way figure. Frequent Miler notes that Virgin Atlantic awards on Delta flights can add $1,000 or more each way.

**Delta.** Amex points move to Delta SkyMiles, where prices follow the cash fare. Thrifty Traveler (April 2026) reports sale fares from 26,000 miles round trip and basic economy above 100,000 on other dates. AwardWallet found Los Angeles to Paris at 68,000.

**Transfer time.** ANA transfers from Amex take two to three days. The seat can go in that time.

## Booking through the card's travel site instead

Any seat for sale can be bought with points at a fixed rate:

- Amex Travel: 1 cent per point on flights.
- Chase Travel: 1 cent per point, or up to 2 cents on a Sapphire Reserve when a booking carries [a Points Boost](/chase-points-boost-explained/).

As an illustration only: a $700 economy fare costs 70,000 points at 1 cent. A $3,500 business fare costs 350,000 points at 1 cent and 175,000 at 2 cents. These fares are made-up round numbers, not quotes.

So for economy, a partner award helps most when cash fares are high. For business class, partner awards are usually far below the travel-site price in points, if a seat is open. To compare a given seat, use [the cents-per-point check](/points-or-cash-when-to-pay-with-points/).

## Where sources disagree

- **Iberia business class.** The Points Guy and a June 2026 AwardWallet page give 40,500 Avios one way off-peak from New York and Boston. An older AwardWallet page still prints 34,000. Frequent Miler gives 50,500, which matches The Points Guy's price from Chicago and Miami.
- **Aeroplan.** Thrifty Traveler (April 2026) gives 70,000 round trip in economy and 70,000 one way in business. Air Canada's chart changed on June 1, 2026; the table uses the newer figures. The business price on trips under 4,000 miles after that change was not confirmed.
- **Flying Blue fees.** Frequent Miler says about $300 to $350 each way; Flying Blue's own business example is $608.

## Who should skip a partner award

- Travelers with fixed dates in July or August. The lowest prices are scarce then.
- Anyone who would pay $1,400 in surcharges to save points on a seat that costs little more in cash.
- People unwilling to search for the seat before transferring. Transfers cannot be reversed.

Which programs take which points: [Amex partners](/amex-transfer-partners-which-are-worth-it/) and [Chase partners](/chase-transfer-partners-which-are-worth-it/).

## Quick answers

**What is the lowest points price to Europe in economy?**
Virgin Atlantic to London, from 6,000 points each way from the East Coast, plus taxes near $160 out and more coming back.

**How many points for business class to Europe?**
From about 81,000 round trip on Iberia off-peak to 120,000 on Flying Blue, plus fees. Most other programs charge more.

**Can Chase points book ANA awards?**
Not through ANA Mileage Club, which takes Amex points only. Chase points reach Europe through Flying Blue, Virgin Atlantic, Avios programs, Aeroplan and United.

# How many Amex or Chase points does a round trip to Japan cost?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/how-many-points-for-a-flight-to-japan/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

At the lowest partner prices, a round trip from the US to Japan costs about 40,000 to 80,000 points in economy and about 100,000 to 120,000 in business class, plus taxes and surcharges of a few hundred dollars. Those prices depend on finding an open award seat, and business-class seats on ANA are hard to find.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## Lowest published prices, round trip

One-way prices from the sources are doubled here. "Both" means Amex and Chase points transfer to the program.

| Program (who can transfer) | Flies on | Economy | Business |
|---|---|---|---|
| ANA Mileage Club (Amex only) | ANA | 40,000 low season, 50,000 regular, 55,000 high | 100,000 low, 105,000 regular, 110,000 high |
| Virgin Atlantic Flying Club (both) | ANA | 60,000 from the West Coast, 65,000 from the Central and Eastern US | 105,000 from the West Coast, 120,000 from the Central and Eastern US |
| United MileagePlus (Chase only) | United, ANA | About 80,000 | About 176,000 to 220,000 |
| Air Canada Aeroplan (both) | Air Canada, United, ANA | 65,000 on routes under 5,000 miles each way; longer routes not confirmed | 170,000 on routes of 5,001 to 7,000 miles each way |
| Avianca LifeMiles (Amex only) | ANA, United | About 110,000 | 180,000 to 200,000 |

Sources and dates: Upgraded Points for the ANA chart and the Virgin Atlantic prices; AwardWallet (April 2026) for Virgin Atlantic; Frequent Miler for United and LifeMiles; Air Canada's chart notice for Aeroplan, effective June 1, 2026.

Los Angeles and San Francisco to Tokyo are longer than 5,000 miles, so the 65,000-point Aeroplan economy price applies to few US routes.

## The cash part

- **ANA Mileage Club.** Upgraded Points says ANA's fuel surcharges can pass $500 on a round trip.
- **Virgin Atlantic on ANA.** Surcharges are passed on and vary. AwardWallet priced Chicago to Tokyo at about $183 one way. Frequent Miler's figures from 2024 were about $360 out and $450 back.
- **Aeroplan and LifeMiles.** No fuel surcharges, per Frequent Miler.

## What makes these awards hard to book

- **Seats.** Upgraded Points says ANA premium-cabin award space is hard to find. AwardWallet calls ANA seats from the mainland US "hit or miss".
- **Virgin Atlantic is booked by phone.** Its website does not show ANA seats. AwardWallet's method: find the seat on United's or Air Canada's site, call Virgin Atlantic to confirm it, then transfer. Reports say Virgin Atlantic cannot book ANA flights leaving the US within 14 days.
- **ANA transfers take about two days** from Amex. The seat can go in that time, and the transfer cannot be reversed.
- **Chase points do not move to ANA Mileage Club.** With Chase points, the routes to an ANA seat are Virgin Atlantic, United and Aeroplan.

## Other routes

**Delta (Amex only).** SkyMiles prices follow the cash fare. Thrifty Traveler, in a page last changed in October 2025, reported sale fares to Tokyo from 30,000 miles round trip in economy, with 30,000 to 50,000 typical in a sale. Outside sales, prices are much higher.

**Japan Airlines.** Chase and Amex points reach Japan Airlines seats through British Airways Avios, and since November 18, 2026 Chase points also move to Cathay Pacific Asia Miles and Qantas, which partner with Japan Airlines. Current prices for those awards were not confirmed. The lowest published Japan Airlines prices are in programs that take neither Amex nor Chase points.

**The card's travel site.** Amex Travel gives 1 cent per point on flights. Chase Travel gives 1 cent, or up to 2 cents on a Sapphire Reserve with [a Points Boost](/chase-points-boost-explained/). As an illustration only: a $1,200 economy fare costs 120,000 points at 1 cent, and a $5,000 business fare costs 500,000 points at 1 cent or 250,000 at 2 cents. Those fares are made-up round numbers, not quotes.

## Where sources disagree

- **ANA's own chart.** Upgraded Points lists 40,000 to 55,000 in economy and 100,000 to 110,000 in business, round trip. Frequent Miler's one-way figures match for low and regular season but give 82,500 one way in business in high season. AwardWallet gives 50,000 and 110,000 round trip on partner airlines. ANA revised its chart on June 24, 2025; its own chart page did not load, so these figures were not confirmed there.
- **United.** Frequent Miler gives 40,000 one way in economy and 88,000 to 110,000 in business. Other 2026 pages in search results give 35,000 and 70,000 to 100,000. United has no fixed chart; the price on the day is the price.
- **Virgin Atlantic.** Sources agree on 52,500 and 60,000 one way in business class. Virgin Atlantic raised these prices in 2024, and older pages show lower figures.

## Who should skip a points ticket to Japan

- Travelers fixed on cherry blossom season or other peak weeks, when award seats are scarce.
- People who will not make a phone booking or wait for a transfer.
- Economy travelers when cash fares are low. At 60,000 to 80,000 points, an $800 fare (an illustration, not a quote) returns about 1 to 1.3 cents per point before fees; run [the cents-per-point check](/points-or-cash-when-to-pay-with-points/).
- Families needing four seats on one flight in business class.

Which programs take which points: [Amex partners](/amex-transfer-partners-which-are-worth-it/) and [Chase partners](/chase-transfer-partners-which-are-worth-it/).

## Quick answers

**What is the lowest points price for business class to Japan?**
About 100,000 ANA miles round trip in low season (Amex points only), or 105,000 Virgin Atlantic points from the West Coast, plus surcharges.

**Can Chase points book ANA?**
Not through ANA's own program. Chase points move to Virgin Atlantic, United and Aeroplan, which can each book ANA seats.

**Can you book one way?**
Yes with Virgin Atlantic, United, Aeroplan and LifeMiles. AwardWallet says ANA Mileage Club has allowed one-way awards since June 2025.

# How do you sign up for Rakuten, and what does it ask for?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/how-to-sign-up-for-rakuten/
Facts checked: 2026-11-26
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

To sign up for Rakuten you give an email address and a password, or you join with a Facebook, Google or Apple account. No payment card or bank account is needed to join; a mailing address and a payment choice are needed later, before Rakuten will pay you.

This page is information, not financial advice. It covers only the joining step, as read on Rakuten's own pages on November 26, 2026. What happens after that is on [how Rakuten works, step by step](/how-does-rakuten-work-step-by-step/), and the costs are on [is Rakuten free](/is-rakuten-free/).

## What the sign-up asks for

| Item | Needed to join? | What Rakuten's pages say |
|---|---|---|
| Email and password | Yes, unless you use a social sign-in | The terms name an email address and password as what creates the account |
| Facebook, Google or Apple account | Optional | The join article lists all three as other ways to join |
| Credit or debit card | No | No card is named as a condition of membership |
| Bank account | No | Not asked for; payment goes by PayPal, check or another method you pick later |
| Mailing address | Not to join; yes to be paid | The terms list a physical address as a condition of payment |
| Friend's email | Optional | Only if a member referred you and you did not use that member's link |
| Name or phone number on the join form | Not confirmed | The help pages read do not list these fields |

A card comes up only if you later choose to link one for in-store offers. That is a separate, optional step.

## Who can join

Rakuten's terms set three limits:

- **Age:** at least 18 years old.
- **Place:** the service is for residents of the 50 United States or Washington D.C. People living elsewhere are told not to use it. Rakuten runs separate sites for some other countries, such as Canada.
- **One account:** each person is limited to one account. The referral terms add that several accounts with the same name, address or email may be flagged.

## The page you join from matters

Rakuten gives a new member one joining bonus, tied to how the account was opened. Join from Rakuten's own pages and the welcome bonus shown there applies. Join through a member's link, or pick "Did someone refer you?" at the bottom of the join form and enter that member's Rakuten email, and the referral bonus applies instead. The join article describes the referral choice only on the join form; adding a referrer after the account exists is not confirmed.

Bonus amounts vary and change, and the two cannot be combined. The comparison is on [welcome bonus or referral bonus](/rakuten-welcome-bonus-vs-referral-bonus/).

## What has to happen after you join

Opening the account does not pay a bonus by itself. Rakuten's new member FAQ lists three steps:

1. Sign up for a new account.
2. Shop through Rakuten and make a qualifying purchase of at least $25 within 90 days of becoming a member.
3. Choose how you want to be paid in Account Settings, with a mailing address on file.

That $25 figure is the welcome bonus requirement as read on November 26, 2026. A referral offer sets its own spending requirement, and either can change. The rules on what counts as a qualifying purchase, and what makes a bonus fail, are on [how the sign-up and referral bonuses work](/rakuten-50-bonus-how-it-works/).

## Choosing cash or Amex points

Every account earns cash back unless you change it. Rakuten lists these ways to be paid: PayPal, check, Bilt Points, Samsung Cash, and Membership Rewards points for eligible American Express card members. The choice is made in Account Settings on the website, or under Account, then Choose How You Get Paid, in the app. Rakuten says it can be updated at any time.

| Choice | What you provide | Minimum to be paid |
|---|---|---|
| PayPal | A valid PayPal email, used on only one Rakuten account | $5 on the help page; $5.01 in the terms |
| Check | The name and mailing address in Account Settings | Same |
| Amex points | The username and password of a US Membership Rewards account | 501 confirmed points |

For points, Rakuten's FAQ says a new member is prompted during sign-up to connect a Membership Rewards account. The card must be enrolled in the US Membership Rewards program and not canceled or past due. Corporate cards and the Rakuten American Express Card are not eligible. Whether a switch to points can be undone is disputed among outside sources; see [how to switch to Amex points](/rakuten-how-to-switch-to-amex-points/) and [taking the sign-up bonus as points](/rakuten-sign-up-bonus-as-amex-points/).

## Who should skip it

- Anyone under 18, or living outside the 50 states and Washington D.C.
- Anyone who already has a Rakuten account, including an old Ebates one. The terms allow one account per person, and the joining bonuses are for new members.
- Anyone who does not want to give a mailing address. Rakuten says it needs one before it pays.
- Anyone who would shop only to reach a bonus requirement. That spending costs more than the bonus returns.

## Quick answers

**Do you need a credit card to sign up for Rakuten?**
No. An email and password, or a Facebook, Google or Apple sign-in, creates the account.

**How old do you have to be to join Rakuten?**
At least 18, and a resident of the 50 United States or Washington D.C., under Rakuten's terms.

**Can you sign up for Rakuten with Google or Apple?**
Yes. Rakuten's join article lists Facebook, Google and Apple as ways to join.

## Sources

- [Rakuten: How to join Rakuten](https://www.rakuten.com/help/article/how-to-join-rakuten-360002101108)
- [Rakuten: Terms and conditions](https://www.rakuten.com/help/article/terms-conditions)
- [Rakuten: Welcome bonus and new member FAQs](https://www.rakuten.com/help/article/welcome-bonus-new-member-faqs)
- [Rakuten: Choosing how you get paid](https://www.rakuten.com/help/article/choosing-how-you-get-paid-360002100828)
- [Rakuten: American Express Membership Rewards points FAQ](https://www.rakuten.com/help/article/american-express-membership-rewards-points-faq-360017609253)
- [Rakuten: Referral program terms](https://www.rakuten.com/help/article/referral-program-terms-360002101348)

# How many points does a Hyatt hotel in Hawaii cost per night?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/hyatt-hotels-hawaii-points-cost/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

A standard room runs from about 12,000 World of Hyatt points a night at Hyatt Place Waikiki Beach to 35,000 to 75,000 a night at Andaz Maui and Grand Hyatt Kauai, depending on the date. Guides disagree on the category of several Hawaii hotels, so treat the table as a starting point and confirm on Hyatt's site.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## How Hyatt prices a night now

Since May 20, 2026, each Hyatt category has five price levels instead of three: Lowest, Low, Moderate, Upper and Top. The hotel's category sets the range. The date sets the level.

| Category | Lowest | Low | Moderate | Upper | Top |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | 12,000 | 15,000 | 20,000 | 22,500 | 25,000 |
| 5 | 15,000 | 20,000 | 25,000 | 30,000 | 35,000 |
| 6 | 20,000 | 25,000 | 30,000 | 35,000 | 40,000 |
| 7 | 25,000 | 30,000 | 35,000 | 45,000 | 55,000 |
| 8 | 35,000 | 45,000 | 55,000 | 65,000 | 75,000 |

These figures come from AwardWallet's chart dated May 9, 2026. A Hawaii travel blog from February 2026 shows higher top prices for Category 6 (50,000) and Category 7 (60,000). Category 5 and Category 8 match in both.

## Hyatt hotels in Hawaii

One guide, updated November 20, 2026, counts eight Hyatt properties in Hawaii and none on the Big Island.

| Hotel | Island | Category | Points per night (AwardWallet chart) | Do sources agree? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hyatt Place Waikiki Beach | Oahu | 4 | 12,000 to 25,000 | Yes, though one guide calls it Category 3 in one place |
| Hyatt Centric Waikiki Beach | Oahu | 5 | 15,000 to 35,000 | Yes |
| Hyatt Regency Waikiki Beach Resort & Spa | Oahu | 5 | 15,000 to 35,000 | No. Two guides say 5, one says 6 |
| Hyatt Regency Maui Resort & Spa | Maui | 6 | 20,000 to 40,000 | Yes on category. One blog puts the top price at 50,000 |
| Hyatt Vacation Club at Ka'anapali Beach | Maui | 7 | 25,000 to 55,000 | One source only |
| Hana-Maui Resort | Maui | 7 | 25,000 to 55,000 | One source only |
| Andaz Maui at Wailea Resort | Maui | 8 | 35,000 to 75,000 | No. Two guides say 8, a February 2026 blog says 7 |
| Grand Hyatt Kauai Resort & Spa | Kauai | 8 | 35,000 to 75,000 | No. Two guides say 8, a February 2026 blog says 7 |

One article says Grand Hyatt Kauai moved from Category 7 to Category 8 in the May 2026 change. That would explain why the older blog shows 7.

A news item also reported a new Hyatt Place and Hyatt House on Oahu at 20,000 points a night. Not confirmed.

## Where the sources conflict most

- **Prices above the chart.** One article cites 66,000 to 90,000 points a night at Grand Hyatt Kauai in July and August 2026. Upgraded Points saw 70,000 shown on a night labeled "Lowest". Both are out of line with a standard-room chart that tops out at 75,000. The likely cause is that only larger room types were left, but that is not confirmed.
- **Old ranges on current pages.** One guide updated this month still shows three-level prices that predate May 2026.
- **Resort fees.** One article says Grand Hyatt Kauai's resort fee, given as $55 a night, is waived on award nights but not on Points + Cash stays. Another guide says Hyatt hotels in Hawaii have no resort fees and then describes one at the same hotel. Ask the hotel.

## What that means in Chase points

Chase points move to Hyatt at 1:1 from a Sapphire Reserve and at 4:3 from a Sapphire Preferred. At 4:3, multiply the Hyatt price by four and divide by three.

| Five nights at | Hyatt points | Chase points from a Reserve | Chase points from a Preferred |
|---|---|---|---|
| Category 4, Lowest | 60,000 | 60,000 | 80,000 |
| Category 8, Lowest | 175,000 | 175,000 | 233,334 |
| Category 8, Top | 375,000 | 375,000 | 500,000 |

To judge a booking, divide the cash rate with taxes and fees by the points needed. The Points Guy values a Hyatt point at 1.65 cents as of November 2026. See also [Chase points for a Hawaii trip](/chase-points-to-hawaii-best-uses/).

## Who should skip it

- Sapphire Preferred holders with under 100,000 points who want a resort. That balance covers about two nights at Category 8, Lowest level.
- Travelers going to the Big Island. No Hyatt was listed there.
- Anyone traveling at Christmas or in midsummer who cannot move dates. Top-level nights cost about twice the Lowest level.

## Quick answers

**What is the cheapest Hyatt in Hawaii on points?**
Hyatt Place Waikiki Beach, listed as Category 4, from 12,000 points a night at the Lowest level.

**How many points is Andaz Maui per night?**
Most recent guides list it as Category 8, which is 35,000 to 75,000 points for a standard room. One older blog says Category 7.

**Do Chase points still move to Hyatt 1:1?**
From a Sapphire Reserve, yes. From a Sapphire Preferred the rate is 4:3.
