# Is Ebates now Rakuten?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/is-ebates-now-rakuten/
Facts checked: 2026-11-25
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

Yes. Ebates and Rakuten are the same cash back service: Rakuten bought Ebates in 2014 and the Ebates name was replaced by Rakuten in 2019. Rakuten's own pages say accounts and cash back balances were unchanged, and the old ebates.com address now forwards to rakuten.com.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## What happened, by year

| Year | What happened | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 1999 | Ebates founded | Rakuten's 2014 press release |
| 2014 | Rakuten announced on September 9 that it would buy all of Ebates for $1 billion in cash; closing was planned for October | Rakuten press release; Rakuten's company history lists it under October 2014 |
| February 2019 | Members with an eligible American Express card could first take Membership Rewards points in place of cash | The Points Guy; Doctor of Credit |
| 2019 | The Ebates name and logo were replaced by Rakuten | Rakuten's blog post of March 6, 2019; Rakuten help center |

The exact day the US site switched is not confirmed. Rakuten's help center says members were moved to the new site "one group at a time", so there was no single day for everyone.

The legal name still shows the history. Rakuten's terms name the company as Ebates Performance Marketing, Inc., doing business as Rakuten Rewards.

## What happened to old Ebates accounts and balances

Rakuten's announcement page says cash back and account details were unchanged, and that the full balance appears at the top of the new site. Its help center says the name change has no effect on how members use the service.

So an Ebates account did not need to be reopened under a new name. Whether an Ebates login that has not been used for years still works today is not confirmed. Two rules in Rakuten's current terms matter for a long-idle account:

- After more than 12 months with no shopping trip, Rakuten may take a $5 monthly maintenance fee from the balance. The fee cannot take the balance below zero.
- Rakuten may close an account that has been inactive for more than 36 months and has a zero balance.

The terms allow one account per person.

## What stayed the same and what changed

| Feature | At the name change | Today |
|---|---|---|
| Stores and rates | Rakuten said the same stores and the same cash back | Rates change daily and can differ by member |
| Payout schedule | Rakuten said the next payment would come at the usual time | Every three months: February 15, May 15, August 15, November 15 |
| Check name | Still called the Big Fat Check, with the Rakuten logo | Same name |
| PayPal payment | Continued, now sent from Rakuten | Still offered |
| Amex points option | Began February 2019 | Still offered to eligible card members |
| In-store cash back | Already offered; Rakuten said it had grown | Offered by linking a card |
| Site address | ebates.com forwards to rakuten.com | Same |

The exact payment dates used in the Ebates years are not confirmed here; the 2019 announcement only says the schedule did not change. Bilt Points and Samsung Cash now appear on Rakuten's list of payment methods. When each was added is not confirmed.

For the details, see [when Rakuten pays](/rakuten-when-do-you-get-paid/) and [what joining costs](/is-rakuten-free/).

## Where the old store pages are now

People still search for "Ebates" with a store name. Those pages now live on rakuten.com. In a check on November 25, 2026, old ebates.com addresses for Macy's, Walmart and eBay each forwarded to that store's page on rakuten.com. The old Hotels.com address led to a page-not-found screen.

Guides on this site for the stores people most often pair with the old name:

- [Macy's](/rakuten-macys-cash-back-how-it-works/)
- [Walmart](/rakuten-walmart-cash-back-how-it-works/)
- [eBay](/rakuten-ebay-cash-back-how-it-works/)
- [Hotels and flights](/rakuten-hotels-flights-cash-back/)

## Who should skip it

- You want payment soon after each purchase. Rakuten pays every three months.
- You shop online once or twice a year. A small balance can sit below the payment minimum, and the inactivity fee can reduce it.
- You do not want a company recording your shopping activity. That is how cash back is tracked, under either name.
- You expect Ebates-era rates. No source confirms that rates today match those years.

## Quick answers

**Is Ebates the same company as Rakuten?**
Yes. Rakuten's help center says Ebates has been a Rakuten company since 2014. The name changed in 2019.

**Did Ebates members lose their cash back in the change?**
No. Rakuten's announcement said cash back and account details were unchanged.

**Does ebates.com still work?**
It forwards to rakuten.com. Rakuten suggests updating old bookmarks to the new address.

# Is Rakuten cash back taxable, and what about the referral bonus?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/is-rakuten-cash-back-taxable/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

Cash back on things you buy is generally treated as a rebate that lowers the price you paid, not as income. A referral bonus is different: you did not buy anything to earn it, Rakuten's terms say you may be taxed on it, and it can be reported to the IRS.

This page is information, not financial advice. It is not tax advice either; a tax professional can apply the rules to your return.

## The short version

| What you received | How sources describe it | Could a tax form arrive? |
|---|---|---|
| Cash back on your own personal purchases | A rebate; generally not income | Not expected |
| Bonus for referring a friend | Generally taxable income | Possibly; see below |
| New-member bonus that requires purchases | Not confirmed for Rakuten | Not confirmed |
| Rewards taken as Amex points | Not confirmed for Rakuten | Not confirmed |

No IRS guidance that names shopping portals was found. The first two rows rest on general IRS rules about rebates and on how tax writers apply them to rewards.

## Why purchase cash back is treated as a rebate

IRS Publication 525 has a short entry on cash rebates. It says a cash rebate you receive from a dealer or manufacturer of an item you buy is not income, and that you reduce your basis in the item by the rebate.

A 2010 IRS letter ruling about credit card rebates took the same line: a rebate to a buyer is an adjustment to the purchase price. A letter ruling applies only to the taxpayer who asked for it, but it shows the reasoning. The Points Guy's tax guide, dated February 2026, sums up the general view that rewards tied to spending are treated as rebates and are generally not taxed.

Rakuten cash back comes through Rakuten, not straight from the store, so it is not word for word the case in Publication 525. The common reading is that it is still a rebate on your purchase.

## Why a referral bonus is different

A referral bonus is paid for bringing in a new member. You bought nothing to get it, so it is not a discount on anything.

- Rakuten's terms, section 10.5, say: "You may be taxed on your receipt of bonuses and other consideration."
- The same section says you are solely responsible for any tax owed on them.
- The Points Guy's guide says referral bonuses are considered taxable income because no spending is needed to earn them.

How the referral bonus works is covered in [the Rakuten bonus page](/rakuten-50-bonus-how-it-works/).

## Will Rakuten send a 1099?

Rakuten's terms and help pages do not say when it issues a tax form or asks for a taxpayer ID. That is not confirmed.

What is known:

- A member wrote in a tax software forum in February 2026 that Rakuten had sent a Form 1099-NEC for a referral bonus.
- Another member reported receiving no form for about $120 of bonuses and cash back.
- The IRS instructions for Forms 1099-MISC and 1099-NEC say that for tax years beginning after 2025, the minimum amount for reporting certain payments rose to $2,000. It was $600 before. The figure may be adjusted for inflation from 2027.

A form and a tax duty are separate things. The Points Guy's guide notes that taxable income is reportable whether or not a 1099 arrives.

## Where it goes on a return

Sources differ; this is a point for a tax professional.

- The Points Guy says rewards income is reported as other income on Schedule 1 of Form 1040, line 8z.
- A tax software support agent, answering the member with the 1099-NEC, said the IRS generally expects amounts on that form to be reported as business income on Schedule C.

## Records worth keeping

- Rakuten's payment history, which shows each payment date and amount.
- A note of how much of each payment was referral bonus and how much was cash back on purchases.

## Who should skip the referral program

- You do not want any income that may need reporting. Purchase cash back alone does not raise that question in the usual case.
- Your tax situation is complex, for example you buy through Rakuten for a business. Ask a professional first.

## Quick answers

**Do I pay tax on Rakuten cash back from shopping?**
Generally no. Sources treat it as a rebate that lowers the price you paid.

**Is the Rakuten referral bonus taxable?**
Rakuten's terms say you may be taxed on bonuses. Tax writers treat referral bonuses as income.

**Does Rakuten send a 1099?**
Not confirmed. One member reported a 1099-NEC for a referral bonus; another reported no form.

## Sources

- [Rakuten: Terms and conditions](https://www.rakuten.com/help/article/terms-conditions)
- [IRS: Publication 525, Taxable and Nontaxable Income](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p525)
- [IRS: Private letter ruling 201027015](https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-wd/1027015.pdf)
- [IRS: Instructions for Forms 1099-MISC and 1099-NEC](https://www.irs.gov/instructions/i1099mec)
- [The Points Guy: Are credit card rewards taxable?](https://thepointsguy.com/credit-cards/complete-guide-to-paying-taxes-on-credit-card-rewards/)
- [FreeTaxUSA community: Reporting a referral bonus on a 1099-NEC](https://community.freetaxusa.com/discussion/2900/question-about-reporting-referral-bonus-on-1099-nec)
- [Intuit community: Rakuten referral bonus](https://ttlc.intuit.com/community/business-taxes/discussion/rakuten-referral-bonus/00/2925711)

# Is Rakuten free? Yes, free to join and use, with one fee that can apply

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/is-rakuten-free/
Facts checked: 2026-11-26
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

Yes, Rakuten is free to join and free to use: there is no membership fee and no charge for shopping through it. The catch is not a price but a trade, because Rakuten collects data on your shopping, pays only four times a year, and holds any balance under about $5.

This page is information, not financial advice. Every figure was re-read on Rakuten's own pages on November 26, 2026; its terms carry the date October 23, 2026. For what happens after you join, see [how Rakuten works, step by step](/how-does-rakuten-work-step-by-step/).

## What it costs in money

| Item | What Rakuten's pages say |
|---|---|
| Fee to join | None. The join page calls it "simple and free." |
| Fee for the app or browser extension | None. Both are described as free. |
| Payment card needed to join | No. An account needs an email and password, or a Facebook, Google or Apple sign-in. |
| Minimum before a payment is sent | $5 on the help page; $5.01 in the terms |
| Fee taken from a payment | None is listed on Rakuten's payment page. Any fee charged by PayPal: not confirmed. |
| Inactive account fee | $5.00 a month, after more than 12 months with no shopping trip |
| Rakuten+ | A separate, optional annual membership that renews automatically. Price: not confirmed. |

A card comes into it only if you choose to link one for [in-store offers](/rakuten-in-store-cash-back-how-it-works/). Rakuten's home page says of linking a card, "You don't have to." Members must be at least 18 and live in the 50 states or Washington D.C., and each person is limited to one account.

The one fee in the terms is for an inactive account. If you have not shopped or started a shopping trip for more than 12 months in a row, Rakuten may take $5.00 a month from your balance. It comes out of cash back you have earned, not from your bank. The terms say the fee cannot make a balance negative or leave you owing money, so an account with nothing in it is not charged. Shopping or starting a shopping trip stops it. After more than 36 idle months with a zero balance, Rakuten may close the account.

## The paid extras you can ignore

Two things with Rakuten's name are not part of the free membership, and neither is needed to earn cash back.

- **Rakuten+.** Rakuten's help center describes an annual membership, offered by invitation, that pays at least 10% at a list of premium stores. It renews automatically on the date you joined, can be canceled up to 3 days before renewal, and gives no refund for a part-used year. The help pages mention a free trial but do not state the price, so it is not confirmed.
- **The Rakuten American Express Card.** A credit card with its own terms. Its fees were not read for this page.

## How Rakuten earns if you pay nothing

Stores pay Rakuten a commission when it sends them a shopper who buys. Rakuten keeps part and passes the rest to you as cash back. Its terms say the cash back is funded from that partner compensation and, for some offers, from its own funds. The longer version is on [how Rakuten makes money](/is-rakuten-legit-how-it-makes-money/).

## The costs that are not money

**Your data.** Rakuten's terms say the browser extension collects information on the pages you visit and on search results pages, whether or not you are interacting with it. That is how it shows offers. What is collected and how to limit it is covered on [the extension and your privacy](/rakuten-browser-extension-safe-privacy/). Rakuten's home page says it does not sell personal data to data brokers, may share limited information with advertising partners, and lets you opt out of that sharing. You can earn without the extension by starting at Rakuten.com each time.

**The wait.** Cash back starts as pending. Rakuten says online and in-store cash back typically takes 3 to 14 weeks to be confirmed, and confirmed cash back is sent by February 15, May 15, August 15 and November 15. A purchase can take months to become money; see [when Rakuten pays](/rakuten-when-do-you-get-paid/). Rakuten also lets members redeem a confirmed balance of at least $5 for a gift card without waiting for a payment date.

**The minimum.** The help page says you need $5 or more in confirmed cash back to be paid. The terms put the minimum at $5.01. Either way, a smaller balance is not lost: it carries over to the next payment date.

**Returns.** Returned or canceled orders do not earn cash back. For a partial return, Rakuten says the cash back is adjusted.

**Coupon codes.** Rakuten's help page says codes not listed on Rakuten "may void Cash Back." If a code from elsewhere saves more than the cash back would pay, the code is the better deal for that order; you usually cannot count on both.

**Tracking that does not happen.** Ad blockers, VPNs, declined cookies, or finishing checkout in a different tab can stop a purchase from being linked to your account. The fix is on [missing cash back](/rakuten-missing-cash-back-what-to-do/).

## Is the joining bonus free too

The bonus for new members costs nothing, but it is not paid for joining alone. As read on November 26, 2026, the welcome bonus terms ask for at least $25 of purchases that earn cash back within 90 days, and the referral offer asks for $50. Amounts vary and change; see [how the sign-up and referral bonuses work](/rakuten-50-bonus-how-it-works/) and [welcome bonus or referral bonus](/rakuten-welcome-bonus-vs-referral-bonus/).

## Who should skip it

- You do not want a company recording which shopping pages you visit. Use the website only, or leave it.
- You shop online once or twice a year for small amounts. The balance may stay under $5, and after 12 idle months the fee can reduce it.
- You rely on coupon codes from other sites at checkout.
- You would buy more than you planned in order to earn cash back. That spending is the real cost.

## Quick answers

**Is Rakuten free to use?**
Yes. Rakuten charges no fee to join, shop, or use its app and extension.

**Do you need a credit card to join Rakuten?**
No. An email and password is enough. A card is linked only for in-store offers, by choice.

**What is the minimum Rakuten will pay out?**
About $5 in confirmed cash back. The help page says $5; the terms say $5.01. Less carries over.

# Is Rakuten legit, and how does it make money if it pays you?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/is-rakuten-legit-how-it-makes-money/
Facts checked: 2026-11-27
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

Yes, Rakuten is legit: it is a real company, owned by Rakuten Group of Tokyo, whose members have earned cash back since 1999. Stores pay it a commission for each shopper it sends, and it passes part of that commission to you; in return it collects data about what you browse and buy.

This page is information, not financial advice. Rakuten's own pages were re-read on November 27, 2026. For what it costs to use, see [is Rakuten free](/is-rakuten-free/); for the joining step, [how to sign up for Rakuten](/how-to-sign-up-for-rakuten/).

## How the money flows

Rakuten's help center puts it in one line: "Stores pay Rakuten a commission for referring shoppers to them." Rakuten keeps a portion and gives the rest to the member as cash back. What portion it keeps is not confirmed; Rakuten does not publish it.

This is affiliate marketing. The store pays only when a sale happens, so it is willing to share part of the sale price. The cash back does not come from a membership fee. Rakuten says joining is free. Confirmed cash back is paid four times a year; see [when Rakuten pays](/rakuten-when-do-you-get-paid/) and [how Rakuten works, step by step](/how-does-rakuten-work-step-by-step/).

Rakuten's terms list other income too: marketing funds, cost-per-click fees and commissions on gift card redemptions. They say this compensation may play a part in which stores and products appear on the site, where they are placed and how they are promoted. So the order of stores on a page is not a neutral ranking. The terms also say Rakuten funds some offers from its own money. New-member bonuses are one kind of offer; the conditions are on [how the sign-up and referral bonuses work](/rakuten-50-bonus-how-it-works/).

## Who owns it

| Fact | Detail |
|---|---|
| Legal name | Ebates Performance Marketing, Inc., doing business as Rakuten Rewards |
| Address | 800 Concar Drive, San Mateo, California |
| Started as | Ebates, in Menlo Park, California |
| Bought by Rakuten | September 2014, for about $1 billion |
| Name changed to Rakuten | 2019 |
| Parent company | Rakuten Group, Inc., Tokyo, founded in 1997 |

Sources differ slightly on the founding year. One encyclopedia entry says Ebates was founded in 1998 and its site launched in May 1999; Rakuten dates its cash back from 1999. Rakuten's Black Friday page gives 1997, which is the parent company's founding year.

## The numbers Rakuten states

These are Rakuten's own figures, read on its pages on November 27, 2026. None was checked against an outside audit.

| Figure | What Rakuten's pages say |
|---|---|
| Members | More than 17 million |
| Cash back earned by members since 1999 | More than $4.6 billion |
| Stores | 3,500+ |
| Trustpilot | 4.6 from about 37,000 reviews, as shown on Rakuten's home page |

The Trustpilot rating could not be re-read on Trustpilot's own site on November 27, so it is Rakuten's statement of it, not confirmed at the source. A Better Business Bureau rating is not confirmed either; that page could not be read.

## What data it collects

Rakuten's privacy policy carries the date October 23, 2026. It lists these kinds of data:

- Name, postal and email address, and phone number.
- IP address, device and session IDs.
- Payment account name and number, card expiration date and billing address.
- Searches, clicks, cart items, store visits, purchases and reward balances.
- URLs you visit, click stream and timestamps, including through the browser extension and the app.
- Precise location, only if you turn it on for the app on your device.

The policy says the browser extension and the app collect data about your online activity on that device even when you are not interacting with them. To withdraw consent for that, you uninstall them. You can still earn by starting at the website each time. More on this is in [is the Rakuten browser extension safe](/rakuten-browser-extension-safe-privacy/).

## Who it shares data with

The policy names affiliate networks (click data and a tracking ID, so the store can credit your purchase), stores, referral and loyalty partners, financial partners, digital advertising providers and other Rakuten Group companies. It says some of these disclosures may be considered selling or sharing under US state privacy laws. Rakuten's home page says it does not sell personal data to data brokers, and that it may share limited information with advertising partners.

You have options. Members can opt out in the Privacy Preference Center, and the policy says Rakuten honors Global Privacy Control signals from a browser. You can also ask to see, correct or delete your data.

The policy also says offers and cash back rates may be personalized based on your account history. Two members may see different rates at the same store.

## Limits written into the terms

- Cash back is not final until the store confirms it. Rakuten may deduct it for returns and cancellations.
- If a store does not pay Rakuten for a transaction, Rakuten may cancel the cash back tied to it.
- After 12 months with no shopping trip, Rakuten may take a $5 monthly maintenance fee from your balance. The fee stops when the balance reaches zero.
- You must report missing cash back within 90 days of the purchase. See [what to do when cash back did not track](/rakuten-missing-cash-back-what-to-do/).

## Who should skip it

- You do not want a company recording which sites you visit. The extension and app do that by design.
- You rarely shop online. With one or two small orders a year, the balance may sit unused and the inactivity fee can reduce it.
- You always check out with coupon codes from other sites. Codes not listed on Rakuten can void the cash back.

## Quick answers

**Does Rakuten cost anything to join?**
No. Rakuten says sign-up is free. Its income is the commission stores pay.

**Who owns Rakuten in the US?**
Rakuten Group, Inc. of Tokyo. It bought Ebates in 2014 and renamed it in 2019.

**Can you stop Rakuten collecting browsing data?**
Uninstall the extension and app, and use the opt-out in the Privacy Preference Center.

# Is TopCashback legit and free, and how does it make money?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/is-topcashback-legit-how-it-makes-money/
Facts checked: 2026-11-25
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

TopCashback is a real cash back site that has run since 2005 and charges no fee to join or to be paid. It says it passes the whole store commission to the member and earns its own money from bonuses stores pay for sending many shoppers, plus advertising on its site.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## How the money moves

TopCashback's help pages describe three steps:

1. You log in, find a store and click through to the store's site from TopCashback.
2. You buy as usual. The store pays TopCashback a commission for sending a customer.
3. TopCashback passes that commission to you as cash back.

That is the same model as Rakuten. The difference TopCashback points to is the share: its help page says it passes "100% of the Cash Back we receive from retailers" to members. Rakuten's terms describe keeping part of the store's payment; see [how Rakuten makes money](/is-rakuten-legit-how-it-makes-money/).

## What TopCashback says it earns from

| Source | What its help page says |
|---|---|
| Store bonuses | Stores pay it a bonus for driving a high volume of shoppers |
| Advertising | On-site advertising and sponsored content |
| A cut of your cash back | None, by its own statement |
| Membership or admin fee | None, by its own statement |

These are the company's own statements. No outside audit of the 100% figure was found, so treat it as a claim from the source, stated plainly on its help pages.

## What "free" leaves out

No fee does not mean no cost. The limits on TopCashback's own help pages are these:

- **A wait.** Cash back shows as tracked first and can be cashed out only once it is "available." Each store sets its own period. For travel, the stay has to be finished first.
- **Tracking can fail.** The help page lists the common reasons: a coupon code not listed on TopCashback, an ad blocker, buying in a different tab from the one TopCashback opened, or clicking another cash back or coupon site afterward.
- **It can take a week or longer** for a purchase to be reported at all.
- **Your shopping is the product.** The store pays because TopCashback sent you. Like any cash back site, it records which stores you click and what the purchase earned.

How to get paid, and what to do when a purchase is missing, is on [how TopCashback pays](/topcashback-how-to-cash-out-and-when/).

## Signs it is a real business

- The site footer dates the company from 2005 and lists sister sites in the UK, Germany, France, Japan, Australia and other countries.
- It publishes its terms, a privacy policy, an advertiser disclosure and a vulnerability disclosure page.
- [NerdWallet](https://www.nerdwallet.com/article/travel/topcashback-vs-rakuten) and [The Points Guy](https://thepointsguy.com/guide/topcashback/) both cover it as a working cash back site.

None of this promises that every purchase will track. It means the company exists, publishes its rules and pays through ordinary methods: bank transfer, Venmo, PayPal or gift cards.

## Who should skip it

- You do not want a company recording which stores you shop at.
- You use coupon codes from other sites at checkout. A code TopCashback does not list can cancel the cash back.
- You keep an ad blocker on everywhere and will not turn it off for a purchase.
- You would spend more than you planned in order to earn cash back.

For how it compares with the larger US site, see [Rakuten or TopCashback](/rakuten-vs-topcashback/).

## Quick answers

**Is TopCashback free?**
Yes. Its help page says there are no fees and no deductions from cash back.

**How does TopCashback make money if it passes on all the commission?**
It says stores pay it bonuses for sending many shoppers, and it sells advertising and sponsored content on its site.

**Is TopCashback a scam?**
No. It is a cash back company operating since 2005 with published terms. Purchases can still fail to track, for the reasons its help page lists.

## Sources

- [TopCashback: How does TopCashback make money?](https://www.topcashback.com/help/how-we-make-money/)
- [TopCashback: Are you the only 100% free Cash Back site?](https://www.topcashback.com/help/completely-free-cash-back/)

# Is the Marriott Bonvoy Brilliant Amex worth its annual fee for an occasional Marriott guest?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/marriott-bonvoy-brilliant-amex-worth-650/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

For an occasional Marriott guest, the Bonvoy Brilliant's $650 annual fee is worth it only if two things are true: you eat at restaurants every month, so the $300 dining credit is used in full, and you will use the yearly free night at a hotel that would cost you $350 or more. The elite status on its own will not earn back the fee on a few stays a year.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## What the $650 buys

| Benefit | What it is | Main limit |
|---|---|---|
| Dining credit | Up to $25 a month ($300 a year) at restaurants worldwide | Monthly; unused months are lost |
| Free night award | One a year, at a hotel costing up to 85,000 points | Issued after each renewal, so the first comes after year one |
| Platinum Elite status | Held while you have the card | Most perks depend on the hotel and on availability |
| 25 elite night credits | Added each year | Useful only if you are chasing a higher status |
| Priority Pass Select | Airport lounges, two guests | Enrollment required; restaurants are not covered |
| Property credit | Up to $100 on 2-night stays at Ritz-Carlton and St. Regis | Only on one specific paid rate |
| Global Entry or TSA PreCheck | Fee credit every four years | $120 or up to $85 |

The card earns 6 points per dollar at Marriott, 3 at restaurants and on flights booked with airlines, and 2 elsewhere.

## The sum for an occasional guest

Start with the fee and take off what you would actually use.

| Step | Amount |
|---|---|
| Annual fee | $650 |
| Dining credit, if used all 12 months | minus $300 |
| Left to cover | $350 |
| Dining credit, if used 6 months of 12 | minus $150 |
| Left to cover in that case | $500 |

The rest has to come from the free night. Sources value it differently:

- One Mile at a Time values the free night at about $350, and Marriott points at 0.7 cents each.
- The Points Guy values Marriott points at 0.75 cents (October 2026). At that rate 85,000 points come to about $637.

The value to you is simpler than either: it is the cash price of the room you would book with it. Used on a $400 night, the card comes out $50 ahead after a full dining credit. Used on a $200 night, it comes out $150 behind. You can add up to 25,000 of your own points to reach a hotel costing up to 110,000 points, and some properties charge a resort fee on a free night.

In the first year there is no free night yet. An occasional guest pays $650 in year one and gets the dining credit, status and lounge access, but not the night.

## What Platinum Elite status is worth on a few stays

One Mile at a Time lists the Platinum Elite benefits as a 50% points bonus on stays, 4 p.m. checkout (guaranteed at non-resort hotels), room upgrades when available, lounge access at most brands, and a welcome gift that includes breakfast at many brands.

These have real value per night, and they are worth more the more nights you stay. On three or four nights a year, the total is small: a few breakfasts where the brand offers them, and a later checkout. Upgrades depend on availability and are not guaranteed.

The 25 elite night credits do not change anything for a guest who stays a handful of nights, since Platinum is already included with the card.

## A quick test

The card tends to work for an occasional guest who can say yes to all three:

1. I pay for a restaurant meal of $25 or more every month.
2. Once a year I stay at a Marriott hotel that costs $350 or more a night, and I could book it with the free night.
3. I plan to keep the card past the first year, when the free night starts.

If the second answer is no, a card with a lower fee, or no hotel card, is likely to cost less.

## Who should skip it

- People who stay at Marriott once or twice a year at mid-priced hotels.
- People who do not eat out every month.
- People who plan to hold the card for one year only.
- People who already have lounge access and hotel status through another card, such as [the Platinum Card](/amex-platinum-credits-real-value/).
- People who do not want to pay $650 up front and earn it back in pieces.

Welcome offers on this card vary by applicant and change often. Sources checked for this page listed three different offers, so none is quoted here.

## Quick answers

**Does the free night come in the first year?**
No. One Mile at a Time reports it is issued each year after renewal, starting at the first anniversary.

**Can the dining credit be saved up?**
No. It is up to $25 each month. A month you do not use is gone.

**Is breakfast guaranteed with Platinum Elite status?**
No. It is offered as a welcome gift choice at many Marriott brands, not all.

## Sources

- [One Mile at a Time: Marriott Bonvoy Brilliant review](https://onemileatatime.com/reviews/marriott-bonvoy-brilliant/)
- [The Points Guy: Is the Marriott Bonvoy Brilliant worth the annual fee?](https://thepointsguy.com/guide/is-marriott-bonvoy-brilliant-amex-worth-annual-fee/)
- [AwardWallet: Marriott Bonvoy Brilliant](https://awardwallet.com/credit-cards/marriott-bonvoy/amex-bonvoy-brilliant/)

# When should you pay with points, and when with cash?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/points-or-cash-when-to-pay-with-points/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

Work out cents per point: take the cash price, subtract the taxes and fees you still pay on the award, and divide by the points needed. If the answer is below what your points fetch the simple way (1 cent for Chase, 0.6 to 1 cent for Amex), pay cash. If it is above the 1.7 to 2 cents that published valuations use, points are doing well.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## The check, in three steps

1. Find the cash price of the exact flight or room, on the same dates.
2. Find the points price, and the taxes, fees and surcharges charged with it.
3. Cents per point = (cash price minus award taxes and fees) divided by points, times 100.

Use a cash price you would in fact pay. A $6,000 business-class fare you would never buy does not make your points worth 6 cents each to you.

## What to compare the answer with

| Yardstick | Amex points | Chase points | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| The floor: cash or statement credit | 0.6 cents | 1 cent | The Points Guy, CNBC Select |
| Flights through the card's travel site | 1 cent | 1 cent; up to 2 cents with a Points Boost on a Sapphire Reserve | The Points Guy, Chase |
| Published average through transfer partners | 2.0 cents (The Points Guy); 1.7 cents (One Mile at a Time) | 2.05 cents (The Points Guy); 1.7 cents (One Mile at a Time) | November 2026 valuations |

Reading the result:

- **Below the floor.** Pay cash. The points would buy more as a plain credit or travel-site booking.
- **Between the floor and about 1.7 cents.** A fair use, not a strong one. Paying with points makes sense if you have more points than plans for them.
- **About 1.7 to 2 cents or more.** In line with or above what experienced users average.

The floors come from [what an Amex point is worth](/amex-membership-rewards-points-value/) and [Chase's Points Boost](/chase-points-boost-explained/).

## Three worked examples

The award prices are from the sources named. The cash fares are illustrations, not quotes.

| Booking | Points and fees (source) | Cash fare (illustration) | Cents per point |
|---|---|---|---|
| Flying Blue business class, US to Europe, one way | 60,000 miles plus $608 (Flying Blue's example, via The Points Guy) | $2,400 | (2,400 − 608) ÷ 60,000 = 2.99 |
| The same seat during a fare sale | 60,000 miles plus $608 | $1,300 | (1,300 − 608) ÷ 60,000 = 1.15 |
| 50,000 Amex points moved to Hilton (100,000 Hilton points) | No fees | $400 of hotel nights, at The Points Guy's 0.4 cents per Hilton point | 400 ÷ 50,000 = 0.8 |

The first is a strong use. The second barely beats booking through the travel site. The third is below the 1 cent that Amex Travel gives on flights, so those points would go further on airfare.

## Three things the sum leaves out

**Points you do not earn.** A cash ticket earns points; an award ticket does not. The Platinum Card earns 5 points per dollar on flights booked with airlines or Amex Travel. On a $1,000 fare that is 5,000 points, worth $50 to $100 at 1 to 2 cents each. Award tickets also usually earn no airline miles.

**Taxes and surcharges.** They vary widely. The Points Guy puts a Virgin Atlantic business-class award from New York to London at 29,000 points plus about $700 one way. Leave that out and the sum flatters the award.

**Flexibility.** A transfer to an airline cannot be reversed, and the miles then follow that airline's rules. Flying Blue's lowest award fares, sold since September 8, 2026, allow no changes or refunds.

## When cash is usually right

- Low fares. As an illustration, a $250 domestic ticket priced at 25,000 miles is 1 cent per point before fees.
- Hotel transfers other than Hyatt. The Points Guy values Marriott at 0.75 cents, IHG at 0.6, Hilton at 0.4 and Wyndham at 0.55 per point.
- Gift cards and checkout purchases with Amex points, at 0.5 to 1 cent.
- Any trip where the award surcharge is close to the cash fare.

## When points are usually right

- Long-haul business class with an open award seat. See the prices for [Europe](/how-many-points-for-a-flight-to-europe/) and [Japan](/how-many-points-for-a-flight-to-japan/).
- Economy on dates when cash fares are high but the award price is fixed.
- Hyatt nights from a Sapphire Reserve at 1 to 1; The Points Guy values a Hyatt point at 1.65 cents.

Which partners clear the bar most often: [Chase partners](/chase-transfer-partners-which-are-worth-it/) and [Amex partners](/amex-transfer-partners-which-are-worth-it/).

## Who should skip the math

- People with a cash-back card. There is nothing to compare.
- People who hold few points and have no trip planned. Points do not earn interest, and programs can raise award prices without notice.
- People who value simplicity over the last half cent. Booking through the travel site at 1 cent takes no award search.

## Quick answers

**What is a good cents-per-point value?**
Above about 1.7 to 2 cents matches the published averages for Amex and Chase points. Above the 1 cent travel-site rate is acceptable.

**Should taxes be subtracted first?**
Yes. Subtract the taxes and fees charged on the award from the cash price before dividing by the points.

**Is it wrong to use points at 1 cent?**
No. It is the base travel-site rate for both programs. It is simply not more than the simple option gives.

# Do premium credit cards offer golf travel packages as well as tee-time bookings?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/premium-credit-card-golf-benefits-tee-times-packages/
Facts checked: 2026-11-23
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

Mostly tee-time help, not packages. The Amex Platinum and Chase Sapphire Reserve offer a concierge that can request tee times and hotel programs that include some golf resorts, but neither lists packaged golf trips as a standing benefit. The clearest packaged trips found were on Mastercard's Priceless site, sold by a tour operator and paid for in full by the cardholder.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## What each card or network offers

| Card or network | Tee-time help | Golf program | Packaged golf trips |
|---|---|---|---|
| Amex Platinum ($895) | Concierge takes golf requests | None on the US card | One 2026 ballot for a St Andrews package |
| Chase Sapphire Reserve ($795) | Visa concierge; golf not named | Visa Infinite rate at Troon Privé clubs | None listed |
| Capital One Venture X ($395) | Visa Infinite concierge; golf not named | Same Visa Infinite rate | None listed |
| World Elite Mastercard | Concierge books TPC tee times | TPC benefit through December 31, 2026 | Listed on Priceless, sold by a tour operator |

## Amex Platinum

The US Platinum Card has no free rounds, green fee credit or tee time priority. See [what the Platinum does for golfers](/amex-platinum-for-golfers/).

Upgraded Points, updated November 11, 2026, says the Platinum Concierge takes "requests for reservations, including restaurants, golf, and spas." The service is free, and the cardholder pays for whatever is booked.

The nearest thing to a package was a single event. In August 2026 Amex and St Andrews Links Trust announced a ballot for Platinum and Centurion members in select countries. Those drawn could buy a golf package for two at St Andrews courses in 2027. The window closed on September 9, 2026, and no price was published. Sources disagree on the countries: the release names none, one trade outlet names only the UK, and one travel site says 15 including the US. A repeat is not confirmed.

For lodging, [Fine Hotels + Resorts and The Hotel Collection](/fine-hotels-resorts-vs-hotel-collection/) include some golf resorts. Golf is paid for separately.

## Chase Sapphire Reserve

Chase's page for the card does not mention golf. The Points Guy describes a Visa concierge for dining, travel arrangements and event access. Golf is not named, so tee-time help is a request, not a listed benefit.

At the 2025 PGA Championship, Reserve cardmembers could buy daily grounds ticket packages through Chase and reserve a free viewing space. Those were tickets to watch, not trips to play. A 2026 version is not confirmed.

For lodging, [The Edit](/chase-sapphire-reserve-the-edit-credit-how-it-works/) gives a $100 property credit, breakfast and an upgrade when available at its hotels. Whether a resort lets that credit be spent on golf varies by hotel.

## The Visa Infinite golf rate

Visa still has a golf benefit with Troon, now run under the name Access. Its terms say US-issued Visa Infinite cardholders can request tee times at more than 20 participating Troon Privé private clubs for $99 plus tax per player per round. Up to three guests pay the same rate, and each club can be played up to two times a year.

The terms show no end date and say the offer can change without notice. The Sapphire Reserve and Venture X are Visa Infinite cards, but neither issuer names this benefit on the pages read, so confirm it with the program first.

## Mastercard: the one place packages appear

Mastercard's Priceless Golf page listed two kinds of offer on November 23, 2026.

**TPC courses.** World Elite Mastercard holders can have a concierge book a round at TPC courses, with 20% off green fees at select courses. The listing runs until December 31, 2026, with one visit per course per year. Whether it continues in 2027 is not confirmed.

**Packaged trips.** The page listed golf trips in Scotland, England and Northern Ireland sold by a golf tour operator, priced from about $3,261 to $6,522 per person. One example, in Troon, includes four hotel nights, three rounds and private transfers. Airfare is not included. It is for four golfers, is non-refundable unless noted, and names no card tier.

These trips are sold to cardholders at full price. No annual fee pays for them.

## The sums

None of these benefits pays for golf. The concierge is free and the round is not. The Troon Privé rate is $99 a player. The Mastercard packages cost thousands of dollars a person before flights. What a premium card returns on a golf trip is mostly hotel credits, lounges and insurance. See [airline fees for golf clubs](/flying-with-golf-clubs-airline-fees/) and [card insurance on a golf trip](/golf-trip-travel-insurance-credit-card/).

## Who should skip it

- Anyone choosing a card with a fee of $395 to $895 mainly for golf. The golf content is thin on all of them.
- Golfers who want a ready-made trip. A golf tour operator sells that without a premium card.
- Golfers who play public courses near home.

## Quick answers

**Does any premium card include a golf trip in its annual fee?**
No. None of the cards covered here does. Packages listed for cardholders are sold at full price.

**Can the Amex Platinum concierge book a tee time?**
It takes golf reservation requests, according to Upgraded Points. The cardholder pays the green fee, and a booking is not guaranteed.

**Is there still a Visa Infinite golf benefit?**
Yes. Troon's terms give US-issued Visa Infinite cardholders a $99 rate at participating Troon Privé clubs, up to twice a year per club.

# What does Priority Pass include with the Amex Platinum versus the Sapphire Reserve?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/priority-pass-by-card-what-you-get/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

Both cards come with a Priority Pass Select membership: unlimited lounge visits, two guests free, and no Priority Pass restaurant credits. The differences are small: Chase enrolls you automatically and puts a digital card in its app, and its version still covers some non-lounge stops such as Minute Suites, while Amex makes you enroll and covers lounges only.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## Side by side

| | Amex Platinum ($895 a year) | Chase Sapphire Reserve ($795 a year) |
|---|---|---|
| Membership | Priority Pass Select | Priority Pass Select |
| Enrollment | Required; a card is mailed | Automatic since October 25, 2025; digital card in the Chase app |
| Lounge visits | Unlimited | Unlimited |
| Free guests | Two per visit, where the lounge takes guests | Two per visit |
| Extra guests | Pay the Priority Pass guest fee; amount not confirmed | $27 each |
| Priority Pass restaurants | Not included | Not included since July 1, 2024 |
| Minute Suites, Be Relax spas, Gameway | Not included | Included (first hour at Minute Suites and Gameway) |
| Authorized users | Each $195 additional Platinum cardholder can enroll in their own membership | Each $195 authorized user gets a membership with two guests |
| Chase Sapphire Lounges | Not through Priority Pass | Yes, with the Reserve card itself |

Sources: The Points Guy (August 2026), Upgraded Points, AwardWallet (March 2026) and Chase's lounge page.

## Guests

Both memberships let you bring two guests at no charge. On the Reserve, a third guest costs $27. On the Platinum, extra guests pay the fee Priority Pass sets; none of the pages read gave the amount.

A guest allowance is not a guarantee. Chase's terms say entry can be refused when a lounge is full, and The Points Guy notes that some lounges limit the hours they take Priority Pass members.

An authorized user is often the cheaper route for a regular travel partner: on either card, $195 a year gives that person their own membership and their own two guests. For the rest of what that fee buys on the Platinum, see [the $195 authorized user card](/amex-platinum-authorized-user-worth-195/).

## Restaurants and other stops

Priority Pass sells some memberships that include a credit at airport restaurants. Neither card's version has it.

- **Amex Platinum:** restaurants are not included, per The Points Guy and Upgraded Points. Upgraded Points also lists Minute Suites, Be Relax and Gameway as not included.
- **Sapphire Reserve:** restaurants have been out since July 1, 2024. AwardWallet lists what still works: Be Relax and XWELL spa treatments, the first hour in a Minute Suite, an hour in a Gameway lounge with a snack and a drink, and the golf simulator at Denver.

The Priority Pass app shows which stops your own membership covers at each airport.

## How many lounges

Sources give different counts. Upgraded Points says more than 1,400 for the Platinum and more than 1,300 for the Reserve; Chase says 1,300+; The Points Guy says more than 1,900 for the Platinum; AwardWallet says Priority Pass as a whole has more than 1,800.

No source read shows a lounge that one card's Priority Pass opens and the other's does not, apart from the non-lounge stops above. Treat the two lounge lists as the same until the app says otherwise.

## What Priority Pass is not

Priority Pass is one part of each card's lounge access, and the larger differences lie outside it.

- **Amex Platinum** also has Centurion Lounges, 10 Delta Sky Club visits a year when flying Delta, Escape and Plaza Premium lounges. See [Centurion guest rules](/amex-platinum-centurion-lounge-guest-rules/).
- **Sapphire Reserve** also has Chase Sapphire Lounges and Air Canada Maple Leaf Lounges on Star Alliance flights. See [Sapphire Reserve lounge access](/chase-sapphire-reserve-lounge-access/).

Chase Sapphire Lounges left the Priority Pass network on August 15, 2026. A Priority Pass card from the Amex Platinum no longer opens them.

Priority Pass coverage is thin at some airports. Honolulu is an example; see [Hawaii airport lounges by card](/hawaii-airport-lounges-by-card/).

## Where sources disagree

- **Sapphire Lounges with an Amex Priority Pass.** Upgraded Points' comparison page still describes one free Sapphire Lounge visit a year for Amex Priority Pass members, then $75. Upgraded Points' own news item and The Points Guy report that the lounges left Priority Pass on August 15, 2026. The later reports are used here.
- **Lounge counts,** as given above.

## Who should skip paying for either card for Priority Pass

- People who fly a few times a year from an airport with no Priority Pass lounge in their terminal. Check the Priority Pass site for your home airport first.
- People who wanted the restaurant credit. Neither card has it.
- Families of five or more. Two free guests cover three people.
- People who would use only Priority Pass and none of the card's other lounges or credits. At $795 or $895 a year, the fee has to be earned back elsewhere; see [what the Platinum credits are worth](/amex-platinum-credits-real-value/) and [what the Reserve credits are worth](/chase-sapphire-reserve-credits-real-value/).

## Quick answers

**Can I use Priority Pass restaurants with either card?**
No. The Amex Platinum version excludes them, and Chase removed them from the Sapphire Reserve on July 1, 2024.

**How many guests can I bring?**
Two free on either card. The Sapphire Reserve charges $27 for each extra guest.

**Do I have to enroll?**
With the Amex Platinum, yes. With the Sapphire Reserve, enrollment has been automatic since October 25, 2025.

- [Upgraded Points: Amex Platinum vs. Sapphire Reserve lounge access](https://upgradedpoints.com/credit-cards/amex-platinum-vs-sapphire-reserve-lounge-access/)

# Rakuten sign-up bonus: how the welcome and referral bonuses work, what to spend, and what makes one fail

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/rakuten-50-bonus-how-it-works/
Facts checked: 2026-11-26
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

A new Rakuten member gets one sign-up bonus, not two: the referral bonus for joining through a member's link, or the welcome bonus for joining from Rakuten's own pages. As read on November 26, 2026, the referral offer asks for purchases that earn cash back totaling at least $50 within 90 days of signing up, and the welcome bonus asks for $25. Neither is paid for joining alone, and amounts and terms vary and change.

This page is information, not financial advice. Rakuten's referral page says the requirement and reward can vary; the offer shown runs from October 1 to December 31, 2026. See also [welcome bonus or referral bonus](/rakuten-welcome-bonus-vs-referral-bonus/) and [is Rakuten free](/is-rakuten-free/).

## The two bonuses as read on November 26, 2026

| | Referral sign-up bonus | Welcome bonus |
|---|---|---|
| How you join | A member's link, or the member's email entered on the join form | Rakuten's own site, app or extension, where the bonus is offered |
| Purchases needed | At least $50 that earn cash back | At least $25 that earn cash back or points |
| Time limit | 90 days from signing up | 90 days from signing up |
| Amount shown that day | $50, after $50 of purchases, in the page's share text | $10 on store pages; an extra 10% cash back, capped at $50, on the home page |
| Other amounts in the same pages' text | $30 after $30 | $20 after $25 |
| Amazon.com orders | Do not count | Do not count |
| Combined with the other bonus | No | No |

Rakuten's pages show more than one amount on the same day; which one a given new member is offered is not confirmed. Rakuten's referral FAQ says the new member gets "the bonus that was available on day of sign up." The amount on the page you join from is the one that applies to you.

The 10% version is a separate offer called the Boost Bonus. Its terms say it adds to the rate only at stores where a boost is advertised, for the period named in the offer, up to $50.00 in total. The length of that period is not confirmed; the public terms do not give it.

## The steps

1. Open the member's referral link and create a new account from it. Rakuten's join article gives a second way: choose "Did someone refer you?" on the join form and enter the email the member uses for Rakuten.
2. Within 90 days, start at Rakuten (site, app or browser extension) each time, click through to a store, and buy. Qualifying purchases must total at least $50, in one order or several; see [how Rakuten works, step by step](/how-does-rakuten-work-step-by-step/).
3. Choose how you want to be paid in Account Settings. A check or PayPal needs a mailing address on file; Rakuten says Membership Rewards points and Bilt Points do not.
4. Wait for the store to confirm the purchase.
5. The bonus is paid with your next cash back payment.

Adding a referrer after an account already exists is not confirmed.

## The numbers

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Purchase confirmed by the store | Typically 3 to 14 weeks on the payment page; 3 to 17 weeks on the status page |
| Travel | 45 to 120 days after the booking on the payment page; 6 to 17 weeks after the trip in the travel article |
| When a bonus is confirmed | At the same time as the cash back on the qualifying order |
| Payment dates | February 15, May 15, August 15, November 15 |
| Minimum balance to be paid | $5 on the help page; $5.01 in the terms |
| Paid by | PayPal, check, Bilt Points or Samsung Cash; Membership Rewards points for eligible American Express Card Members |

See also [the sign-up bonus as Amex points](/rakuten-sign-up-bonus-as-amex-points/).

## When the money really arrives

The store confirms your purchase, the bonus is confirmed with it, and it goes out on the next payment date after that. A late November purchase confirmed in three weeks is paid on February 15, 2027; one confirmed in 14 weeks is paid on May 15, 2027. More in [when Rakuten pays](/rakuten-when-do-you-get-paid/).

## What counts as a qualifying purchase

A purchase qualifies only if it earns cash back through Rakuten.com, the app or the extension. These do not count:

- Purchases on Amazon.com (music.amazon.com is the one exception in the terms).
- Stores listed with no cash back, as Walmart was on November 26, 2026.
- Most gift-card purchases.
- Tax and shipping.
- Items or categories the store excludes.
- Orders placed by phone, chat or customer service.

## What makes it fail

**Problems with the account**

- You already had a Rakuten account. Both bonuses are for new members, and the terms allow one account per person.
- You joined without the member's link or email.
- You referred yourself, or the two accounts share a name, address or email. The program terms say such accounts may be flagged.
- You live outside the 50 states or D.C. The program terms also list Canada; the current offer terms name only the 50 states and D.C.
- Someone else paid for the purchase.

**Problems with the purchase**

- You returned, exchanged or canceled it.
- You spent under the total, or bought after the 90 days.
- You used a coupon code not listed on Rakuten.
- An ad blocker, VPN, declined cookies or another coupon extension stopped the tracking.
- You added items to the cart first and activated Rakuten afterwards.
- You left the tab idle for a long time, or checked out in a different tab.

**Problems with payment**

- No payment method chosen, or no mailing address on file for a check or PayPal.

If a purchase does not show up after 48 hours, see [what to do about missing cash back](/rakuten-missing-cash-back-what-to-do/).

## For the member who refers

The referral page's terms give the referring member a $50 Referral Bonus for each new member who joins between October 1 and December 31, 2026 and meets the purchase test, with no limit on referrals. It is added to the next cash back payment.

## Who should skip it

- You would be buying $50 of something you do not need.
- You will not turn off an ad blocker or VPN for one purchase.
- You plan to make the purchases at Amazon.com or on gift cards.
- You already have a Rakuten account.

## Quick answers

**How much do I need to spend for the Rakuten referral bonus?**
At least $50 in purchases that earn cash back, within 90 days of joining, under the offer read on November 26, 2026.

**Can I get the welcome bonus and the referral bonus?**
No. The welcome bonus terms say it cannot be combined with the Referral Sign Up Bonus.

**When is the Rakuten bonus paid?**
After the store confirms your purchase, with the next payment: February 15, May 15, August 15 or November 15.

# Rakuten Academy Sports cash back: does it work, and what is excluded?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/rakuten-academy-sports-cash-back-how-it-works/
Facts checked: 2026-11-25
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

Yes, but only on part of the store. On November 25, 2026, Rakuten's Academy Sports & Outdoors page showed 2% cash back, with no raised rate. Clearance and sale items, Hot Deals, firearms, ammunition and gift cards earn nothing.

This page is information, not financial advice. Rates change daily, so check the store page on Rakuten on the day you buy. For this morning's headline rate at other stores, see [Rakuten rates today, by store](/rakuten-cash-back-rates-today-by-store/).

## The rate seen on November 25, 2026

| Item | What the page showed |
|---|---|
| Headline rate | 2% |
| Rakuten's "was" label | None |
| Rate by category | No category list |

A "was" label appears when a rate has been raised above the store's base rate. Academy's page has none, so 2% is the plain rate. Nothing on the page promises a higher rate on Black Friday (November 27, 2026).

## What is excluded

Rakuten's terms for Academy list these as earning nothing:

- Clearance and sale items
- Hot Deals
- Firearms
- Ammunition
- Gift cards
- Orders Academy deems to be for reselling

The first two lines matter most this week. On November 25, 2026, the offers on Rakuten's own Academy page were nearly all discounts: up to 25% off Nike, 20% off select drinkware, up to 50% off game tables, and doorbusters. Each was shown with a "2% Cash Back" label beside it. The terms say sale items do not earn.

The page does not explain how the two fit together. Whether a marked-down item in one of those offers earns the 2% is not confirmed. The terms are the stricter reading. One member review shown on the page describes placing an order and then finding the exclusions meant no cash back.

The terms do not define "sale items" or "Hot Deals". Whether an item with a lower price for a few days counts is not confirmed.

## What earns and what does not

| Purchase | Earns cash back? |
|---|---|
| Regular-price item, ordered online after a Rakuten click | Yes, 2% |
| Clearance or sale item | No |
| Hot Deals item | No |
| Firearms and ammunition | No |
| Gift card | No |

At 2%, a $100 order of regular-price items earns $2.00. A $100 order of sale items earns $0 under the terms.

## Coupon codes

The Academy terms on Rakuten have no rule about coupon codes. Whether a code from outside Rakuten affects cash back is not confirmed. The page says Academy offers 10% off for military, teachers and first responders with ID; how that discount interacts with the sale-item exclusion is not confirmed.

## Where Academy does not ship

The special terms say Academy does not ship to Alaska, California, Hawaii or U.S. territories such as Puerto Rico, and does not ship outside the United States. The page says shipping is free on orders of $50 or more.

## Pickup, app and stores

- **Pickup.** The terms do not mention store pickup. Not confirmed.
- **App.** The terms do not mention an Academy app. Not confirmed.
- **In stores.** The Academy page showed an online rate only. Academy did not appear in the part of Rakuten's in-store offer list that loaded on November 25, 2026; the list does not load in full, so this is not confirmed. See [how in-store cash back works](/rakuten-in-store-cash-back-how-it-works/).

## When it shows up

The posting line says cash back is added to the Rakuten account "tomorrow". Payment follows on Rakuten's schedule; see [when Rakuten pays](/rakuten-when-do-you-get-paid/). If an order does not appear, see [what to do when cash back did not track](/rakuten-missing-cash-back-what-to-do/). For a similar store's terms, see [Rakuten at Dick's Sporting Goods](/rakuten-dicks-sporting-goods-cash-back-how-it-works/).

## Who should skip it

- Your cart is mostly clearance, sale or Hot Deals items. The terms say they earn nothing.
- You are buying firearms, ammunition or a gift card.
- You live in Alaska, California, Hawaii or a U.S. territory. Academy does not ship there.
- You are shopping Black Friday doorbusters and expect 2% on them. That is not confirmed.
- You shop in an Academy store. The rate is for online orders.

## Quick answers

**What rate does Rakuten pay at Academy Sports?**
2% on November 25, 2026, with no raised rate shown. Rates change daily.

**Do sale items earn cash back at Academy?**
The terms say no. Clearance items, sale items and Hot Deals are excluded.

**Do firearms and ammunition earn cash back?**
No. Both are named in the exclusions, along with gift cards.

## Not a Rakuten member yet

Joining costs nothing; the one fee in the terms is covered in [is Rakuten free](/is-rakuten-free/). How the joining bonus is earned is laid out in [how the Rakuten bonus works](/rakuten-50-bonus-how-it-works/).

# Rakuten Ace Hardware cash back: does it work, and what is excluded?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/rakuten-ace-hardware-cash-back-how-it-works/
Facts checked: 2026-11-25
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

Yes. On November 25, 2026, Rakuten's Ace Hardware page showed up to 6% cash back, raised from a base of 2%: 6% on most items and 3% on snow equipment. Delivery and assembly charges and the purchase or redemption of gift cards earn nothing.

This page is information, not financial advice. Rates change daily, so check the store page on Rakuten on the day you buy. For this morning's headline rate at other stores, see [Rakuten rates today, by store](/rakuten-cash-back-rates-today-by-store/).

## Rates seen on November 25, 2026

| Category, as listed | Rate shown |
|---|---|
| All other items | 6% |
| Snow equipment | 3% |
| Headline | Up to 6%, "was 2%" |

Here the headline rate is the general one, and the named category is lower. The page does not define "snow equipment". Whether shovels, ice melt or only powered machines fall under it is not confirmed. The activation page on the day of purchase is the place to look.

The "was 2%" label means the rate was raised above the store's base that day. Nothing on the page says how long it lasts.

## What is excluded

Rakuten's terms for Ace Hardware are short. Listed as earning nothing:

- Delivery and assembly
- The purchase of gift cards
- The redemption of gift cards

One special term: using coupon codes not listed on Rakuten may void cash back. The page adds that the store accepts only one coupon or promo code per order.

## What it comes to

| Purchase | Price | Rate seen | Cash back |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hand tools and paint | $100 | 6% | $6.00 |
| Grill | $500 | 6% | $30.00 |
| Snow equipment | $500 | 3% | $15.00 |
| Assembly or delivery charge | Any | Excluded | $0 |
| Gift card | Any | Excluded | $0 |

These are worked examples, not prices from the page. Rakuten's general help page says taxes and shipping fees are never eligible. At the 2% base, the $100 order would earn $2.00.

## Pickup, rewards and local stores

- **Store pickup.** The page describes free store pickup for orders placed on the website, and free shipping to stores. The terms do not exclude pickup, and they do not mention it either. Not confirmed.
- **Ace Rewards.** The page describes the free rewards program: 10 points per $1 and a $5 reward for every 2,500 points. It says a reward and a coupon can be used on the same order. Whether the part of an order paid with a reward earns cash back is not confirmed; the terms name gift cards, not rewards.
- **App.** The page mentions the store's mobile app. The terms do not. A purchase earns only if it starts from a Rakuten link, the Rakuten app or the extension; whether an order finished in the store's app tracks is not confirmed.
- **In stores.** The store page showed an online rate only. The store did not appear in the part of Rakuten's in-store offer list that loaded on November 25, 2026; the list does not load in full, so this is not confirmed. See [how in-store cash back works](/rakuten-in-store-cash-back-how-it-works/).

## When it shows up

The page says cash back is added to the Rakuten account "in a few days". Payment follows on Rakuten's four dates a year; see [when Rakuten pays](/rakuten-when-do-you-get-paid/). Rates at two larger chains are in [Rakuten at Home Depot](/rakuten-home-depot-cash-back-how-it-works/) and [Rakuten at Lowe's](/rakuten-lowes-cash-back-how-it-works/).

## Who should skip it

- You walk into a local store and pay at the register. The rate shown is for online orders.
- You are buying a gift card or paying with one.
- A large share of the bill is delivery or assembly.
- You have a coupon from the store's emails that is not on Rakuten and saves more than the cash back.
- You are waiting for the 6% to hold. It is a raised rate, and none is promised.

## Quick answers

**What rate does Rakuten pay at Ace Hardware?**
Up to 6% on November 25, 2026; snow equipment was at 3%. Rates change daily.

**Do delivery and assembly earn cash back?**
No. Both are on the excluded list, along with gift cards.

**Does store pickup count?**
The terms do not exclude it and do not mention it. Not confirmed.

# Rakuten Adidas cash back: does it work, and what is excluded?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/rakuten-adidas-cash-back-how-it-works/
Facts checked: 2026-11-21
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

Yes. On November 21, 2026, Rakuten's Adidas page showed up to 6% cash back, raised from a usual 2%. Samba, Gazelle, Spezial and EVO SL shoes earn 2%, and named collaborations, gift cards and purchases in the Confirmed app earn nothing.

This page is information, not financial advice. Rates change daily, so check the store page on Rakuten on the day you buy. For this morning's headline rate here and at other stores, see [Rakuten rates today, by store](/rakuten-cash-back-rates-today-by-store/).

## The rate, and how it moves

| Date checked | Rate shown | Rakuten's "was" label |
|---|---|---|
| November 21, 2026 | Up to 6% | 2% |

"Was" is Rakuten's own label for the store's usual rate. "Up to" matters here, because the page splits the rate in two:

| What you buy | Rate on November 21, 2026 |
|---|---|
| Samba, Gazelle, Spezial, EVO SL | 2% |
| All other non-excluded items | 6% |

So the raised rate did not reach those four shoe lines that day.

## What is excluded

Rakuten's terms for Adidas list these as earning nothing:

- Collaborations "such as" Edison Chen, Y-3, Fear of God, Bad Bunny, Wales Bonner, Pharrell, Song for the Mute and Willy Chavarria
- Gift cards
- Purchases made in the Confirmed app
- Orders Adidas judges to be for reselling
- High-volume orders, defined as 10 or more of the same eligible item
- Orders from outside the US

The words "such as" mean the list of collaborations is examples, not the full list. Whether a collaboration that is not named earns cash back is not confirmed.

## Terms worth knowing before you order

- **Orders over $1,500.** These may be subject to review and reversal. Nike's terms set that line at $500.
- **Coupon codes.** The terms say codes not listed on Rakuten may void cash back.
- **Returns.** The Adidas terms on Rakuten say nothing about returns. Rakuten's general rule is that a returned item loses its cash back. Nike's terms are stricter on this point; see [how Rakuten works at Nike](/rakuten-nike-cash-back-how-it-works/).

## App, pickup and member discounts

- **App.** Only the Confirmed app is named as excluded. The terms do not mention the main Adidas app. A purchase earns only if it starts from a Rakuten link, the Rakuten app or the extension, so an order started directly in a store app is not expected to track.
- **Pickup.** The terms do not mention pickup. Not confirmed.
- **adiClub.** Whether a member discount, an adiClub voucher or adiClub points affect cash back is not confirmed.
- **Student and hero discounts.** The page mentions a 15% student discount and discounts for verified groups such as first responders and military. These usually arrive as a code. A code not listed on Rakuten may void cash back.

## What it comes to

| Purchase | Price | Rate that day | Cash back |
|---|---|---|---|
| Samba shoes | $100 | 2% | $2.00 |
| Running shoes, not a 2% line | $130 | 6% | $7.80 |
| Apparel order | $200 | 6% | $12.00 |
| Named collaboration or gift card | Any | 0% | $0 |

Taxes and shipping do not count.

Other retailers on Rakuten sell Adidas shoes, each with its own rate and exclusions. On the same page that day, Foot Locker showed 6% (was 3%), JD Sports 8% (was 3%) and Finish Line 2%. Whether a Samba earns the full rate at those stores is not confirmed. A higher rate helps only if the price is the same.

## In stores

Adidas did not appear in the part of Rakuten's in-store offer list that loaded on November 21, 2026. The list was cut off, so this is not confirmed. See [how in-store cash back works](/rakuten-in-store-cash-back-how-it-works/).

## When you get the money

The Adidas page says cash back is added to a Rakuten account the next day. It then waits to be confirmed, which typically takes 3 to 14 weeks, and is paid on the next of four dates a year. See [when Rakuten pays](/rakuten-when-do-you-get-paid/) and [what to do when cash back did not track](/rakuten-missing-cash-back-what-to-do/). Card rewards are separate and come on top; see [stacking with card rewards](/rakuten-stack-with-credit-card-rewards/).

## Who should skip it

- You buy collaborations. The named ones are excluded.
- You buy through the Confirmed app.
- You have a student or hero discount code worth more than the cash back. On a $100 order, 15% off is $15 and 6% back is $6.
- You pay with or buy Adidas gift cards.
- You buy 10 or more of one item, or buy to resell.

## Quick answers

**What rate does Rakuten pay at Adidas?**
Up to 6% on November 21, 2026, against a usual 2%. Rates change daily.

**Do Sambas earn cash back?**
Yes, at 2% on that date. Samba, Gazelle, Spezial and EVO SL were held at 2% while other items earned 6%.

**Can I use an Adidas promo code and still get cash back?**
The terms say codes not listed on Rakuten may void cash back. Codes shown on Rakuten are the safe ones.

## Not a Rakuten member yet

Joining costs nothing; the one fee in the terms is covered in [is Rakuten free](/is-rakuten-free/). A new member gets one joining bonus, not two. [Welcome bonus or a friend's referral bonus](/rakuten-welcome-bonus-vs-referral-bonus/) compares the two offers as read on November 26, 2026.

# Can you get Amex points from Rakuten instead of cash, and is it worth switching?

Source: https://itsworththefee.com/rakuten-amex-points-instead-of-cash/
Facts checked: 2026-11-20
Publisher: Worth the Fee (independent; some pages end with a disclosed referral link)

Yes. If you hold a US American Express card that earns Membership Rewards, Rakuten will pay you 1 point for every cent of cash back in place of the cash. It is worth switching only if you reliably get more than 1 cent of value from each point, which in practice means moving points to airline or hotel programs.

This page is information, not financial advice.

## The rate

| Rakuten offer at a store | Paid as cash | Paid as points |
|---|---|---|
| $1 of cash back | $1 | 100 points |
| 2% back | 2 cents per dollar | 2 points per dollar |
| 10% back | 10 cents per dollar | 10 points per dollar |

Stores on Rakuten keep showing "cash back" after you switch. The amount is turned into points behind the scenes.

## Who qualifies

- You need a US Amex card enrolled in Membership Rewards. Rakuten names the Gold, Green and Platinum cards as examples.
- The card must be open and not past due.
- Corporate cards do not qualify. The Rakuten American Express Card does not qualify by itself either.
- You do not have to pay with the Amex card. Any card works at checkout; the Amex card only decides where the reward goes.

Amex cards that earn cash back or an airline's or hotel's own points are outside Membership Rewards, so they do not count.

## How to switch, step by step

1. Sign in to Rakuten and open Account Settings.
2. Change your payment method to Membership Rewards points.
3. Sign in to your Membership Rewards account when asked, to link the two.
4. Shop through Rakuten as usual.

If you are new to Rakuten, you can pick points while signing up.

If you later replace or close the linked card, you have to link the new one in Account Settings or transfers stop.

## When the points arrive

Rakuten sends points on the same four dates it pays cash: February 15, May 15, August 15 and November 15. Only rewards the store has confirmed before the date are included. Confirmation typically takes 3 to 14 weeks for shopping and 6 to 17 weeks after a trip ends for travel.

You need at least 501 confirmed points. A balance of 500 or fewer carries over to the next date. In your Amex account the line reads "Rakuten Additional MR Points".

## Is it worth it?

It comes down to one question: what do you do with Amex points?

| How you use a point | Rough value | Switch? |
|---|---|---|
| Statement credit or similar | 1 cent or less | No. Take the cash. |
| Transfers to airline partners, used with care | 1.7 to 2 cents, by two travel sites' estimates | Yes, if you really do this |

Those higher figures are other people's estimates. They assume you find award seats and book them. Points you never use are worth nothing, and programs can raise their prices at any time. Cash cannot lose value that way.

Reasons to stay on cash:

- You like a check or PayPal payment four times a year and do not want to manage points.
- You have no trip in mind that points would pay for.
- You use offers on Rakuten from other card issuers. Rakuten's terms say those may not be available once you choose Amex points.

## Two things that are not settled

**Can you switch back?** One large travel site reported that the choice cannot be undone, and in the same article said you can always change your preference. Rakuten's own help pages do not say either way. Treat the switch as possibly permanent until you see otherwise in your own account settings.

**What happens to your existing balance?** Rakuten says cash back confirmed before you switch is turned into points and sent on the next transfer date. One travel site says the opposite. If you want that balance as cash, wait until after a payment date before switching.

Whether a new-member bonus arrives as points or cash is also unclear. Rakuten's terms mention both payment types, while an older article says the bonus stays as cash.

## Quick answers

**How many Amex points is $1 of Rakuten cash back?**
100 points. The rate is 1 point per cent.

**Do I have to pay with my Amex card?**
No. You only need to hold a qualifying card and link it.

**When do the points show up?**
On February 15, May 15, August 15 or November 15, once you have at least 501 confirmed points.

## Sources

- [Rakuten: Membership Rewards points FAQ](https://www.rakuten.com/help/article/american-express-membership-rewards-points-faq-360017609253)
- [Rakuten: Membership Rewards points terms](https://www.rakuten.com/help/article/american-express-membership-rewards-points-at-rakuten-terms-360017609913)
- [Rakuten: When will I get paid?](https://www.rakuten.com/help/article/when-will-i-get-paid-360002117667)
- [Rakuten: Why didn't I earn cash back?](https://www.rakuten.com/help/article/why-didnt-i-earn-cash-back-360036367393)
- [Rakuten: Welcome bonus terms](https://www.rakuten.com/help/article/welcome-bonus-terms)
- [One Mile at a Time: Earning Amex points with Rakuten](https://onemileatatime.com/guides/amex-points-rakuten/)
- [The Points Guy: Earn Amex points with Rakuten](https://thepointsguy.com/news/earn-amex-points-with-rakuten)
